Have you ever had someone try to explain something to you a dozen times with no luck, but then when you see a picture, the idea finally clicks?
If that sounds familiar, maybe you might consider yourself a visual learner.
Or, if reading or listening does the trick, maybe you feel like you’re a verbal learner.
We call these labels learning styles. But is there really a way to categorize different types of students?
Well, it actually seems that multiple presentation formats, especially if one of them is visual, help most people learn.
When psychologists and educators test for learning styles, they’re trying to figure out whether these are inherent traits that affect how well students learn, instead of just a preference.
Usually they start by giving a survey to figure out what style a student favors, like visual or verbal learning.
Then, there try to teach the students something with a specific presentation style, like using visual aids, and do a follow-up test to see how much they learned.
That way, the researchers can see if the self-identified verbal learners really learned better when the information was just spoken aloud, for example.
But, according to a 2008 review, only one study that followed this design found that students actually learned best with their preferred style.
But the study had some big flaws.
The researchers excluded two-thirds of the original participants because they didn’t seem to have any clear learning style from the survey at the beginning, and they didn’t even report the actual test scores in the final paper.
So ... it doesn’t really seem like learning style learning styles are an inherent trait that we all have.
But, that doesn’t mean that all students will do amazingly if they just spend all their time reading from a textbook.
Instead, most people seem to learn better if they’re taught in several ways — especially if one is visual.
In one study, researchers tested whether students remembered lists of words better if they heard them, saw them, or both.
And everyone seemed to do better if they got to see the words in print, even the self-identified auditory learners.
Their preference didn’t seem to matter.
Similar studies tested whether students learned basic physics and chemistry concepts better by reading plain text or viewing pictures, too.
And everyone did better with the help of pictures.

Free-market capitalism hasn’t freed us; it has trapped us.
It’s imperative for us to embrace a workplace revolution.
We are unlikely to spend our last moments regretting that we didn’t spend enough of our lives slaving away at work.
We may instead find ourselves feeling guilty about the time we didn’t spend watching our children grow, or with our loved ones, or travelling, or on the cultural or leisure pursuits that bring us happiness.
Unfortunately, the average full-time employee in the world works 42 hours a week — well over a third of the time we’re awake. Some of our all too precious time is being stolen: office workers do around two billion hours of unpaid overtime each year.
So it’s extremely welcome that some government coalitions have started looking into potentially cutting the working week to four days.
The champions of free market capitalism promised their way of life would bring us freedom.
But it wasn’t freedom at all; from the lack of secure, affordable housing to growing job insecurity and rising personal debt, the individual is trapped.
Nine decades ago, leading economists predicted that technological advances and rising productivity would mean that we’d be working a 15-hour week by now: that target has been somewhat missed.
Here is the most malignant threat to our personal freedom, particularly as the balance of power in the workplace has been shifted so dramatically from worker to boss.
A huge portion of our lives involves the surrender of our freedom and personal autonomy.
It’s time in which we are directed by the needs and desires of others, and denied the right to make our own choices.
That’s bad for us: it’s hardly surprising that over half a million workers suffer from work-related mental health conditions each year, or that 15.4 million working days were lost to work-related stress last year, a jump of nearly a quarter.
Yes, there are those who, far from being overworked, actually seek more hours.
But a shorter working week would enable us to redistribute hours from the overworked to the under worked.
We need to look at ways of cutting the working week without slashing living standards: after all, the world’s workers have already suffered the worst deduction in wages since the early 1800s.
And cutting the working week would be conducive to the individual, giving millions of workers more time to spend as they see fit.

Today I’m going to talk about Germany’s dream airport in Berlin.
The airport looks exactly like every other major modern airport in Europe, except for one big problem: more than seven years after it was originally supposed to open, it still stands empty
Germany is known for its efficiency and refined engineering, but when it comes to its new ghost airport, this reputation could not be further from the truth.
Plagued by long delays, perpetual mismanagement and ever-soaring costs, the airport has become something of a joke among Germans — and a source of frustration for local politicians, business leaders and residents alike.
Planning for the new airport began in 1989.
At the time, it became clear that the newly-reunited Berlin would need a modern airport with far greater capacity than its existing airports.
The city broke ground on the new airport in 2006.
The first major sign of problems came in summer 2010, when the construction corporation pushed the opening from October 2011 to June 2012.
In 2012, the city planned an opening ceremony but less than a month beforehand, inspectors found significant problems with the fire safety system and pushed the opening back again to 2013.
It wasn’t just the smoke system: many other major problems subsequently emerged.
More than 90 metres of cable were incorrectly installed; 4,000 doors were wrongly numbered; escalators were too short.
And there was a shortage of check-in desks.
So why, with so many problems discovered, didn’t the airport corporation decide to give up on the project and start over?
The reason is simple: people are often hesitant to terminate a project when they’ve already invested time or resources into it, even if it might make logical sense to do so.
The longer the delays continued, the more problems inspectors found. Leadership of the planning corporation has changed hands nearly as many times as the opening date has been pushed back.
Initially, rather than appointing a general contractor to run the project, the corporation decided to manage it themselves despite lack of experience with an undertaking of that scale.
To compound the delays, the unused airport is resulting in massive costs.
Every month it remains unopened costs between €9m and €10m.
Assuming all goes well, the airport should open in October 2020.
But the still-empty airport stands as the biggest embarrassment to Germany’s reputation for efficiency — and a continuing drain on city and state resources.

23. Why was there a need for a new airport in Berlin?
24. Why did Berlin postpone the opening of its dream airport again and again?
25. What happens while the airport remains unused?

sections.passage:
1 As British poet John Donne said, “No one is an island.” 2 Human beings are social animals who live in groups and work together. 3 Because of this, the importance of having a sense of social responsibility cannot be overvalued.
1 For one thing, the sense of social responsibility will make us behave ourselves in public, which is helpful to build a harmonious society. 2 For instance, those with a good sense of social responsibility always pay attention to protecting the environment when they travel. 3 On the contrary, those who lack a sense of social responsibility always put their needs first instead of public environment. 4 For another, the sense of social responsibility is beneficial to our social cohesion. 5 For example, whenever a disaster occurs, a large number of volunteers with a sense of social responsibility devote themselves to the relief and reconstruction work in disaster-affected areas, thereby helping the disaster-hit people overcome the difficulties successfully.
1 All in all, if all the citizens have a sound sense of social responsibility, it is hopeful that the society will enjoy a better future. 2 Therefore, let’s take our social responsibility and contribute to our society.

sections.passage: 1 The plum blossom, which ranks first among the top ten famous flowers in China, originated in the South of China and has been cultivated and planted for more than 3,000 years. 2 In the dead of winter, colorful plum blossoms brave the bitter cold and blossom proudly against the wind and snow. 3 In traditional Chinese culture, the plum blossom symbolizes toughness, purity and elegance, inspiring people to brave hardship and forge ahead. 4 Since ancient times, many poets and painters have drawn inspiration from the plum blossom and created countless immortal works. 5 The common people also love plum blossoms, which are often used as home decorations during the Spring Festival. 6 The city of Nanjing has designated the plum blossom as its city flower and holds a plum blossom festival every year, during which thousands of people brave the bitter cold to take a walk in the snow and enjoy the plum blossoms on the Plum Blossom Hill.

questions.stem: ①梅花(plum blossom)位居中国十大名花之首，源于中国南方，已有三千多年的栽培和种植历史。②隆冬时节，五颜六色的梅花不畏严寒，迎着风雪傲然绽放。③在中国传统文化中，梅花象征着坚强、纯洁、高雅、激励人们不畏艰难、砥砺前行。④自古以来，许多诗人和画家从梅花中获取灵感，创作了无数不朽的作品。⑤普通大众也都喜爱梅花，春节期间常用于家庭装饰。⑥南京市已将梅花定为市花，每年举办梅花节，成千上万的人冒着严寒到梅花山踏雪赏梅。
questions.answer: 1 The plum blossom, which ranks first among the top ten famous flowers in China, originated in the South of China and has been cultivated and planted for more than 3,000 years. 2 In the dead of winter, colorful plum blossoms brave the bitter cold and blossom proudly against the wind and snow. 3 In traditional Chinese culture, the plum blossom symbolizes toughness, purity and elegance, inspiring people to brave hardship and forge ahead. 4 Since ancient times, many poets and painters have drawn inspiration from the plum blossom and created countless immortal works. 5 The common people also love plum blossoms, which are often used as home decorations during the Spring Festival. 6 The city of Nanjing has designated the plum blossom as its city flower and holds a plum blossom festival every year, during which thousands of people brave the bitter cold to take a walk in the snow and enjoy the plum blossoms on the Plum Blossom Hill.

questions.explanation:
【考点】

副词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格所在句子成分完整，空格前面是不及物动词died，后面为介词短语from outdoor air pollution作状语，因此空格处需要填入副词。

【答案解析】

逗号前面的分句提到，全球超过80%的城市人口正在呼吸的空气不符合世界卫生组织的标准。空格所在分句进一步指出，2015年估计有450万人因室外空气污染而死亡。因此，空格处需要填入一个可以修饰“死亡”的副词。备选的副词中，simply“仅仅，只是”与此处意思不符，故排除。由此确定副词K) prematurely为本题答案。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格所在句的主语是the decisions,  that we make now about the design of our cities是定语从句修饰主语，空格前面是will，空格后面是并列的名词短语the everyday lives and health of the coming generations，由此推断空格处应填入及物动词原形作谓语。

【答案解析】

空格前一句提到，在全球范围内，预计未来40年内城市人口将翻一番，另外20亿人口将需要新的居住地以及在城市内出行所需的服务和道路。紧接着空格所在句提到“我们现在做出的城市设计决策”和“子孙后代的日常生活和健康状况”，两者之间的关系通常是前者影响或决定后者，因此空格处应填入一个表示“影响”或“决定”的及物动词。备选词中符合以上要求的只有determine“决定”，由此确定答案为C)。

【考点】

语义推断题。

【确定词性】

空格前为系动词become，空格后是介词with，因此空格处应填入形容词或动词的分词形式，与with短语搭配作表语。

【答案解析】

在空格所在句中，and连接的第二个分句提到，许多国家打算在未来20年内禁止销售新的汽油和柴油汽车，而第一个分句提到“交通”和“空气污染”。由此可知，人们认为汽油和柴油汽车会造成污染，所以才打算禁止销售这类汽车。

也就是说，“交通（汽油和柴油汽车）”与“空气污染”之间密切相关，因此空��处所填词应与后面的with air pollution搭配表达“与空气污染密切相关”的意思。备选词中符合以上要求的只有synonymous, be synonymous with...意为“与……相同的，与……近似的”，由此确定答案为N)。空格处需要填入形容词或动词的分词形式，且能与介词with搭配，因此可以排除alternate和peak。generated 和merged虽然可以和with搭配，但与句意不符，故排除。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格所在句的谓语是will not mean，宾语是pollution-free cities，空格前为副词simply，由此推断空格处需要填入动名词，与to electric cars一起作句子主语。

【答案解析】

空格前一句提到，交通已成为空气污染的同义词，许多国家打算在未来20年内禁止销售新的汽油和柴油汽车。空格所在句句首的But表示转折，说明仅仅使用电动汽车并不意味着就是无污染城市。因此，空格处需要填入一个表示“使用转变”的动词，且能与介词to搭配。备选项中只有M) switching“转变，转换”符合要求，故为答案。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格位于how引导的宾语从句中，从句的主语是the electricity，不定式短语to run them作后置定语修饰the electricity，空格前是系动词is，how“如何”在从句中作方式状语，从句的主语the electricity是物，故推断空格处应填入动词的过去分词形式，和is一起构成被动语态。

【答案解析】

空格前面提到，电动汽车造成的排放水平取决于它们运行所需要的电力如何________。备选项中只有D) generated“产生（电等能量）”符合以上要求，故为答案。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格位于while连接的第二个分句中，该分句的主语是brakes，tyre and roads，谓语是create，空格前还有形容词tiny和airborne，所以需要填入可数名词的复数形式或者不可数名词。

【答案解析】

前一句提到，仅仅转用电动汽车并不意味着就是无污染城市，空格所在句进一步说明电动汽车的污染。第一个分句提到电动汽车的排放，空格所在分句也应该是在说明电动汽车的污染。再根据此处句意“刹车、轮胎和道路在磨损时都会产生微小的在空气中悬浮的________”可知，空格处应填入一个表示刹车、轮胎和道路在磨损时能产生的微小的在空气中悬浮的“物体”的名词。备选项中只有I) particles“微粒”符合要求，故为答案。miniatures意为“缩影，微小模型”，虽然可以被tiny修饰，但并非刹车、轮胎和道路在磨损时产生的物体，也和电动汽车造成的污染无关，故排除。

【考点】

固定搭配题。

【确定词性】

通过分析句子结构可知，空格位于while连接的并列分句中，从句的主语是young people，空格前为系动词are，空格后为介宾结构for other means of travel，由此推断空格处需要填入动词的分词形式或形容词，与be动词搭配构成谓语或者系表结构，而且空格处所填单词能与for搭配。

【答案解析】

while前的句子指出，在发达国家，随着更多的人搬到市中心，汽车的使用量正在下降，空格所在句意在说明年轻人会使用其他的出行方式。因此，空格处所填词应与后面的for other means of travel搭配表达“使用其他的出行方式”的意思，备选词中符合以上要求的只有opting，opt for...是固定搭配，意为“选择……”，由此确定答案为H)。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格位于if引导的从句中，该从句的主语是motor vehicle use，谓语是has reached，宾语是its ________，后面为并列连词and和并列谓语will decline，因此空格处需要填入名词作reached的宾语。

【答案解析】

本句提到机动车辆的使用情况：一方面是机动车辆的使用是否已达到某种水平，另一方面是机动车辆的使用是否将开始下降。因此，空格处需要填入一个表示“某种水平”的名词。备选名词中只有J) peak“高峰，顶点”符合要求，故为答案。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格前有介词with和限定词this，所以需要填入名词的单数形式，与this 搭配作with的宾语。

【答案解析】

but前面的分句提到，研究人员已在询问机动车辆的使用是否将下降。空格所在分句则表示转折，指出交通规划人员仍在铺设新路来解决交通堵塞问题，还未跟上前一分句提到的“机动车辆的使用已达高峰并将下降”这一“趋势”。由此确定名词trend“趋势，倾向”为本题答案。

【考点】

副词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格所在句句子成分完整，空格前面是情态动词can，后面为动宾结构double the traffic，因此空格处需要填入副词。

【答案解析】

上文以伦敦M25外环高速公路为例，指出铺设新路并非解决交通堵塞问题的好办法，其使用者将会知道新道路很快就会挤满更多的车辆。空格所在句继续以美国为例说明将道路规模扩大一倍会使交通流量增加一倍，结果将我们带回到起点。因此，空格处需要填入一个强调“将道路规模扩大一倍”会导致“交通流量增加一倍”这一结果的副词。由此确定副词simply“仅仅，只是”为本题答案。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 The marketing is tempting: Get stronger muscles and healthier bodies with minimal effort by adding protein powder to your morning shake or juice drink. 2 Or grab a protein bar at lunch or for a quick snack. 3 Today, you can find protein supplements everywhere — online or at the pharmacy, grocery store or health food store. 4 They come in powders, pills and bars. 5 With more than $12 billion in sales this year, the industry is booming and, according to the market research company, Grand View Research, is on track to sell billions more by 2025. 6 But do we really need all this supplemental protein? 7 It depends. 8 There are pros, cons and some other things to consider.?
1 For starters, protein is critical for every cell in our body. 2 It helps build nails, hair, bones and muscles. 3 It can also help you feel fuller longer than eating foods without protein. 4 And, unlike nutrients that are found only in a few foods, protein is present in all foods. 5 “The typical American diet is a lot higher in protein than a lot of us think,” says registered dietician Angela Pipitone. 6 “It’s in foods many of us expect, such as beef, chicken and other types of meat and dairy. 7 But it’s also in foods that may not come immediately to mind like vegetables, fruit, beans and grains.”?
1 The U.S. government’s recommended daily allowance (RDA) for the average adult is 50 to 60 grams of protein a day. 2 This may sound like a lot, but Pipitone says: “We get bits of protein here and there and that really adds up throughout the day.” 3 Take, for example, breakfast. 4 If you eat two eggs topped with a little bit of cheese and an orange on the side, you already have 22 grams of protein. 5 Each egg gives you 7 grams, the cheese gives you about 6 grams and the orange—about 2 grams. 6 Add a lunch of chicken, rice and broccoli（西兰花）, and you are already over the recommended 50 grams. 7 “You can get enough protein and meet the RDA before you even get to dinner,” says Pipitone.?
1 So if it’s so easy to get your protein in food, why add more in the form of powders, snack bars or a boost at your local juice bar? 2 No need to, says Pipitone, because, in fact, most of us already get enough protein in our diet. 3 “Whole foods are always the best option rather than adding supplements,” she says, noting the FDA does not regulate supplements as rigorously as foods or drugs. 4 So there could be less protein, more sugar and some additives you wouldn’t expect, such as caffeine（咖啡因）.?
1 If you are considering a supplement, read the list of ingredients, she says, although this is not always reliable. 2 “I’ve seen very expensive protein supplements that claim to be high quality but they might not really be beneficial for the average healthy adult,” she says. 3 “It could just be a waste of money.”?
1 But there are certain situations that do warrant extra protein. 2 “Anytime you’re repairing or building muscle,” Pipitone says, such as if you’re an extreme endurance athlete, training for a marathon, or you’re a body builder. 3 If you’re moderately exercising for 150 minutes a week, as the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommends, or less than that, you’re probably not an extreme athlete. 4 Extreme athletes expend lots of energy breaking down and repairing and building muscles.? 5 Protein can give them the edge they need to speed that process.
1 Vegans can benefit from protein supplements sine they do not eat animal-based protein sources like meat, dairy or eggs. 2 And, for someone always on-the-go who may not have time for a meal, a protein snack bar can be a good option for occasional meal replacement. 3 Also, individuals recovering from surgery or an injury can also benefit from extra protein. 4 So, too, can older people. 5 At around age 60, “muscles really start to break down,” says Kathryn Starr, an aging researcher, “and because of that, the protein needs of an older adult actually increase.”?
1 In fact, along with her colleague Connie Bales, Starr recently conducted a small study that found that adding extra protein foods to the diet of obese older individuals who were trying to lose weight strengthened their muscles. 2 Participants in the study were separated into two groups—one group was asked to eat 30 grams of protein per meal in the form of whole foods. 3 That meant they were eating 90 grams of protein a day. 4 The other group—the control group—was put on a typical low-calorie diet with about 50 to 60 grams of protein a day. 5 After six months, researchers found the high protein group had significantly improved their muscle function — almost twice as much as the control group. 6 “They were able to walk faster, had improved balance, and were also able to get up out of a chair faster than the control group,” Starr says. 7 All 67 participants were over 60 years of age, and both groups lost about the same amount of weight.?
1 Starr is now looking into whether high-protein diets also improve the quality of the muscle itself in seniors. 2 She’s using CT scans to measure muscle size and fat, and comparing seniors on a high-protein diet with those on regular diets. 3 She says her findings should be available in a couple of months.
1 In the meantime, 70-year-old Corliss Keith, who was in the high protein group in Starr’s latest study, says she feels a big difference. 2 “I feel excellent,” she says. 3 “I feel like I have a different body, I have more energy, I’m stronger.” 4 She says she is able to take Zumba exercise classes three times a week, work out on the treadmill（跑步机）, and take long, brisk walks. 5 Keith also lost more than 15 pounds. 6 “I’m a fashionable person, so now I’m back in my 3-inch heels,” she says.
1 As people age, Starr says muscle strength is key to helping them stay strong and continue living on their own in their own home. 2 “I feel very much alive now,” says Keith. 3 “I feel like I could stay by myself until I’m 100.”
1 But can people overdo protein? 2 Pipitone says you do have to be careful. 3 Other researchers say too much protein can cause cramps（痉挛）, headaches, and fatigue. 4 Dehydration（脱水）is also a risk when you eat too much protein. 5 Pipitone says if you increase protein, you also have to increase your fluid intake. 6 “I always tell people to make sure they’re drinking enough fluids,” which for the average person is 60 to 70 ounces a day, which translates into eight 8-ounce glasses of water or liquid per day.?
1 There have been some indications that extra protein makes the kidneys work harder, which could be problematic for individuals with a history of kidney disease and for them, the supplements may increase the risk of kidney stones, she says.?
1 Bottom line, if you think you need more protein in your diet, consider these questions: Are you an extreme athlete; are you recovering from injury or surgery; or are you 60 years or older? 2 If so, adding high protein foods like eggs and meat products to your diet can be beneficial. 3 And, if you’re not sure, it is always a good idea to check with your primary care provider.

questions.explanation:
【定位】

由题干中的recommended amount of protein定位到文章C)段第一句和最后一句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题，定位句提到，美国政府对普通成年人的每日建议摄入量是50至60克蛋白质，人们甚至在晚餐前就可以达到每日建议摄入量。题干中的recommended amount of protein对应定位句中的recommended daily allowance (RDA) ...is 50 to 60 grams of protein a day，题干中的easy是对定位句中You can get enough protein and meet the RDA before you even get to dinner的概括归纳，故答案为C)。

【定位】

由题干中的Pipitone、healthy adults和protein supplements定位到E)段最后两句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，皮皮托内认为蛋白质补充剂实际上可能对普通健康成年人没有好处，这可能只是在浪费钱。由上文可知，该段中的she指代Pipitone。题干中的healthy adults和protein supplements在定位句中均有提及，题干中的need not spend money是对定位句中a waste of money的同义转述，故答案为E)。

【定位】

由题干中的protein supplement business和thriving定位到文章A)段第五句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，该行业正在蓬勃发展，今年的销售额超过120亿美元，并且该行业的销售额有望在2025年再增加数十亿美元。定位句中的the industry是指protein supplement industry。题干中的thriving是定位句中booming的近义词，故答案为A)。

【定位】

由题干中的Protein和repairing of damaged muscles定位到文章F)段最后两句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，极限运动员消耗大量的能量来分解、修复和塑造肌肉，而蛋白质可以为他们提供所需的优势来加速该过程。题干中的speed the repairing of damaged muscles 是对定位句中speed that process的同义转述，故答案为F)。

【定位】

由题干中的some internal organ和malfunctioning定位到文章M)段。

 

【答案解析】

细节推断题。定位段提到，额外的蛋白质会使肾脏工作更困难，这可能给有肾脏病史的人带来问题，如补充剂可能会增加患肾结石的风险。题干中的overburden some internal organ是对定位句中makes the kidneys work harder的同义转述，题干中的leading to its malfunctioning是对定位句中be problematic for individuals with a history of kidney disease的推断，故答案为M)。

【定位】

由题干中的Older adults、take in more protein和keep their muscles strong定位到G)段最后一句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句提到，在60岁左右，肌肉真的开始分解了，正因为如此，老年人对蛋白质的需求实际上增加了。题干中的take in more protein是对定位句中the protein needs… actually increase的同义转述。定位句提到老年人需要摄入更多蛋白质的原因提示词是because of that，that指代直接引语中的muscles really start to break down。由此可知，题干中的to keep their muscles strong是对定位句中because of that和muscles really start to break down的概括归纳，故答案为G)。

【定位】

由题干中的Protein、in more foods和people might realize定位到文章B)段最后一句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句前一句提到，它存在于我们很多人可以想到的食物中，如牛肉、鸡肉和其他肉类和奶制品。定位句提到，它也存在于人们不会立刻想到的食物中，如蔬菜、水果、豆类和谷物等。由上文可知，定位句中的it指代protein。题干是对It’s in foods many of us expect和it’s also in foods that may not come immediately to mind的概括归纳，故答案为B)。

【定位】

由题干中的Additional protein、strengthen the muscles和overweight seniors定位到文章H)段第一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，一项研究发现在试图减肥的肥胖老年人的饮食中添加额外的蛋白质食物强化了他们的肌肉。题干中的Additional是定位句中extra的同义词，题干中的overweight seniors是对定位句中obese older individuals的同义转述，题干中的seeking weight loss是对定位句中trying to lose weight的同义转述，故答案为H)。

【定位】

由题干中的Pipitone、whole foods和the best source of protein定位到文章D)段第三句。

 

【答案解析】

细节推断题。定位句提到，她认为天然食品总是最好的选择，而不是添加补充剂。由上一句可知，定位句中的she是指Piptione，题干中的the best source of protein是对定位句中the best option rather than adding supplements的同义转述，故答案为D)。

【定位】

由题干中的drink more liquid和take in more protein定位到文章L)段第五句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，皮皮托内指出，如果增加蛋白质，还必须增加液体摄入量。题干中��drink more liquid是对定位句中increase your fluid intake的同义转述，题干中take in more protein是对定位句中increase protein的同义转述，故答案为L)。

sections.title: Section C passage 1
sections.passage:
1 Last year, a child was born at a hospital in the UK with her heart outside her body. 2 Few babies survive this rare condition, and those who do must endure numerous operations and are likely to have complex needs. 3 When her mother was interviewed, three weeks after her daughter’s birth, she was asked if she was prepared for what might be a daunting （令人生畏的） task caring for her. 4 She answered without hesitation that, as far as she was concerned, this would be a “privilege”.
1 Rarely has there been a better example of the power of attitude, one of our most powerful psychological tools. 2 Our attitudes allow us to turn mistakes into opportunities, and loss into the chance for new beginnings. 3 An attitude is a settled way of thinking, feeling and / or behaving towards particular objects, people, events or ideologies. 4 We use our attitudes to filter, interpret and react to the world around us.? 5 You weren’t born with attitudes; rather they are all learned, and this happens in a number of ways.
1 The most powerful influences occur during early childhood and include both what happened to you directly, and what those around you did and said in your presence. 2 As you acquire a distinctive identity, your attitudes are further refined by the behavior of those with whom you identify — your family, those of your gender and culture, and the people you admire, even though you may not know them personally.? 3 Friendships and other important relationships become increasingly important, particularly during adolescence. 4 About that same time and throughout adulthood, the information you receive, especially when ideas are repeated in association with goals and achievements you find attractive, also refines your attitudes.
1 Many people assume that our attitudes are internally consistent, that is, the way you think and feel about someone or something predicts your behavior towards them. 2 However, many studies have found that feelings and thoughts don’t necessarily predict behavior.? 3 In general, your attitudes will be internally consistent only when the behavior is easy, and when those around you hold similar beliefs. 4 That’s why, for example, many say they believe in the benefits of recycling or exercise, but don’t behave in line with their views, because it takes awareness, effort and courage to go beyond merely stating that you believe something is a good idea.?
1 One of the most effective ways to change an attitude is to start behaving as if you already feel and think the way you’d prefer to.? 2 Take some time to reflect on your attitudes, to think about what you believe and why. 3 Is there anything you consider a burden rather than a privilege? 4 If so, start behaving—right now—as if the latter is the case.

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What do we learn from the passage about attitude?

关于态度，我们从本文了解到什么？

A) It shapes our beliefs and ideologies.

它塑造我们的看法和意识形态

B) It improves our psychological wellbeing.

它改善我们的心理健康

C) It determines how we respond to our immediate environment.

它决定我们如何应对当前环境

D) It changes the way we think, feel and interact with one another.

它改变我们思考、感受及彼此互动的方式

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的attitude和题文同序原则定位到2段④句。定位句指出，我们用自己的态度来过滤、解释和回应周围世界。由此可知，态度决定了我们如何应对周围环境，故答案为C。

 

【错误选项分析��

A选项【偷换概念】：2段③句提到，态度是对特定物体、人物、事件或意识形态的一种固定的思考、感受和/或行为方式，而非塑造了人们的意识形态，故排除A)。

B选项【无中生有】：2段①句提到了psychological，但是指态度是我们最强大的心理工具之一，并未说明态度改善了我们的心理健康，故排除B)。

D选项【偷换概念】：2段③句提到，态度是一种固定的思考、感受和行为方式，而不是改变我们思考、感受和彼此互动的方式，故排除D)。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What can contribute to the refinement of one’s attitude, according to the passage?

本文指出，什么有利于完善人们的态度？

A) Their idols’ behaviors.

他们的崇拜对象的行为

B) Their educational level.

他们的教育程度

C) Their contact with the opposite gender.

与异性的接触

D) Their interaction with different cultures.

与不同文化的互动

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的 refinement定位到3段②句。定位句提到，当具有鲜明个性时，态度会通过你认同之人的行为得到进一步完善，而认同之人包括家人、性别和文化相同的人以及崇拜的人，即使你自己可��并不认识他们。崇拜的人就是偶像，属于个人所认同之人。由此可知，偶像的行为有助于完善一个人的态度，故答案为A)。

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【无中生有】：原文并未提及B)“他们的教育程度”，故排除。

C/D选项【反向干扰】：3段②句提到性别和文化相同的人也属于认同之人，是这些人的行为有助于完善态度，C)“与异性的接触”和D)“与不同文化的互动”与原文表述相反，故均排除。

What do many studies find about people’s feelings and thoughts?

关于人们的感受和想法，许多研究有何发现？

A) They may not suggest how a person is going to behave.

它们可能无法预示一个人的行为

B) They are in a way consistent with a person’s mentality.

它们在某种意义上与人们的心态一致

C) They may not find expression in interpersonal relations.

它们可能不会在人际关系中表现出来

D) They are in line with a person’s behavior no matter what.

它们总是与人们的行为相一致

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的many studies和feelings and thoughts定位到4段②句。定位句指出，许多研究发现，感觉和想法并不一定能预示行为，即不会表明一个人将如何行事，故答案为A)。

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【偷换概念】：4段③句提到，通常情况下，只有当行为简单且周围的人与你观点相似时，你的态度才会是内在一致的。这是指观点相似时态度的内在一致，而不是人们的感受和想法与心态一致，故排除B)。

C选项【无中生有】：原文并未提及人际关系，故排除C)。

D选项【反向干扰】：4段最后一句提到，许多人表示他们相信回收利用或锻炼身体有好处，但其言行却不一致，由此可知，人们的感受和想法并非总是与行为一致，D)与原文表述相反，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

How come many people don’t do what they believe is good?

为什么许多人不去做自己认为对的事

A) They can’t afford the time.

他们抽不出时间

B) They have no idea how to.

他们不知道怎么做

C) They are hypocritical.

他们虚伪

D) They lack willpower.

他们缺乏意志力

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的many people don’t do what they believe is good定位到4段末句。定位句提到，这就是为什么许多人表示他们相信回收利用或锻炼身体有好处，但其言行却不一致，因为这需要意识、努力和勇气，而不仅仅只是说你相信某事是个好主意。由此可知，许多人不去做他们认为好的事情就是因为他们缺乏意识、努力和勇气，也就是意志力，故答案为D)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A/B/C选项【无中生有】：选项原文并未提及A)“他们抽不出时间”、B)“他们不知道怎么做”和C)“他们虚伪”，故排除。

What is proposed as a strategy to change attitude?

本文提出的一种改变态度的策略是什么？

在一段时间内逐渐调整自己的行为

由题干中的a strategy to change attitude定位到5段①句。定位句指出，改变态度最有效的方法之一就是开始行动，如同你已经按照自己喜欢的方式去感觉和思考。由此可知，作者建议改变态度的策略是开始以一种体现个人渴望的方式行动，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A/D选项【无中生有】：原文并未提及A)“改变需要人们立即注意的事情”和D)“考虑减轻个人心理负担的方法”，故均排除。

C选项【偷换概念】：5段②句提到一段时间，但是指花一些时间反思自己的态度，思考自己相信什么以及为什么相信，而不是在一段时间内逐渐调整个人行为，故排除C)。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 Industrial fishing for krill （磷虾） in the unspoilt waters around Antarctica is threatening the future of one of the world’s last great wildernesses, according to a new report.
1 The study by Greenpeace analysed the movements of krill fishing vessels in the region and found they were increasingly operating “in the immediate vicinity of penguin colonies and whale-feeding grounds”.? 2 It also highlights incidents of fishing boats being involved in groundings oil spills and accidents, which posed a serious threat to the Antarctic ecosystem.
1 The report, published on Tuesday, comes amid growing concern about the impact of fishing and climate change on the Antarctic.? 2 A global campaign has been launched to create a network of ocean sanctuaries to protect the seas in the region and Greenpeace is calling for an immediate halt to fishing in areas being considered for sanctuary status.
1 Frida Bengtsson from Greenpeace’s Protect the Antarctic campaign said: “If the krill industry wants to show it’s a responsible player, then it should be voluntarily getting out of any area which is being proposed as an ocean sanctuary, and should instead be backing the protection of these huge tracts of the Antarctic.”?
1 A global campaign has been launched to turn a huge tract of Antarctic seas into ocean sanctuaries, protecting wildlife and banning not just krill fishing, but all fishing. 2 One was created in the Ross Sea in 2016, another reserve is being proposed in a vast area of the Weddell Sea, and a third sanctuary is under consideration in the area west of the Antarctic Peninsula —— a key krill fishing area.
1 The Commission for the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources (CCAMLR) manages the seas around Antarctica. 2 It will decide on the Weddell Sea sanctuary proposal at a conference in Australia in October, although a decision on the peninsula sanctuary is not expected until later.
1 Keith Reid, a science manager at CCAMLR, said that the organisation sought “a balance between protection, conservation and sustainable fishing in the Southern Ocean.”? 2 He said although more fishing was taking place nearer penguin colonies it was often happening later in the season when these colonies were empty.
1 “The creation of a system of marine protected areas is a key part of ongoing scientific and policy discussions in CCAMLR,” he added. 2 “Our long-term operation in the region depends on a healthy and thriving Antarctic marine ecosystem, which is why we have always had an open dialogue with the environmental non-governmental organisations. 3 We strongly intend to continue this dialogue, including talks with Greenpeace, to discuss improvements based on the latest scientific data. 4 We are not the ones to decide on the establishment of marine protected areas, but we hope to contribute positively with our knowledge and experience.”?

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What does Greenpeace’s study find about krill fishing?

关于“磷虾捕捞”，绿色和平组织的研究有什么发现？

A) It caused a great many penguins and whales to migrate.

它导致了大量的企鹅和鲸鱼迁徙

B) It was depriving penguins and whales of their habitats.

它剥夺了企鹅和鲸鱼的栖息地

C) It was carried out too close to the habitats of penguins and whales.

它开展的地方是企鹅聚居地和鲸鱼觅食地的临近地区

D) It posed an unprecedented threat to the wildlife around Antarctica.

它对南极周围的野生生物造成了前所未有的威胁

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Greenpeace’s study和krill fishing定位到2段①句。定位句指出，绿色和平组织的研究分析了该地区磷虾渔船的行踪，发现它们越来越多地在“企鹅聚居地和鲸鱼觅食地的临近地区”作业。换句话说，渔船在非常靠近企鹅和鲸鱼栖息地的地方进行磷虾捕捞，故答案为C)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A/B选项【无中生有】：文中未提及A)“它导致了大量的企鹅和鲸鱼迁徙”和B)“它剥夺了企鹅和鲸鱼的栖息地”，故排除。

D选项【偷换概念】：2段末句提到对南极生态系统造成严重威胁的是涉及搁浅、石油泄漏和事故的渔船事件，而不是捕捞磷虾，故排除D)“它对南极周围的野生生物造成了前所未有的威胁”。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

For what purpose has a global campaign been launched?

一场全球运动的发起有什么目的？

A) To reduce the impact of climate change on Antarctica.

减少气候变化对南极的影响

B) To establish conservation areas in the Antarctic region.

为了在南极地区建立保护区

C) To regulate krill fishing operations in the Antarctic seas.

规范南极海域的磷虾捕捞作业

D) To publicize the concern about the impact of krill fishing.

宣传对磷虾捕捞影响的担忧

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的a global campaign和launched定位到3段②句和5段①句。3段②句中的第一个分句提到，一场全球性运动已经启动，旨在创建海洋保护区网络来保护该区域的海洋。5段①句也指出，一场全球性运动已经启动，旨在将大片南极海域变成海洋保护区，保护野生动植物，不但禁止捕捞磷虾，还禁止所有的捕捞活动。由此可见，发起全球性运动的目的是要在南极地区建立保护区，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A/D选项【答非所问】：3段①句虽然提到了人们对渔业影响的关心以及气候变化对南极的影响，这是指研究报告发布时的背景，而不是发起全球性运动的目的，故排除A)“减少气候变化对南极的影响”和D)“宣传对磷虾捕捞影响的担忧”。

C选项【答非所问&偷换概念】：5段①句提到禁止捕捞磷虾，这是在南极海域建立海洋保护区的一项举措，而不是全球性运动的目的，并且原文只提到禁止而非规范南极海域的磷虾捕捞作业，故排除C)“规范南极海域的磷虾捕捞作业”。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What is Greenpeace’s recommendation to the krill industry?

绿色和平组织向磷虾业提出了什么建议？

A) Opting to operate away from the suggested conservation areas.

选择在远离被提议设保护区的地方作业

B) Volunteering to protect the endangered species in the Antarctic.

自愿保护南极的濒危物种

C) Refraining from krill fishing throughout the breeding season.

停止在繁殖季捕捞磷虾

D) Showing its sense of responsibility by leading the global campaign.

领导全球运动以示其责任感

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的Greenpeace’s recommendation和krill industry定位到4段。定位段提到，来自绿色和平组织“保护南极运动的弗里达·本特松认为，如果磷虾产业想表明自己是负责任的参与者，那么它就应该主动撤出任何被提议为海洋保护区的地区，并应该支持保护南极的这些巨大海域。由此可知，绿色和平组织建议磷虾产业远离被提议为海洋保护区的地方进行捕捞，故答案为A)。

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【词汇干扰&偷换概念】：4段中的voluntarily 意为”主动地，自愿地”，是指磷虾产业应该主动撤出任何被提议为海洋保护区的地区，而不是自愿保护南极的濒危物种，并且原文并未提及对濒危物种的保护，故排除B)“自愿保护南极的濒危物种”。

C选项【无中生有】：原文并没有提到禁止在繁殖季节捕捞磷虾，故排除C)。

D选项【偷换概念】：4段提到，绿色和平组织建议磷虾行业付出行动来表明自己是负责任的参与者，没有提到建议磷虾行业通过领导全球性运动来显示其责任感，故排除D)。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What did CCAMLR aim to do according to its science manager?

根据其科学主管所言，CCAMLR的目的是什么？

A) Raise public awareness of the vulnerability of Antarctic species.

提高公众对“南极物种脆弱性”的认识

B) Ban all commercial fishing operations in the Southern Ocean.

禁止在南大洋的所有商业捕捞作业

C) Keep the penguin colonies from all fishing interference.

使企鹅栖息地免受捕捞行为的打扰

D) Sustain fishing without damaging the Antarctic ecosystem.

在不损害南极生态同的前提下

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的CCAMLR和science manager定位到7段①句。定位句指出，南极海洋生物资源养护委员会的科学经理基思·里德表示，该组织寻求“在南大洋的保护、养护和可持续捕捞之间取得平衡”。由“取得平衡”可知，该组织的目标是既能维持捕捞，又能保护南大洋，也就是说不破坏南���生态系统，故答案为D)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【无中生有】：原文并未提及提高公众对南极物种脆弱性的认识，故排除A)。

B选项【答非所问】：5段①句提到禁止在南极海洋保护区进行所有的捕捞活动，但这是绿色和平组织发起的全球性运动，而不是南极海洋生物资源养护委员会的倡议，更不是其目标，故排除B)“禁止在南大洋的所有商业捕捞作业”。

D选项【反向干扰】：7段②句提到基思·里德的观点，即尽管越靠近企鹅聚居地，捕捞活动越多，但通常发生在（繁殖）季节快结束的时候，那时这些聚居地都是空的。由此可知，基思·里德认为靠近企鹅聚居地的捕捞活动并未对企鹅造成影响，自然就不会将目标设为不让企鹅聚居地受到任何捕捞干扰故排除C)。

choices.text: A provider of the needed expertise.

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

How does CCAMLR define its role in the conservation of the Antarctic environment?

CCAMLR如何界定自己在保护南极环境中的角色？

A) A coordinator in policy discussions.
政策讨论的协调者

B) An authority on big data analysis.

大数据分析的权威

C) A provider of the needed expertise.

必要专业知识的提供者

D) An initiator of marine sanctuaries.

海洋保护区的发起者

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的CCAMLR和the conservation of the Antarctic environment定位到8段④句。定位句提到，南极海洋生物资源养护委员会的科学经理表示，他们不是决定建立海洋保护区的人，但他们希望凭借自己的知识和经验作出积极的贡献。由此可见，南极海洋生物资源养护委员会认为他们能提供自己的知识和经验去保护南极环境，故答案为C)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【词汇干扰】：8段①句提到了政策讨论，但是指建立海洋保护区系统是南极海洋生物资源养护委员会正在进行的科学和政策讨论的关键部分，而不是指南极海洋生物资源养护委员会在保护南极环境中是政策讨论协调员，故排除A)“政策讨论协调员”。

B选项【过度推理】：最8段③句提到，南极海洋生物资源养护委员会想与环保非政府组织讨论基于最新科学数据的改进，并未说明自己就是大数据分析权威，故排除B)“大数据分析权威”。

D选项【反向干扰】：8段④句直接指出南极海洋生物资源养护委员会不是决定建立海洋保护区的人，故排除D)“海洋保护区的发起者”。

sections.title: Part 1 Writing 写作
sections.passage:
1 As every individual is a member of a specific group called the community, a sense of community responsibility is a valuable quality that each of us should have.
1 The reasons are as follows. 2 To begin with, having a good sense of community responsibility is helpful to avoid disagreements among team members, promote teamwork and improve work efficiency, which is particularly important in contemporary society. 3 Therefore, there is no modern enterprise that does not pay attention to cultivating the collective consciousness of employees. 4 Furthermore, people with a sense of community responsibility are more likely to adhere to the rules and regulations set by their communities, consciously conduct themselves politely and guard against such uncivilized behavior as making a loud noise, casting peels and shells, smoking, and spitting, thus contributing to promoting the establishment of a harmonious society.
1 In short, a good sense of community responsibility can motivate us to perfect the communities where we live and work and promote the sustainability of our environment.

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 The lotus flower is one of the famous flowers in China, which is deeply loved by people. 2 The lakes and ponds in many parts of China are hospitable for the lotus to grow. 3 The lotus, which features bright color, blooms in the early morning and closes at night in summer with a flowering period of up to two to three months, attracting tourists across the country to appreciate it. 4 The lotus has multiple functions. Not only can it green water and beautify courtyards, but it can also purify water, reduce pollution and improve the environment. 5 The lotus does not fear the strong sunshine and comes out of the dirty mud unsoiled. Therefore, it is regarded as the symbol of purity and elegance and is often used as a metaphor for a person’s noble character, making it a key theme in poetic and painting creation throughout history. 6 The places where the lotus is in full bloom are also frequented by many photography enthusiasts.

questions.stem: ①荷花(lotus flower)是中国的名花之一，深受人们喜爱。②中国许多地方的湖泊和池塘都适宜荷花生长。③荷花色彩鲜艳，夏日清晨绽放，夜晚闭合，花期长达两三个月，吸引来自各地的游客前往观赏。④荷花具有多种功能，既能绿化水面，又能美化庭园，还可净化水质、减少污染、改善环境。⑤荷花迎骄阳而不惧，出污泥而不染，象征纯洁、高雅，常常用来比喻人的高尚品德，历来是诗人画家创作的重要题材。⑥荷花盛开的地方也是许多摄影爱好者经常光顾之地。
questions.answer: 1 The lotus flower is one of the famous flowers in China, which is deeply loved by people. 2 The lakes and ponds in many parts of China are hospitable for the lotus to grow. 3 The lotus, which features bright color, blooms in the early morning and closes at night in summer with a flowering period of up to two to three months, attracting tourists across the country to appreciate it. 4 The lotus has multiple functions. Not only can it green water and beautify courtyards, but it can also purify water, reduce pollution and improve the environment. 5 The lotus does not fear the strong sunshine and comes out of the dirty mud unsoiled. Therefore, it is regarded as the symbol of purity and elegance and is often used as a metaphor for a person’s noble character, making it a key theme in poetic and painting creation throughout history. 6 The places where the lotus is in full bloom are also frequented by many photography enthusiasts.

questions.explanation:
【考点】

固定搭配题。

【确定词性】

分析句子结构可知，空格所在的短语在句中作状语，空格前有介词under和形容词certain。由此可以推断，空格处应填入名词，构成介宾短语。

【答案解析】

根据句意和第二段中的Sometimes we see things as...以及第三段中的At other times, we personify...可知，此处要表达的是在怎样的情况下，人们认为日常物品有人的特性。circumstances“情况，情形”通常与介词under连用，构成under... circumstances结构，意为“在……情况下”，故E) circumstances为本题答案

【考点】

语义推断题。

【确定词性】

空格位于原因状语从句中，空格前是主语we和系动词are。由此可以推断，空格处需要填入形容词、名词或动词的分词形式。

【答案解析】

由下一句中的people who reported feeling isolated were more likely than others to...可知，此处主要是讲我们将物品人格化与人们感觉孤独之间的关系，因此空格处需要填入一个表示“孤独”的形容词。由此确定，L) lonely“孤单的，寂寞的”为本题答案。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格前为动词attribute，空格后为介词to。由此可以推断，空格处需填入一个名词，构成attribute sth. to sth.结构，意为“认为某物具有某物的特性”。

【答案解析】

通读本段可知，本段主要是讲将物品人格化与人们感觉孤独之间的关系。由此可推断，那些感到孤独的人比其他人更有可能认为各种物品________。空格处所填名词与本句中的feeling形成呼应，表示“感觉，意识”等。由此确定，H) consciousness“意识”为本题答案。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格前为情态动词can，由此推断空格处需填入动词原形。

【答案解析】

根据常识可知，与事物有亲密关系可以消除孤独感或缓解孤独的状态。因此，空格处应填入一个含有“缓解，减少”意思的动词，结合备选项中的动词原形可知，A) alleviate为本题答案。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【确定词性】

分析句子结构可知，空格位于时间状语从句中的定语从句they had been ________中。空格前已有had been，因此空格处需要填入动词的过去分词构成被动语态。

【答案解析】

空格所在句指出，他们会通过夸大朋友的数量来进行心理上的补偿，他们这么做是因为感到孤独，或者受到了别人的孤立或排挤。分析备选项可知，J) excluded“排斥，不准……参与”为本题答案。

【考点】

副词辨析题。

【确定词性】

分析句子结构可知，空格所在句基本成分完整，因此空格处应填入副词修饰谓语动词。

【答案解析】

空格前一句中提到，大学生们被要求完成的任务是与手机进行互动，就好像手机具有人类的特性一样，也就是说，手机好像取代了人类。由此推断，空格处需要填入一个表示“好像，看起来”的副词，同时与上句中的as if形成呼应。由此确定，B) apparently“看来，似乎”为本题答案。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格前有连词and连接两个并列的成分，因此空格处应填入一个可数名词复数与beliefs并列。

【答案解析】

根据上下文语境可知，本段讲的是我们将物品人格化是为了努力理解它们，而电脑出的问题越多，受访者越有可能说电脑有自己的“信仰和欲望”，即人的特性。在备选的复数名词中，除去已经在第26题使用过的circumstances，只剩下desires，填入空格处符合句意。由此确定I) desires“渴望，欲望”为本题答案。

【考点】

固定搭配题

【确定词性】

空格前是系动词are，空格后是介宾结构with dominance，由此推断空格处需要填入动词的分词形式或形容词构成系表结构。

【答案解析】

上一句提到，在某种程度上，我们依靠外貌。下一句则举例指出，人们常常会认为那些宽脸的车、时钟和手表比小脸的更有优势。由此可推断，此处是说“宽脸”与“优势”有关。be associated with...意为“与……相关”，是固定搭配，符合句意，由此确定答案为D) associated。

【考点】

形容词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格前为介词in，空格后为名词situations，因此空格处应填入一个形容词修饰situations。

【答案解析】

根据上文可知，人们认为宽脸的物品比小脸的物品更有优势，此处将宽脸和小脸的物品进行比较。根据常识可知，有比较就意味着有“竞争”。由此推断，空格处应填入一个表示“有竞争的，有对比的”的形容词。由此确定，F) competitive“竞争性的，竞争的”为本题答案。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格位于see sth. as sth.结构中，因此空格处应填入名词。

【答案解析】

上一句提到，那些前保险杠向上翘像是在微笑的汽车卖得最好。空格所在句做出解释：因为具备这种特点能增加汽车的友善度。由此可见，空格处所填名词应表示“特点，特色”，因此K) feature“特色，特征”为本题答案。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Though he didn’t come from a farming family, from a young age Tim Joseph was fascinated by the idea of living off the land. 2 Reading magazines like The Stockman Grass Farmer and Graze, he got hooked on the idea of grass-fed agriculture. 3 The idea that all energy and wealth comes from the sun really intrigued him. 4 He thought the shorter the distance between the sun and the end product, the higher the profit to the farmer.?
1 Joseph wanted to put this theory to the test. 2 In 2009, he and his wife Laura launched Maple Hill Creamery, an organic, all grass-fed yogurt company in northern New York. 3 He quickly learned what the market has demonstrated: Demand for grass-fed products currently exceeds supply. 4 Grass-fed beef is enjoying a 25-30% annual growth rate. 5 Sales of grass-fed yogurt and kefir（发酵乳饮品）, on the other hand, have in the last year increased by over 38%. 6 This is in comparison with a drop of just under 1% in the total yogurt and kefir market, according to natural and organic market research company SPINS. 7 Joseph’s top priority became getting his hands on enough grass-fed milk to keep customers satisfied, since his own 64-cow herd wasn’t going to suffice.?
1 His first partnership was with Paul and Phyllis Amburgh, owners of the Dharma Lea farm in New York. 2 The Amburghs, too, were true believers in grass-fed. 3 In addition to supplying milk from their own 85-head herd, they began to help other farmers in the area convert from conventional to certified organic and grass-fed in order to enter the Maple Hill supply chain. 4 Since 2010, the couple has helped 125 small dairy farms convert to grass-fed, with more than 80% of those farms coming on board during the last two years.?
1 All this conversion has helped Maple Hill grow 40-50% every year since it began, with no end in sight. 2 Joseph has learned that a farmer has to have a certain mindset to successfully convert. 3 But convincing open-minded dairy people is actually not that hard, when you look at the economics. 4 Grass-fed milk can fetch up to 2.5 times the price of conventional milk. 5 Another factor is the squeeze that conventional dairy farmers have felt as the price of grain they feed their cows has gone up, tightening their profit margins. 6 By replacing expensive grain feed with regenerative management practices, grass-fed farmers are insulated from jumps in the price of feed. 7 These practices include grazing animals on grasses grown from the pastureland’s natural seed bank, and fertilized by the cows’ own fertilizer.?
1 Champions of this type of regenerative grazing also point to its animal welfare, climate and health benefit: Grass-fed animals live longer out of confinement. 2 Grazing herds stimulate microbial（微生物）activity in the soil, helping to capture water and separate carbon. 3 And grass-fed dairy and meat have been shown to be higher in certain nutrients and healthy fats.?
1 In the grass-fed system, farmers are also not subject to the wildly fluctuating milk prices of the international commodity market. 2 The unpredictability of global demand and the lag-time it takes to add more cows to a herd to meet demand can result in events like the recent cheese surplus. 3 Going grass-fed is a safe refuge, a way for family-scale farms to stay viable. 4 Usually a farmer will get to the point where financially, what they’re doing is not working. 5 That’s when they call Maple Hill. 6 If the farm is well managed and has enough land, and the desire to convert is sincere, a relationship can begin. 7 Through regular regional educational meetings, a large annual meeting, individual farm visits and thousands of phone calls, the Amburghs pass on the principles of pasture management. 8 Maple Hill signs a contract pledging to buy the farmer’s milk at a guaranteed base price, plus quality premiums and incentives for higher protein, butter-fat and other solids.?
1 While Maple Hill’s conversion program is unusually hands on and comprehensive, it’s just one of a growing number of businesses committed to slowly changing the way America farms. 2 Joseph calls sharing his knowledge network through peer-to-peer learning a core piece of the company’s culture. 3 Last summer, Massachusetts grass-fed beef advocate John Smith launched Big Picture Beef, a network of small grass-fed beef farms in New England and New York that is projected to bring to market 2,500 head of cattle from 125 producers this year. 4 Early indications are that Smith will have no shortage of farm members. 5 Since he began to informally announce the network at farming conferences and on social media, he’s received a steady stream of inquiries from interested farmers.?
1 Smith says he’ll provide services ranging from formal seminars to on-farm workshops on holistic（整体的）management, to one-on-one hand-holding and an almost 24/7 phone hotline for farmers who are converting. 2 In exchange, he guarantees an above-market price for each animal and a calf-to-customer electronic ear tag ID system like that used in the European Union.
1 Though advocates portray grass-fed products as a win-win situation for all, they do have downsides. 2 Price, for one, is an issue. 3 Joseph says his products are priced 10-20% above organic versions, but depending on the product chosen, compared to non-organic conventional yogurt, consumers could pay a premium of 30-50% or more for grass-fed. 4 As for the meat, Smith says his grass-fed hamburger will be priced 20-25% over the conventional alternative. 5 But a look at the prices on online grocer Fresh Direct suggests a grass-fed premium of anywhere from 35-60%.?
1 And not every farmer has the option of going grass-fed. 2 For both beef and dairy production, it requires, at least in the beginning, more pastureland. 3 Grass-fed beef production tends to be more labor-intensive as well. 4 But Smith counters that if you factor in the hidden cost of government corn subsidies, environment degradation, and decreased human health and animal welfare, grass-fed is the more cost-effective model. 5 “The sun provides the lowest cost of production and the cheapest meat,” he says.?
1 Another grass-fed booster spurring farmers to convert is EPIC, which makes meat-based protein bars. 2 Founders Taylor Collins and his wife, Katie Forrest, used to be endurance athletes; now they’re advocates of grass-fed meat. 3 Soon after launching EPIC’s most successful product—the Bison Bacon Cranberry Bar—Collins and Forrest found they’d exhausted their sources for bison（北美野牛）raised exclusively on pasture. 4 When they started researching the supply chain, they learned that only 2-3% of all bison is actually grass-fed. 5 The rest is feed-lot confined and fed grain and corn.?
1 But after General Mills bought EPIC in 2016, Collins and Forrest suddenly had the resources they needed to expand their supply chain. 2 So the company teamed up with Wisconsin-based rancher Northstar Bison. 3 EPIC fronted the money for the purchase of $2.5 million worth of young bison that will be raised according to its grass-fed protocols, with a guaranteed purchase price. 4 The message to young people who might not otherwise be able to afford to break into the business is, “‘You can purchase this $3 million piece of land here, because I’m guaranteeing you today you’ll have 1,000 bison on it.’ 5 We’re bringing new blood into the old, conventional farming ecosystem, which is really cool to see,” Collins explains.

questions.explanation:
【定位】

由题干中的grass-fed、milk prices和global market定位到F)段第一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，在草饲体系中，奶农也不受国际商品市场上牛奶价格剧烈波动的影响。题干中的not affected by是对定位句中not subject to的同义转述，题干中的ever-changing milk prices对应定位句中的the wildly fluctuating milk prices，故答案为F)。

【定位】

由题干中的many dairy farmers和switch to定位到C)段第三句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句指出，阿姆伯格夫妇开始帮助他们那个地区的其他农民从传统农业转向认证有机农业和草饲农业，以便进入枫山乳制品厂的供应链。题干中的Tim Joseph’s partners指的是The Amburghs，也就是定位句中的they，题干中的switch to是对定位句中convert from... to的同义转述，故答案为C)。

【定位】

由题干中的advocate、cost-effectiveness和grass-fed farming定位到J)段第四句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句提到，史密斯表示如果把政府玉米补贴、环境恶化和人类健康及动物福利下降的隐性成本等考虑在内，用草喂养是更划算的模式。题干中的One advocate指的是定位句中的Smith，题干中的other benefits是对定位句中the hidden cost of government corn subsidies，environment degradation，and decreased human health and animal welfare的归纳概括，故答案为J)。

【定位】

由题干中的dairy farmers、persuaded和saw its advantage in terms of profits定位到D)段第三句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，从经济角度来看，说服思想开明的从事乳制品工作的人其实并没有那么难。D)段第四、五句通过具体的数据说明用草养殖的农场利润可观。题干中的persuaded是对定位句中convincing的同义转述，题干中的in terms of profits 是对定位句中look at the economics的同义转述，故答案为D)。

【定位】

由题干中的one example和American farming practice定位到G)段第一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，枫山乳制品厂的转化项目只是致力于缓慢改变美国农场经营方式的越来越多的事项之一。题干中的one example of是对定位句中one of a growing number of的同义转述，题干中的American farming practice is changing是对定位句中changing the way America farms的同义转述，故答案为G)。

【定位】

由题干中的sunlight和energy and wealth定位到A)段第三句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，所有能量和财富均来源于太阳的想法确实引起了他的兴趣。题干中的Tim Joseph was fascinated是对定位句中intrigued him的同义转述，题干中的sunlight brings energy and wealth是对定位句中energy and wealth comes from the sun的同义转述，故答案为A)。

【定位】

由题干中的grass-fed products和expensive定位到I)段。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位段前两句提到，虽然支持者把草饲产品描绘成对所有人都有利的双赢局面，但它们也有缺点，价格就是一个问题。文章接下来通过列举数据说明草饲产品的价格偏高。题干是对定位段内容的归纳概括，故答案为I)。

【定位】

由题干中的Grass-fed products、healthier和more nutritious定位到E)段最后一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，据证明，草饲乳制品和肉类中，某些营养成分和健康脂肪的含量更高。题干中的Grass-fed products对应定位句中的grass-fed dairy and meat，题干中的healthier and more nutritious是对定位句中higher in certain nutrients and healthy fats的同义转述，故答案为E)。

【定位】

由题干中的Tim Joseph、started his business和demand定位到B)段第二、三句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，约瑟夫创办了枫山乳制品厂，但很快就发现市场上对草饲产品的需求超过了供应。题干中的grass-fed products fell short of demand是对定位句中Demand for grass-fed products currently exceeds supply的同义转述，故答案为B)。

【定位】

由题干中的snack bar producer、bison和scarce定位到K)段第三句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，在EPIC最成功的产品——野牛培根蔓越莓棒——上市后不久，柯林斯和福雷斯特发现他们的牧场上专门养殖的北美野牛用完了。题干中的snack bar指的是定位句中的the Bison Bacon Cranberry Bar，题干中的the supply of purely grass-fed bison meat was scarce是对定位句中exhausted their sources for bison的同义转述，故答案为K)。

sections.title: Section C passage 1
sections.passage:
1 Schools are not just a microcosm （缩影） of society; they mediate it too. 2 The best seek to alleviate the external pressures on their pupils while equipping them better to understand and handle the world outside — at once sheltering them and broadening their horizons.? 3 This is ambitious in any circumstances, and in a divided and unequal society the two ideals can clash outright （直接地）.
1 Trips that many adults would consider the adventure of a lifetime — treks in Borneo, a sports tour to Barbados — appear to have become almost routine at some state schools. 2 Parents are being asked for thousands of pounds. 3 Though schools cannot profit from these trips, the companies that arrange them do. 4 Meanwhile, pupils arrive at school hungry because their families can’t afford breakfast. 5 The Child Poverty Action Group says nine out of 30 in every classroom fall below the poverty line. 6 The discrepancy is startlingly apparent.? 7 Introducing a fundraising requirement for students does not help, as better-off children can tap up richer aunts and neighbours.
1 Probing the rock pools of a local beach or practising French on a language exchange can fire children’s passions, boost their skills and open their eyes to life’s possibilities. 2 Educational outings help bright but disadvantaged students to get better scores in A-level tests. 3 In this globalised age, there is a good case for international travel, and some parents say they can manage the cost of a school trip abroad more easily than a family holiday. 4 Even in the face of immense and mounting financial pressures, some schools have shown remarkable determination and ingenuity in ensuring that all their pupils are able to take up opportunities that may be truly life-changing. 5 They should be applauded.? 6 Methods such as whole-school fundraising, with the proceeds （收益） pooled, can help to extend opportunities and fuel community spirit.
1 But £3,000 trips cannot be justified when the average income for families with children is just over £30,000. 2 Such initiatives close doors for many pupils. 3 Some parents pull their children out of school because of expensive field trips. 4 Even parents who can see that a trip is little more than a party or celebration may well feel guilt that their child is left behind.?
1 The Department for Education’s guidance says schools can charge only for board and lodging if the trip is part of the syllabus, and that students receiving government aid are exempt from these costs. 2 However, many schools seem to ignore the advice; and it does not cover the kind of glamorous, exotic trips, which are becoming increasingly common. 3 Schools cannot be expected to bring together communities single-handed. 4 But the least we should expect is that they do not foster divisions and exclude those who are already disadvantaged.?

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What does the author say best schools should do?

作者说最好的学校应该做什么？

A) Prepare students to both challenge and change the divided unequal society.

让学生做好准备，挑战并改变不公、分化的社会

B) Protect students from social pressures and enable them to face the world.

保护学生免受社会压力并让他们能够勇敢的面对世界

C) Motivate students to develop their physical as well as intellectual abilities.

激励学生发展体能与智力

D) Encourage students to be ambitious and help them to achieve their goals.

鼓励学生胸怀抱负并帮助他们达成目标

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的best schools定位到1段②句。定位句指出，最好的学校在设法减轻学生的外在压力的同时，让学生具备更好地理解和应对外部世界的能力——既能庇护他们，又能拓宽他们的眼界。选项B)中，Protect students from social pressures是对定位句中alleviate the external pressures 的同义转述，enable them to face the world是对定位句中equipping them better to understand and handle the world outside的同义转述，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：该选项虽然复现③句divided and unequal society,但将学校的培养内容“理解并应对世界”夸大为“挑战并改变世界”

C选项【词汇干扰】：该选项将定位句信息understand and handle错误理解为“利用智力思考(understand)、利用体格应对(handle)",从而捏造出“体能与智力”.

D选项【张冠李戴】：该选项将原文“学校使命的宏大艰巨(ambitious)"张冠李戴,歪曲为“学生胸怀抱负”。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What does the author think about school field trips?

作者对校外旅行持有什么看法？

A) They enable students from different backgrounds to mix with each other.

他们让来自不同背景的学生彼此融合

B) They widen the gap between privileged and disadvantaged students.

它们扩大了特权阶层和贫困阶层学生之间的差距

C) They give the disadvantaged students a chance to see the world.

他们给予贫困阶层的学生看看世界的机会

D) They only benefit students with rich relatives and neighbors.

它们仅惠及那些有富裕亲戚和邻居的学生

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的school field trips定位到2段。定位段提到，旅行在一些州立学校似乎成了一种惯例。父母需要为之支付几千英镑，然而有些学生却因为家庭负担不起早餐而饿着肚子上学。2段⑥句提到，这种差异显而易见，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A、C选项【反向干扰】：该选项被3段“认可校外旅行本身”的内容干扰,但与4段信息“校外旅行扼杀了许多学生经济条件较差的学生)的机会”所体现的“主要是富有阶层学生参加研学旅行,贫困生很少有机会参加”相悖。

D选项【偷换概念&反向干扰】：该选项将2段末⑦句“他们更容易借助亲戚和邻居的力量完成筹款活动要求/更有望参加研学旅行”夸大为“他们是旅行唯一的受惠者”,且与第三段②句“教育性旅行帮助聪颖但贫困的孩子在高级考试中取得更好成绩”矛盾。

【题干及选项概览】

What does the author suggest can help build community spirit?

作者暗示什么有助于增强团队精神?

A) Events aiming to improve community services.

旨在改善社区服务的活动

B) Activities that help to fuel students’ ingenuity.

有助于培养学生独创力的活动

C) Events that require mutual understanding.

对互相理解有所要求的活动

D) Activities involving all students on campus.

让全校学生参与其中的活动

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的community spirit定位到3段⑤句。定位句指出，利用全校募捐等方式，将所得款项集中起来，有助��扩大机会并激发团队精神。因此，涉及学校所有学生的活动会有助于建立团队精神，故答案为D)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【词汇干扰】：该选项利用通常认识干扰,但文中community spirit指的是“将自己视为学校一分子并积极参与学校活动的团体精神”,与社区服务无关。

B选项【偷换概念】：该选项将作者用以描述部分学校的说法“独创力(ingenuity)"偷换到学生身上，而原文并不涉及“培养学生的独创力”。

C选项【常识干扰】：该选项利用常识干扰,但原文并不涉及“相互理解”。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What do we learn about low-income parents regarding school field trips?

在校外旅行的问题上，关于低收入父母我们了解到什么？

A) They want their children to participate even though they don’t see much benefit.

他们想让自己的孩子参与进来，即使他们不觉得有多大好处

B) They don’t want their kids to participate but find it hard to keep them from going.

他们不想让自己的孩子参加，但是很难阻止他们参加

C) They don’t want their kids to miss any chance to broaden their horizons despite the cost.

他们不想让自己的孩子错过任何开拓眼界的机会，不论付出什么代价

D) They want their children to experience adventures but they don’t want them to run risks.

他们想让自己的孩子体验冒险经历，但不想让他们冒风险

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的low income parents和school field trips定位到4段④句。定位句提到，即使是那些认为旅行只不过是一次聚会或庆祝活动的父母，也很可能因为孩子被落在后面而感到内疚。由此可见，即使父母们没有看到太多好处，也希望自己的孩子参加游学旅行，故答案为A)。

 

【错误选项分析】

B/D选项【无中生有】：文中未提及B)“他们不想让孩子参加，但很难阻止孩子”和D)“他们希望自已的孩子经历冒险，但不希望他们有任何风险”，故排除。

C选项【反向干扰】：4段④句中提到那些父母认为旅行与聚会或庆祝活动没有什么区别，这与C)“虽然贵，但他们不想让孩子错过任何可以开阔他们视野的机会”表述不符，故排除。

【题干及选项概览】

What is the author’s expectation of schools?

作者对学校的期望是什么？

A) Bringing a community together with ingenuity.

用智慧将团队力量集合起来

B) Resolving the existing discrepancies in society.

解决社会中存在的差异

C) Avoiding creating new gaps among students.

避免在学生间制造新的差距

D) Giving poor students preferential treatment.

给予贫困学生以优待

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的expectation of schools定位到5段③④句。定位句指出，不能指望学校凭借一己之力把社区集合起来。但至少我们应该期望它们不加剧分化，不排斥那些家庭经济状况已经处于不利地位的学生。这与C)的表述一致，故答案为C)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【反向干扰】：定位句指出，不能指望学校凭借一己之力把社区集合起来,这与A)“用智慧将团队力量集合起来”的表述相矛盾，故排除。

B选项【无中生有】：文中没有提及B)“解决社会中存在的差异”，故排除。

D选项【答非所问】：5段①句中教育部的指导意见表示，接受政府资助的学生可以免除这些费用，���而许多学校似乎忽视了这一建议。作者只是说明了现状如何，并非对学校的期望，故排除D)。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 Rising temperatures and overfishing in the pristine （未受污染的） waters around the Antarctic could see king penguin populations pushed to the brink of extinction by the end of the century, according to a new study.? 2 The study’s report states that as global warming transforms the environment in the world’s last great wilderness, 70 percent of king penguins could either disappear or be forced to find new breeding grounds.
1 Co-author Celine Le Bohec, from the University of Strasbourg in France, warned: “If there’re no actions aimed at halting or controlling global warming, and the pace of the current human-induced changes such as climate change and overfishing stays the same, the species may soon disappear.” 2 The findings come amid growing concern over the future of the Antarctic. 3 Earlier this month a separate study found that a combination of climate change and industrial fishing is threatening the krill （磷虾） population in Antarctic waters, with a potentially disastrous impact on whales, seals and penguins.? 4 But today’s report is the starkest warning yet of the potentially devastating impact of climate change and human exploitation on the Antarctic’s delicate ecosystems.
1 Le Bohec said: “Unless current greenhouse gas emissions drop, 70 percent of king penguins —— 1.1 million breeding pairs —— will be forced to relocate their breeding grounds, or face extinction by 2100.”? 2 King penguins are the second-largest type of penguin and only breed on specific isolated islands in the Southern Ocean where there is no ice cover and easy access to the sea. 3 As the ocean warms, a body of water called the Antarctic Polar Front —— an upward movement of nutrient-rich sea that supports a huge abundance of marine life —— is being pushed further south.? 4 This means that king penguins, which feed on fish and krill in this body of water, have to travel further to their feeding grounds, leaving their hungry chicks for longer. 5 And as the distance between their breeding grounds and their food grows, entire colonies could be wiped out.
1 Le Bohec said: “The plight of the king penguin should serve as a warning about the future of the entire marine environment in the Antarctic. 2 Penguins, like other seabirds and marine mammals, occupy higher levels in the food chain and they are what we call bio-indicators of their ecosystems.” 3 Penguins are sensitive indicators of changes in marine ecosystems. 4 As such, they are key species for understanding and predicting impacts of global change on Antarctic and sub-Antarctic marine ecosystems. 5 The report found that although some king penguins may be able to relocate to new breeding grounds closer to their retreating food source, suitable new habitats would be scarce. 6 Only a handful of islands in the Southern Ocean are suitable for sustaining large breeding colonies.?

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What will happen by 2100, according to a new study?

根据一项最新研究，到2100年将会发生什么？

A) King penguins in the Antarctic will be on the verge of dying out.

南极的王企鹅将处于灭绝边缘

B) Sea water will rise to a much higher level around the Antarctic.

南极附近的海水将上升到更高的水平线

C) The melting ice cover will destroy the great Antarctic wilderness.

融化的冰层将摧毁南极大荒野

D) The pristine waters around the Antarctic will disappear forever.

南极周围未受污染的水域将永远消失

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的by 2100和according to a new study定位到1段①句。定位句指出，一项新的研究显示，到本世纪末，温度升高和南极周围原始水域的过度捕捞可能会导致王企鹅种群濒临灭绝。题干中的by 2100也就是定位句中的by the end of the century，选项A)中的on the verge of dying out是对定位句中the brink of extinction 的同义转述，故答案为A)。

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【答非所问】：该选项根据①句Rising temperatures主观推测“全球变暖将导致南极冰川融化,海平面上升”,但这并非新研究发现。

C选项【无中生有&偷换概念】：该选项将1段②句全球变暖对南极大荒野环境的影响由“改变”夸大为“摧毁",且研究并未明确提及“冰层融化”.

D选项【东拼西凑】：该选项由①句the pristine waters around the Antarctic和②句disappear糅杂而来,文中信息实则为“南极未受污染的水域正被过度捕捞"“王企鹅可能会灭绝”。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What do we learn from the findings of a separate study?

我们从另一项独立的研究中了解到了什么？

A) Shrinking krill population and rising temperatures could force Antarctic whales to migrate.

磷虾总量缩减和气温上升或将迫使南极鲸迁徙

B) Human activities have accelerated climate change in the Antarctic region in recent years.

近年来人类活动加快了南极地区气候变化的速度

C) Industrial fishing and climate change could be fatal to certain Antarctic species.

工业捕捞和其后变化对某些南极物种来说可能是致命的

D) Krill fishing in the Antarctic has worsened the pollution of the pristine waters.

南极磷虾捕捞进一步加剧了原始水域的污染

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的a separate study定位到2段③句。定位句指出，本月早些时候，另一项研究发现，气候变化和工业捕捞的综合作用正在威胁南极水域的磷虾数量，对鲸鱼、海豹和企鹅造成潜在的灾难性影响。由此可知，工业捕捞和气候变化对某些南极物种的影响可能是致命的，故答案为C)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：该选项改变了句中关系,将文中链条式关系“气候变暖危及磷虾,进而危及鲸鱼”改为二对一关系“磷虾数量降低和气候变暖共同危及鲸鱼”,且“危及鲸鱼”和“迫使鲸鱼迁徙”有一定差异。

B选项【东拼西凑&答非所问】：该选项结合2段①句human-induced changes such as climate change和背景知识“人类行为加速南极地区气候变暖”设置干扰,也并非题目所问“另一研究发现”.

D选项【东拼西凑】：该选项杂糅首段①句“南极未受污染海域目前正遭过度捕捞”和第二段③句的“磷虾"而来，但该独立研究并未提及此因果关联。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What does the passage say about king penguins?

关于王企鹅，文中说了什么？

A) They will turn out to be the second-largest species of birds to become extinct.

它们将会是走向灭绝的第二大鸟类

B) Many of them will have to migrate to isolated islands in the Southern Ocean.

它们大多数将被迫迁徙至南大洋的孤岛

C) They feed primarily on only a few kinds of krill in the Antarctic Polar Front.

它们主要以南大洋极锋中少数几种磷虾为食

D) The majority of them may have to find new breeding grounds in the future.

它们大多数将来可能不得不寻找新的繁殖地

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的king penguins和题文同序原则定位到3段①句。3段介绍了王企鹅的特点、生活习性以及外在环境的改变给它们的生存带来的困境。定位句提到，除非目前温室气体排放量下降，否则70%的王企鹅将被迫迁移繁殖地，不然将在2100年前面临灭绝。由此可见，面对生存环境的不断恶化，王企鹅不得不寻找新的繁殖地，故答案为D)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：该选项将3段②句“王企鹅是第二大企鹅种类(the second-largest type of penguin)"偷换为“第二大灭绝的鸟类(the second-largest species of birds to become extinct)".

B选项【偷换概念】：该选项将②句所述的王企鹅现状“仅在南大洋特定孤岛上繁殖”窜改为其未来“将被迫迁徙至南大洋孤岛”.

C选项【范围缩小&偷换概念】：该选项将3段④句“王企鹅以极锋中的鱼和磷虾(fish and krill)为食"缩窄范围至“仅以海流中少数几种磷虾(only a few kinds of krill)为食"。

A) Many baby king penguins can’t have food in time.

大量王企鹅幼崽无法及时得到喂食

B) Many king penguins could no longer live on krill.

许多王企鹅不能再以磷虾为食

C) Whales will invade king penguins’ breeding grounds.

鲸鱼会入侵王企鹅的繁殖地

D) Whales will have to travel long distances to find food.

鲸鱼必须长途跋涉才能找到食物

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的sea levels rise in the Antarctic 定位到3段③句。定位句提到，随着海水变暖，被称为南极极锋的水体被向南推进。第四句紧接着提到，这意味着，在这片水域以鱼和磷虾为食的王企鹅不得不进一步前往更远的觅食地，让饥饿的王企鹅雏鸟等待更长时间。由此可以推断，南极海平面上升时，王企鹅雏鸟不能及时进食，故答案为A)。

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【过度推理】：该选项根据3段③④句“南大洋极锋南移”“王企鹅以极锋中的鱼虾为食”主观推测王企鹅无法再以磷虾为食,而忽略随后的have to travel further(王企鹅为获取磷虾需跋涉更远).

C选项【偷换概念&词汇干扰】：该选项利用2段提及的whales与3段①句king penguins. .. be forced to relocate their breeding grounds捏造干扰,而实际上迫使王企鹅迁移的是“气温升高”而非“鲸鱼”。

D选项【偷换概念】：文中“不得不为了觅食跋涉更远”的是“王企鹅”,不是“鲸鱼”。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What do we learn about the Southern Ocean?

关于南大洋，我们了解到什么？

A) The king penguins there are reluctant to leave for new breeding grounds.

南大洋的王企鹅不愿意离开前往新的繁殖地

B) Its conservation is key to the sustainable propagation of Antarctic species.

保护南极物种是南极物种可持续繁殖的关键

C It is most likely to become the ultimate retreat for species like the king penguin.

南大洋很可能成为像王企鹅这样的物种的最终归宿

D) Only a few of its islands can serve as huge breeding grounds for king penguins.

它的岛屿中只有极少数可以作为王企鹅的大型繁殖地

 

【定位及答案】

本题考查“南大洋”的相关信息。根据题干关键词the Southern Ocean初步定位至第三段②句直至文末,再综合选项共同指向“王企鹅及其他南极物种的迁徙/未来命运”可进一步定位至第四段⑤⑥句,锁定答案]D。第四段⑤⑥句指出,虽然一些王企鹅或许能迁徙到新的繁殖地,以离食物源更近,但实际上合适的栖息地极为稀缺。南大洋中只有少数岛屿适合承载大型繁殖群体,D正确(Only a few of its islands同义替换Only a handful of islands in the Southern Ocean)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【曲解文意】：该选项曲解⑤句:文中并非指出“南大洋的王企鹅不愿意搬迁”而是强调“很少有合适的地方可搬”。

B选项【过度推理】：该选项根据⑤⑥句“南大洋上王企鹅可搬迁的新繁殖地稀缺”主观臆测“保护物种的关键在于保护南大洋”,而文中意在强调的是“搬迁也并非解决办法,阻遏全球变暖才是关键”。

C选项【反向干扰】：该选项与⑥句“即便将来王企鹅可以迁徙,南大洋上也只有少数岛屿可作为新的繁殖地”相矛盾。

 

【解题思路】

与上题相似,本题仅根据题干也难以准确定位,解决途径在于综合题干关键词the Southern Ocean和选项共同指向——“王企鹅(及南极其他物种)未来的迁徙繁衍”与“南大洋”的关系——锁定第四段5⑥句。然后对比发现:A将原文的“客观条件不允许”改为“主观不愿意”;B将原文的“不可能”变为“可实现”;C与文意完全相反;只有D与原文一致。
