D) A limit on the maximum work hours.

【定位及答案】

由题干中的voice actors和demanding定位到4段③句。定位句指出，配音演员一直在呼吁追加酬金，即每当配音游戏发行量达到200万份，或者下载量达到200万次，再或者游戏用户达到200万人（上限为800万）时，配音演员应获得一定的绩效奖励。因此，C)“基于销售量的额外报酬”为答案。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【答非所问】：5段②句提到，对于并不是每天都有配音工作的自由从业者来说，追加薪酬是很重要的一方面。也就是说，配音演员的诉求还是薪酬问题，而非就业问题，故排除A)“更为正规的就业”；

B选项【无中生有】：原文未提及B)“非歧视性的合同”，故排除；

D选项【无中生有】：4段②句提到，配音演员的薪酬是固定的，即四个小时配音时段的标准工资通常为825美元。但并未提及工作时长有问题，故排除D)“限制最高工作时长”。

What does Keythe Farley say about voice actors?

他们被隐瞒很多有关工作的细节

由题干中的Keythe Farley定位到6段②句和7段。定位句指出，配音演员凯瑟·法利认为电子游戏业的保密性太强，演员在工作时都不知道自已是在为哪款游戏配音。A)项中的are kept in the dark意为“被隐瞒，无所知”，故A)“他们被隐瞒很多有关工作的细节”为答案。

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【断章取义】：该选项对6段断章取义,误认为the secrecy of the industry...I can't imagine if there's any other acting job...是在指出“游戏业对待配音演员明显不如其他人员”,而实际含义为“在其他表演行业无法想象的事情在游戏业却每天都在发生”.

C/D选项【答非所问】：该选中，说明“配音演员不是全职雇员(isn't regularly employed)、(由此导致)没有稳定收入”的是Crispin Freeman,而非Keythe Farley。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What is the argument of lawyer Scott Witlin?

斯科特·维特林律师的论点是什么？

A) Voice actors should have a pay raise if they prove to be top craftsmen.

如果配音演员被证明是行业翘楚，他们应该得到加薪

B) Changing the pay system would cause the industry more problems.

改变薪酬体系将给行业造成更多的问题

C) Voice actors are mere craftsmen, not professional performers.

配音演员只是工匠，不是专业演员

D) Paying voice actors on an hourly basis is in line with the law.

按小时支付配音演员薪酬符合法律规定

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的lawyer和Scott Witlin定位到8段。定位段指出，电子游戏公司的律师代表斯科特·威特林认为，配音演员的工作在电子游戏制作过程中所占比例很小，如果只改变这一部分人的薪酬体系，那将给电子游戏公司带来更多的麻烦。因此，B)“改变薪酬体系将给行业造成更多的问题”为答案。

 

【错误选项分析】

A、C选项【词汇干扰】：��选项均利用top craftsmen干扰：

A将原文转折关系(即使是顶尖工匠/配音演员,对其采用不同的薪酬体系也会带来问题)窜改为假设关系(如果顶尖,则可采用不同薪酬体系/加薪);

C将原文同指关系(工匠即指配音演员)改为对立关系(工匠不是专业演员)

D选项【过度推理】：该选项由Scott Witlin的资方律师立场(代表电子游戏公司的利益)及现行薪酬制度$ 825 for a standard four-hour vocal session臆断而来,原文并无根据。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 Officials at the White House announced a new space policy focused on managing the increasing number of satellites that companies and governments are launching into space. 2 Space Policy Directive-3 lays out general guidelines for the United States to mitigate （缓解） the effects of space debris and track and manage traffic in space.?
1 This policy sets the stage for the Department of Commerce to take over the management of traffic in space. 2 The department will make sure that newly launched satellites don’t use radio frequencies that would interfere with existing satellites, and schedule when such new satellites can be launched.? 3 This only applies to American space activities, but the hope is that it will help standardize a set of norms in the dawning commercial spaceflight industry throughout the world.?
1 Space, especially the space directly around our planet, is getting more crowded as more governments and companies launch satellites. 2 One impetus for the policy is that companies are already starting to build massive constellations （星座）, comprising hundreds or thousands of satellites with many moving parts among them. 3 With so much stuff in space, and a limited area around our planet, the government wants to reduce the chances of a collision. 4 Two or more satellites slamming into each other could create many more out-of-control bits that would pose even more hazards to the growing collection of satellites in space.
1 And it’s not like this hasn’t happened before. 2 In 2009 an old Russian craft slammed into a communications satellite, creating a cloud of hundreds of pieces of debris and putting other hardware at risk. 3 Journalist Sarah Scoles reports that NASA currently tracks about 24,000 objects in space, and in 2016 the Air Force had to issue 3,995,874 warnings to satellite owners alerting them to a potential nearby threat from another satellite or bit of debris.
1 That’s why this new policy also includes directions to update the current U.S. Government Orbital Debris Mitigation Standard Practices, which already require any entity that launches a satellite or spacecraft to vigorously analyse the likelihood that any of their actions, from an unexpected failure or normal operations, will create more space debris.? 2 It includes accounting for any piece of debris they plan to release over 5mm that might stay in orbit for 25 years or more. 3 It might seem surprising to think about an item staying in space for that long, but the oldest satellite still in orbit —— Vanguard 1 —— turned 60 in 2018.
1 Agencies and companies throughout the world are working on developing technology that would dispose of or capture space debris before it causes serious damage.? 2 But for now, the U.S. government is more focused on preventing new debris from forming than taking the trash out of orbit.

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What is the purpose of the new U.S. space policy?

美国新太空政策的目标是什么？

A) To lay out general guidelines for space exploration.

为太空探索制定总方针

B) To encourage companies to join in space programs.

鼓励企业参与太空项目

C) To make the best use of satellites in space.

充分利用太空卫星

D) To improve traffic conditions in space.

改善太空的交通状况

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的the new U.S. space policy定位到文章1段②句。定位句指出，《太空政策指令-3》为美国制定了一个总方针来缓解太空碎片的影响，追踪和管理太空交通。接下来的第二段第一句提到，这一政策为美国商务部接手太空交通管理奠定了基础。因此，答案为D)“改善太空的交通状况”。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：2段③句提到，此政策仅涉及美国的太空活动，但美国政府希望这将有助于使全球范围内正在兴起的商用航天工业的一套规范标准化，而不是为太空探索制定方针，故排除A)“为太空探索制定总方针”；

B选项【偷换概念】：1段①句提到，企业和政府发射卫星到太空，企业参与太空项目是已经存在的客观事实，而不是新政策的目的，故排除B)“鼓励企业参与太空项目”；

C选项【偷换概念】：1段①句提到，该政策专注于管理企业和政府发射到太空的日益增多的卫星，而不是要充分利用卫星，故排除C)“充分利用太空卫星”。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What is the Department of Commerce expected to do under the new policy?

A) Reduce debris in space.

减少太空碎片

B) Monitor satellite operations.

监控卫星运行

C) Regulate the launching of new satellites.

管理新卫星的发射

D) Update satellite communications technology.

升级卫星通信技术

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的the Department of Commerce定位到文章2段第①②句。定位句指出，这一政策为美国商务部接手太空交通管理奠定了基础。商务部需确保新发射的卫星不使用会干扰现有卫星的无线电频率，并安排何时发送这些新卫星。C)项中的Regulate对应第二段第二句中的make sure和schedule故C)“管理新卫星的发射”为答案。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【反向干扰】：该选项背离末段所述美国政策核心“防止形成新碎片,而非清理现有太空碎片".

B选项【偷换概念&范围过大】：该选项将2段②句商务部监管对象“新发射卫星的无线电频率”泛化为“所有卫星的运行状况(包括速度、周期、轨道高度等)".

D选项【词汇干扰】：该选项源自2段②句radio frequencies,但商务部只负责协调分配无线电频率的管理工作,不负责“通信技术升级”。

促进空间探索方面的国际合作

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的U.S. government、hope和the new space policy定位到文章第2段③句。定位句指出，此政策仅适用于美国的太空活动，但美国政府希望这将有助于使全球范围内正在兴起的商用航天工业形成一套标准化的规范。A)项中的international standards对应定位句中的standardize a set of norms和throughout the world，故A)“为航天工业制定国际化标准”为答案。

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【过度推理】：该选项由2段③句“美国希望其新政策有助于国际商业航天标准化(即希望他国也能参考、借鉴)"臆断出“美国欲垄断行业”。

C选项【曲解文意】：该选项将2段③句美国愿景-商业航天业能“形成全球统一标准”曲解为“取得进一步发展”。

D选项【偷换概念】：该选项由throughout the world捏造出“美国欲推进国际合作”,且将新政策核心内容“太空交通治理”窜改为“太空探索"

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What is a space vehicle launching entity required to do according to the current U.S. Government Orbital Debris Mitigation Standard Practices?

根据现行《美国政府轨道碎片减缓标准操作规范》，空间飞行器发射实体需要做什么？

A) Give an estimate of how long its debris will stay in space.

预估碎片在太空中停留的时间

B) Account for the debris it has released into space at any time.

对任何时候释放到太空的碎片负责

C) Provide a detailed plan for managing the space debris it creates.

对其产生的太空碎片提供详细的管理计划

D) Make a thorough analysis of any possible addition to space debris.

对任何可能增加的太空碎片进行彻底的分析

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的current U.S. Government Orbital Debris Mitigation Standard Practices定位到文章5段①句。定位句指出，《美国政府轨道碎片���缓标准操作规程》已经要求任何发射卫星或航天器的机构都要努力分析他们会不会因意外故障或正常操作而产生更多的太空碎片。D)项中的a thorough analysis对应定位句中的vigorously analyze，D)项中的any possible addition to space debris对应likelihood和create more space debris，故D)“对任何可能增加的太空碎片进行彻底的分析”为答案。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：文章5段②句提到，其中包括对他们计划释放的任何超过5毫米的碎片负责，这些碎片可能在轨道上停留25年或更长时间，卫星所有者必须对其负责，而不是让他们预估卫星在太空中停留的时间，故排除A)“预估碎片在太空中停留的时间”；

B选项【范围过大】：B)“对任何时候释放到太空的碎片负责”夸大了范围，故排除；

C选项【无中生有】：文章5段提到，发射航天器的机构需要做的事情是对其行为产生太空碎片的可能性进行分析，并对一定的情况负责，并未提到提供管理计划，故排除C)“对其产生的太空碎片提供详细的管理计划”。

【题干及选项概览】

What are space agencies and companies aiming to do at present?

航天机构及企业目前打算做什么？

A) Recycle used space vehicles before they turn into debris.

在航天器变成碎片前对其进行回收利用

B) Develop technology to address the space debris problem.

发展技术来解决太空碎片问题

C) Limit the amount of debris entering space.

控制进入太空的碎片数量

D) Cooperate closely to retrieve space debris.

密切合作以找回太空碎片

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的space agencies and companies定位到6段①句。 定位句指出，全世界的机构和企业都在努力开发能够在太空碎片造成严重破坏之前对其进行处理或搜集的技术。B)项中的address the space debris problem对应定位句中的dispose of or capture space debris，故B)“发展技术来解决太空碎片问题”为答案。

 

【错误选项分析】

A/C选项【反向干扰】:A、C提及的空间碎片属“尚未形成的、未进入太空的(before they turn into debris, debris entering space)",背离政府机构和企业的普遍努力方向“清理太空现有垃圾”.

D选项【词汇干扰】：该选项利用未段throughout the world编造出“合作”,同时将文中“处理、捕获(dispose of or capture)"篡改为“收回(retrieve)"。

1 When it comes to learning, there is a famous Chinese saying, which goes “Learning without thinking leads to confusion; thinking without studying results in tardiness.” 2 Evidently, it is meant to tell us that learning methods are as important as hard work. 3 I totally agree with it. 4 Besides, I insist that in addition to diligence and methods, motivation in learning should also be paid attention to.
1 As for me, motivation is an indispensable part of learning, for a person won’t even start the learning process without motivation. 2 After you start studying, you may easily give up when faced with difficulties without motivation that drives you to keep going. 3 Apart from motivation, we also need the right way to learn. 4 Because hard work is not enough in the learning process, we may fall into the dilemma of studying mechanically if we don’t attach importance to learning methods. 5 Instead, equipped with effective learning methods, we will get double the result by doing half the work.
1 In brief, motivation and methods are critical to successful learning. 2 Therefore, only when we are clearly aware of this can we form good learning habits and achieve satisfactory effects.

sections.title: Section A 选词填空
sections.passage:
1 Steel is valued for its reliability, but not when it gets cold. 2 Most forms of steel 1 become brittle (脆的) at temperatures below about -25°C unless they are mixed with other metals.? 3 Now, though, a novel type of steel has been developed that resists 2 at much lower temperatures, while retaining its strength and toughness — without the need for expensive 3.?
1 Steel’s fragility at low temperatures first became a major concern during the Second World War. 2 After German U-boats torpedoed （用鱼雷攻击） numerous British ships, a 2, 700-strong fleet of cheap-and-cheerful “ Liberty ships “ was introduced to replace the lost vessels, providing a lifeline for the 4 British.? 3 But the steel shells of hundreds of the ships 5 in the icy north Atlantic, and 12 broke in half and sank.?
1 Brittleness remains a problem when building steel structures in cold conditions, such as oil rigs in the Arctic. 2 So scientists have 6 to find a solution by mixing it with expensive metals such as nickel.?
1 Yuuji Kimura and colleagues in Japan tried a more physical 7.? 2 Rather than adding other metals, they developed a complex mechanical process involving repeated heating and very severe mechanical deformation, known as tempforming.
1 The resulting steel appears to achieve a combination of strength and toughness that is 8 to that of modern steels that are very rich in alloy content and, therefore, very expensive.?
1 Kimura’s team intends to use its tempformed steel to make ultra-high strength parts, such as bolts. 2 They hope to reduce both the number of 9 needed in a construction job and their weight — by replacing solid supports with 10 tubes, for example.? 3 This could reduce the amount of steel needed to make everything from automobiles to building and bridges.

questions.explanation:
【考点】

副词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格前面为主语Most forms of steel，空格后面是谓语become brittle，因此空格处需要填入副词来修饰谓语部分。

【答案解析】

第一段第一句提到，钢材的价值在于它坚固耐用，但是当天气变冷的时候就不一样了。第二段第一句中的Steel’s fragility at low temperatures则明确提出了本文的主题，即钢在低温下的易碎性。因此，空格所在句是说大多数的钢在大约零下25°C以下时会________变脆，容易破裂，由此确定副词A) abruptly“突然地”为本题答案。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格位于that引导的定语从句中，此处that充当从句的主语，空格前的resists是从句的谓语动词。因此，空格处需要填入一个名词，作定语从句中resists的宾语。

【答案解析】

型钢已经被研发出来以解决钢在天冷时容易变脆的问题，变脆则容易断裂，由此可以确定名词J) fractures“裂缝，裂痕”为本题答案。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格前面是介词for和形容词expensive，因此空格处应填入一个名词。

【答案解析】

空格所在分句的意思是，同时保持其强度和韧性——不需要昂贵的________。上文提到除非和其他金属混合，大多数钢材在低于大约零下25°C时会变得易碎，但是空格所在句出现了转折，提到出现了一种新型钢材，即下文第四段第二句出现的不添加其他金属的钢材，所以可以确定名词B) additives“添加物，添加剂”为本题答案。

【考点】

语义推断题。

【确定词性】

空格前面是定冠词the，后面是名词British，因此空格处需要填入形容词或动词的分词形式来修饰名词British。

【答案解析】

本句指出，在德国U型潜水艇用鱼雷击沉了许多英国船只之后，一支强大的舰队被派出，取代了这些失踪的船只，为英国人提供了一条生命线。由此可推断，正是因为英国人遭遇不幸，才会派出这支强大的舰队来解救他们。由此可以确定英国人是“被围困的“或“处于困境中的，所以E) besieged“包围，围困”为本题答案。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【确定词性】

分析句子结构可知，本句主语为the steel shells of hundreds of the ships，句中缺少谓语，故空格处需要填入一个动词。此处叙述的是过去发生的事情，因此该动词形式应为过去式。

【答案解析】

空格所在句的后半句提到，12艘船裂成两半沉没，本句前后两个分句由and连接，说明数百艘船只的钢壳在冰冷的北大西洋中也遭遇了类似的事情。由此可以确定动词I) cracked“（使）破裂，（使）裂开”为本题答案。

【考点】

动词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格前面是助动词have，空格后面是动词不定式结构，因此空格处应填入动词的过去分词形式，构成现在完成时态，且能与不定式结构搭配使用。

【答案解析】

空格所在句指出，科学家们一直________寻找一种解决方案，将其与镍等昂贵金属混合使用。上文提到，在寒冷条件下建造钢结构时，钢的易脆性一直是一个问题。因此，空格处是在说明科学家们一直在寻找解决钢的易脆问题的方案，空格处应填入一个含有“努力”或“致力于”意思的动词。动词N) strived“努力，奋斗”符合语义，故为答案。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格前面有不定冠词a和形容词physical因此空格处应填入可数名词的单数形式，与a more physical一起作tried的宾语。

【答案解析】

________。下文提到，木村裕二及其同事采用了“反复加热和重度机械变形”来加工钢材，这是一种加工方法，是对上一句话的解释说明，故空格处应填入一个表示“方式，方法”的名词。名词C) approach“方法，方式”符合语义，为本题答案。

【考点】

语义推断题。

【确定词性】

空格前面是be动词is，后面是介词to，因此空格处需填入一个形容词或动词分词形式，构成系表结构或被动语态，且能与介词to搭配使用。

【答案解析】

空格所在句指出，由此产生的钢看起来兼具强度和韧性，可与合金含量非常丰富、也非常昂贵的现代钢________。此处是把木村裕二及其同事研发的新型钢材与现代钢材进行比较。空格处所填的词应含有“比较”的意思，故G) comparable“相当的，可相比的”符合语境，且能与介词to构成be comparable to... 的搭配，意为“比得上……的；可与……比较的”。

【考点】

名词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格前面是介词of，后面是过去分词结构needed in a construction job作后置定语，因此空格处应填入一个名词，作介词of的宾语。

【答案解析】

空格所在句指出，他们希望减少建筑工程所需的________的数量和重量。根据常识可知，建筑工程需要原材料之类的东西，因此空格处所填名词应含有“原材料”或“零件，部件”的意思，由此可以确定本题答案为H) components“零件，组成部分”。

【考点】

形容词辨析题。

【确定词性】

空格前面是介词with，后面是名词tubes，因此空格处应填入形容词修饰名词tubes，二者共同作介词with的宾语。

【答案解析】

空格所在句指出，木村教授的研究小组希望用________管代替实心支柱，从而减少建筑工程所需的________数量和重量。根据常识可知，用空心材料代替实心材料可以减轻材料的重量，因此空格处所填形容词应与solid“实心的”对应，含有“空心的”之意，故形容词K) hollow“空（心）的，中空的”为本题答案。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Satellites used to be the exclusive playthings of rich governments and wealthy corporations. 2 But increasingly, as space becomes more democratized, they are coming within reach of ordinary people. 3 Just like drones （无人机） before them, miniature satellites are beginning to fundamentally transform our conceptions of who gets to do what up above our heads.
1 As a recent report from the National Academy of Sciences highlights, these satellites hold tremendous potential for making satellite-based science more accessible than ever before. 2 However, as the cost of getting your own satellite in orbit drops sharply, the risks of irresponsible use grow. 3 The question here is no longer “Can we?” but “Should we?” 4 What are the potential downsides of having a slice of space densely populated by equipment built by people not traditionally labeled as “professionals”? 5 And what would the responsible and beneficial development and use of this technology actually look like? 6 Some of the answers may come from a nonprofit organization that has been building and launching amateur satellites for nearly 50 years.?
1 Having your personal satellite launched into orbit might sound like an idea straight out of science fiction. 2 But over the past few decades a unique class of satellites has been created that fits the bill: CubeSats. 3 The “Cube” here simply refers to the satellite’s shape. 4 The most common CubeSat is a 10cm cube, so small that a single CubeSat could easily be mistaken for a paperweight on your desk. 5 These mini-satellites can fit in a launch vehicle’s formerly “wasted space.” 6 Multiples can be deployed in combination for more complex missions than could be achieved by one CubeSat alone.?
1 Within their compact bodies these minute satellites are able to house sensors and communications receivers / transmitters that enable operators to study Earth from space, as well as space around Earth. 2 They’re primarily designed for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) — an easily accessible region of space from around 200 to 800 miles above Earth, where human-tended missions like the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station (ISS) hang out. 3 But they can attain more distant orbits; NASA plans for most of its future Earth-escaping payloads (to the moon and Mars especially) to carry CubeSats.?
1 Because they’re so small and light, it costs much less to get a CubeSat into Earth’s orbit than a traditional communications or GPS satellite. 2 For instance, a research group here at Arizona State University recently claimed their developmental small CubeSats could cost as little as $3,000 to put in orbit. 3 This decrease in cost allows researchers, hobbyists and even elementary school groups to put simple instruments into LEO or even having them deployed from the ISS.?
1 The first CubeSat was created in the early 2000s, as a way of enabling Stanford graduate students to design, build, test and operate a spacecraft with similar capabilities to the USSR’s Sputnik （前苏联的人造卫星）. 2 Since then, NASA, the National Reconnaissance Office and even Boeing have all launched and operated CubeSats. 3 There are more than 130 currently in operation. 4 The NASA Educational Launch of Nano Satellite program, which offers free launches for educational groups and science missions, is now open to U.S. nonprofit corporations as well. 5 Clearly, satellites are not just for rocket scientists anymore.?
1 The National Academy of Sciences report emphasizes CubeSats’ importance in scientific discovery and the training of future space scientists and engineers. 2 Yet it also acknowledges that widespread deployment of LEO CubeSats isn’t risk-free. 3 The greatest concern the authors raise is space debris — pieces of “junk” that orbit the earth, with the potential to cause serious damage if they collide with operational units, including the ISS.?
1 Currently, there aren’t many CubeSats and they’re tracked closely. 2 Yet as LEO opens up to more amateur satellites, they may pose an increasing threat. 3 As the report authors point out, even near-misses might lead to the “creation of a burdensome regulatory framework and affect the future disposition of science CubeSats.”
1 CubeSat researchers suggest that now’s the time to ponder unexpected and unintended possible consequences of more people than ever having access to their own small slice of space. 2 In an era when you can simply buy a CubeSat kit off the self, how can we trust the satellites over our heads were developed with good intentions by people who knew what they were doing? 3 Some “expert amateurs” in the satellite game could provide some inspiration for how to proceed responsibly.?
1 In 1969, the Radio Amateur Satellite Corporation (AMSAT) was created in order to foster ham radio enthusiasts ’（业余无线电爱好者） participation in space research and communication. 2 It continued the efforts, begun in 1961, by Project OSCAR — a U.S. based group that built and launched the very first nongovernmental satellite just four years after Sputnik. 3 As an organization of volunteers, AMSAT was putting “amateur” satellites in orbit decades before the current CubeSat craze. 4 And over time, its members have learned a thing or two about responsibility. 5 Here, open-source development has been a central principle. 6 Within the organization, AMSAT has a philosophy of open sourcing everything — making technical data on all aspects of their satellites fully available to everyone in the organization, and when possible, the public. 7 According to a member of the team responsible for FOX 1-A, AMSAT’s first CubeSat, this means that there’s no way to sneak something like explosives or an energy emitter into an amateur satellite when everyone has access to the designs and implementation.?
1 However, they’re more cautious about sharing information with nonmembers, as the organization guards against others developing the ability to hijack and take control of their satellites. 2 This form of “self-governance” is possible within long-standing amateur organizations that, over time, are able to build a sense of responsibility to community members, as well as society in general. 3 But what happens when new players emerge, who don’t have deep roots within the existing culture??
1 Hobbyists and students are gaining access to technologies without being part of a long-standing amateur establishment. 2 They’re still constrained by funders, launch providers and a series of regulations — all of which rein in what CubeSat developers can and cannot do. 3 But there’s a danger they’re ill-equipped to think through potential unintended consequences. 4 What these unintended consequences might be is admittedly far from clear. 5 Yet we know innovators can be remarkably creative with taking technologies in unexpected directions. 6 Think of something as seemingly benign as the cellphone — we have microfinance and text-based social networking at one end of the spectrum, and improvised （临时制作的） explosive devices at the other.?
1 This is where a culture of social responsibility around CubeSats becomes important — not simply to ensure that physical risks are minimized, but to engage with a much larger community in anticipating and managing less obvious consequences of the technology. 2 This is not an easy task. 3 Yet the evidence from AMSAT and other areas of technology development suggests that responsible amateur communities can and do emerge around novel technologies. 4 The challenge here, of course, is ensuring that what an amateur community considers to be responsible, actually is. 5 Here’s where there needs to be a much wider public conversation that extends beyond government agencies and scientific communities to include students, hobbyists, and anyone who may potentially stand to be affected by the use of CubeSat technology.

questions.explanation:
【定位】

由题干中的the easier accessibility to space和it is time to think about定位到文章I)段第一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，立方体卫星的研究人员表示，有机会进入自己那一小块空间的人数比以往更多，而现在是时候考虑这一切所带来的意想不到的、非预期的后果了。题干中的Given the easier accessibility to space是对定位句中consequences of more people than ever having access to their own small slice of space的概括归纳，题干中的think about是对定位句中ponder的同义转述，故答案为I)。

【定位】

由题干中的A group of mini-satellites、work together 和more complex tasks定位到文章C)段最后一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，与单颗立方体卫星所能完成的任务相比，多颗卫星可以联合部署起来去执行更复杂的任务。题干中的A group of mini-satellites对应定位句中的Multiples，题干中的work together 是对定位句中be deployed in combination的同义转述，题干中的tasks是定位句中missions的同义词，故答案为C)。

【定位】

由题干中的The greater accessibility、increases和the risks of their irresponsible use定位到文章B)段第一、二句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，这些卫星潜力巨大，使卫星科学比以往任何时候都更易于接受。然而，随着将个人卫星送入轨道的成本急剧下降，不负责任地使用卫星的风险也在增加。由上文可知，第一句中的these satellites是指A)段最后一句中的miniature satellites，而题干中的mini-satellites与此对应，题干中的The greater accessibility对应本段第一句中的more accessible，题干中的increases the risks of their irresponsible use是对第二句中the risks of irresponsible use grow的同义转述，故答案为B)。

【定位】

由题干中的school pupils、put in orbit和the lowered launching cost定位到文章E)段最后一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，成本的降低使得研究人员、业余爱好者，甚至小学生团体都能够将简单的仪器放入近地轨道，甚至可以从国际空间站部署它们。题干中的school pupils对应定位句中的elementary school groups，题干中的put in orbit是对定位句中put simple instruments into LEO的同义转述，题干中的owing to the lowered launching cost是对定位句中This decrease in cost allows的同义转述，故答案为E)。

【定位】

由题干中的AMSAT和hijacking of their satellites定位到文章K)段第一句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，为了防范其他大具备动持和控制其卫星的能力，在与非成员分享信息时，他们会更加谨慎。由上文可知，定位句的主语they指代上一段中的AMSAT成员。题干中的careful about是对定位中cautious about的同义转述，题干中的outsiders对应定位句中的nonmembers，题干中的prevent对应定位句中的guards against，故答案为K)。

【定位】

由题干中的NASA、Launch CubeSats、Free of charge和educational定位到文章F)段第四句。

 

【答案解析】

同义转述题。定位句提到，美国国家航空航天局的微型卫星教育性发射项目为教育团体和科学任务提供免费发射，目前也向美国非营利性公司开放。题干中的offers to launch… free of charge是对定位句中offers free launches的同义转述，题干中的CubeSats对应定位句中的Nano Satellite，题干中的for educational and research purposes对应定位句中的for educational groups and science missions，故答案为F)。

【定位】

由题干中的constraints和take the CubeSat technology in directions定位到文章L)段第二句和第五句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句提到，他们仍然受到资助者、发射供应商和一系列法规的限制——所有这些都限制了立方体卫星开发者可以做和不能做的事情。然而，我们知道，创新者可以非常有创造力地将技术带往意想不到的方向。题干中的with constraints是对定位句中They’re still constrained by funders, launch providers and a series of regulations—all of which rein in what CubeSat developers can and cannot do的概括归纳，题干中的creative developers对应定位句中的innovators can be remarkably creative，题干中的take the CubeSat technology in directions that result in harmful outcomes对应定位句中的taking technologies in unexpected directions，故答案为L)。

【定位】

由题干中的making significant contributions和pose hazards to other space vehicles定位到文章G)段第一句和最后一句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句提到，这份美国国家科学院的报告强调了立方体卫星在科学发现和未来太空科学家与工程师的培训这两方面的重要性。报告的作者们提出的最大担忧是太空碎片垃圾，如果它们与包括国际空间站在内的运行装置相撞，可能会造成严重的损害。题干中的making significant contributions to space science是对定位句中CubeSats’ importance in scientific discovery and the training of future space scientists and engineers的概括归纳，题干中的pose hazards是对定位句中cause serious damage的同义转述，题干中的space vehicles对应定位句中的operational units，故答案为G)。

【定位】

由题干中的enable operators、study Earth和LEO and space around it定位到文章D)段第一、二句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句提到，在其紧凑的机体内，这些微型的卫星可以容纳传感器和通信接收器或发射器，使操作人员能够从太空以及地球周围的空间来研究地球。它们主要是为近地轨道设计的。一些需要人类维护的太空任务，像哈勃太空望远镜和国际空间站就在这里运行。由第一句可知，第二句的主语They是指minute satellites，也就是说微型卫星主要是在近地轨道上运行，这使操作人员能够从近地轨道上研究地球。题干中的Mini-satellites对应定位句中的minute satellites，题干中的study Earth from LEO and space around it是对定位句中study Earth from space, as well as space around Earth的概括归纳，故答案为D)。

【定位】

由题干中的AMSAT、principle、all its technical data和amateur satellites定位到文章J).段最后两句。

 

【答案解析】

细节归纳题。定位句提到，业余无线电卫星组织的理念是开放一切资源——使组织中的每个人都能充分获得他们卫星的各个方面的技术数据，并在可能的情况下向公众开放。这意味着当每个人都有机会参与设计和实施时，将炸药或能量发射器之类的东西偷偷放入业余卫星里就行不通了。题干中的operates on the principle of是对定位句中has a philosophy of的同义转述，题干中的having all its technical data accessible to its members是对定位句中making technical data on all aspects of their satellites fully available to everyone in the organization的同义转述，题干中的preventing the abuse of amateur satellites是对定位句中there’s no way to sneak something like explosives or an energy emitter into an amateur satellite的概括归纳，故答案为J)。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 When I re-entered the full-time workforce a few years ago after a decade of solitary self-employment, there was one thing I was looking forward to the most: the opportunity to have work friends once again. 2 It wasn’t until I entered the corporate world that I realized, for me at least, being friends with colleagues didn’t emerge as a priority at all.? 3 This is surprising when you consider the prevailing emphasis by scholars and trainers and managers on the importance of cultivating close interpersonal relationships at work. 4 So much research has explored the way in which collegial （同事的） ties can help overcome a range of workplace issues affecting productivity and the quality of work output such as team-based conflict, jealousy, undermining, anger, and more.?
1 Perhaps my expectations of lunches, water-cooler gossip and caring, deep-and-meaningful conversations were a legacy of the last time I was in that kind of office environment. 2 Whereas now, as I near the end of my fourth decade, I realize work can be fully functional and entirely fulfilling without needing to be best mates with the people sitting next to you.
1 In an academic analysis just published in the profoundly-respected Journal of Management, researchers have looked at the concept of “indifferent relationships”. 2 It’s a simple term that encapsulates （概括） the fact that relationships at work can reasonably be non-intimate, inconsequential, unimportant and even, dare I say it, disposable or substitutable.?
1 Indifferent relationships are neither positive nor negative. 2 The limited research conducted thus far indicates they’re especially dominant among those who value independence over cooperation, and harmony over confrontation. 3 Indifference is also the preferred option among those who are socially lazy. 4 Maintaining relationships over the long term takes effort. 5 For some of us, too much effort.?
1 As noted above, indifferent relationships may not always be the most helpful approach in resolving some of the issues that pop up at work. 2 But there are nonetheless several empirically proven benefits.? 3 One of those is efficiency. 4 Less time chatting and socializing means more time working and churning （产出）.
1 The other is self-esteem. 2 As human beings, we’re primed to compare ourselves to each other in what is an anxiety-inducing phenomenon. 3 Apparently, we look down on acquaintances more so than friends. 4 Since the former is most common among those inclined towards indifferent relationships, their predominance can bolster individuals’ sense of self-worth.
1 Ego aside, a third advantage is that the emotional neutrality of indifferent relationships has been found to enhance critical evaluation, to strengthen one’s focus on task resolution, and to gain greater access to valuable information. 2 None of that might be as fun as after-work socializing but, hey, I’ll take it anyway.

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What did the author realize when he re-entered the corporate world?

重回职场后，作者意识到了什么？

A) Making new friends with his workmates was not as easy as he had anticipated.

和同事交朋友并不像他预料得那么容易

B) Cultivating positive interpersonal relationships helped him expel solitary feelings.

培养积极的人际关系有助于消除他的孤独感

C) Working in the corporate world requires more interpersonal skills than self-employment.

在公司工作比自营职业更需要人际交往技巧

D) Building close relationships with his colleagues was not as he had expected.

与同事建立密切关系并非如他预想的那样重要

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的re-entered the corporate world定位到1段②句。定位句指出，作者直到进入公司以后才意识到，至少对他来说，与同事交朋友并非头等大事。由此可见，他发现与同事关系密切并不是那么重要，故答案为D)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A/C选项【无中生有】：定位句没有提及与同事交朋友是否容易，也没有提到人际交往的技巧，故排除A)“和同事交朋友并不像他预料得那么容易”和C)“在公司工作比自营职业更需要人际交往技巧”；

B选项【词汇干扰】：作者虽然在1段①句提到自营职业是solitary“单独的，无伴的”，但是并没有说与同事交往是否会驱散孤独感，故排除B)“培养积极的人际关系有助于消除他的孤独感”。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What do we learn from many studies about collegial relationships?

根据许多有关同事关系的研究，我们可以了解到什么？

A) Inharmonious relationships have an adverse effect on productivity.

不和谐的关系对工作效率有不利影响

B) Harmonious relationships are what many companies aim to cultivate.

和谐的关系是许多公司的培养目标

C) Close collegial relationships contribute very little to product quality.

密切的同事关系对产品质量儿乎没有影响

D) Conflicting relationships in the workplace exist almost everywhere.

工作场所中，冲突无处不在

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的studies about collegial relationships定位到1段④句。定位句提到，有很多研究探索了同事关系用何种方式去帮助解决一些职场问题，这类问题包括团队内部的冲突、嫉妒、破坏、愤怒等，它们影响了生产效率和产品质量。由此可知，不和谐的同事关系会影响生产效率，故答案为A)。

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【无中生有】：从文中可知，作者没有提及公司对发展和谐的同事关系的态度，B)“和谐的关系是许多公司的培养目标”没有依据，故排除；

C选项【反向干扰】：从定位句可知，这些研究认为不和睦的关系会影响生产效率和产品质量，那么和睦的同事关系应该会有利于生产效率和产品质量的提高，C)“密切的同事关系对产品质量儿乎没有影响”不合语义，故排除；

D选项【过度推理】：定位句虽然指出职场中存在冲突，但是D)“工作场所中，冲突无处不在”属于过度推断，故排除。

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are vital to corporate culture.

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What can be inferred about relationships at work from an academic analysis?

我们可以从一片学术分析中对职场关系推断出什么？

A) They should be cultivated.

它们应该被加以培养

B) They are virtually irrelevant.

它们几乎无关紧要

C) They are vital to corporate culture.

它们对企业文化至关重要

D) They should be reasonably intimate

它们应该亲密无间

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的an academic analysis定位到3段。定位段提到了一项学术分析，研究人员审视了“冷漠关系”的概念，认为工作中的关系可以不亲密，可以无关紧要，甚至可以是一次性的或可替代的。换言之，同事关系并不像人们以往普遍认为的那么重要，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【答非所问】：从1段中可知，强调培养和谐的同事关系是以往的研究者、学者和管理者的观点，而非此处提到的学术分析的结论，故排除A)“它们应该被加以培养”；

C选项【无中生有】：根据定位句可知，这项学术分析没有涉及企业文化，故排除C)“它们对企业文化至关重要”；

D选项【反向干扰】：定位句指出，冷漠的、不亲密的同事关系完全是合理的，由此可知D)“它们应该亲密无间”的表述与原文相悖，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What does the author say about people who are socially lazy?

关于社交懒人，作者说了什么？

A) They feel uncomfortable when engaging in social interactions.

他们在参与社交活动时感到不自在

B) They often find themselves in confrontation with their colleagues.

他们经常发现自己陷入与同事的冲突之中

C) They are unwilling to make efforts to maintain workplace relationships.

他们不愿意努力维持职场关系

D) They lack basic communication skills in dealing with interpersonal issues.

他们缺乏处理人际关系的基本沟通技巧

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的people who are socially lazy定位到4段③④⑤句。定位句提到，懒得社交的人会喜欢“冷漠关系”，因为维持亲密的职场关系需要付出努力，而这些人会觉得这太过费力，由此可知他们不愿维持职场关系的原因是懒得去做，故答案为C)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A/D选项【无中生有】：由定位句可知，文中并未提到这些懒于社交的人是否在社交活动中感觉不适或缺乏基本的沟通技巧，故排除A)“他们在参与社交活动时感到不自在”和D)“他们缺乏处理人际关系的基本沟通技巧”；

B选项【过度推理&常识干扰】：定位句指出，懒得社交的人只是懒得花力气去维持人际关系，并没有提及选项B)“他们经常发现自己陷入与同事的冲突之中”，故排除。

【题干及选项概览】

What is one of the benefits of indifferent relationships?

淡漠关系的好处之一是什么？

A) They provide fun at work.

它们给工作带来乐趣

B) They help control emotions.

它们有助于控制情绪

C) They help resolve differences.

它们有助于解决分歧

D) They improve work efficiency.

它们提升工作效率

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的the benefits of indifferent relationships定位到5段①②句。在定位句之后，作者具体提到了冷漠关系的三点益处。而第五段最后两句指出，其中的一项益处就是效率，少花时间聊天和社交意味着有更多的时间工作和做出成绩，D)项的表述与此相符，故为答案。

 

【错误选项分析】

A/C选项【无中生有】：文章5，6，7段谈及“冷漠关系”的益处时，没有提到工作乐趣，也没有提到要解决分歧，故排除A)“它们给工作带来乐趣”和C“它们有助于解决分歧”

B选项【偷换概念】：文章7段虽然指出冷漠关系可以让人们在情感上保持中立，但这并不等同于能帮助人们控制情绪，B)“它们有助于控制情绪”曲解了原文的意思，故排除。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 In a few decades, artificial intelligence (AI) will surpass many of the abilities that we believe make us special.? 2 This is a grand challenge for our age and it may require an “irrational” response.
1 One of the most significant pieces of news from the US in early 2017 was the efforts of Google to make autonomous driving a reality. 2 According to a report, Google’s self-driving cars clocked 1,023,330 km, and required human intervention 124 times. 3 That is one intervention about every 8,047 km of autonomous driving. 4 But even more impressive is the progress in just a single year: human interventions fell from 0.8 times per thousand miles to 0.2, a 400% improvement.? 5 With such progress, Google’s cars will easily surpass my own driving ability later this year.
1 Driving once seemed to be a very human skill. 2 But we said that about chess, too. 3 Then a computer beat the human world champion, repeatedly. 4 The board game Go （围棋） took over from chess as a new test for human thinking in 2016, when a computer beat one of the world’s leading professional Go players. 5 With computers conquering what used to be deeply human tasks, what will it mean in the future to be human? 6 I worry about my six year-old son. 7 What will his place be in a world where machines beat us in one area after another? 8 He’ll never calculate faster, never drive better, or even fly more safely. 9 Actually, it all comes down to a fairly simple question: What’s so special about us? 10 It can’t be skills like arithmetic, which machines already excel in. 11 So far, machines have a pretty hard time emulating creativity, arbitrary enough not to be predicted by a computer, and yet more than simple randomness.?
1 Perhaps, if we continue to improve information-processing machines, we’ll soon have helpful rational assistants. 2 So we must aim to complement the rationality of the machine, rather than to compete with it. 3 If I’m right, we should foster a creative spirit because a dose of illogical creativity will complement the rationality of the machine. 4 Unfortunately, however, our education system has not caught up to the approaching reality. 5 Indeed, our schools and universities are structured to mould pupils to be mostly obedient servants of rationality, and to develop outdated skills in interacting with outdated machines.? 6 We need to help our children learn how to best work with smart computers to improve human decision-making. 7 But most of all we need to keep the long-term perspective in mind: that even if computers will outsmart us, we can still be the most creative.? 8 Because if we aren’t, we won’t be providing much value in future ecosystems, and that may put in question the foundation for our existence.

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What is the author’s greatest concern about the use of AI?

关于AI的应用，作者最担忧什么？

A) Computers are performing lots of creative tasks.

计算机正在执行许多创造性的任务

B) Many abilities will cease to be unique to human beings.

许多能力将不再为人类所独有

C) Computers may become more rational than humans.

计算机可能会变得比人类更理性

D) Many human skills are fast becoming outdated.

许多人类的技能很快就过时了

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的the use of AI定位到1段①句。定位句指出，在几十年内，人工智能将在许多我们自认为是人类特有的能力上实现超越。而随后的2段最⑤句和3段①②句也以驾驶和下棋为例，说明很多以前被认为是人类专属的能力，现在都被机器超越了，故答案为B)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【反向干扰】：由后文可知，作者认为具有创造力才是人类的特别之处，可知A)“计算机正在执行许多创造性的任务”与原文相悖，故排除；

C选项【答非所问】：作者在4段指出机器是理性的，但是这并不是他担忧的，因为机器的理性可以协助人类，故C)“计算机可能会变得比人类更理性”不符合原文，应排除；

D选项【曲解文意】：D)“许多人类的技能很快就过时了”曲解了原文，虽然机器在很多技能方面超越了人类，但这些技能本身并没有过时，故排除。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What impresses the author most in the field of AI?

在AI领域，最令作者印象深刻的是什么？

A) Google’s experimental driverless cars require little human intervention.

谷歌的无人驾驶实验车几乎不需要人工干预

B) Google’s cars have surpassed his driving ability in just a single year.

谷歌的汽车仅用一年时间就超过了他的驾驶能力

C) Google has made huge progress in autonomous driving in a short time.

谷歌仅在短时间内就在无人��驶领域取得了巨大进步

D) Google has become a world leader in the field of autonomous driving

谷歌已经成为自主驾驶领域的世界领先者

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的impress定位到2段④句。定位句提到，更令人叹为观止的是在仅一年内它取得的进步，人类干预从每一千英里0.8次下降到0.2次，改进了400%。故而，自动驾驶在短时间内取得的巨大进步最令作者印象深刻，故答案为C)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【无中生有】：从2段可知，作者并没有对自动驾驶所需人为干预的绝对次数进行评价，故排除A)“谷歌的无人驾驶实验车几乎不需要人工干预”；

B选项【反向干扰】：由2段⑤句可知，目前谷歌自动驾驶车的技能还没有超过作者的驾驶能力���故排除B)“谷歌的汽车仅用一年时间就超过了他的驾驶能力”；

D选项【无中生有】：文章中并没有提及D)“谷歌已经成为自主驾驶领域的世界领先者”，故也排除。

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is yet to be emulated by AI.

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What do we learn from the passage about creativity?

关于创造力，我们从中了解到什么？

A) It is rational.

它是合理的

B) It is predictable.

它是可以预测的

C) It is human specific.

它是人类特有的

D) It is yet to be emulated by AI.

它上不能被AI模仿

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的creativity定位到3段11句。定位句指出，因为创造力具有随意性，而又不仅仅是简单的随机性，足以让计算机无法预测。因此，到目前为止，机器很难模伤人类的创造力，可以推知，创造力尚未被人工智能模仿，故答案为D)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【无中生有】：原文中没有提及A)“它是合理的”，故排除；

B选项【反向干扰】：定位句指出，创造力不可预测，因此B)“它是可以预测的”与原文相悖，故排除；

C选项【过度推理】：虽然作者在定位句中表明机器很难模仿人类的创造力，但据此断定它是人类特有的，属于过度推断，故排除C)“它是人类特有的”。

【题干及选项概览】

What should schools help children do in the era of AI?

在AI时代，学校应该帮助学童做什么？

A) Cultivate original thinking.

培养原创思维

B) Learn to work independently.

学会独立工作

C) Compete with smart machines.

与智能机器竞争

D) Understand how AI works.

了解人工智能的工作原理

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的schools help children do定位到4段⑤⑥句。定位句指出，我们的中小学和大学在把学生塑造成屈从于理性的人，培养与落伍的机器互动的落伍的技能，我们需要帮助我们的孩子们学习如何有效地使用智能计算机来改进人类的决策力，而之前的③句更是认为，人类应该培养自已的创造性，与机器的理性相互补充。综合这些信息可知，学校应培养孩子的创造力，以更好地使用机器，故答案为A)。

 

【错误选项分析】

B/D选项【无中生有】：文章没有提到人类是否应独立工作，也没有提到孩子们是否该了解人工智能的原理，故排除B)“学会独立工作”和D)“了解人工智能的工作原理”；

C选项【反向干扰】：4段②句明确指出，人类应该做的是与机器的理性相互补充，而不是与之竞争，故排除C)“与智能机器竞争”。

choices.label: D

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

How can we humans justify our future existence?

人类怎么样才能为未来自身的存在正名？

A) By constantly outsmarting computers.

通过不断超越计算机

B) By adopting a long- term perspective.

通过接受有远见的观点

C) By rationally compromising with AI.

通过理性地与人工智能妥协

D) By providing value with our creativity.

利用自身创造力创造价值

 

【定位及答案】

由题干中的future existence 定位到4段⑧句。定位句指出，如果我们不能如此，在未来的生态系统中，我们存在的价值将会降低，从而可能会给我们存在的根基带来挑战。结合⑦句可知，“不能如此”就是如果人类不能保持创造力，换言之，要想体现和证实自身的存在价值，必须要用创造力为未来的生态体系提供价值，故答案为D)。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【反向干扰】：由4段⑦句可知，在作者看来，人类在聪明程度上未必会超越计算机，故排除A)“通过不断超越计算机”；

B选项【答非所问】：B)“通过接受有远见的观点”是利用4段⑦句设置的干扰项，作者让大家把眼光放长远一点，要保持创造力，因为这才是体现人类价值的根本所在，接受观点本身并不能体现人类存在的价值，故排除；

C选项【反向干扰】：由前文可知，作者认为，人类与机器的协作方式是以人类的创意去弥补机器的理性，而不是理性地与其妥协，故排除C)“通过理性地与人工智能妥协”。

My name is Paul. How can I help you today?
Morning. I wouldn't say that it's good from where I am standing.
This is Miss Wilson, and this is the third time I've called this week since receiving your letter about our insurance claim.
I'm getting a little fed up with my calls about my claim being completely disregarded.
Miss Wilson, thank you for calling back.
Can I take some details to help me look at your claim?
It's Miss May Wilson of 15 South Sea Road in Cornwall.
And the details are that our village was extensively flooded two months ago.
The entire ground floor of our cottage was submerged in water, and five of us have been living in a caravan ever since.

And it's not acceptable? Paul!
Miss Wilson, according to the notes on your account, the bizarre technical detail that you mentioned refers to the fact that you hadn't paid house insurance the month before the incident.
That money left our account, and now that you should be paying out, you are suddenly saying that you didn't receive it on time.
I'm really skeptical about this claim.
The contract does say that any mispayment in a year will affect the terms and conditions of the insurance contract, and may affect claims.

To achieve financial security, how much you save is always more important than the amount you earn or how shrewdly you invest.
If you're under 30 years old, your goal should be to save 20% of your monthly income after tax deductions.
This is irrespective of how much you earn.
Approximately 50% should be reserved for essentials like food and accommodation.
The remaining 30% is for recreation and entertainment.
But for many young people, it'll be difficult to designate such a large proportion of their income for savings.
If you find it hard to save any money at all, start by cutting all unnecessary spending.
Allocate a tiny amount of 1 or 2 percent for savings and gradually increase that amount.
Always keep that 20% goal in mind, prevents yourself from becoming complacent.
It can be challenging to stick to such a strict plan.
But if you adopt the right mindset, you should be apt to make it work for you.
So, what should you be doing with the money that you're saving?
Some must be kept easily accessible in case you need some cash in an emergency.
The largest proportion should be invested retirement plans either through your employer or privately.
And you can keep some money for high-risk but potentially lucrative investments. Dividends can be reinvested or used to purchase something you like.
By following this plan, you should hopefully be able to enjoy your life now and still be financially secure in the future.

Did you know that Americans have approximately three times the amount of space we had 50 years ago?
Therefore, you'd think we'd have sufficient room for all of our possessions.
On the contrary, the personal storage business is now a growing industry.
We've got triple the space, but we've become such enthusiastic consumers that we require even more.
This phenomenon has resulted in significant credit card debt, enormous environmental footprints, and perhaps not coincidentally, our happiness levels have failed to increase over the same half century.
I'm here to suggest an alternative that having less might actually be a preferable decision.
Many of us have experienced, at some stage, the pleasure of possessing less.
I propose that less stuff and less space can not only help you economize, but also simplify your life.
I recently started an innovative project to discover some creative solutions that offered me everything I required.
By purchasing an apartment that was 40 square meters instead of 60.
I immediately saved $ 200,000.
Smaller space leads to reduced utility bills, and also a smaller carbon footprint.
Because it is designed around an edited collection of possessions, limited to my favorite stuff, I'm really excited to live there.
How can we live more basically?
Firstly, we must ruthlessly cut the unnecessary objects out of our lives.
To stem consumption, we should think before we buy, and ask ourselves, "Will it truly make me happier?"
Obviously, we should possess some great stuff.
But we want belongings that we're going to love for years.
Secondly, we require space efficiency.
We want appliances that are designed for use most of the time, not for occasional use.
Why own a six-burner stove when you rarely use even three burners?
Finally, we need multifunctional spaces and housewares.

Consider my coffee table.
It increases in size to accommodate ten.

But consider the benefits of an edited life.

Now, believe it or not, people sometimes lie in order to maintain a good, honest reputation—even if it hurts them to do so.
At least, this is what a team of scientists is suggesting, with evidence to prove it.
Picture this scenario : You often drive for work and can be compensated for up to 400 miles per month.
Most people at your company drive about 300 miles each month, but this month you drove 400 miles.
How many miles do you think you'd claim in your expense report?
The scientists asked this exact question as part of the study we're discussing today.
With surprising results, they found that 12% of respondents reported the distance they drove as less than the actual figure, giving an average answer of 384 miles.
In other words, they lied about the number of miles, even though they would forfeit money they were owed.
The researchers believe this was to seem honest, with the assumption being that others would be suspicious of a high expense claim.
But why would people fabricate numbers to their own detriment?
The researchers explained that many people care a great deal about their reputation and how they'll be judged by others.
If they care enough, their concern about appearing honest and not losing the respect of others may be greater than their desire to actually be honest.
The researchers assert that the findings suggest that when people obtain very favorable outcomes, they anticipate other people's suspicious reactions and prefer lying and appearing honest to telling the truth and appearing as selfish liars.
So why is this research important?
Well, experts generally agree there are two main types of lie — selfish lies and lies that are meant to benefit others.
The first, as you may predict, is for selfish gain, such as submitting a fraudulent claim to an insurance company.
While the second involves lying to help others or not offend others, for example, telling a friend whose outfit you don't like that they look great.
But the researchers are suggesting a third type of lying — lying to maintain a good reputation.
Now, this hypothesis is new and some skeptics argue that this isn't a whole new category of lie.
But the findings seem intuitive to me.
After all, one of the main motivations for lying is to increase our worth in the eyes of others. So it seems highly likely that people will lie to seem honest.

Why do old people dislike new music?
As I've grown older, I often hear people my age say things like “They just don't make good music like they used to.”
Why does this happen?
Luckily, psychology can give us some insights into this puzzle.
Musical tastes begin to crystallize as early as age 13 or 14.
By the time we're in our early 20s, these tastes get locked into place pretty firmly.
In fact, studies have found that by the time we turned 33, most of us have stopped listening to new music.
Meanwhile, popular songs released when you're in your early teens are likely to remain quite popular among your age group through the rest of your life.
There could be a biological explanation for this, as there is evidence that the brain's ability to make subtle distinctions between different chords, rhythms and melodies deteriorates with age.
So to older people, newer, less familiar songs might all "sound the same. ”
But there may be some simpler reasons for older people's aversion to newer music.
One of the most researched laws of social psychology is something called the "mere exposure effect,” which, in essence, means that the more we're exposed to something, the more we tend to like it.
This happens with people we know, the advertisements we see, and the songs we listen to.
When you're in your early teens, you probably spend a fair amount of time listening to music or watching music videos.
Your favorite songs and artists become familiar, comforting parts of your routine.
For many people over 30, job and family obligations increase, so there's less time to spend discovering new music.
Instead, many will simply listen to old, familiar favorites from that period of their lives when they had more free time.
Of course, those teen years weren't necessarily carefree.
They're famously confusing, which is why so many TV shows and movies revolve around high school turmoil.
Psychology research has shown that the emotions that we experience as teens seem more intense than those that come later.
And we also know that intense emotions are associated with stronger memories and preferences.
Both of these might explain why the songs we listen to during this period become so memorable and beloved.
So there's nothing wrong with your parents because they don't like your music.
Rather it's all part of the natural order of things.

questions.explanation: 【细节推断题】【题目】What should people do if they find it difficult to follow the speaker's advice on their financial plan?讲话者提到,如果按他提出的理财计划建议很难做到,可以先从削减不必要的开支做起，先存1%〜2%,然后逐渐增加这个 比例。
【题目】What does the speaker think is important for achieving financial security?（讲话者认为什么对于实现财务安全很重要？）第一段首句指出,要实现财务安全,存下多少钱很重要。第二段末两句指出,坚持执行严格的储蓄计划可能具有一定挑战性,但如果能树立正确的心态,便能使这一计划起作用,进而实现财务安全的目标。综上,A符合题意。

【细节推断题】【题目】 What has prevented Americans' happiness levels from increasing?讲座开头提到，美国人的空 间是50年前的三倍,但他们已经成为如此热情的 消费者，以至于没有足够的空间容纳自己的物品。 这种现象导致信用卡欠债、环境遭到破坏、人们的幸福水平在过去的半个世纪里并没有提高。由此可知，美国人对消费的痴迷阻碍了其幸福感的提升。

【细节推断题】【题目】What do we learn about the items in the speaker's home?讲座中提到，我们需要要多功能的空间和家庭用品。讲话者家中的咖啡桌增大后可容纳十个人，他的办公室很容易藏起来，床能够从墙上弹出来。由此可知，讲话者家里的物品是多功能的。

【细节辨认题】【题目】What might explain the fact that songs people listen to in their teen years are memorable and beloved?讲座最后提到，心理学研究 表明，青少年时期的情感更加强烈,这种强烈的情 感与更强的记忆力和偏好有关。这就解释了为什 么我们在这一时期所听的歌曲变得如此难忘和受 人喜爱。

sections.title: Part 1 Writing 写作
sections.passage:
1 Creativity tends to be considered as an ability with which only a few people are endowed. 2 In fact, it can be taught, practiced and developed. 3 Unfortunately, the conventional teaching method focuses on convergent instead of divergent thinking. 4 Simply put, students are always asked to solve problems that have one correct and well-established answer rather than come up with multiple solutions to open-ended questions.
1 Such neglect of developing creativity will hamper students' career growth. 2 As everyone knows, creative minds are able to think out of the box. 3 By making novel, original or even unorthodox suggestions, they often act as a savior of a team stuck on a tricky problem. 4 It is no wonder that creativity is one of the soft skills employers value most. 5 Furthermore, lack of this ability may have an adverse effect on students' mental health. 6 That is because creativity goes a long way to equipping them for the real world characterized by rapid changes. 7 It allows them to look at difficulties and frustrations from a fresh perspective, so that they can live with and adapt to the unknown.
1 To sum up, a creative person has a competitive edge over other job candidates and is more likely to keep composure amid uncertainties. 2 School education should therefore lay more emphasis on fostering creativity among students.

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 The Qinghai-Tibet Railway is the highest and longest plateau railway in the world, with a total length of 1, 956 kilometers, of which 960 kilometers are over 4,000 meters above the sea level. 2 It is the first railway connecting Tibet with the rest of China. 3 As the railway travels through the most fragile ecosystem in the world, ecological protection measures have been taken during and after the construction to ensure that it becomes a "green railway". 4 The Qinghai-Tibet Railway has greatly shortened the travel time to Tibet. 5 More importantly, it has greatly promoted the economic development of Tibet and improved the life of local residents. 6 Since the opening of the railway, more and more people have chosen to travel to Tibet by train so that they will have the opportunity to enjoy the beautiful scenery along the route.

questions.answer: 1 The Qinghai-Tibet Railway is the highest and longest plateau railway in the world, with a total length of 1, 956 kilometers, of which 960 kilometers are over 4,000 meters above the sea level. 2 It is the first railway connecting Tibet with the rest of China. 3 As the railway travels through the most fragile ecosystem in the world, ecological protection measures have been taken during and after the construction to ensure that it becomes a "green railway". 4 The Qinghai-Tibet Railway has greatly shortened the travel time to Tibet. 5 More importantly, it has greatly promoted the economic development of Tibet and improved the life of local residents. 6 Since the opening of the railway, more and more people have chosen to travel to Tibet by train so that they will have the opportunity to enjoy the beautiful scenery along the route.

questions.explanation:
【确定词性】

空格所在句中,破折号前为完整的主谓宾结构,破折号后以并列连词while also连接两部分,空格词应与providing一致,为及物动词的-ing分词。

【锁定答案】

空格前文提到,“对有害社会的事物征税”具有强大的诱惑力,提供了“双重收益”的可能。破折号引出对“双重收益”的解释说明，___ harmful activities应与providing the government with revenue语义同向,体现正面、积极的作用,故空格词应表“抑制/消除/控制”等,A符合文意。

【确定词性】

空格词所在的which从句中存在两种情形:1. and并列连接excessive drinking和___driving,空格词应为driving的修饰成分,可能为名词、形容词、ing分词、ed分词。2, and并列连接reducerexcessive drinking和 ___driving,空格词应为及物动词的第三人称单数,

【锁定答案】

本题的解题思路有二:一、从句内逻辑来看,“减少过量饮酒和___驾驶”为“喝醉成本提高”的结果,结合常识可知,醉酒行为越少,危险/醉酒驾车几率越低;二、从段际关系来看,第二段①句提出以“罪恶税”为例论证首段(对有害社会的事物征税的双重益处),③句指出酒税带来财政收入。②句应该体现酒税“抑制有害活动”的效果。综上可知,空格词应意为“危险的/有害的/醉酒的”等,impaired driving为固定搭配,意为“危险驾驶,不清醒驾驶(尤指醉驾)",E正确.D) fragments,G) incentives似乎是动词第三人称单数,符合“确定词性”的第二种情形。但fragments和driving语义上明显无法搭配,先排除。incentives似乎能体现“减少酒驾,改善驾驶”,有一定干扰,但进一步分析发现: incentive只能用作名词(刺激、激励)或形容词(刺激的),没有动词义项,而且“刺激、激励驾驶”并不等于“改善驾驶”,也可排除。

【确定词性】

空格所在句主句结构为Tobacco taxes have proven ____ in. . , 空格词可能为形容词或名词。

【锁定答案】

空格句指出,烟税带来的财政收入超过酒税的两倍,已经(被)证实在减少吸烟上___ (____in the decline of smoking),这拯救了数百万人的生命。空格所在部分一方面应体现“拯救数百万人生命”的原因,另一方面应呼应首段“抑制有害活动”,故空格词应表��“(在减少吸烟方面)起作用/有帮助”等,J正确。

【确定词性】

空29所在从句that ___ carbon dioxide into the sky显然缺少谓语动词(that指代companies,在从句中作主语),句子整体时态为一般现在时,空格词应为及物动词原形。

【锁定答案】

空格句前一分句指出,碳税能提高经济效率。后一分句指出,由于将二氧化碳 __29__ 空中的公司一直未为自己造成的气候变化买单,所以碳税将恢复对市场的正当__30__ 。借助分号作用和语义逻辑可知:分号前后两分句为“概说一解释”关系;分号之后语义重点在主句,即“恢复对市场的正当 30 "应与“提高经济效率”同向,空30应表“促进/激励/改善"等,G正确。空29所在从句(because...)聚焦这类公司(companies) :将二氧化碳____空中,造成气候变化。显然空格词应表示“排放/输出(二氧化碳)"。再看整句逻辑:一直以来排碳者不为自己的行为买单(因此市场缺乏激励),现在碳税(让排碳者为自己的行为买单,所以)将恢复对市场的恰当刺激(从而提高经济效率)。因果关系完全成立,确认N正确。

【确定词性】

空30所在主句carbon taxes would restore the proper __30___ to the market缺少宾语中心词,空格词应为名词或动名词。

【锁定答案】

空格句前一分句指出,碳税能提高经济效率。后一分句指出,由于将二氧化碳 __29__ 空中的公司一直未为自己造成的气候变化买单,所以碳税将恢复对市场的正当__30__ 。借助分号作用和语义逻辑可知:分号前后两分句为“概说一解释”关系;分号之后语义重点在主句,即“恢复对市场的正当 30 "应与“提高经济效率”同向,空30应表“促进/激励/改善"等,G正确。空29所在从句(because...)聚焦这类公司(companies) :将二氧化碳____空中,造成气候变化。显然空格词应表示“排放/输出(二氧化碳)"。再看整句逻辑:一直以来排碳者不为自己的行为买单(因此市场缺乏激励),现在碳税(让排碳者为自己的行为买单,所以)将恢复对市场的恰当刺激(从而提高经济效率)。因果关系完全成立,确认N正确。

【确定词性】

空格词在which从句中位于情态动词would和系动词be之间,只能为副词。

【锁定答案】

which从句指出,碳税带来的财政收入每年____达数千亿美元,强调“税收潜力巨大/现有量庞大",故空格词应表示“可能/实际/通常”等, probably正确。initially作为备选项中另一副词有一定干扰,但此处若强调“起初,最初”,下文必会提及后来的变化,而实际上并未提及,故排除。

【确定词性】

空格前为冠词a,空格词应为可数名词单数。

【锁定答案】

空格句句首What's more表明,该句承接上句所述的碳税价值,继续说明碳税的其他用途:该项收入数额巨大，可作为____分发给市民,或用于资助绿色基础设施项目。"____分发给市民"和“资助绿色基础设施项目”应为两项并列的碳税收入用途,结合受益者身份“市民"可知,空32应为“福利/红利”等,B正确。

【确定词性】

空格所在从句结构为:which(引导词作主语)+ some experts____+ will be(系动词)+ over $4 trillion per decade(表语)。句中已有完整的主系表成分,故some experts____只能作插入成分,空格词应为动词。

【锁定答案】

空格所在的which从句指出,财产税收入将超4万亿美元/10年, will表明这是对未来数据的预测,some experts为常见的预测者,联系可知,空格词应表“预测/推断/估计”等,L正确。

【确定词性】

空34位于系动词is和形容词bad之间,应为副词。

【锁定答案】

末段①句“同样,财产税的提出也是为了在减少不平等的同时增加财政收入”表明,财产税被视为前文所述酒税、烟税、碳税的同类。②句具体说明财产税如何增加财政税收,减少不平等。空格句(③句)指出,如果认为财富不平等__34__有害,那么财产税在改善社会的同时也__35__政府的金库。可见,空格句承上总结财产税的作用(抑制有害活动、增加政府收入)。空34指向财富不平等“有害社会”的本质,即“本质上/根本上/内在地(有害)",H正确

【确定词性】

空35位于while引导的状语中,空格后为名词短语government coffers,空格词应为及物动词的-ing分词(while doing sth为while sb be doing sth的省略形式,当主从句间主语一致时,从句中的主语和be动词可省略)。

【锁定答案】

末段①句“同样,财产税的提出也是为了在减少不平等的同时增加财政收入”表明,财产税被视为前文所述酒税、烟税、碳税的同类。②句具体说明财产税如何增加财政税收,减少不平等。空格句(③句)指出,如果认为财富不平等__34__有害,那么财产税在改善社会的同时也__35__政府的金库。可见,空格句承上总结财产税的作用(抑制有害活动、增加政府收入)。“空35应表“扩充/增加(政府的金库/财政收入)",O正确。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 A group of corn farmers stands huddled around an agronomist （农学家） and his computer on the side of an irrigation machine in central South Africa. 2 The agronomist has just flown over the field with a hybrid unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) that takes off and lands using propellers yet maintains distance and speed for scanning vast hectares of land through the use of its fixed wings.
1 The UAV is fitted with a four spectral band precision sensor that conducts onboard processing immediately after the flight, allowing farmers and field staff to address, almost immediately, any crop abnormalities that the sensor may have recorded, making the data collection truly real-time.
1 In this instance, the farmers and agronomist are looking to specialized software to give them an accurate plant population count. 2 It's been 10 days since the corn emerged and the farmer wants to determine if there are any parts of the field that require replanting due to a lack of emergence or wind damage, which can be severe in the early stages of the summer rainy season.?
1 At this growth stage of the plant's development, the farmer has another 10 days to conduct any replanting before the majority of his fertilizer and chemical applications need to occur. 2 Once these have been applied, it becomes economically unviable to take corrective action, making any further collected data historical and useful only to inform future practices for the season to come.?
1 The software completes its processing in under 15 minutes producing a plant population count map. 2 It's difficult to grasp just how impressive this is. without understanding that just over a year ago it would have taken three to five days to process the exact same data set, illustrating the advancements that have been achieved in precision agriculture and remote sensing in recent years. 3 With the software having been developed in the United States on the same variety of crops in seemingly similar conditions, the agronomist feels confident that the software will produce a near accurate result.?
1 As the map appears on the screen, the agronomist's face begins to drop. 2 Having walked through the planted rows before the flight to gain a physical understanding of the situation on the ground he knows the instant he sees the data on his screen that the plant count is not correct, and so do the farmers, even with their limited understanding of how to read remote sensing maps.?
1 Hypothetically, it is possible for machines to learn to solve any problem on earth relating to the physical interaction of all things within a defined or contained environment by using artificial intelligence and machine learning
1 Remote sensors enable algorithms (算法) to interpret a field's environment as statistical data that can be understood and useful to farmers for decision-making. 2 Algorithms process the data, adapting and learning based on the data received. 3 The more inputs and statistical information collected, the better the algorithm will be at predicting a range of outcomes. 4 And the aim is that si farmers can use this artificial intelligence to achieve their goal of a better harvest through making better decisions in the field.?
1 In 2011, IBM, through its R&D Headquarters in Haifa, Israel, launched an agricultural cloud-computing project. 2 The project, in collaboration with a number of specialized IT and agricultural partners, had one goal in mind —— to take a variety of academic and physical data sources from an agricultural environment and turn these into automatic predictive solutions for farmers that would assist them in making real-time decisions in the field.
1 Interviews with some of the IBM project team members at the time revealed that the team believed it was entirely possible to "algorithm" agriculture, meaning that algorithms could solve any problem in the world. 2 Earlier that year, IBM's cognitive learning system, Watson, competed in the game Jeopardy against former winners Brad Rutter and Ken Jennings with astonishing results. 3 Several years later, Watson went on to produce ground-breaking achievements in the field of medicine.
1 So why did the project have such success in medicine but not agriculture? 2 Because it is one of the most difficult fields to contain for the purpose of statistical quantification. 3 Even within a single field, conditions are always changing from one section to the next. 4 Theres unpredictable weather, changes in soil quality, and the ever-present possibility that pests and diseases may pay a visit. 5 Growers may feel their prospects are good for an upcoming harvest, but until that day arrives, the outcome will always be uncertain.?
1 By comparison, our bodies are a contained environment. 2 Agriculture takes place in nature, among ecosystems of interacting organisms and activity, and crop production takes place within that ecosystem environment. 3 But these ecosystems are not contained. 4 They are subject to climatic occurrences such as weather systems, which impact upon hemispheres as a whole, and from continent to continent. 5 Therefore, understanding how to manage an agricultural environment means taking literally many hundreds if not thousands of factors into account.?
1 What may occur with the same seed and fertilizer program in the United States' Midwest region is almost certainly unrelated to what may occur with the same seed and fertilizer program in Australia or South Africa. 2 A few factors that could impact on variation would typically include the measurement of rain per unit of a crop planted, soil type, patterns of soil degradation, daylight hours, temperature and so forth.?
1 So the problem with deploying machine learning and artificial intelligence in agriculture is not that scientists lack the capacity to develop programs and protocols to begin to address the biggest of growers' concerns; the problem is that in most cases, no two environments will be exactly alike which makes the testing, validation and successful rollout of such technologies much more laborious than in most other industries.?
1 Practically, to say that Al and Machine Learning can be developed to solve all problems related to our physical environment is to basically say that we have a complete understanding of all aspects of the interaction of physical or material activity on the planet. 2 After all, it is only through our understanding of 'the nature of things' that protocols and processes are designed for the rational capabilities of cognitive systems to take place. 3 And, although AI and Machine Learning are teaching us many things about how to understand our environment, we are still far from being able to predict critical outcomes in fields like agriculture purely through the cognitive ability of machines
1 Backed by the venture capital community, which is now investing billions of dollars in the sector, most agricultural technology startups today are pushed to complete development as quickly as possible and then encouraged to flood the market as quickly as possible with their products.
1 This usually results in a failure of a product, which leads to skepticism from the market and delivers a blow to the integrity of Machine Learning technology. 2 In most cases, the problem is not that the technology does not work, the problem is that industry has not taken the time to respect that agriculture is one of the most uncontained environments to manage. 3 For technology to truly make an impact on agriculture, more effort, skills, and funding is needed to test these technologies in farmers' fields.?
1 There is huge potential for artifical intelligence and machine learning to revolutionize agriculture by integrating these technologies into critical markets on a global scale. 2 Only then can it make a difference to the grower, where it really counts.

questions.explanation:
【题干翻译】

种植户一旦在田地里施用了大部分肥料和其他化学品,就无法从补种中获利。


【答案解析】

36题not profit from replanting同义改写2句economically unviable to take corrective action, most of the fertilizer and other chemicals复现①句the majority of his fertilizer and chemical...

D段①②句明确补种时机:一旦施用了大部分肥料和化学品,再进行补种在经济上便不可行了。②句中的these回指D句中的the majority of his fertilizer and chemical. .. , take corrective action呼应①句中的conduct... replanting,试题是对该句信息的同义改写。


【段落分析】

D段补充玉米补种的相关知识,强调“时效性"。

①句At this growth stage,another 10 days接续C段时间点“玉米出苗已有10天”,明确补种时间要求“未来10天内完成(another 10 days)",即植株统计必须尽快。

②句以Once假定情形,说明错过补种期的后果“大部分肥料和化学品已经施用,补种失去经济效益”,强调数据搜集的时效性。

全段核心信息:

(1)玉米补种期;

(2)错过补种期的后果;

(3)数据时效性。

【题干翻译】

农业与人体医学的区别在于其环境是不受控制的。


【答案解析】

37题human body对应D句our bodies, not a contained one复现③句not contained

L段前三句对比医药与农业,强调后者环境的特点“不受控制的”。试题是对二者区别的概括,differs from体现了①句By comparison,③句But所体现的比较之意;medical science明确了①句ourbodies(呼应上段medicine)所暗指的对象。


【段落分析】

L段通过对比人类身体,展现农业的不确定性:农业环境是不受控制的,诸多因素相互关联、牵一发而动全身。

①至③句By comparison、But继续对比医药(our bodies为医学研究对象,呼应K段medicine)、农业两大领域,凸显后者“不受控制(not contained)"的特点。

④⑤句具体说明该特点及影响:农业生产受到复杂外部环境的影响,其统计量化需考虑成百上千种因素,难度极大。全段核心信息:农业生产环境具有不受控制的特征,其统计量化涉及诸多因素。

【题干翻译】

农学家确信可以使用其软件获得一个近乎精确的植株数量。


【答案解析】

38题The agronomist复现③句原词,sure,a near accurate count同义复现③句confident,a near accurate result。

E段描述专业软件的性能,其中③句表明农学家对其软件性能的信心:(由于软件开发时所使用的作物品种及实验条件均相同/似)该软件将会得出近乎精确的结果。试题是对该句信息的同义改写, a near accurate count of plant population对应a near accurate result (result指代该段首句a plant population count map).


【段落分析】

E段指出软件计算速度非常快,农学家们对试验结果相当自信。

①②句先明确试验中软件的计算速度"15分钟内完成(in under 15 minutes)",后以impressive(令人赞叹的)高度评价其速度表现,并对比一年前所需时间(3到5天)凸显其进步之飞速,最后以illustrating引出其意义:展现了近些年来在精准农业和遥感方的巨大进步。

③句主句以confident... near accurate明确农学家的乐观预期“将得出近乎精确的结果";With引导的状语说明原因:软件开发时使用的作物品种相同,实验条件极其相似(on the same variety of cropsin seemingly similar conditions)。

全段核心信息:

(1)软件的速度表现;

(2)农学家对试验结果的乐观预期。

【题干翻译】

在农业领域应用人工智能比大多数其他行业更具挑战性。


【答案解析】

39题much more challenging改写much more laborious,most other industries复现段末表达。

N段明确在农业领域应用人工智能的问题所在:人工智能技术的实测、验证和上市都远比其他大多数行业耗时费力。试题是对该内容的概括 application对应deploying.


【段落分析】

N段总结:农业领域人工智能应用的问题在于农业环境极度不可控。So承上作结, the problem. .. is notthat... the problem is that..取舍结构重申原因:农业生产环境千差万别,农业领域人工智能技术的实测、验证和上市都远比其他行业更难。

全段核心信息:人工智能在农业领域的应用远比其他行业更难。

【题干翻译】

就连种植户都知道无人机提供的数据不正确。


【答案解析】

40题the data provided by the UAV对应②句the data, not correct在②句中复现。②句信息“种植户也知道软件得出的数据明显不正确”匹配40题核心义。

F段②句揭示专业软件所得结果:一看到屏幕上的数据,农学家立马知道植株数量不对;种植户也发现不对,虽然他们对如何解读遥感地图了解有限。试题是对该句信息的整合概括,Even对应原文even with their limited understanding of how to read remote sensing maps,强调“计算结果错误过于明显,连身为非专业人士的种植户都能看出来”。


【段落分析】

F段指出随后生成的结果明显不准确。

①句以农学家看到数据后的神情变化(face begins to drop)暗示试验结果不如人意。

②句is not correct明示试验结果“计算不准确"; he knows the instant. .. and so do the farmers,even with... limited. .则以“不仅农学家一眼看出数量不对,就连对软件缺乏了解的种植户也是如此”强调计算结果精确性严重不足。

全段核心信息:

(1)软件的精确性表现;

(2)农学家、种植户对试验结果的判断。

【题干翻译】

要求速见成效会导致产品失败,而产品失败又转而引发人们对人工智能技术在农业领域的适用性的怀疑。


【答案解析】

41题The pressure for quick results对应①句主语This(回指P段as quickly as possible所凸显的行业乱象“大量资本涌入农技术行业,一味追求速度”), product failure改写①句a failure of a product, arousesdoubts改写leads to skepticism.

Q段①句顺承上文内容指出一味追求速见成效的后果:产品失败,市场对机器学习技术在农业领域的适用性产生怀疑。试题是对该句的同义改写,句中This回指上段所述“一味求快”的行业乱象, The pressure for quick results是对此内容的概括。


【段落分析】

Q段指出农业技术行业只求速见成效导致的不良后果,并就此提议。

①句results in、leads to,delivers ablow to明示因果:一味追求速度→产品失败一市场怀疑→机器学习技术遭到质疑。

②句为机器学习/人工智能技术正名,指出实际问题在于业内未能真正尊重农业自身的特点。

③句For. . is needed提议:应在技术的田间实测方面增加投入。

全段核心信息:

(1)农业技术行业一味追求速度的后果;

(2)技术如何真正影响农业

【题干翻译】

使用遥感器的目的是帮助种植户改善决策,提高产量。


【答案解析】

42题Remote sensors复现于本段段首,improve decision-making to increase yields同义改写④句 achieve their goal of a better harvest through making better decisions in the field.④句大意“使用遥感器是为了让种植户做出更好的决策,增加收成” 匹配42题核心义。

H段介绍遥感器在农业领域的潜能,其中④句指出使用遥感器的目的/作用:让种植户能够利用这种人工智能在田间做出更好的决策,从而达到增加收成的目的。试题是对该句信息的整合,are aimed to help farmers...义改写the aim is that farmers can...。


【段落分析】

H段具体介绍人工智能在农业领域的潜能。Remote sensors呼应上文precision sensor,remote sensing,说明农业领域所借助的主要技术:遥感技术。段内以Remote sensors enable algorithms. .. Algorithms processthe data. .. And the aim is that...明确遥感器技术的作用机制:利用算法得到田间数据→对数据进行处理,基于收到的数据进行调整和学习一帮助种植户及时做出更好的决策→收成得以提高。

全段核心信息:

遥感器在农业领域的巨大潜能及作用机制。

【题干翻译】

种植户希望软件能告诉他农田里是否有任何需要补种的部分。


【答案解析】

43题the software对应①句specialized software, replant any parts of his farm fields同义改���②句there are any parts of the field that require replanting。本段种植户对专业软件效用的期待“帮助其确定是否有田块需要补种”匹配43题核心义。

C段说明种植户对专业软件效用的期待,①句提出期待“专业软件提供准确的植株数量",②句解释说明期待“由此确定是否有田块需补种”。试题是对两句信息的提炼, expects对应are looking to, tell him whether...对应determine if...


【段落解析】

C段明确实验的预期效果,突出“精确性”,暗示“时效性”, In this instance, specialized software承接上文UAV机载精密传感器的一般作用,聚焦本次试验的预期效果。... looking to. .. wants to determine. ..呈递“预期效果(利用专业软件准确计算植株数量-->使用目的(帮助农民确定是否有田块需要补种)"的逻辑。It's been 10 days since the corn emerged暗示时效性“玉米已经出苗10天,补种正当时”。

全段核心信息:种植户和农学家对软件效用的预期。

【题干翻译】

事实证明,由于涉及的条件时刻都在变化,农业极难量化。


【答案解析】

44题difficult to quantify概括②句one of the most difficult fields. ..for... statistical quantification, constantly changing conditions改写3句conditions are always changing.②至⑤句内容“农业是最难统计量化的领域之一,因为其环境条件随时随地在变,不可预测”匹配44题核心义。

K段②句指出农业是最难统计量化的领域之一,③句以“即使是在同一片农田内部,每个地段的环境条件都在时刻发生变化”凸显农业环境“变化莫测”的特点,说明其量化难度之大。试题是对两句大意的概括, because of是对两句间暗含因果关联的明确。


【段落解析】

K段总领段群,概括原因:农业极难进行统计量化控制(极具不确定性)。

①句why抛出问题:为何人工智能在医药领域大获成功,却在农业领域折戟?

②句Because引出总体原因, it is one of the most difficult fieldsto contain回应G段within a defined or contained environment,明确原因。

③至⑤句always changingunpredictable,changes、the ever-present possibility, always. .. uncertain近义复现凸显农业的“不确定性”特点:农业生产环境变化莫测,难以收集可靠数据。

全段核心信息:

(1)IBM项目在农业领域折戟;

(2)农业环境不确定性强，难以统计量化.

【题干翻译】

同样一项播种和施肥计划在不同地区可能产生截然不同的效果。


【答案解析】

45题The same seed and fertilizer program完整复现M段①句表达。

M段①句指出一项播种和施肥计划在美国中西部的效果与其在澳大利亚、南非等地的效果互不相干,即同样的计划可能在不同地区产生完全不同的效果。试题是对该句大意的概括,completelydifferent明确unrelated的内涵,outcomes改写What may occur.


【段落分析】

M段进一步展现农业的不确定性:地区差异大,同一计划在不同地区效果可能完全不同。

①句以“同一播种和施肥计划可能在不同国家产生完全不同的效果”为例说明农业的地区差异之大;

②句以A few factors.. would typically include...补充列举造成该差异的若干典型原因。

全段核心信息:同一农业计划在不同地区的影响可能完全不同，

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 What is the place of art in a culture of inattention? 2 Much of that time, for some of them, is spent taking photographs not even of the painting but of themselves with the painting in the background.
1 One view is that we have democratised tourism and gallery-going so much that we have made it effectively impossible to appreciate what we've travelled to see. 2 In this oversubscribed society, experience becomes a commodity like any other.? 3 There are queues to climb Mt. Jolmo Lungma as well as to see famous paintings. 4 Leisure, thus conceived, is hard labour, and returning to work becomes a well-earned break from the ordeal.
1 What gets lost in this industrialised haste is the quality of looking. 2 Consider an extreme example, the late philosopher Richard Wollheim. 3 When he visited the Louvre he could spend as much as four hours sitting before a painting. 4 The first hour, he claimed, was necessary for misperceptions to be eliminated. 5 It was only then that the picture would begin to disclose itself.? 6 This seems unthinkable today, but it is still possible to organise. 7 Even in the busiest museums there are many rooms and many pictures worth hours of contemplation which the crowds largely ignore. 8 Sometimes the largest crowds are partly the products of bad management; the Mona Lisa is such a hurried experience today partly because the museum is being reorganised. 9 The Uffizi in Florence, another site of cultural pilgrimage has cut its entry queues down to seven minutes by clever management.? 10 And there are some forms of art, those designed to be spectacles as well as objects of contemplation, which can work perfectly well in the face of huge crowds.
1 Olafur Eliasson's current Tate Modern show, for instance, might seem nothing more than an entertainment, overrun as it is with kids romping (喧闹地玩耍) in fog rooms and spray mist installations. 2 But it's more than that: where Eliasson is at his most entertaining, he is at his most serious too, and his disorienting installations bring home the reality of the destructive effects we are having on the planet — not least what we are doing to the glaciers of Eliasson's beloved Iceland.?
1 Marcel Proust, another lover of the Louvre, wrote: "It is only through art that we can escape from ourselves and know how another person sees the universe, whose landscapes would otherwise have remained as unknown as any on the moon." 2 If any art remains worth seeing, it must lead us to such escapes. 3 But a minute in front of a painting in a hurried crowd won't do that.?

choices.label: B
choices.text: The near impossibility of appreciating art in an age of mass tourism.

choices.label: C

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. The enormous appeal of a great piece of artistic work to tourists.

    伟大的艺术作品对游客的吸引力极大

B. The near impossibility of appreciating art in an age of mass tourism.

    在大众旅游时代，欣赏艺术近乎不可能

C. The ever-growing commercial value of long-cherished artistic works

    珍藏已久的艺术作品的商业价值日益增长

D. The real difficulty in getting a glimpse at a masterpiece amid a crowd.

    要在人群中短暂感受一下杰出画作实在太难


【定位及答案】

本题考查“卢浮宫的景象”的本质。由the Louvre定位至首段。该段③句描述卢浮宫内的场景:卢浮宫要求参观者只能在《蒙娜丽莎》前停留一分钟,而在这宝贵的一分钟中,很多游客只顾着拍照,而且是以画像为背景给自己拍照,并非把画作拍下来。第二段①句作者对这种场景作出评价:我们现在将旅游和观展变得太过普及,以至于根本无法欣赏奔波前往观看的作品,即在大众旅游时代欣赏艺术愈发困难,可见B正确。该项The near impossibility同义转述effectivelyimpossible, an age of mass tourism概括we have democratised tourism. .. so much所展现的时代特点。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：A虽与“游客排队参观《蒙娜丽莎》”所展露的“艺术品的巨大吸引力”相契合,但文意重点在于“吸引参观者的是“自己观赏名画,这一体验,而非“名画,本身(not even of the painting but of themselves)"

C选项【东拼西凑】：C将“卢浮宫内参观《蒙娜丽莎》的游客众多”这一事实与第二段@句commodity(商品)一词强加关联,主观臆测《蒙娜丽莎》等珍责作品的商业价值越来越高,但原文commodity实际描述的是旅行经历从“一种私人体验”到“可买卖的商品”的转交。

D选项【词汇干扰】：D利用“每位游客在《蒙娜丽莎》前只能停留一分钟”设置干扰,但作者意在强调“在有限的一分钟里,游客也没能好好欣赏画作,而只是给自己拍照,把画作当背景”

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

A. It takes time to appreciate a piece of art fully.

    充分欣赏一件艺术作品需要时间

B. It is quite common to misinterpret artistic works.

    误读艺术作品十分常见

C. The longer people contemplate a picture, the more likely they will enjoy it.

    凝视一幅画的时间越长，就越可能享受它的乐趣

D. The more time one spends before a painting, the more valuable one finds it.

    在画作前停留时间越长，就越能发觉它很珍贵


【定位及答案】

本题考查“Wollhim长时间欣赏画作”的原因。由Richard Wollbeim定位互第三段③至⑤句。第三段②句首先明确Wollheim的事例为视端例子(就此追溯至①句观点句“工业化的仓促和快旅游风尚使旅游和观展的品质降低”,并判断②句Wollheim事例意在以过去情形之“慢”凸显当今情形之“快”，③句进而描述事例本身“Wollheim会在画作前停留四个小时之久",④⑤句接着 引Wollheim本人话语说明原因：第一个小时是为消除误解，后面三个小时才开始逐断领悟画作真语。故A正确。


【错误选项分析】

B选项【以偏概全】：该选项对染可以根据“第一个小时对于消除误解很必要”正确推理出“误读很常见”,但没有涵盖“后三个小时用以理解画作真谛”。

C选项【偷换概念】：将长时间凝视画作的原因由“领悟真谛”偷换为“享受乐趣”

D选项【偷换概念】：将长时间凝视画作的原因由“领悟真谛”偷换为“发现珍贵之处”

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

 What does the case of the Ufizi in Plorence show?

   俄罗伦萨乌菲兹美术馆这一事例说明了什么?

A. Art works in museums should be better taken care of.

    馆藏艺术品应得到更好的保护。

B. Sites of cultural pilgrimage are always flooded with visitors.

    文化朝圣地常常挤满游客。

C. Good management is key to handling large crowds of visitors.

    良好的管理是应对大批游客的关键。

D. Large crowds of visitors cause management problems for museums.

    大批游客会给博物馆带来管理问题。


【定位及答案】

本题考查“乌菲兹美术馆事例”的写作目的,可定位至第三段⑨句(并追溯至⑥句观点句)。第三段⑥句指出"Wollheim式的深度参观(即长时间停留欣赏画作以领悟其真谛)可通过组织管理来实现”,⑦⑧句指出“博物馆人满为患、资源配置不当、游客仓促参观的原因是管理不善或正处修整期",⑨句介绍乌菲兹美术馆做法“通过巧妙的管理极大地缩短了入场排队时间”。综合可知,文章提及乌菲兹美术馆的事例是为了说明“良好的管理可应对大批游客,为其提供更多空间及时间来实现深度参观",C正确。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：A由⑦句largely ignore望文生义出“馆藏艺术品未得到很好的保护”,而句意实为“游客大多忽略/不好好欣赏艺术品". 

B选项【答非所问】：虽能根据⑦⑧⑨句中the crowds/the largest crowds/huge crowds,anothersite of cultural pilgrimage 合理推断而来,属事实,但均非题干所问事例(佛罗伦萨乌菲兹美术馆通过巧妙的管理大大缩短了游客入场排队时间)所服务的目的。

D选项【答非所问】：虽能根据⑦⑧⑨句中 bad management/reorganised/clever management合理推断而来,属事实,但均非题干所问事例(佛罗伦萨乌菲兹美术馆通过巧妙的管理大大缩短了游客入场排队时间)所服务的目的。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What do we learn from Olafur Eliasson's current Tate Modern show?

根据奥拉维尔·埃利亚松当前正在泰特现代美术馆举办的展览,我们可以获知什么?

A. Children learn to appreciate art works most effectively while they are playing.

     孩子们在玩乐中学会最有效地欣赏艺术作品。

B. It is possible to combine entertainment with appreciation of serious art.

    将消遣娱乐和欣赏严肃艺术结合起来是可实现的

C. Art works about the environment appeal most to young children

    与环境相关的艺术作品对小孩子最具吸引力。

D. Some forms of art can accommodate huge crowds of visitors. 

    有些艺���形式所在场地可容纳大批游客。


【定位及答案】

本题考查“奥拉维尔·埃利亚松的展览”的相关事实细节,可定位至第四段。第四段先指出“埃利亚松的展览看起来不过是一场娱乐活动,满是嬉闹的孩子”,后转而指出“这次展览不止于此,埃利亚松娱乐大众,也给人以严肃之感,整个展览意在警示人类行为对环境的影响”。综合可知,该展览表明“娱乐消遣和欣赏严肃艺术可以很好地结合起来", B正确。


【错误选项分析】

A、C选项【无中生有】：均源自第四段①句kids romping in fog rooms and spray mist installations,但文中并未比较“孩子们在不同状态下学习艺术品欣赏的效果(most effectively while. . )"及“不同艺术品对小孩子的吸引力(appeal most to...） ".

D选项【以偏概全】：利用第三段末句与第四段首句for instance之间的例证关联设置干扰,干扰性很强,但第三段末句实际上并非单单指向“艺术形式空间容量大,可容纳大批游客”,更意在指向“场面壮观,游客体验感好(spectacles. . . work perfectly well)",选项以偏概全,而且与第四段语义重心不符。
