questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What can art do according to Marcel Proust?

    据马塞尔·普鲁斯特所言,艺术可以做什么?

A. Enable us to live a much fuller life

    让我们的生活更充实。

B. Allow us to escape the harsh reality.

    让我们逃离严酷的现实。

C. Help us to see the world from a different perspective.

    帮助我们从另一个角度看世界。

D. Urge us to explore the unknown domain of the universe.

    激励我们探索宇宙的未知领域。


【定位及答案】

本题考查马塞尔·普鲁斯特对于“艺术的作用”的观点,由Marcel Proust可定位至末段。末段①句引用普鲁斯特之言指出“唯有通过艺术,我们才能超脱自我,了解他人如何看待天地万物”。由此可知,普鲁斯特认为“艺术可以帮助我们超越自身的固有认知,从另一个角度看世界",C正确。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：该选项将①句艺术的功能“拓展认知边界:让我们看到不同视角下的世界”曲解为“丰富生活经历:使我们过上丰富得多的生活(full指富于经历的,有很多活动的)", 

B选项【偷换概念】：将①句我们要脱离的对象“自身的认知(ourselves)"篡改为“严酷的现实(the harsh reality)"

D选项【词汇干扰】：D源自①句the universe,unknown as any on the moon,但unknown as any on the moon(月球上的未知景象)是“他人眼中的景象”的类比对象,用以强调其“(在没有艺术的情况下)遥不可及,极难知晓”,全文未提及“艺术对于宇宙探索的意义”。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 Every five years, the government tries to tell Americans what to put in their bellies. 2 Eat more vegetables. 3 Dial back the fats. 4 It's all based on the best available science for leading a healthy life. 5 But the best available science also has a lot to say about what those food choices do to the environment, and some researchers are annoyed that new dietary recommendations of the USDA (United States Department of Agriculture) released yesterday seem to utterly ignore that fact.?
1 Broadly, the 2016--2020 dietary recommendations aim for balance: More vegetables, leaner meats and far less sugar.
1 But Americans consume more calories per capita almost any other country in the world. 2 So the things Americans eat have a huge impact on climate change. 3 Soil tilling releases carbon dioxide, and delivery vehicles emit exhaust. 4 The government's dietary guidelines could have done a lot to lower that climate cost. 5 Not just because of their position of authority: The guidelines drive billions of dollars of food production through federal programs like school lunches and nutrition assistance for the needy.?
1 On its own, plant and animal agriculture contributes 9 percent of all the country's greenhouse gas emissions. 2 That's not counting the fuel burned in transportation, processing, refrigeration, and other waypoints between farm and belly. 3 Red meats are among the biggest and most notorious emitters, but trucking a salad from California to Minnesota in January also carries a significant burden. 4 And greenhouse gas emissions aren't the whole story. 5 Food production is the largest user of fresh water, largest contributor to the loss of biodiversity, and a major contributor to using up natural resources.?
1 All of these points and more showed up in the Dietary Guidelines Advisory Committee's scientific report, released last February. 2 Miriam Nelson chaired the subcommittee in charge of sustainability for the report, and is disappointed that eating less meat and buying local food aren't in the final product. 3 Especially if you consider that eating less meat, especially red and processed, has health benefits, she says.
1 So what happened? 2 The official response is that sustainability falls too far outside the guidelines official scope, which is to provide "nutritional and dietary information.
1 Possibly the agencies in charge of drafting the decisions are too close to the industries they are supposed to regulate. 2 On one hand, the USDA is compiling dietary advice. 3 On the other, their clients are US agriculture companies.?
1 The line about keeping the guidelines' scope to nutrition and diet doesn't ring quite right with researchers. 2 David Wallinga, for example, says, "In previous guidelines, they've always been concerned with things like food security — which is presumably the mission of the USDA. 3 You absolutely need to be worried about climate impacts and future sustainability if you want secure food in the future."?

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

Why are some researchers irritated at the USDA's 2016 — 2020 Dietary Guidelines?

   为什么一些研究者恼怒于美国农业部2016-2020年的膳食指南?

A. It ignores the harmful effect of red meat and processed food on health.

    它忽视了红肉和加工食品对健康的有害影响。

B. Too much emphasis is given to eating less meat and buying local food.

    过分强调少吃肉类和购买本地食品。

C. The dietary recommendations are not based on medical science.

    膳食建议并非基于医学。

D. It takes no notice of the potential impact on the environment. 

    它忽略了对环境的潜在影响。


【定位及答案】

本题考查一些研究者恼怒于美国农业部的膳食指南的原因,根据题干关键词someresearchers irritated at the USDA's 2016-2020 Dietary Guidelines定位至第一段末句(... some researchers are annoyed that new dietary recommendations of the USDA...)。第一段末句指出,一些研究者恼怒的是美国农业部的新版膳食建议似乎完全忽视了“食物选择会对环境造成诸多影响”这一事实(that fact的具体所指),故D正确。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【以偏概全】：源自第五段③句,但该句援引Nelson(对膳食指南倍感恼怒的研究员之一)之言“少吃红肉与加工肉制品有益健康”,意在说明②句Nelson对膳食指南的看法“忽略可持续性发展”,选项舍本逐末、偏离观点核心“忽略对环境可待续的影响”, 

B选项【反向干扰&无中生有】：源自第五段@句,该句指出Nelson对“膳食指南未提及“少吃肉、购买当地食品”感到失望，换言之，膳食指南并非过分强调“少吃肉、购买当地食品”,而是根本未提及。

C选项【偷换概念】：与第一段④句“膳食建议建立在现有最佳科学的基础之上”不符,且将the best available science for leading ahealthy life"关乎健康生活的现有最佳科学"窄化为medical science"医学”

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

Why does the author say the USDA could have contributed a lot to lowering the climate cost through its dietary guidelines? 

为什么作者说美国农业部本可以通过其膳食指南为降低气候成本作出巨大贡献?

A. It has the capacity and the financial resources to do so.

    它有能力以及财力这样做。

B. Its researchers have already submitted relevant proposals. 

    其研究者已经提交了相关建议。

C. Its agencies in charge of drafting the guidelines have the expertise.

    其负责起草膳食指南的机构拥有专业知识。

D. It can raise students' environmental awareness through its programs.

    它可以通过自身的项目来提高学生的环保意识。


【定位及答案】

本题考查作者的观点。由题干关键词Why... contributed a lot to lowering the climate cost 定位至第三段④⑤句 ... could have done a lot to lower that climate cost. Not just because of...)。第三段④句指出政府(USDA)的膳食指南本可以为降低气候成本作出巨大贡献,句进而点明原因:这些指导方针不仅仅象征着权威,还可通过各种形式的联邦计划推动数十亿美元的粮食生产,由此可推断,美国农业部不仅有能力(具有威望)、也有财力(享有财政资源)去降低气候成本,A符合文意。


【错误选项分析】

B选项【答非所问】：该选项虽由第五段①句All of these points and more showed up in... scientific report. ..合理推断而来,但并非作者所认为的USDA膳食指南有助降低气候成本的原因:这些建议即便被纳入USDA终版膳食指南(由②句可知实际并未被纳入其中),如若USDA本身能力及财力有限,该指南的影响力也将有限,为降低气候成本作出的贡献也有限。

C选项【东拼西凑】：由第七段①句the agencies in charge of drafting the decisions are...和第五段①句所述研究人员的“专业性报告(scientific report)"杂糅捏造而来,但第七段①句实际指的是“负责起草膳食指南的机构与他们本应监管的行业走得过近(暗示即便是拥有专业性、权威性的美国农业部仍会受到相关利益团体的影响而罔顾食物选择对气候的消极影响)”,而并未谈及“起草机构的专业性”。 

D选项【望文生义】：由第三段⑤句“这些指导方针可通过诸如学校午餐等联邦计划推动数十亿的粮食生产”望文生义,得出“美国农业部可以通过联邦计划提高学生的环保意识”。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What do we learn from the Dietary Guidelines Advisory Committes scientific report?

从膳食指南咨询委员会的科学报告中,我们解到什么?

A. Food is easily contaminated from farm to belly

    食物在从农场到餐桌的途中很容易被污染

B. Greenhouse effect is an issue still under debate.

    温室效应是一个仍存在争议的问题。

C. Modern agriculture has increased food diversity.

    现代农业增加了食物的多样性。

D. Farming consumes most of our natural resources.

    农业消耗了我们大部分的自然资源。


【定位及答案】

本题考查膳食指南咨询委员会科学报告的具体内容。由题干关键词the Dietary GuidelinesAdvisory Committee's scientific report可初步定位至第五段首句,再根据首句中these points的回指功能最终锁定第四段。第四段末句指出,粮食生产是自然资源枯竭的主要原因,D中most of,consumes. ...

natural resources分别对应句中major contributor、using up natural resources。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【过度推理】：虽复现原文from farm to belly，却增补文中未提及信息“易被污染”。

B选项【偷换概念】：利用第四段greenhouse gas emissions与第五段所列举的"Nelson等研究员对(USDA最终拟定的)膳食指南的失望”捏造干扰,将研究员之间的争议焦点由“膳食指南是否应考虑可持续性”偷换为“温室效应是否真实存在”。

C选项【断章取义】：对第四段末句Food production... largest contributor to... biodiversity断章取义,将文意“农业损害了生物多样性”反向由解为“农业丰富了盘中餐”


【解题思路提示】

本题针对第四段设题,段中提及多种事物(温室气体排放、食品加工与运输、生物多样性、自然资源),相应地,选项也较为发散。对于此类事实细节题,最稳妥的办法是将“定位法”与“排除法”相结合:先由此项关键词from farm to belly,Greenhouse effect food diversity, natural resources分别定位至②句、①句、⑤句前半句与⑤句后半句;随后将选项对比原文可知,A中easily contaminated与B中still under debate均无据可循,C中food diversity与文中biodiversity不符,只有D契合原文。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What may account for the neglect of sustainability in the USDA's Dietary Guidelines according to the author?

作者认为,美国农业部的膳食指南忽略可持续性的原因可能是什么?

A. Its exclusive concern with Americans' food safety.

    它只关心美国民众的食品安全。

B. Its sole responsibility for providing dietary advice.

    它只负责提供饮食建议。。

C. Its close ties with the agriculture companies

    它与农业公司关系密切。

D. Its alleged failure to regulate the industries.

    它被指未能对行业进行监管。


【定位及答案】

本题考查作者对“膳食指南为何忽略可持续性”的看法,由题干关键词What may account for theneglect of sustainability定位至第六段及之后的内容(So what happened?. . . sustainability falls too far outside. ..)。第七段①句中作者先概述指出,负责草拟膳食决议的官方机构(USDA)与其本应监管的行业走得过近,后于③句明确本应被监管行业的具体所指“美国农业公司”,可见C正确。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【答非所问】：源自第八段②句concerned with ..food security,但选项中"exclusive(只关心)”与句中thingslike暗示的“也关心包括粮食安全之外的其他问题”相悖,且该句实为研究者观点,并非作者观点。

B选项【答非所问】：源自第六段②句,但该句为USDA官方说辞而非作者观点。

D选项【过度推理】：源自第七段①句,虽属作者观点,但将原文“与其应监管的行业走得过近”的言外之意“农业部对行业的监管较为宽松”夸大为“农业部完全没有进行监管”。


【解题思路分析】

解答本题难点有二:一是定位有难度,根据题千信息the neglect of sustainability似乎应定位到第五段aren't in the final product,但题目并未局限于现象本身,而是进一步考查其成因(account for... ),故初步定位至第六段及之后的段落(So what happened?. .. sustainability falls too far outside)。二是人物观点错综复杂、难以辨别,需仔细审题,根据题干中may与according to the author可明确题目考查作者对原因的测,由此排除第六段的官方说辞(official response)、第八段的研究者观点(researchers),锁定第七段(Possibly),故可直接排除非第七段信息的A与B,进一步对比原文后发现D夸大其词,也可排除。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What should the USDA do to achieve food security according to David Wallinga?

大卫·沃林加认为,美国农业部应该采取什么措施来实现粮食安全?

A. Give top priority to things like nutrition and food security.

    将营养和粮食安全这类问题作为第一要务

B. Endeavor to ensure the sustainable development of agriculture. 

    努力保障农业的可持续发展。

C. Fulfill its mission by closely cooperating with the industries. 

    与行业紧密合作,以完成自身使命

D. Study the long-term impact of climate change on food production.

    研究气候变化对粮食生产的长期影响。


【定位及答案】

本题考查文中人物所提的建议。根据题干关键词David Wallinga定位至第八段②③句。第八段③句大卫·沃林加指出,美国农业部若想在未来保障粮食安全,就必须关注气候影响和未来可持续性,意即美国农业部要想实现粮食安全,就必须考虑农业发展/粮食生产的可持续性,B正确。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【东拼西凑】：由第八段nutrition,things like food security杂糅而来,与沃林加的态度“需把粮食安全、可持续性等问题与营养和膳食同等重视起来”相悖。

C选项【东拼西凑】：由第七段0句close to the industries、第八段②句missionof the USDA杂糅捏造出“与行业密切合作,以完成自身使命". 

D选项【曲解文意】：将第入段③句worried about climateimpacts... food in the future曲解为"应开展相关研究”。


【解题思路】

本题借“人物建议”考查考生对于“文章核心观点”的把握。解题可:

1.根据建议标记词(should,must.it's necessary/essential等)锁定建议内容,第八段③句以absolutely need to引出沃林加的建议(be worried about climate impacts and future sustainability),排除与此无关的A与C, D虽相关但将“考虑(worried about)"曲解为“研究(Study)",判断合理概括此建议的B正确。

2.梳理文章脉络,明确“核心观点",首段指出“研究者对“农业部的新版膳食指南完全忽视食物选择对环境的消极影响,倍感失望”,二至五段细述新版膳食指南对可持续性的忽略,第六、七段阐明“膳食指南不考虑可持续性”的原因,第八段重申研究者对新版膳食指南的不满,可见文章主旨为“膳食指南必须考虑可持续性",确认B为正确项。

Unlike any video game five ever played before, it's so boring, yet so relaxing at the same time.
How did you hear about this driving simulator?
My brother introduced it to me last year.
I was surprised to find how educational and realistic it was.
It's called Euro Truck Simulator, but they have other versions as well for America and so on.
I was really drawn to the scenery.
The routes go through parts of the country you don't normally see as a tourist.
Yeah, I can see that.
It seems so simple, just transporting cargo from point A to point B, driving from one city to another.
But I really appreciate all the details that go into the game.
It's even given me a new appreciation for the logistics industry and traffic on the road.
I completely agree.
My brother also introduced me to some videos of someone that streams the game online.
It was fascinating to watch, really.
This guy drove very carefully, obeyed all the road signs and traffic rules — such a contrast to most violent games.
Honestly? playing has inspired me to look into the industry more.
I've read articles about how self-driving trucks may soon be available and could greatly impact cargo logistics.
Considering all that goes into driving these larger vehicles, it's amazing that we could soon have that kind of technology.
Ah. I've gone one step further.
I registered to take a safe driving course to improve my real-life driving skills.
In a way, I feel like I have a head start compared to other students in the class.
Playing this video game has given me some maneuvering practice already.

How do you like being self-employed?
There are obvious benefits, though I don't seem to have the freedom I anticipated as I just don't seem able to decline work offers.
And working alone, there have been times when I've found that money alone provides insufficient motivation.
Have you experienced the same since you began working for yourself?
Sometimes, yes.
Unlike the rest of the workforce who have managers to prompt motivation whenever they're feeling lazy or bored, we self-employed workers perform our jobs without a manager to lift our spirits.
There's no one around to offer praise or initiate collaboration, no one to make greater use of our interests and talents.
That's a fact.
Not every manager behaves with such awareness and care, of course.
And certainly not all managers have a clue how to motivate people.
Still, having a manager nearby at least indicates there's an opportunity they'll be decent enough to look out for you when your energy and focus begin to deplete.
The motivator I value most is autonomy.
I've learned not to sacrifice my prized autonomy by working all hours of the day and by saying yes to every client request.
Yes. I need to remind myself that I selected this lifestyle for the independence.

Weather is a constant force in our lives, but there is little marketing research on how it affects businesses.
Now, a new study reveals how sunny and snowy conditions influence consumer behavior.
Those weather conditions trigger consumers to mentally visualize using products associated with the respective weather.
This leads to consumers placing a higher value on those products.
That is, they're willing to pay more money for them.
But the correlation is only found with products related to being outside. How does this work?
Researchers give the example of a beach towel.
On a sunny day, consumers who see that product are not just looking at the towel itself, they are likely imagining themselves lying on the towel in the sun.
This mental picture of using the towel increases the value of the product in the consumers' mind.
Researchers put forward the following hypothesis to explain their findings.
They think the mental picture works in sunshine and snow because these weather conditions have a positive association with outside activities.
The effect is not seen with rainy weather.
Researchers assert this is because there aren't many activities that are enabled by rain.
Most products associated with rain, like umbrellas, are only used for protection from the weather, and not for any activities.
Researchers believe that companies that sell a wide array of products online can benefit most from the insights this study provides.
Online sellers often use complex mathematical formulas to determine what products to feature and how to price these products.
Incorporating more data about weather would allow them to make better decisions.
This could bolster sales.

Setting the office air-conditioning at about 22℃ has become standard practice across the world.
Numerous guidebooks across the world on heating, ventilation and air-conditioning claim office performance peaks at 22 degrees.
Many people indeed find relief from soaring summer temperatures in air-conditioned offices.
But recent studies have challenged the accepted wisdom that a cool office is more productive.
The reality is more complex.
Researchers conducted a review of all studies relating to air-conditioning and productivity.
They found that 22 degrees was probably a little chilly, even at the height of summer.
For a person dressed in typical summer clothing, an optimal range would be between 23 and 26 degrees.
And people can even tolerate temperatures beyond this comfort zone as long as they can adjust their clothing and expectations.
In fact, even on very hot days, it makes sense to turn the air-conditioning up.
People often chase just one optimum temperature, and this is understandable when people feel hot.
But there is a range of at least three to four degrees which does not have any adverse impact.
Another issue related to this is that people can become psychologically dependent on air conditioning.
If they're used to the environment which is air-conditioned, they tend to prefer lower temperatures.
But the studies found that almost all humans became accustomed to the new temperature.
It was only at the extreme ends of the temperature range where people's productivity suffered.
This range was above 26 degrees and below 19 degrees.
What is the accepted wisdom concerning the office environment?
What did researchers find from their review of all studies relating to air-conditioning and productivity?

Psychology research has tended to portray solitude as a negative experience.
Studies conducted in the 1970s and 1990s suggested that people felt less happy when alone as compared to being with others.
However, a new paper shows an alternative view of solitude, one in which solitude can be positive.
Let's start by looking at the earlier research.
It had a couple of shortcomings.
First, it measured emotion on a scale from positive to negative, overlooking the possibility that our positive and negative emotions can fluctuate independently.
Also, it categorized emotions as simply positive or negative.
It didn't consider that emotions arouse us to different degrees, and that both positive and negative emotions can arouse us a lot or a little.
That is, whether positive or negative, emotions can be either high-arousal or low-arousal.
High-arousal emotions include excitement on the positive side or anger on the negative side, while low-arousal ones include feeling calm on the positive side or lonely on the negative.
This new research attempted to overcome these shortcomings.
Researchers began with a simple study.
They asked participants to spend 15 minutes sitting alone without engaging in any activity, and measured how this solitude influences their emotional state.
This experiment specifically aimed to determine the effect of solitude on high-arousal emotions.
It looked at positive emotions such as being excited or interested, and negative emotions including being scared or distressed.
The results were clear.
After 15 minutes of solitude, the participants showed reductions in both types of emotion.
A second study measured the effects of solitude on low-arousal emotions.
These included both positive and negative emotions, such as feeling calm, relaxed, sad or lonely.
That experiment found that all of these emotions were increased by time alone.
Thus it seems past depictions of solitude were wrong.
It doesn't have a simple emotional effect that can be characterized as good or bad.
Rather, it changes the intensity of our inner experience.
It amplifies quieter emotions, but it diminishes the intensity of stronger feelings.
It's worth clarifying that these findings relate to relatively brief periods of solitude.
This is distinct from prolonged loneliness.
Research has demonstrated that the latter is correlated with an assortment of negative physical and psychological effects.
How can people benefit from being alone?
The findings here suggest that people can use solitude to regulate their emotions.
Solitude can help us become quiet after excitement, calm after an angry episode, or simply feel at peace.
What is one of the criticisms directed at the early research on solitude?
What do we learn about the results of the new research?
What did the second experiment in the new research find about solitude?
In 1984, the World Chess Championship was called off abruptly, due to the withered frame of a player who was competing for the title.
He wasn't alone in experiencing the extreme physical effects of the game.
Elite players can reportedly burn up to an absurd 6,000 calories in one day.
Does that mean that thinking harder is a simple route to losing weight?
Well, when the body is at rest, we know that the brain uses up a startling 20%-25% of the body's overall energy.
This level of utilization actually makes the brain the most energy-expensive organ in the body, and yet it makes up only 2% of the body's weight overall.
So the more we put this organ to work, the more calories will burn?
Technically, the answer is yes, for cognitively difficult tasks.
What counts as a "difficult" mental task varies between individuals.
But generally, it could be described as something that the brain cannot solve easily using previously learned routines, or tasks that change the conditions continuously.
However, deep thinking will not burn off the calories gained from eating a sugary snack.
Because in relation to the brain's huge, overall energy usage, which is devoted to a multitude of tasks, the energy required just to think harder is actually comparatively tiny.
We are unconscious of most of what uses up the brain's energy.
A lot of that activity is unrelated to conscious activities like learning how to sing or play the guitar.
The brain is able to allocate blood and thus energy to particular regions that are being active at that point.
But the overall energy availability in the brain is thought to be constant.
So, while there might be significant increases in energy use at localized regions of the brain when we perform difficult cognitive tasks, when it comes to the whole brain's energy budget overall, these activities don't significantly alter it.
So, why did the chess champion grow too skinny to compete in his chess competition?
The general consensus is that it mostly comes down to stress and reduced food consumption, not mental exhaustion.
Keeping your body pumped up for action for long periods of time is very energy demanding.
If you can't eat as often or as much as you can or would normally — then you might lose weight.

" Tell me about yourself " may seem like an easy job interview question, but the open-ended nature of this question often leaves job seekers at a loss where to start.
This common question is actually a critical test of a job candidate's communication skills, so it's important not to give an unprepared response or mess it up.
" Tell me about yourself " is often the first question professional career coaches prepare people for when they give interview guidance.
It's the opportunity for the candidate to take control of the narrative and tell their story in a way that really matters to their audience.
It takes hard work and extensive preparation to answer this question well.
When a person goes to a job interview, their interviewer has presumably read their resume, so they don't need to repeat the information.
But that's what most people will do, as it's their instinct to recite things that are already on their resume.
It's important for job seekers to do their homework on two crucial aspects.
First, they are not just telling someone a fact about themselves.
They're telling a story, and stories take work to create.
Coming up with a good story means getting reflective about what made their career accomplishments something they're proud of and what strengths those accomplishments highlight.
Candidates shouldn't pick a broad general strength to elaborate on, such as "I'm smart. I work hard and I get things done."
To come up with multiple career accomplishments or examples for different interview questions, job seekers should talk with others, especially people who know them, partners, friends or co-workers who will bring up different stories than the ones they remember.
Secondly, candidates should know what's at stake for the company with this job opening.
What they really are asking you is "tell me why you are going to help me."
If the person is a prepared candidate, they should have already figured out those things.
They've read the job description and researched the company on the Internet.
What job applicants ought to be looking for is what the company is up to, what they are trying to accomplish and what is preventing them from accomplishing those things.
How long should it take to answer?
Around a minute.
That's about right for most people's attention spans.
Under a minute could seem rushed, while over two minutes, will start to feel more like a speech.
But the length of the answer is not an exact science, and candidates need to keep their career story focused and tailored to their audience.
What does the speaker say about the job interview question " tell me about yourself "?
What will most people do when they come to a job interview?
Why should job seekers talk with partners, friends and co-workers?
What other important preparations should job seekers make before an interview?

sections.title: Part 1 Writing 写作
sections.passage:
1 Chinese students have a reputation for faring pretty well in tests but showing poor performance in other dimensions, especially communication skills. 2 And our society in general tends to brush off this issue as "not so important." 3 In view of this, I feel obliged to bring forward a few points to highlight the necessity of cultivating students effective communication skills.
1 As opposed to the widely shared concern among parents that too much communication distracts students from their supposed focus on study, communication is in fact an essential booster of students' learning capabilities. 2 Through effective communication, not only are students academic questions spotted and solved faster, but troubles they encounter in their teenage life get acknowledged and addressed more straightforwardly and humanely. 3 Another reason we should encourage students to develop communication skills is that a healthy relationship requires healthy forms of communication. 4 Only by constantly engaging ourselves in honest communication can we sustain harmonious relationships with others.
1 Implementing the ideas discussed above into our education system takes time and patience. 2 But the first thing we can and must do is to acknowledge our current neglect of this issue and pay due attention to it.

sections.passage: 1 With a total length of 55 kilometers, the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge is an unusual engineering feat of China. 2 Connecting the three cities, the bridge is the longest sea-crossing bridge and tunnel system in the world, which shortens the travel time between the three cities from 3 hours to 30 minutes. 3 This huge-span reinforced concrete bridge makes it abundantly clear that China has the ability to build record-breaking huge constructions. 4 It will boost regional integration and economic growth. 5 The bridge is the key to China's development of its own master plan for the Great Bay Area. 6 China hopes to make the bay area comparable to the bay areas of San Francisco, New York and Tokyo in terms of technological innovation and economic prosperity.

questions.answer: 1 With a total length of 55 kilometers, the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge is an unusual engineering feat of China. 2 Connecting the three cities, the bridge is the longest sea-crossing bridge and tunnel system in the world, which shortens the travel time between the three cities from 3 hours to 30 minutes. 3 This huge-span reinforced concrete bridge makes it abundantly clear that China has the ability to build record-breaking huge constructions. 4 It will boost regional integration and economic growth. 5 The bridge is the key to China's development of its own master plan for the Great Bay Area. 6 China hopes to make the bay area comparable to the bay areas of San Francisco, New York and Tokyo in terms of technological innovation and economic prosperity.

questions.explanation:
【确定词性】

空格词位于are experiencing(谓语)和rates之间,应为rates的修饰限定成分,可能是形容词、名词、-ed分词或-ing分词。

【锁定答案】

空格句指出,旧金山酒店正在经历70%~80%的____率。结合上文“疫情暴发浇灭了美国人的旅行愿望”“美铁订票量下降/退票量上升”可知,空格句应意在说明“旅游业萧条导致酒店经营惨淡”,再结合70 and 80 percent这一较高占比可知空格词应传递“空房/退订/下滑/亏损"等负面语义,故N正确。

【确定词性】

空格词位于this之后,应为单数名词形式。

【锁定答案】

空格句指出,大学正在清校,开始尝试此前从未尝试过的____在线学习。由上下文“人际互动活动彻底崩溃”“员工居家办公”可知,空格句意在说明疫情使大学被迫清空校园,全面开启在线学习,"on this___" 应凸显线上学习“规模之大/范围之广/参与人数之多”等,故空格词应表示“范围/规模/程度”等意,故I选项正确。

【解题思路】

从程度词、绝对化表达体味作者的情感态度,寻找解题突破口。首句多个程度词和绝对化表达(Virtually every, total meltdown,erases)奠定总体基调,传递作者态度:人际互动彻底崩溃,疫情影响广泛而深远。②3句以百分比数据(50 percent,300 percent,70 and 80 percent),④句以形象化表达(goes dark，emptying their campuses)进一步论证首句主旨“疫情全面阻断线下交流”,可推知have never tried online learning on this____ 应传递“线下学习彻底崩溃,线上学习以前所未有之势全面开启”之意。

【确定词性】

空格前为定冠词the,后为名词future,可推知空格词为future的修饰限定成分,可能为形容词、名词、-ed分词或-ing分词。

【答案解析】

空格句指出,白领公司要求员工在____未来居家办公。可见,"for the ____  future"限定居家办公的持续时间,结合上文“新冠病毒肆虐,人际互动崩塌”可知,在疫情影响下,“居家办公”这一新型工作模式会在未来一段时间内一直持续,空格词应传递出这种可预见性、可预估性。for the foreseeable future为固定搭配,表示“(在)可预见的将来”,结合语境即“在受疫情影响的未来一段时间内",故F正确。

【确定词性】

____economies与take lives,destroy routines为并列关系,且都由助动词will辖域,空格词应为动词原形.

【答案解析】

空格句指出,这场大流行病会夺去生命、____、 经济、坏破日常生活,但它终将过去。可见,“____经济”应与“夺去生命”“坏破生活”为并列关系,空格词应指向对经济的“抑制/破坏/阻碍”等作用,J正确。

【确定词性】

空格词前为名词所有格technologists',空格后为介词短语to the contrary 做technologists' _____ 的后置定语,可推知空格词为这些限定成分的中心词(名词或动名词)。

【答案解析】

空格句指出,迄今为止,没有哪项分散性的技术削弱了人们握手的欲望,尽管技术专家们的____ 与之相反。"de-(否定词缀)+centralizing(集中的)”暗示这些技术的设计初衷/理念应该是使人们分散化(降低人们面对面交流/握手的欲望),故让步状语despite technologists’ ____ to the contrary 应指向技术专家与前述事实“分散性技术未能让人们停止握手”相反的看法/观点/预测等,G正确。

H) preference具有一定干扰性,填入句中看似能够形成human desire与technologists' preference的对比(despite/to the contrary),但是句内对比双方实为“技术专家的____ ”与“分散技术并未降低人们握手的欲望这一现实情况”,即存在理想与现实之间的差异,

【确定词性】

Small __31__ 在句子中作主语,动词原形create充当谓语,故空__31__应为名词复数。

【答案解析】

第四段②句指出,小的__31__ 带来小的社会转变;大的__31__ (ones回指空31)则导致永久性改变。③句指出,纽约交通系统大罢工__32__ 促进长远变革。④句则具体介绍了1918年西班牙大流感对欧洲各国医疗保健系统发展的巨大促进作用。可见,③④句意在以“纽约交通系统大罢工、西班牙大流感”为例说明②句后半句“大的 __31__ 则导致永久性改变”这一观点,空31应传递“社会重大危机/问题/破坏”等含义,D正确。

【解题技巧】

句间逻辑可成为解题关键:本段②句与③④句为"观点一事例”关系,而观点所述事物之间的关联应与事例所述事物之间的关联一致,观点中的论述对象与事例中的论述对象应为上下义关联,即空32应与create,change、prompted语义指向一致,说明某物对另一事物的“促进/改变/导致”作用;空31应与The NewYork transit strike.The Spanish flu pandemic指向一致,并为两者的上义词,体现“社会危机/问题/破坏”等。

【确定词性】

空32位于is和with promoting sth之间,有以下可能:

1.is为系动词,空32为形容词或名词,构成系表结构;

2. is为助动词,空32为-ed分词,构成被动语态;

3. is为助动词,空32为-ing分词,构成现在进行时。

【答案解析】

4段③句指出,纽约交通系统大罢工__32__ 促进长远变革。④句则具体介绍了1918年西班牙大流感对欧洲各国医疗保健系统发展的巨大促进作用。可见,③④句意在以“纽约交通系统大罢工、西班牙大流感”为例说明②句后半句“大的__31__ 则导致永久性改变”这一观点，而is __32__ with应体现“交通大罢工”与“促进长远变革”之间的关系,结合上文观点“破坏导致社会变革”可知,“交通大罢工”为“因”,“促进长远变革”为“果”,故is with应体现因果逻辑, B符合文意,Abe credited with B表示“把B归功于A"

【解题技巧】

句间逻辑可成为解题关键:本段②句与③④句为"观点一事例”关系,而观点所述事物之间的关联应与事例所述事物之间的关联一致,观点中的论述对象与事例中的论述对象应为上下义关联,即空32应与create,change、prompted语义指向一致,说明某物对另一事物的“促进/改变/导致”作用;空31应与The NewYork transit strike.The Spanish flu pandemic指向一致,并为两者的上义词,体现“社会危机/问题/破坏”等。

【确定词性】

空33作介词of的宾语,与其共同修饰限定question,应为名词或动名词。

【答案解析】

第五段首句指出,“疫情过后会发生什么,疫情过后还能不能恢复到过去那样(this所指代内容)”甚至可能不是一个 __33__ 问题。②③句则并列指出,不确定邮轮业会(不会) __34__ ,也不确定公共交通会)不会破产。②⑤句对“邮轮业是否幸存,公共交通是否破产”的探讨实际意在说明①句“疫情后的变化(还能不能回到过去)"不是由人们的主观意愿决定,而是客观实际所向,这不是一道选择题,空33应传递“取舍/偏好/意愿”等意, H正确。

【解题技巧】

解答空33的关键在于了解this的所指。由空33所在句主干this might not even be aquestion初步推断this指向某问题/议题,追溯上文可发现其指向第二段what happens after the coronavirus(新冠疫情过后会发生什么),结合第三、四段的探讨可知这一问题实际指向的是“疫情后到底能不能回到过去”。第三段让步指出“在某些方面是能恢复到过去的”,但第四、五段紧而转折指出“无法回到过去,基础设施、公共交通、旅游业等能不能存活都难说,遑论恢复”,由此可知,“能否恢复如初”不是“想不想”的问题,而是“能不能”的问题，且句群整体透露出“不能”之意。

【确定词性】

空34位于主语从句中will之后，应为动词原形。

【答案解析】

第五段首句指出,“疫情过后会发生什么,疫情过后还能不能恢复到过去那样(this所指代内容)”甚至可能不是一个 __33__ 问题。②③句则并列指出,不确定邮轮业会(不会) __34__ ,也不确定公共交通会)不会破产。并列连词Or提示②③句应传递相似语义,故空34应传递“衰败/消失/存活”等意,M正确。

【确定词性】

____ assistance作介词without的宾语,空格词应为assistance的修饰限定成分,可能是形容词、名词、-ed分词或-ing分词。

【答案解析】

空格句指出,(目前尚不清楚)没有____援助,公共交通会不会破产。空格下句指出,基础设施无法就位来做2019年能做的事。结合常识“公共交通、基础设施均隶属国家/政府机构,主要仰仗政府财政补贴”推测空格词应表“国家/政府/联邦”等意,E正确。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Our world is full of — mostly untold — stories of slow hope, driven by the idea that change is possible. 2 They are ' slow ' in their unfolding, and they are slow because they come with setbacks.?
1 At the beginning of time — so goes the myth — humans suffered, shivering in the cold and dark until the titan (巨人) Prometheus stole fire from the gods. 2 Just as in the myth, technology — first fire and stone tools, and later farming, the steam engine and industry, fossil. fuels, chemicals and nuclear power — has allowed us to alter and control the natural world. 3 The myth also reminds us that these advances have come at a price: as a punishment for Prometheus' crime, the gods created Pandora, and they gave her a box filled with evils and curses. 4 When Pandora's box was opened, it unleashed swarms of diseases and disasters upon humankind?
1 Today we can no longer ignore the ecological curses that we have released in our search for warmth and comfort. 2 In engineering and exploiting and transforming our habitat, we have opened tens of thousands of Pandora's boxes. 3 In recent decades, environmental threats have expanded beyond regional boundaries to have global reach and, most hauntingly, are multiplying at a dizzying rate. 4 On a regular basis, we are reminded that we are running out of time. 5 Year after year faster and faster, consumption outpaces the biological capacity of our planet. 6 Stories of accelerated catastrophe multiply. 7 We fear the breakdown of the electric grid, the end of non-renewable resources, the expansion of deserts, the loss of islands, and the pollution of our air and water.?
1 Acceleration is the signature of our time. 2 Populations and economic activity grew slowly for much of human history. 3 For thousands of years and well into early modern times, world economies saw no growth at all, but from around the mid-19th century and again, in particular, since the mid-20th, the real GDP has increased at an enormous speed, and so has human consumption. 4 In the Middle Ages, households in Central Europe might have owned fewer than 30 objects on average; in 1900, this number had increased to 400, and in 2020 to 15,000. 5 The acceleration of human production, consumption and travel has changed the animate and inanimate spheres. 6 It has echoed through natural processes on which humans depend. 7 Species extinction, deforestation, damming of rivers, occurrence of floods, the depletion of ozone, the degradation of ocean systems and many other areas are all experiencing acceleration. 8 If represented graphically, the curve for all these changes looks rather like that well-known hockey stick: with little change over millennia (数千年) and a dramatic upswing over the past decades.?
1 Some of today's narratives about the future seem to suggest that we too, like Prometheus, will be saved by a new Hercules, a divine engineer, someone who will mastermind, manoeuvre and manipulate our planet.? 2 They suggest that geoengineering, cold fusion or faster-than-light spaceships might transcend once and for all the terrestrial constraints of rising temperatures, lack of energy, scarcity of food, lack of space, mountains of waste, polluted water — you name it.
1 Yet, if we envisage our salvation to come from a deus ex machina (解围之神), from a divine engineer or a tech solutionist who will miraculously conjure up a new source of energy or another cure-all with revolutionary potency, we might be looking in the wrong place. 2 The fact that we now imagine our planet as a whole does not mean that the ' rescue' of our planet will come with one big global stroke of genius and technology. 3 It will more likely come by many small acts. 4 Global heating and environmental degradation are not technological problems. 5 They are highly political issues that are informed by powerful interests. 6 Moreover, if history is a guide, then we can assume that any major transformations will once again be followed by a huge set of unintended consequences. 7 So what do we do??
1 This much is clear: we need to find ways that help us flatten the hockey-stick curves that reflect our ever-faster pace of ecological destruction and social acceleration. 2 If we acknowledge that human manipulation of the Earth has been a destructive force, we can also imagine that human endeavours can help us build a less destructive world in the centuries to come. 3 We might keep making mistakes. 4 But we will also keep learning from our mistakes.?
1 To counter the fears of disaster, we need to identify stories, visions and actions that work quietly towards a more hopeful future. 2 Instead of one big narrative, a story of unexpected rescue by a larger-than-life hero, we need multiple stories: we need stories, not only of what Rob Nixon of Princeton University has called the slow 'violence' of environmental degradation (that is, the damage that is often invisible at first and develops slowly and gradually), but also stories of what I call ‘slow hope'.
1 We need an acknowledgement of our present ecological plight but also a language of positive change, visions of a better future. 2 In The Principle of Hope (1954-1959), Ernst Bloch, one of the leading philosophers of the future, wrote that 'the most tragic form of loss...is the loss of the capacity to imagine that things could be different'. 3 We need to identify visions and paths that will help us imagine a different, more just and more ecological world. 4 Hope, for Bloch, has its starting point in fear, in uncertainty, and in crisis: it is a creative force that goes hand in hand with utopian (乌托邦的) "wishful images'.? 5 It can be found in cultural products of the past — in fairy tales, in fiction, in architecture, in music, in the movies — in products of the human mind that contain ' the outlines of a better world'. 6 What makes us 'authentic' as humans are visions of our 'potential'. 7 In other words: living in hope makes us human.?
1 The power of small, grassroots movements to make changes that spread beyond their place of origin can be seen with the Slow Food movement, which began in Italy in the 1980s. 2 The rise of fast-food restaurants after the Second World War produced a society full of cheap, industrially made foodstuffs. 3 Under the leadership of Carlo Petrini, the Slow Food movement began in Piedmont, a region of Italy with a long history of poverty, violence and resistance to oppression. 4 The movement transformed it into a region hospitable to traditional food cultures — based on native plants and breeds of animals. 5 Today, Slow Food operates in more than 160 countries, poor and rich. 6 It has given rise to thousands of projects around the globe, representing democratic politics, food sovereignty, biodiversity and sustainable agriculture.
1 The unscrupulous (无所顾忌的) commodification of food and the destruction of foodstuffs will continue to devastate soils, livelihoods and ecologies. 2 Slow Food cannot undo the irresistible developments of the global food economy, but it can upset its theorists, it can speak differently and it can allow people and their local food traditions and environments to flourish. 3 Even in the United States-the fast-food nation-small farms and urban gardens are on the rise. 4 The US Department of Agriculture provides an Urban Agriculture Toolkit and, according to a recent report, American millennials (千禧一代) are changing their diets. 5 In 2017, 6 percent of US consumers claimed to be strictly vegetarian, up from 1 percent in 2014. 6 As more people realise that ' eating is an agricultural act ', as the US poet and environmental activist Wendell Berry put it in 1989, slow hope advances.?

questions.explanation:
【题干翻译】

如今,有些人似乎幻想着能有一项尖端新技术将他们从当前的生态灾难中拯救出来。


【题目解析】

36题a cutting-edge new technology可以看作E段②句geoengineering, cold fusion or fasterthan-light spaceships的上义词。E段介绍当下某些人的技术(工程师)拯救论“地球工程、超光速飞船等技术能拯救人类,助其摆脱全球变暖、能源紧缺等种种问题”。试题是对该段内容的同义概述,其中ecological disaster是对rising temperatures, mountains of waste, polluted water等生态问题的高度概括。


【段落分析】

E段介绍某种大跃进式的设想“借助某项神奇技术迅速拯救生态”, today's narratives about the future承接上段our time,预示由当下过渡到对未来的展望。saved by a new Hercules, a divine engineer,transcendonce and for all,you name it凸显人们对技术的盲目崇拜“认为其具有神灵般的巨大力量,可快速解决所有问题”。全段核心信息:人们对未来的展望/技术拯救论:当前生态灾难有望被某项神奇技术拯救。本段所述某些人的设想“我们会被一位从天而降的工程师拯救,他将带领我们解决各种生态问题；地球工程、冷聚变或超光速宇宙飞船等技术可以帮助人们摆脱各种生态问题”的语义指向“借助某神奇工程师(即高精尖技术)的力量来拯救人类生态”匹配36题核心义。

【题干翻译】

根据一位伟大的思想家的观点,如果我们丧失了设想不同可能性的能力,那是极为不幸的。


【答案解析】

37题one great thinker对应②句Ernst Bloch, one of the leading philosophers of the future; the ability to think differently同义改写②句the capacity to imagine that things could be different. 

I段2句指出,未来哲学的领军人物之一布洛赫在《希望的原理》中写道,“最可悲的一种损失……莫过于想象未来存在不同可能性的能力的丧失”。试题是对此的同义转述。其中According toone great thinker是对句中Ernst Bloch, one of the leading philosophers of the future, wrote的同义改写。


【段落分析】

I段明确“希望”之于人类(应对生态困境)的重要性。

①句运用与上段末句相似的结构(We need [notonly] A but also B) ,明确“慢暴力”故事、“慢希望”故事的具体指向:承认当前生态困境,积极改变并对未来怀揣美好憧憬。

②至末句分别借助Ernst Bloch. .. wrote与for Bloch所提示的“人物观点”, the loss of thecapacity to imagine. .. different与We need to identify... help us imagine a different. ..所提示的“设想不同可能性的能力:因缺乏这种能力而需努力去寻找相关的故事或途径来帮助我们设想”以及Hope, It(指代hope)、potential, hope复现所体现的语义场“希望”表明本句群意在借专家Bloch的观点说明“设想不同可能性的能力的重要性”以及“希望之于人之为人的重要性:怀揣美好梦想是人性”,其中goes hand in hand,can be found in表明希望与幻想、故事、憧憬等一切人类思想的产物密切相关。全段核心信息:

  (1)人类最大的不幸:失去想象未来存在不同可能性的能力; 

  (2)憧憬未来/怀揣美好希望对人类的重要性:是人的本性

②句“未来哲学的领军人物之一恩斯特·布洛赫在《希望的原理》中写道,"最可悲的一种损失……莫过于想象未来存在不同可能性的能力的丧失”与37题核心义匹配。

【题干翻译】

应当迫切关注我们在追求舒适生活的过程中造成的生态问题


【答案解析】

38题Urgent attention,our pursuit of a comfortable life分别对应D句can no longer ignore search for...comfort.

C段①句指出“不能再忽视我们在追求温暖和舒适过程中引发的生态问题”。试题同义转述该句,其中the ecological problems we have created是对the ecological curses that we have released这一比喻性表达的具象化解释(由上文B段内容可知curses即技术这个潘多拉之盒里装着的灾难)。


【段落分析】

C段以现实情况“生态灾难正加速暴发”说明人类不能再忽视技术进步带来的生态代价。ecological curses承接上段末的神话情节,明确代价所在,即技术既赋予人类改造自然的能力,也使人类受其反噬、遭遇生态灾难。can no longer ignore,beyond regional boundaries, at a dizzying rate. .. faster and faster. .. accelerated从普遍性与紧迫性两方面说明人类应加紧应对生态灾难“灾难不仅波及世界各国,而且正加速暴发”。

全段核心信息:

(1)人类不能再忽视自己在追求舒适和温���过程中造成的生态灾难;

(2)人类生态灾难加速暴发。

【题干翻译】

即使在美国这个快餐国家,素食主义者的人数也在上涨。


【答案解析】

39题the fast-food nation America对应③句the United States-the fast-food nation,vegetarians 现于⑤句。K段③句以同位语的形式明确“美国”即是“快餐国家",随后⑤句指出,2017年6%的美国消费者称自己是严格的素食主义者,而2014年这一比例仅为1%。可知,试题是对上述两条信息的合理概括,其中the number.. is on the rise是对⑤句6 per cent... up from 1 per cent的概述性表达。③⑤两句信息“在美国这一快餐国家,声称自己是严格的素食者的消费者从2014年的1%涨到了2017年的6%”，匹配39题核心义。


【段落分析】

K段明确“慢餐”运动的意义,并列举更多类似的事例以升华主题:慢希望在前进。

①②句以The unscrupulous commodification of food and the destruction of foodstuffs与the irresistible developments of the global food economy的互指、cannot undo与but. ..can upset...can "speak differently'...can allow...的对比明确“慢餐”运动的意义:虽无力阻止粮食商业化、食品原料破坏行为带来的生态恶化,但可传递不同声音,可对人们的生计、特色食物文化、生态环境有利。

③④⑤句以Even in the United States引出美国这一快餐国家的变化,借small farms ,urban gardens、changing their diets,consumers claimed to be strictly vegetarian指出具体变化:小型农场、城市园林及素食者增多。

⑥句以As more people realise that... slow hope advances终结全文,升华指出:只要人们意识到自身行为的生态影响进而做出改变,生态逐渐向好的慢希望故事就可继续前进。

全段核心信息:

(1)慢餐运动的积极意义;

(2)美国小型农场、城市园林、素食者增多;

(3)慢希望在前进。

【题干翻译】

由于人类生产和消耗急剧增加,生态系统正在加速恶化。


【答案解析】

40题the dramatic increase of human production and consumption对应⑤句The accelerationof human production, consumption.

D段⑤至⑧句指出人类生产和消耗急剧加速的后果“改变了生物界和非生物界,在整个自然界引发反响,使得各种灾难沿着同样的曲线加速暴发”。试题是对此句群的合理概括,其中 deterioration of the ecological system概括包括Species extinction, deforestation, the degradation of ocean systems在内的种种现象, because of正确解读changed,echoed蕴含的因果关联。


【段落分析】

D段揭示生态灾难加速暴发的原因“(技术进步引发的)人类生产和消耗的加速"。

①句signature of ourtime承接上段末,将“加速”上升至当今时代大趋势,暗示生态灾难加速并非孤立现象,而是与其他方面的加速密切相关。

②至④句"grew slowly for much of human history. .. For thousands of years. .. no growth vs from... mid-19th century... increased at an enormous speed"及"In the Middle Ages... 30 vs in 1900... 400 vs in 2020... 15,000"以生产及消耗的长期停滞凸显其近一两百年加速之迅猛。

⑤至⑧句changed,echoed. ..allexperiencing. .. looks rather like先指出生产消耗加速与生态灾难加速的因果关联,再借两种趋势的同步性加以证实。

全段核心信息:

(1)加速是我们这个时代的特征;

(2)在人类历史的大部分时间里,人口和经济活动增长缓慢;

(3)人类生产和消耗的加速使得人类生态灾难加速暴发。

【题干翻译】

许多人相信改变世界是有可能的，尽管这或许要花费一些时间，遇到一些挫折。


【答案解析】

41.【定位】由题于中的solutions must be found 和social acceleration定位到 G)段第一句。【精析】同义转述题。定位句提到,这一点很清楚，我们需要找到一些方法来帮助我们拉平那个反映出我们日益加快的生态破坏和社会加速步伐的曲棍球棒曲线。题干中的obvious和定位句中的clear是同义词，题干中的curb the fast worseningenvironment and social acceleration 是对定位句中 flatten the hockeystick curves that reflect ourever-faster pace of ecological destruction andsocia acceleration 的同义转述，故答案为 G)。
【题干翻译】

【题干翻译】

指望用某项神奇的技术就能一举拯救我们的世界,这样想可能是错误的。


【答案解析】

43题be saved at one stroke对应②句"rescue'. .. will come with one... stroke; miraculoustechnology分别现于①句及②句。

F段①②句指出技术(专家/工程师)拯救论不切实际“不能指望科学家去创造技术奇迹来拯救我们,单凭天才和技术设计出的一个宏大计划难以拯救我们的星球”。试题是对上述观点的合理概括,其中It might be wrong to expect对应if we envisage. .. we might be looking in the wrong place.


【段落分析】

F段反驳上段设想,提出应“通过大量微小行动渐渐拯救生态(即不可一蹴而就,而应缓慢迁回前进)"。Yet提示段间语义转折。

①至③句借we might be looking in the wrong place、does not meanthat... come with A、It will more likely come by B明确观点“指望大型技术来一举拯救生态不太实际,多采取微小行动更加可行”。

④至⑥句借Moreover构成并列,分别从生态问题的本质(多方权力的调节制衡)和大型变革的缺陷(引发意外的后果)两方面进一步说明为何应依靠微小行动的积累。0句what do we do设问引出下文具体建议。

全段核心信息:

(1)技术拯救论不切实际;

(2)应靠微小行动来拯救生态;

(3)生态问题关乎政治,不是简单的技术问题;

(4)重大变革都会引发意外(不良)后果。

【题干翻译】

怀有对一个更美好的世界的向往是人之本性。


【答案解析】

44题human nature契合I段⑥⑦句中What makes us 'authentic' as humans,makes us human所反映出的“人性”,hopes、a better world则分别现于⑦句和⑤句。I段⑤句先指出“人类心灵产物中蕴藏着一个更美好的世界的轮廓",⑥⑦句随后指出"憧憬自身潜力、生活在希望中,这些使得我们人得以成为人”,可见,三句意在说明“怀揣对美好世界的向往是人之本性”,试题是对此三句的合理归纳与概括。


【段落分析】

I段明确“希望”之于人类(应对生态困境)的重要性。

①句运用与上段末句相似的结构(We need [notonly] A but also B) ,明确“慢暴力”故事、“慢希望”故事的具体指向:承认当前生态困境,积极改变并对未来怀揣美好憧憬。

②至末句分别借助Ernst Bloch. .. wrote与for Bloch所提示的“人物观点”, the loss of thecapacity to imagine. .. different与We need to identify... help us imagine a different. ..所提示的“设想不同可能性的能力:因缺乏这种能力而需努力去寻找相关的故事或途径来帮助我们设想”以及Hope, It(指代hope)、potential, hope复现所体现的语义场“希望”表明本句群意在借专家Bloch的观点说明“设想不同可能性的能力的重要性”以及“希望之于人之为人的重要性:怀揣美好梦想是人性”,其中goes hand in hand,can be found in表明希望与幻想、故事、憧憬等一切人类思想的产物密切相关。全段核心信息:

  (1)人类最大的不幸:失去想象未来存在不同可���性的能力; 

  (2)憧憬未来/怀揣美好希望对人类的重要性:是人的本性

⑤⑥⑦句“人类心灵产物中蕴藏着一个更美好世界的轮廓,对自身潜力有期待、生活在希望中才使人之为人”的语义焦点“人类怀揣对美好世界的向往是人之本性”与44题核心义匹配。

【题干翻译】

技术赋予人类改造自然界的力量,但我们为这种改造付出了代价。


【答案解析】

45题the power to change the natural world,a price for the change分别对应②句allowed us to alter... the natural world,③句 price.

B段②句指出技术的正面作用“让人类得以改造和控制自然界”,③句转而暗示其负面效果“使人类为此付出代价”。试题是对两句内容的归纳概括,其中the change契合③句中these advances的真实所指“技术带来的对自然界的改造和控制”。


【段落分析】

B段借神话传说揭示技术的两面性“使人类更加强大,也让其付出代价".①②句和③④句之间借these advances(回指alter and control the natural world)构成回指衔接。

①②句so goes the myth. ..Just as in themyth...以神话中“普罗米修斯从众神处盗取火种,使人类不再怕黑受冻”类比现实中技术使人类能力实现巨大飞跃，由被动适应自然转向主动改造自然。

③④句The myth also reminds us...以故事的后续情节“众神借潘多拉之盒的诅咒惩罚普罗米修斯及人类”暗示技术在赋予人类能力的同时也必将使其付出相应代价。

全段核心信息：

(1)技术进步赋予人类改造自然界的能力;

(2)人类要为技术进步付出相应代价。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 Vegetarians would prefer not to be compelled to eat meat. 2 Yet the reverse compulsion (强迫) is hidden in the proposals for a new plant-based "planetary diet." 3 Nowhere is this more visible than in India.?
1 Earlier this year, the EAT-Lancet Commission released its global report on nutrition and called for a global shift to a more plant-based diet and for "substantially reducing consumption of animal source foods." 2 In countries like India, that call could become a tool to aggravate an already tense political situation and stress already undernourished populations.?
1 The EAT report presumes that "traditional diets" in countries like India include little red meat which might be consumed only on special occasions or as minor ingredients in mixed dishes.
1 In India, however, there is a vast difference between what people would wish to consume and what they have to consume because of innumerable barriers around class, religion, culture, cost geography, etc. 2 Policymakers in India have traditionally pushed for a cereal-heavy "vegetarian diet' on a meat-eating population as a way of providing the cheapest sources of food.?
1 Currently, under an aggressive Hindu nationalist government, Muslims, Christians, disadvantaged classes and indigenous communities are being compelled to give up their traditional foods.
1 None of these concerns seem to have been appreciated by the EAT-Lancet Commission's representative, Brent Loken, who said "India has got such a great example" in sourcing protein from plants.
1 But how much of a model for the world is India's vegetarianism? 2 In the Global Hunger Index 2019, the country ranks 102nd out of 117. 3 Data from the National Family Health Survey indicate that only 10 percent of infants of 6 to 23 months are adequately fed.
1 Which is why calls for a plant-based diet modeled on India risk offering another whip with which to beat already vulnerable communities in developing countries.?
1 A diet directed at the affluent West fails to recognize that in low-income countries undernourished children are known to benefit from the consumption of milk and other animal source foods, improving cognitive functions, while reducing the prevalence of nutritional deficiencies as well as mortality.
1 EAT-Lancet claimed its intention was to "spark conversations" among all Indian stakeholders. 2 Yet vocal critics of the food processing industry and food fortification strategies have been left out of the debate. 3 But the most conspicuous omission may well be the absence of India's farmers.
1 The government, however, seems to have given the report a thumbs-up. 2 Rather than addressing chronic hunger and malnutrition through an improved access to wholesome and nutrient-dense foods, he government is opening the door for company-dependent solutions, ignoring the environmental and economic cost, which will destroy local food systems. 3 It's a model full of danger for future generations.?

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

   What is more visible in India than anywhere else according to the passage?

   根据文章所述,什么事情在印度比在其他国家更明显？

A. People's positive views on the proposals for a "planetary diet."

   人们对“行星饮食”倡议的积极看法。

B. People's reluctance to be compelled to eat plant-based food.

   人们不愿被迫食用植物性食品。

C.People's preferences for the kind of food they consume.

   人们对其摄入的食品种类的偏好。

D. People's unwillingness to give up their eating habits.

   人们不愿放弃自己的饮食习惯。


【定位及答案】

本题考查印度相比其他国家的突出之处。由题干关键信息more visible in India定位至首段末句。首段末句指出: 这一点(this)在印度最为明显。this回指前一句中the reversecompulsion,即与首句“强迫素食者吃肉”相反的“强迫肉食者吃素”。可见,印度的突出之处在于人们(概指食肉的人)不愿被迫吃素(即食用植物性食品),故B正确。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【无中生有】：文中未明确提及人们对“行星饮食”倡议的看法,只谈及作者的看法“有强迫人们吃素之意",A错误。

C选项【词汇干扰&答非所问】：利用首句中prefer一词设置干扰,但它的对象为“被他人强迫吃肉的行为”,并非“自己所摄入的食物种类";

D选项【偷换概念&答非所问】：利用首句中prefer not to be compelled to eat设置干扰,但它实指“不愿被迫改变自己的饮食习惯”,并不等于“主动放弃自己的饮食习惯”; C，D两项均非题干所问“印度的突出之处”(指向②句,而非用作引子的①句)。


【解题思路】

本题实际考查代词回指以及上下文关联,解题关键在于明确定位处this所指,难点是this所指为抽象表达the reverse compulsion。这时可先根据compulsion的“被迫”之意,将蕴含积极、主观意味的Apositive).C (preferences)两项排除;再回看首句Vegetarians. .. be compelled to eat meat"强迫素食者食肉”明确the reverse compulsion指代“强迫肉食者食素”,至此敲定正确项为B,并排除与“被迫改变”之意不符的D项。

choices.label: B
choices.text: Keep them further away from politics

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What would the EAT-Lancet Commission's report do to many people in countries like India? 

柳叶刀饮食委员会的报告会对印度这类国家的众多人群产生什么影响?

A. Radically change their dietary habits.

    彻底改变他们的饮食习惯。

B. Keep them further away from politics

    让他们更加远离政治。

C. Make them even more undernourished.

   使他们更加营养不良。

D. Substantially reduce their food choices.

    大幅减少他们的饮食选择。


【定位及答案】

本题考查EAT-Lancet委员会报告对印度等国的民众的影响。由题干关键词the EATLancet Commission's report定位至其首次出现的第二段。第二段①句介绍EAT-Lancet委员会报告所呼吁的内容,@句指出该呼吁对印度等国的影响:使本已紧张的政治局势恶化,给本就营养不良的人群加压。C符合后一影响,即加剧人们营养不良的问题。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【过度推理】：源自①句a global shift to a. .. diet,但却忽略其前called for(呼吁)所传递出的“意见,建议”之意,“饮食建议”未必能达成“彻底改变饮食习惯”的效果,故错误。

B选项【偷换概念】：将②句报告的影响“加剧本已紧张的政治局势”窜改为“让人们进一步远离政治"。

D选项【偷换概念】：利用D句substantially reducing. ..设置干扰,但该句实际在介绍报告内容“呼吁大幅减少动物源食品的摄取”,而非报告影响“将会大幅减少人们的饮食选择”。


【解题思路】

本题实际为广义的因果关联题,解题基本思路为“借助因果标识词寻找EAT-Lancet委员会可能产生的影响(果),比对选项确定答案”:第二段 句that call could become a tool to. ..标识“手段一结果”逻辑, EAT-Lancet委员会的号召为“手段", aggravate. .. political situation和stress. ..undernourishedpopulations为“结果”,将两大结果与选项比对很容易就可确定C为正确项。而干扰项往往利用文中个别词汇shift to a.. diet (A) 、political (B) ,substantially reducing. ..(D)捏造干扰。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What do we learn from the passage about food consumption in India? 

关于印度的饮食状况,我们从文中了解到什么？

A. People's diet will not change due to the EAT-Lancet report.

    人们的饮食不会因柳叶刀饮食报告而改变

B. Many people simply do not have access to foods they prefer. 

    许多人根本无法获得自己喜欢的食物,

C. There is a growing popularity of a cereal-heavy vegetarian diet. 

    以谷类为主的素食越来越受欢迎

D. Policymakers help remove the barriers to people's choice of food.

    政策制定者帮助人们消除选择食物的


【定位及答案】

本题考查印度的食物摄取状况。根据题干关键词food consumption in India及题目顺序定位至第四段(In India. .. they have to consume. ..)。第四段①句指出,由于受阶层、宗教、文化等差异的影响,人们想要食用的食物与不得不食用的食物存在巨大差别。可见,印度人根本没有办法按照自己意愿选择自己所喜欢的食物,故B正确。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【反向干扰】：与第五段“在印度教民族主义政府(支持EAT-Lancet报告)的领导下,其他教徒、弱势阶层及本地社群正被迫放弃传统食物”不符。

C选项【偷换概念】：由第四段②句“政策制定者历来向食肉人群推行以谷类为主的素食”臆断出“以谷类为主的素食越发受欢迎”,但谷类素食是政策制定者迫使(pushed for)人们食用的,与选项“受人喜爱(popularity)"所展现的主观意愿相悖。

D选项【东拼西凑】：由第四段barriers,Policymakers杂糅捏造干扰, 文中“政策制定者迫使肉食者吃素”实际在“阶层、宗教、文化等隔阂”之外进一步从政策角度增加了人们选择喜爱食物的障碍。


【解题思路】

本题针对第四段①句长难句设题。首先提取句子主干、明确句内逻辑: there is a vastdifference between X and Y because of Z,然后细看句内各部分内容:X=what people would wish to consume（人们想要吃的食物),Y=what they have to consume(人们不得不吃的食物),Z罗列原因。X和Y体现了“意愿”与“现实”的巨大反差,表明人们无法随心获得自己想要的食物,B正确。其余三项则体现人们的主观意愿:坚持不做饮食改变(A)、喜爱/接受素食(C)、毫无障碍地选择食物(D),均与文中人们的“被动处境”相悖。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What does the passage say about a plant-based diet modeled on India? 

关于效仿印度的植物性饮食,这篇文章说了什么？

A. It may benefit populations whose traditional diet is meat based.

    它可能有益于传统饮食以肉类为主的人群。

B. It may be another blow to the economy in developing countries.

    它可能会进一步打击发展中国家的经济。

C. It may help narrow the gap between the rich and poor countries.

    它可能有助于缩小富国与穷国之间的差距。

D. It may worsen the nourishment problem in low-income countries.

    它可能会使低收入国家的营养问题恶化。


【定位及答案】

本题考查“效仿印度的植物性饮食”相关信息,由关键词a plant-based diet modeled on India 初步定位至第七、八段(a model for the world is India's vegetarianism ,a plant-based diet modeled on India)第七段首句设问“印度素食主义的典范作用有多大?",②③句说明印度的饥饿问题与婴温饱问题严峻。第八段继而明确效仿印度植物性饮食的危害:进一步打击发展中国家本已脆弱的社会群体。综合可知,植物性饮食会使发展中国家的营养问题恶化,D正确。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【东拼西凑】：该选项杂糅traditional diets(第三段首句)、meat-eating population(第四段末句)、benefit(第九段首句)捏造干扰,但文中未提及“植物性饮食对传统饮食以肉类为主的人群的影响"。

B选项【偷换概念】：将第八段中“效仿印度植物性饮食可能进一步打击”的对象由“本已脆弱的社会群体”偷换为“国家经济"。

C选项【断章取义】：该选项对第九段A diet... theaffluent West. .. low-income countries... reducing断章取义: 将原文“针对富裕国家的植物性饮食不适合贫穷国家,贫穷国家可从牛奶和动物源食品中获益”曲解为“植物性饮食缩减贫困国家和富裕国家的差距”。


【解题思路】

统览选项"It may benefit/be another blow to/help/ worsen”,可知本题考查“效仿印度植物性膳食的潜在影响(果)",可借助“因果关系词(既包括显性标记because,as a result等,又包括隐性标记pushwith, as等)”找到答案信息,即“对谁的影响,什么样的潜在影响”。根据第八段a plant-based diet modeled orIndia risk offering another whip... to beat already vulnerable communities锁定影响对象“发展���国家本已脆弱的社会群体”及影响性质“负面(使之更脆弱)”。对比选项后发现,A与C指向积极影响,B针对发展中国家的经济,只有D正确。且Which is why... another whip中Which与another whip回指上段的“印度民众饥饿问题”,可进一步佐证B影响对象错误,D为正确答案

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

How does the Indian government respond to the EAT-Lancet Commission's proposals?

印度政府对柳叶刀饮食委员会的提议作何反应?

A. It accepts them at the expense of the long-term interests of its people.

    它以牺牲人民的长期利益为代价接受了它们。

B. It intends them to spark conversations among all Indian stakeholders.

    它想借它们来促成印度所有利益相关者之间的对话

C. It gives them approval regardless of opposition from nutrition experts.

    它不顾营养专家的反对批准了它们

D. It welcomes them as a tool to address chronic hunger and malnutrition.

    它将它们作为解决严重饥钱与营养不良的工具欣然接受了


【定位及答案】

本题考查印度政府对EAT-Lancet委员会提议的反应。由Indian government, the EATLancet Commission's proposals可定位至末段(The government. . the report,the government is. .. It's..)。末段先指出“印度政府似乎对EAT-Lancet委员会的提议赞赏有加”,后介绍这一态度的影响:政府对“依靠公司”的处理方案敞开了大门,忽视经济和环境成本,破坏当地食品系统,最终危害后代。可见,印度政府不顾提议对人民的深远危害而将其接受,A正确。


【错误选项分析】

B选项【偷换概念】：该选项将第十段中“借提议促成利益相关者的对话”的观点持有者由委员会本身偷换为印度政府。

C选项【无中生有&过度推理】：C选项中印度政府的态度"gives them approval"虽契合末段的"given the report a thumps-up",但增补了文中未提及的信息“不顾营养专家的反对". 

D选项【偷换概念】：该选项源自第二段末句a tool,却将可能性语气could become偷换为肯定性语气welcomes,同时将to aggravate. .. and stress...的贬义语义偷换为to address..的褒义语义,且由末段②句可知“印度政府并未致力于解决严重的饥饿与营养不良问题”。


【解题思路】

四个选项中政府的立场(accepts/intends/approval/welcomes)均契合末段①句“政府似乎对委员会的提议赞赏有加”,区别在于A关注其危害,B关注其目的,C关注其所受的反对,D关注其用途。因此,解题关键在于借助语法衔接、逻辑词、语义场、特殊句式等把握末段的语义重心。“强调影响”的取含结构Rather than addressing.., the government is opening the door for. .. (②)与“消极影响”的语义场ignoring the environmental and economic cost/destroy local food systems/full of danger for future generations (②③句)点名本段核心主题为“政府支持提议的深远危害”，故唯有A选项符合题意。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 Back in 1964, in his book Games People Play, psychiatrist Eric Berne described a pattern of conversation he called "Why Don't You —— Yes But ", which remains one of the most irritating aspects of everyday social life. 2 The person adopting the strategy is usually a chronic complainer. 3 Something is terrible about their relationship, job, or other situation, and they moan about it ceaselessly, but find some excuse to dismiss any solution that's proposed. 4 The reason, of course, is that on some level they don't want a solution; they want to be validated in their position that the world is out to get them. 5 If they can "win" the game —— dismissing every suggestion until their interlocutor (对话者) gives up in annoyance —— they get to feel pleasurably righteous (正当的) in their resentments and excused from any obligation to change.?
1 Part of the trouble here is the so-called responsibility / fault fallacy (谬误). 2 When you're feeling hard done by —— taken for granted by your partner, say, or obliged to work for a half-witted boss —— it's easy to become attached to the position that it's not your job to address the matter, and that doing so would be an admission of fault. 3 But there's a confusion here. 4 For example, if I were to discover a newborn at my front door, it wouldn't be my fault, but it most certainly would be my responsibility. 5 There would be choices to make, and no possibility of avoiding them, since trying to ignore the matter would be a choice. 6 The point is that what goes for, the baby on the doorstep is true in all cases: even if the other person is 100% in the wrong, there's nothing to be gained, long-term, from using this as a justification to evade responsibility.?
1 Should you find yourself on the receiving end of this kind of complaining, there's an ingenious way to shut it down —— which is to agree with it, ardently. 2 Psychotherapist Lori Gottlieb describes this as "over-validation".? 3 For one thing, you'll be spared further moaning, since the other person's motivation was to confirm her beliefs, and now you're confirming them. 4 But for another, as Gottliet notes, people confronted with over-validation often hear their complaints afresh and start arguing back. 5 The notion that they're utterly powerless suddenly seems unrealistic —— not to mention rather annoying —— so they're prompted instead to generate ideas about how they might change things.?
1 “And then, sometimes, something magical might happen," Gottlieb writes. 2 The other person "might realise she's not as trapped as you are saying she is, or as she feels." 3 Which illustrates the irony of the responsibility/fault fallacy: evading responsibility feels comfortable, but turns out to be a prison; whereas assuming responsibility feels unpleasant, but ends up being freeing.?

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What is characteristic of a chronic complainer, according to psychiatrist Eric Berne?

根据精神病学家埃里克·伯恩所述,惯性抱怨者的特征是什么?

A. They only feel angry about their ill treatment and resent whoever tries to help.

    他们只对自己所受的糟糕对待感到愤怒,而且怨恨每一个试图提供帮助的人。

B. They are chronically unhappy and ceaselessly find fault with people around them.

    他们总是不快乐,而且不停地对身边的人吹毛求疵。

C. They constantly dismiss others' proposals while taking no responsibility for tackling the problem.

    他们总是拒绝考虑别人的建议，不承担解决问题的责任。

D. They lack the knowledge and basic skills required for successful conversations with their interlocutors.

    他们缺乏与对话者成功交谈所需的知识和基本技能。


【定位及正确答案】

本题考查惯性抱怨者的特征,根据题干中人名Eric Berne以及关键词characteristic of achronic complainer定位至第一段②至⑤句(...a chronic complainer. ..).第一段②③句指出惯性抱怨者的行为特征:当人际关系、工作或其他方面出现糟糕的事情时,他们便会一边喋喋不休地抱怨,一边却又找借口拒绝别人提出来的任何解决方案。⑤句进一步指出他们的心理特征:自己的怨艾理所应当,没有任何责任/义务做出改变。故C正确,选项中dismiss others' proposals, taking no responsibility for tackling the problem同义替换原文dismiss any solution that's proposed,excused from any obligation to change.


【错误选项分析】

A选项【曲解文意】：A选项后半部分利用⑤句个别词汇their interlocutor, resentments杂糅设障,将文意“无视对话者针对其愤懑(resentments)提出来的建议”曲解为“怨恨(resent)对话者(试图帮助他们的人)".

B选项【偷换概念】：B选项后半部分将③句“找借口拒绝他人提出来的建议”偷换为“找他人的错误/挑他人的错误”. 

D选项【过度推理】：过度引申⑤句“他们拒绝每一个建议,直到对话者愤然放弃”,文中并未提及惯性抱怨者缺乏与对话者成功交谈所需的知识和基本技能。


【解题技巧】

本题考查惯性抱怨者的特征,纵观各选项发现多个选项属于X and/while Y型,即至少含有两个特征。而对“抱怨者”这种常规话题,命题人常会利用人们的常识捏造干扰,所以要避免受到常识的干扰,

choices.label: A
choices.text: People tend to think that one should not be held responsible for others' mistakes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is easy to become attached to the position of overlooking one's own fault.

choices.label: C
choices.text: People are often at a loss when confronted with a number of choices.

choices.label: D

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What does the author try to illustrate with the example of the newborn on one's doorstep?

作者试图用“家门口的新生儿”这个例子来说明什么？

A. People tend to think that one should not be held responsible for others' mistakes.

    人们往往认为自己不应为他人的错误买单。

B. It is easy to become attached to the position of overlooking one's own fault.

    人们容易陷入“忽视自己过错”的思维境地。

C. People are often at a loss when confronted with a number of choices.

    而临许多选择时人们往往会不知所措。

D. A distinction should be drawn between responsibility and fault

    责任与过错应当有所区分


【定位及正确答案】

本题考查事例的写作目的。由题干关键词the newborn on one's doorstep定位至第二段④⑤⑥句(if I were to discover a newborn. .. what goes for the baby on the doorstep. ..)第二段①②③句先引出新概念“责任/过错谬误”,即,将“责任”与“过错”混为一谈,④⑤⑥句再以“家门口的新生儿”为例指出“责任”与“过错”并不对等,以“过错并不在我”作为逃避责任的借口并不可取。可见“新生儿”的事例旨在解释“责任/过错谬误”这一概念,即“责任不等于过错/二者应当有所区分。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：A选项将“惯性抱怨者面对不当对待时的惯常心态(这不是我的错,我没有义务去解决问题)"偷换为作者的观点,而作者意在批驳这一观念。

B选项【偷换概念】：B选项将②句"it's easy to become attached to the position. .. tha tdoing so would be an admission of fault"及④句"it wouldn't be my fault"改写为“人们很容易忽视自己的过错",但文章实际指“人们容易曲解过错(将过错等同于责任)". 

C选项【曲解文意】：曲解⑤句"There would be choicesto make, and no possibility of avoiding them...",原文实际强调“人一定得做出选择”,而非“人不知如何做出选择”。


【解题思路】

本题考查写作目的(论据用意),关键在于找到论据所服务的论点,同时应警惕此类题型的常见干扰方式:摘取文中细枝末节;歪曲事例中具体细节;扭曲论点。解题步骤:

一、找到体现论据与论点关系的提示词,锁定论点所在(由For example向上寻找论点,发现明显观点句为Part of the trouble here is the socalled responsibility/fault fallacy, But there's a confusion here);

二、提炼论点大意,确定正确项(“惯性抱怨者的认知存在责任/过错谬误,,两个概念被混为一谈”,本着“论据为论点服务”的原则,可初步判定D项符合文意);

三、排除干扰项,A扭曲论点,B.C歪曲事例中具体细节,故均排除并确定答案为D.

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What does the author advise people to do to chronic complainers?

作者建议人们怎样对待惯性抱怨者?

A. Stop them from going further by agreeing with them.

    赞同他们,以阻止他们进一步抱怨

B. Listen to their complaints ardently and sympathetically.

    热心且满怀同情地倾听他们的抱怨。

C. Ask them to validate their beliefs with further evidence.

    要求他们用更多证据证实自己的看法。

D. Persuade them to clarify the confusion they have caused.

    劝说他们澄清自己造成的混淆。


【定位及答案】

本题考查作者就应对惯性抱怨者的建议,由advise... to do定位至第三段(there's an ingenious way to...)。第三段①②句指出,针对惯性抱怨者,使其停止抱怨的方法是对其抱怨表示赞同,可见A正确,Stop them from going further是对原文shut it down所含语义的明示。


【错误选项分析】

B选项【偷换概念】：该选项将①句中ardently的语义指向“很热情地、强烈地赞同抱怨者的抱怨”偷换为“热情地倾听其抱怨”。

C选项【偷换概念】：利用②句validation、③句confirm her beliefs/you're confirming them设障,但它们意在强调“听抱怨的人对抱怨者的看法表示认可、证实”,而非“抱怨者自己证实自己怨言的正确性”. 

D选项【东拼西凑】：利用④句arguingback(反驳)、⑤句prompted(激发)以及上段⑤句confusion杂糅捏造而���,但文意实为“抱怨者自身存在"混淆概念,的错误,而且对这种混淆他们并不自知,但是通过对话者对他们抱怨的高度认可,他们便能加以扭转”。


【解题思路】

本题考查作者建议,解题关键在于找到文中的建议表达。第三段首句there's ...way..提示本段围绕“建议/方法”展开,不定式to shut it down说明该方法的目的,指向“关闭/阻止抱怨”,故全段主要论述“阻止抱怨的方法”,破折号及which is再引出这一方法:对其表示赞同。至此可明确作者就应对惯性抢怨者提出的建议要点即为A项“赞同其抱怨→使其停止”。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What happens when chronic complainers receive over validation?

当惯性抱怨者受到过度认可时会发生什么？

A. They are motivated to find ingenious ways to persuade their interlocutor.

    他们被激励去寻找巧妙的方法来说服对话者。

B. They are prompted to come up with ideas for making possible changes.

    他们被鼓励去想办法以做出可能的改变

C. They are stimulated to make more complaints.

    他们受到刺激而发出更多抱怨

D. They are encouraged to start arguing back.

    他们受到鼓励而开始反驳。


【定位及答案】

本题考查惯性抱怨者被过度认可后的反应。由receive over-validation定位至第三段,第三段③句指出惯性抱怨者受到过度认可后的反应一：停止抱怨。④⑤句指出反应二：重新审视并反驳这种抱怨,并开始想办法改变现状。可见B正确,其中are prompted to come up with ideas对应⑤句they're prompted... to generate ideas; making possible changes对应how they might change things.


【错误选项分析】

A选项【东拼西凑】：该选项利用段中①句ingenious way、④句start arguing back杂糅捏造而来,将其曲解为抱怨者欲采取方法反驳并说服与自己观点不同的对话者,但arguing back实际指抱怨者推翻自己的旧有观点,ingenious way指向的是“过度认可”这一阻止抱怨者抱怨的巧妙办法。

C选项【反向干扰】：该选项与③句“你(对话者)将免于听到更多1抱怨/抱怨者不再抱怨”相悖。

D信息【东拼西凑】：该选项中start arguing back复现于④句, 但are encouraged to却曲解句中hear... afresh and所暗藏的语义“被刺激后(开始反驳)",两者并不完全等同,而且该反应并不指向惯性抱怨受到高度认可之后的最终反应。


【解题思路】

本题考查事实细节,纵观选项发现各项着力点在to do sth结构上,即解题时应将与原文比对的重点放在“找到巧妙的办法来说服对话者”“想办法做出可能的改变”“更多抱怨”“开始反驳”上。其中最有干扰性的是复现文中用词的D,看似正确,但仔细比对发现该选项并非惯性抱怨者在受到高度认可之后的终极反应,而是其多个反应(开始反驳,进而意识到自己并没有那么惨,从而开始想办法改变)中的一个,不具有高度,且真题对正确项的表述原则通常是对原文进行同义改写，而不可能是原词复现。

choices.label: B
choices.text: Avoiding hazardous traps in everyday social life.

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

How can one stop being a chronic complainer according to the author? 

根据作者所言,如何才能不再做惯性抱怨者？

A. Analysing the so-called responsibility/fault fallacy.

    分析所谓的责任/过错谬误。

B. Avoiding hazardous traps in everyday social life.

    避免日常社交生活中的危险困境。

C. Assuming responsibility to free oneself.

    承担责任以解脱自我。

D. Awaiting something magical to happen.

    等待神奇之事的发生。


【定位及答案】

本题考查摆脱习惯性抱怨的方法,根据各选项关键词“责任/过错谬误”“困境"“神奇之事”以及试题命制顺序原则可定位至末段。末段首两句先承上继续说明过度认可给惯性抱怨者带来的认知改变:他们并非深陷困境、除了抱怨外无计可施,而是具备主动权、有能力改变现状。末句随后揭示这一转变的启示:只有承担责任才能获得自由、解脱自我。可见C正确,其中Assuming responsibility to free oneself概括assumingresponsibility feels unpleasant, but ends up being freeing暗含的应有做法。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【答非所问】：该选项利用文中关键概念responsibility/fault fallacy干扰,但分析这一谬误的作用在于解释“惯性抱怨”这一行为背后的认知错误,而非摆脱它的方式。

B选项【偷换概念】：利用末段②句not... trapped干扰,但原文指“抱怨者并非像他们所感觉的那样深陷困境”,强调的是避免错误认知/感觉,而非生活中的危险困境。

D选项【断章取义】：对末段①句something magical might happen断章取义,但它指向的是对话者对惯性抱怨者表达过度认可后引发的正向积极反应,而非针对惯性抱怨者的建议。


【解题思路】

本文看似考查事实细节,实则考查段落/全文主旨。题干中并无明显的定位信息,此时可结合题目顺序(最后一题)、全文行文脉络(提出问题一提出解决方案)及选项关键词(“责任/过错谬误”“困境”“神奇之事”均在末段提及)定位至末段。解题时应注意,51,53.54题已针对“惯性抱怨者的特征、对待方法、被过变认可后的反应”命制了事实细节题,因此本题很可能不再囿于具体的实际操作,而是意在考查更深层次的观念/启发,应更具概括性。纵观各选项,只有C涉及摆脱惯性抱怨的观念认识,且符合文中表述;其余各项利用个别字词干扰,不但固于具体操作,而且存在事实性错误。

1 In a time of constant change and stiff competition, challenges are everywhere, ranging from taking a test to seeking a job. 2 Therefore, it is especially important for us students to cultivate the ability to meet challenges.
1 When running into daunting challenges, many of us will almost instinctively shy away from them, reluctant or frightened to step out of our comfort zone. 2 This passive approach could easily hinder us from making progress. 3 On the contrary, if we pluck up the courage to challenge ourselves, we may reap the rewards even of failure. 4 As German philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche said, "what doesn't kill me makes me stronger." 5 Confronting challenges and striving to navigate through them help us build resilience and mental strength. 6 This will in turn lay a solid foundation for our success in the future, because the ability to take on challenges is a prerequisite for realizing our full potential and achieving significant breakthroughs.
1 Life is not all plain sailing but full of hardships and obstacles. 2 We have no other choice than to equip ourselves with the determination and ability to meet and overcome challenges.
