questions.explanation:
【确定词性】

空格所在部分It has been _____ by fear构成典型的被动语态,空格词应为-ed分词。

【答案解析】

①句说明社交隔离造成的一系列社会问题。②句指出,它/社交隔离由恐惧_____,且正在制造出更多的恐惧。结合两句时态变换(is putting... has been... is creating even more. .. )可知该句形成时间线条,说明“社交隔离由(对新冠传播的)恐惧造成-->造成诸多问题-->将会造成更多恐惧/问题(creating evenmore fear回应putting. ..canceling. ..and tanking. .. )”的过程。空格词应表“造成/驱动”等,C正确。

【确定词性】

空格所在句为倒装语序,可还原为love, and a sacrifice(主语)+ to protect those most_____ to the coronavirus effects(a sacrifice的后置定语)+is(系动词)+at its core(表语)。空格词应为形容词,且能与to 搭配, most_____ to the coronavirus effects为those的后置定语。

【答案解析】

空格句首先指出,社交隔离的核心是爱,是为了保护那些人(those)而做出的一种牺牲。随后破折号引出三类人群:老年人、免疫系统受损的人、救命资源将被耗尽的人。those most ____ to the coronavirus effects (最____冠状病毒影响的人)显然是对三类人群特征的概括,空格词应意为“易感的/易受影响的/易受侵害的", vulnerable to为固定搭配,表示“易受……的侵害”,O正确。

【确定词性】

空格位于冠词a和名词epidemic间,可能为名词、形容词、ing分词、ed分词。

【答案解析】

those. .. by a _____ epidemic与其前两类群体(the elderly, people with... )一样指向“冠状病毒易感人群”,可推知a ____ epidemic即指“冠状病毒大流行",空格词既应体现该流行病的性质/特点,又应契合“救命资源会被 _____ 流行病耗尽”这一句内语义,故空28应表示“危险的/恶性的/大规模的”等,E符合文意,此处指向冠状病毒大流行对医疗资源等的巨大耗费。

【确定词性】

空格所在句结构为social distancing(名词短语/主语)+is(系/助动词)+ ____ +in that...(状语从句),空格词可能为名词、形容词(句子为主系表结构,空格词充当表语),或-ing分词(句子为现在进行时,空格词与is构成谓语动词),或-ed分词(句子为被动语态,空格词与is构成谓语动词)。

【答案解析】

空格前两句介绍美国人不时在做出拯救生命的决定,“将食物切成小块、系好安全带、不超速”这些做法涉及“自己、家人以及其他人的生命安全”。空格句指出,但社交隔离是 _____ ,因为它完全是自我牺牲式的(completely self-sacrificing,即完全是为了他人的生命安全)。借助①②句和③句间的对比可知,空格词应体现“社交隔离作为挽救生命之举的独特之处/不同寻常",N正确。

【确定词性】

空格词位于冠词the和名词person间,应为person的修饰成分,可能为名词、形容词、-ing分词、-ed分词

【答案解析】

空格句指出,(社交隔离的)受益者可能是我们在星巴克、地铁或电梯里都未曾擦肩而过的____ 某个人的年长亲属。结合上句“社交隔离完全是自我牺牲式的(我们与受益者毫无关联/完全不相识)”可知, the _____ person(we didn't pass in.. elevator)应该体现我们(we,即实行社交隔离的人)与这些老人(the elderly relatives,即受益者)的“毫无瓜葛/完全不相识”. H) random意为“任意的;胡乱的;随意的”符合要求, the random person强调“任意的/随便的/毫不相干的某个人”,与定语从句信息(以点带面,说明我们与这些人完全未曾谋面)一致,共同强调这些老人“并非我们自己的亲人,而是陌生人的亲人”

【确定词性】

空格前为及物动词include和冠词the,后为不定式to run from...,空格词应为名词,跟the一起作include的宾语

【答案解析】

第三段前三句Social distancing is...、It doesn't include... What it does include...提示句群逻辑为“说明社交隔离的内涵→说明社交隔离不包含的做法→说明社交隔离真正应包含的做法”,初步判断空格词表负面语义,备选项中只有K满足条件。进一步聚焦 句发现,破折号后内容解释说明one' s obligations, 即 _____ to... or..—such as...整体语义为“(借社交隔离之名)逃离社会或逃避责任(如不去参加救生医疗工作,不履行为人父母的义务、出门购买日用品)的_____ "。空格词应表示“(错误的)做法/趋势/想法”等, temptations可表示“采取某种(不良)行为的想法/欲望”,确定K为正确项。

【确定词性】

空格词位于冠词an和名词opportunity间,应为opportunity的修饰成分,可能为名词、形容词、-ing分词、-ed分词,且以元音音素开头。

【答案解析】

空格前句指出,社交隔离真正包含的是谨慎地去爱。空格句指出,在这样做的过程中,它为那些关心老人的人们提供了找到关爱新方式的 ____ 机会。两句均传达出作者强烈的建议和肯定,可推知空格词应含正面语义,表示“宝贵的/绝佳的/神奇的”等,A符合文意, amazing opportunity"良机/令人惊喜的机会”可体现文中“无心插柳柳成荫,坏事(被迫社交隔离)变好事(找到关爱老人新方式的良机)"的情景。

【解题思路】

作者的隐含态度是解答空31，32的重要线索。本段各句采用陈述句式(Social distancing is.... It doesn't include. ... What it does include. ... And in doing so, it offers. ..),看似在客观陈述社交隔离的内容,实则结合millions of... hundreds of... run from. .. make an excuse. .. does include...等暗中传递作者态度。空31，32分别对应作者所反对、支持的做法,可推知两空的语义色彩,进而快速选定答案。

【确定词性】

空格前为we're not(主语+系/助动词),后为as much in...(表示程度的副词短语),空格词为形容词、ing分词、-ed分词,且能与in搭配

【答案解析】

本题的解题思路有二:

1,从句内逻辑来看,空格所在条件状语从句“如果我们不再那样____正常的工作和学习”为主句“有更多时间打电话给父母和祖父母”成立的条件,“有更多的空闲时间”势必意味着“减少了在工作和学习上投入的时间”。

2.从上下文关联来看,空格所在句恰好呼应首段“社交隔离正令人们失业、停学”。综上,空格词应表“(不再)忙于/专注于”等, be engaged in为固定搭配,意为“忙于",D正确

【确定词性】

空格所在句第一个and前的结构为We(主语)+can also ask(谓语)+elderly relatives(宾语) → how to best support them_____ 。空格词只能为副词,修饰support them.

【答案解析】

We can also表明空格句承接上句(多给老人打打电话),引出作者的另外的建议:我们还可以问问年长亲属怎样才能 _____ 最好地支持他们。可见此处指向为老年人提供精神上的/更大的/实际的支持。support sb spiritually 表示“在精神上支持某人",空格选项为J。I) sentimentally可表“情感地”,乍看下与spiritually属于同一层面,对空34有较大干扰,但该词实际上与rationally (理性地)相对,侧重于“情感地,感性地(而非理性地)", 且很少与support搭配,故排除。

【确定词性】

空格所在句第一个and后的结构为(We can also) use our sacrifices as an opportunity tobring A, B, and C ____ ,空格词可能为名词(构成bring sb sth双宾语结构),或形容词、副词(作宾补)。

【答案解析】

空35所在部分指出作者另一建议: 化逆境(因疫情而被迫社交隔离)为机遇, 将我们的牺牲, 社交隔离用作一种机会, 使整个社会(更)团结/和谐/紧密联系。bring sb closer为固定搭配, 表示“拉近某些人的距离", 符合文意, 由此确定答案为B.

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Picture yourself at a college graduation day, with a fresh cohort (—群) of students about to set sail for new horizons. 2 What are they thinking while they throw their caps in the air? 3 What is it with this thin sheet of paper that makes it so precious? 4 It's not only the proof of acquired knowledge but plays into the reputation game of where you were trained. 5 Being a graduate from Harvard Law School carries that extra glamour, doesn't it? 6 Yet take a closer look, and the diploma is the perfect ending to the modern tragedy of education.
1 Why? 2 Because universities and curricula are designed along the three unities of French classical tragedy: time, action, and place. 3 Students meet at the university campus (unity of place) for classes (unity of action) during their 20s (unity of time). 4 This classical model has traditionally produced prestigious universities, but it is now challenged by the digitalisation of society — which allows everybody who is connected to the internet to access learning — and by the need to acquire skill in step with a fast-changing world.? 5 Universities must realise that learning in your 20s won't be enough. 6 If technological diffusion and implementation develop faster, workers will have to constantly refresh their skills.
1 The university model needs to evolve. 2 It must equip students with the right skills and knowledge to compete in a world ' where value will be derived largely from human interaction and the ability to invent and interpret things that machines cannot', as the English futurist Richard Watson put it. 3 By teaching foundational knowledge and up-to-date skills, universities will provide students with the future-proof skills of lifelong learning, not just get them 'job-ready'.?
1 Some universities already play a critical role in lifelong learning as they want to keep the value of their diplomas. 2 This new role comes with a huge set of challenges, and needs largely to be invented. 3 One way to start this transformation process could be to go beyond the ' five-year diploma model ' to adapt curricula to lifelong learning. 4 We call this model the lifelong passport.
1 The Bachelor's degree could be your passport to lifelong learning. 2 For the first few years, students would ' learn to learn' and get endowed with reasoning skills that remain with them for the rest of their lives. 3 For instance, physics allows you to observe and rationalise the world, but also to integrate observations into models and, sometimes, models into theories or laws that can be used to make predictions.? 4 Mathematics is the language used to formulate the laws of physics or economy, and to make rigorous computations that turn into predictions. 5 These two disciplines naturally form the foundational pillars of education in technical universities.
1 Recent advances in computational methods and data science push us into rethinking science and engineering. 2 Computers increasingly become principal actors in leveraging data to formulate questions, which requires radically new ways of reasoning. 3 Therefore, a new discipline blending computer science, programming, statistics and machine learning should be added to the traditional foundational topics of mathematics and physics. 4 These three pillars would allow you to keep learning complex technical subjects all your life because numeracy (计算) is the foundation upon which everything else is eventually built.?
1 According to this new model, the Master of Science (MSc) would become the first stamp in the lifelong learning journey. 2 The MSc curriculum should prepare students for their professional career by allowing them to focus on acquiring practical skills through projects.
1 Those projects are then interwoven with fast-paced technical modules (模块) learned 'on-the-fly' and 'at will' depending on the nature of the project. 2 If, for instance, your project is developing an integrated circuit, you will have to take a module on advanced concepts in microelectronics. 3 The most critical skills will be developed before the project even starts, in the form of boot camps (短期强化训练), while the rest can be fostered along with the project, putting them to immediate use and thus providing a rich learning context.?
1 In addition to technical capabilities, the very nature of projects develops social and entrepreneurial skills, such as design thinking, initiative taking, team leading, activity reporting or resource planning. 2 Not only will those skills be actually integrated into the curriculum but they will be very important to have in the future because they are difficult to automate.?
1 After the MSc diploma is earned, there would be many more stamps of lifelong learning over the years. 2 If universities decide to engage in this learning model, they will have to cope with many organisational challenges that might shake their unity of place and action. 3 First, the number of students would be unpredictable. 4 If all of a university's alumni (往届毕业生) were to become students again, the student body would be much bigger than it is now, and it could become unsustainable for the campus in terms of both size and resources. 5 Second, freshly graduated students would mix with professionally experienced ones. 6 This would change the classroom dynamics, perhaps for the best. 7 Project-based learning with a mixed team reflects the reality of the professional world and could therefore be a better preparation for it.?
1 Sound like science fiction? 2 In many countries, part-time studying is not exceptional: on average across OECD countries, part-time students in 2016 represented 20 percent of enrolment in tertiary education. 3 In many countries, this share is higher and can exceed 40 percent in Australia, New Zealand and Sweden.?
1 If lifelong learning were to become a priority and the new norm, diplomas, just like passports, could be revalidated periodically. 2 A time-determined revalidation would ease administration for everybody. 3 Universities as well as employers and employees would know when they have to retrain. 4 For instance, graduates from the year 2000 would have to come back in 2005.
1 This could fix the main organisational challenges for the university, but not for the learners, due to lack of time, family obligations or funds. 2 Here, online learning might be an option because it allows you to save your travel time', but it has its limits. 3 So far, none of the major employers associated with online learning platforms such as Coursera and Udacity has committed to hire or even interview graduates of their new online programmes.?
1 Even if time were not an issue, who will pay for lifelong learning? 2 That's the eternal debate: should it be the learner' s responsibility, that of his employer, or of the state? 3 For example, in Massachusetts, the healthcare professions require continuing education credits, which are carefully evidenced and documented. 4 Yet the same state's lawyers don't require continuing legal education, although most lawyers do participate in it informally. 5 One explanation is that technology is less of a factor in law than it is in healthcare.?
1 Europe has many scenarios, but the French and Swiss ones are interesting to compare. 2 In France, every individual has a right to lifelong learning organised via a personal learning account that is credited as you work. 3 In Switzerland, lifelong learning is a personal responsibility and not a government one. 4 However, employers and the state encourage continuing education either by funding parts of it or by allowing employees to attend it.
1 Universities have a fundamental role to play in this journey, and higher education is in for a change. 2 Just like classical theatre, the old university model produced talent and value for society. 3 We are not advocating its abolition but rather calling for the adaptation of its characteristics to meet the needs of today.

questions.explanation:
【题干翻译】

学生应当在开展项目之前学会关键技能。


【答案解析】

36题the key skills, before they start a project同义改写③句The most critical skills、before the project even starts.

H段③句指出,学生必须在项目开始之前学会最关键的技能(其他技能则可在项目推进期间加以培养),试题是对此处信息的复现, the key skills对应原文的The most critical skills.


【段落解析】

H段介绍项目式课程应如何培养技术能力(硬技能)。

①句Those projects实现段际衔接,引出对理学硕士学位项目的进一步介绍。段内三句以for instance呈现“概述(①句)→采用事例细述(②③句)”的逻辑:

①句概述指出,技术模块的习得是“需快速进行(on-the-fly)"还是“可灵活安排(at will)"由项目性质决定;

②句继续指出集成电路开发项目须掌握微电子学的进阶概念模块;

③句以while形成对比, The most criticalskills..the rest分别引出“关键技能”和“其他技能”的习得安排,即前者必须在项目开始前获得(回应①句on-the-fly) ;后者可在项目推进期间逐步培养(回应①句at will),

全段核心信息:项目式课程如何培养专业技能

【题干翻译】

大学起初几年获得的推理技能可为学生奠定终身学习的基础。


【答案解析】

37题acquiring reasoning skills同义改写②句get endowed with reasoning skills, first fewyears of college则直接复现。

E段①句指出,学士学位是通向终身学习的通行证;②句指出,大学教育在起初几年将让学生学会学习,掌握伴其一生的推理能力。因此,学生在大学起初几年获得的推理技能是终身学习的基础。试题是对两句信息的整合, a foundation for lifelong learning是对推理技能持续时间remain with them for the rest of their lives及学士学位的最终功能passport to lifelong learning的高度概括。


【段落分析】

E段介绍当前学士学位的功能及课程重点(以数学和物理学为支柱学科,培养学生的推理能力)。段内整本呈现“概述一细述一举例论证”的逻辑。

①句借The Bachelor's degree开启对学士学位的介绍,明确其功能为终身学习之旅提供护照/颁发通行证”。

②句For the first few years指本科教育,引出其培养目标,learn toearn ,reasoning skills... for the rest of their lives是对上句passport to lifelong learning内涵的明确;学士学位的课程重点在于培养令学生终身受用的推理技能。

③至⑤句进而以For instance为标记举例说明,physics...Mathematics... These two disciplines串起对物理学和数学的学科功能的介绍, observe and rationalise theworld,integrate observations into models等等具体展现两大支柱学科对学生推理技能的培养作用,foundational pillars则确立这两门学科在技术类大学/理工科大学中的核心地位。

全段核心信息:

(1)本科教育的重点;

(2)数学和物理学在技术类本科教育中的核心地位。

【题干翻译】

知识易于获得,技术变化迅速,这让传统的教育模式受到了挑战。


【答案解析】

38题The easy access to learning是对④句allows everybody. . to access learning的正确解读, rapid technological changes对应a fast-changing world, traditional model of education under challenge同义替换④句it is now challenged(it即指传统大学模式)。

B段④句后半部分指出,传统的大学教育模式如今面临两方面挑战:社会的数字化(人人均可联网学习)和人们对最新技能的需求(以跟上快速变化的世界)。试题是对此部分信息的改写,其中The easy access to learning和rapid technological changes分别是对everybody who is connected to the internet to access learning和a fast-changing world的概括。


【段落分析】

B段解释大学教育的悲剧性所在:现有模式已经无法满足人们的需求。①句Why设问,②至⑥句由Because引领,展开回答。②至④句three unities. .. unity of place/action/time. .. This classical model. ..先聚焦现行大学教育的设置模式“三一律”,介绍其具体内容(时间、地点和行动/情节一致:学生在20多岁的时候来到校园进行学习)和曾经的正面作用(造就有名望的大学),然后由but引发转折,凸显这一模式现受到的两方面挑战:不仅不再是获得知识的必需之地(只要能联网就能学习知识),而且无法让人们紧跟时代所需(急速变化的世界需要人们不断学习最新技能)。⑤⑥句借Universities must realise that,If... workers will haveto....强调大学必须明白的新现实:单纯一次性的大学学习并不足够(learning in your 20s won't be enough),从业者需跟上技术的快速发展,不断更新自己的技能(constantly refresh their skills)。

全段核心信息:

(1)传统大学教育的理论基础;

(2)传统大学教育当前受到的挑战。

PS：“三一律”是西方古典主义戏剧结构理论,要求一出戏所叙述的故事发生在一天之内,地点在一个场景,情节服从于一个主题。它是17世纪古典主义的产物,可以使剧本结构更趋集中、严谨;但18世纪以后,剧作家认为它对剧本创作是一种严重的束缚,并用创作实践突破了这一法规。

【题干翻译】

虽然这可能令人难以置信,但在全球许多大学中,在职学生在学生群体中占有相当高的比例。


【答案解析】

39题Unbelievable是对①句like science fiction的合理解读, part-time students完整复现于②句,considerable portion对应②③句比例数据20 per cent、can exceed 40 percent.

K段首句针对上文情形“已参加工作的毕业生重返校园学习”指出,这或许让人觉得像是科幻小说(令人难以置信),②③句随即以多国数据进行反驳:经合组织成员国的在职学生数量平均占高校入学人数的20%,在某些国家甚至超过了40%。试题是对段落信息的提炼与概括,considerable portion准确体现文意:人们通常认为在职学生占比极低,实际占比却达20%、甚至40%以上(已经相当高了)。


【段落分析】

K段指出上述挑战让终身学习看似不可行,但现实情形表明终身学习大有可期。

首句承上反问:听起来像科幻小说(看起来难以相信)吗? 

②③句以真实数据作答:这并非天方夜。具体情形“在职学生并不罕见,在许多国家占高等教育总人数的20%,在有些国家占比甚至超过40%(即,在职学生在全球许多大学中都已占相当大比例)”足以说明终身学习模式大有前途。

全段核心信息: 在职学生在多国大学中占较高比例

【题干理解】

一些不易实现自动化的社交���管理技能将对学生未来的职业生涯至关重要。


【答案解析】

40题social and managerial skills近义替换D句social and entrepreneurial skills; not easilyautomated对应②句difficult to automate, of great importance改写very important.

I段末句指出社交与创业技能不仅会真正被融入课堂教学, 且在未来会非常重要, 因为它们很难实现自动化/不容易被机器取代 (those skills回指首句social and entrepreneurial skills)。试题是对该句的同义改写, 其中managerial skills与entrepreneurial skills同指企业经营与管理技能, of great importance to students' future careers改写very important to have in the future.


【段落分析】

I段指出项目式课程注重培养社交与创业技能(软技能)。首句In addition to technical capabilities承接上段项目式课程的一大作用“培养学生的专业技能(硬技能)”,引出另一作用“培养学生的社交与创业技能(软技能)", the very nature of projects强调项目之所以能够锻炼软技能,正是由其本质(要求多人协作、主动探索整合信息等)所决定的。末句先以Not only will those skills. .. but they will... 显软技能的重要性“不仅是硕士课程必不可少的部分,对未来也非常重要”,后以because. .. difficult to automate解释其重要的原因“不容易波自动化/被机器替代”。

全段核心信息:

(1)项目式课程可培养社交与创业技能;

(2)社交与创业技能的重要性。

【题干翻译】

大学教育新模式应当为学生提供这样的知识和技能,即让他们更加善于创新、能够做到终身学习。


【答案解��】

41题A new model of college education与 句It(指变革后的大学模式,即大学教育新模式)指向相同,more inventive复现于②句the ability to invent.

C段②句指出,在当今世界,价值主要源自人际互动以及发明和解释事物的能力;③句又提出,通过教授基础知识和最新技能,大学教育新模式将赋予学生与时俱进的终身学习技能。试题是对两句信息的提炼,A new model of college education是对②句It的正确解读, capable of lifelong learning同义改写 skills of lifelong learning.


【段落分析】

C段首先说明大学教育模式应该达到的目标。0句和@③句借The university model needs to evolve....It must. .. universities will形成“总一分”结构,首先概述大学的模式需要改变(evolve意为“发展,进化”,这里指大学的模式需要超越现状并发展),然后借in a world. .. By teaching. .. provide students with. ..建立完整的语义链:明确当今时代需要的技能(人际互动以及发明和解释事物的能力)-介绍大学应当传授的相应内容(基础知识和最新技能)-指出这一新模式旨在达到的效果(授人以渔,让学生获得终身学习的技能)。

全段核心信息:

(1)当下时代对大学生技能的要求;

(2)大学新模式的内容和目标。

【题干翻译】

多元的学生群体或将改变课堂互动方式,有利于学习。


【答案解析】

42题mixed student body改写⑦句mixed team, classroom dynamics原词复现于⑥句。

J段⑤句介绍“终身学习”模式下大学将面临的第二大挑战:刚毕业的学生与职业经验丰富的学生共聚一堂。⑥⑦句进而指出“混合式/多元化(mixed)”学生群体的益处:改善课堂互动方式;反映了职场的真实情况,是一种更好的就业准备方式。试题改写⑥⑦句, benefit learning是对change the classroom dynamics. .. for the best, a better preparation for it(it指代the professional world)的合理概括。


【段落分析】

J段介绍终身学习模式给大学带来的两大组织性挑战。

首句After the MSc diploma is earned... manymore stamps承接上文“理学硕士学位是终身学习之旅的第一枚印戳”,并指出在终身学习中还有更多的印戳等待获取,暗示终身学习模式相当复杂、难于管理。

②句提出段落主旨:终身学习模式下大学将面临诸多组织方面的挑战。

③至⑦句以First... Second形成并列关系,说明两大组织性挑战:学生数量无法预估(学校规模与资源或许无法承载太过庞大的学生数量);学生集体的工作经验参差不齐(这将改变课堂互动方式)。但随后的评述性表达would change. .. for the best,better preparation for (the professional world)补充指出第二大挑战实则是件好事:“混合式/多元化(mixed)"学生群体对提升学习效果、更好备战职场大有助益。

全段核心信息: 

(1)终身学习模式给大学带来的组织性挑战;

(2)多元化学生群体的好处。

【题干翻译】

谁将承担终身学习的费用,这一问题一直是争论的话题。


【答案解析】

43题the cost of lifelong learning同义转述①句pay for lifelong learning, a topic of constantdebate近义复现②句eternal debate.

N段①②句抛出疑问“该由谁来为终身学习买单?是学习者、其雇主,还是政府?",并评价指出这是一场永无休止的争论。试题是对两句的同义改写, bear the cost of lifelong learning和a topic of constant debate分别同义替换pay for lifelong learning和the eternal debate。


【段落分析】

N段介绍“终身学习”模式下的争议性问题:谁来买单?

首句Even if time... not an issue承接上文“时间不足可通过在线学习来解决”, who will pay引出另一问题“学习费用又该由谁来承担"。

②句设问should it be theresponsibility of A, of B, or of C,指出多种可能“由学习者、雇主、政府中的谁来承担”;评述短语the eternal debate强调这是一个长期的争议性问题。

③至⑤句举例(For example)说明争议性。③④句以Yet形成转折, in Massachusetts, the same state强调“同一地点", healthcare professions require continuing education, lawyers don't require形成行业对比,强调争议性情形“同是马萨诸塞州,医护行业要求进行继续教育,而律师行业尽管不作要求,但仍有不少从业人员自行进修(故而很难判定进修费用到底该由谁来承担)".⑤句One explanation...作出推测性分析:不同行业对继续教育的要求不同。

全段核心信息: 终身学习的费用该由谁来承担。

【题干分析】

除了传统的数学和物理学之外,还应加入一门结合了计算机科学、统计学及其他科目的新学科。


【答案解析】

44题math and physics完整复现于3句,combines computer science with statistics同义改写 blending computer science...statistics.

F段⑤句指出,一门融合计算机科学、编程、统计学和机器学习的新学科应加入数学和物理学这两门传统基础学科的行列,试题是对原文信息的同义改写, combines... with... and...与原文blending... and... 。


【段落分析】

F段指出,当下情形要求学士学位项目增加一门基础学科(即,三大支柱学科奠定终身学习的基础)。段内以Therefore为标记构成因果逻辑:先明确增加基础学科的原因,再引出新增的基础学科。

①②句Recentadvances.. increasingly become提示“当下时代”的视角, computational methods and data science和Computers的强语义关联指向当下变化“计算机的作用越来越大", requires radically new ways of reasoning凸显改变推理方式的必要性(暗示需要新增相关学科),

③④句借a new discipline. .. These three pillars先描述新增的基础学科(融合计算机科学、编程、统计学等),再介绍三大基础学科(数学、物理、新增学科)的功能,keep learning... all your life, everything else is eventually built凸显三大基础学科对终身学习的巨大作用。

全段核心信息:

(1)需要增加一门基础学科;

(2)三大基础学科的作用。

【题干分析】

需要承担家庭责任的学生可能会选择参加线上课程。


【答案解析】

45题Students who are burdened with family duties是对①句the learners. .. familyobligations的同义转述,online courses复现②③句online learning、online programmes

M段首句指出问题:定期认证文凭可解决大学所面临的主要组织性挑战,但对于缺少时间、家庭义务缠身或有资金困难的学习者而言无济于事。②句提出解决办法:在线学习或许是一种选择,因为它可以节省你的时间。试题是对这两句内容的提取及转述。


【段落分析】

M段介绍学习者面临的第一大问题“(因工作或家庭责任在身)缺少时间”及其解决方案。

首句为过渡句,先以This could fix...challenges for the university总结上文,指出定期重新认证文凭可以解决大学面临的组织性挑战,后以but not for the learners转折指出学习者面临的问题(缺时间、缺资金)却无法得到解决。

②③句(其中③句是对②句的例证)聚焦“缺时间”并提出可考虑方案“在线学习”,却转而指出其局限性(limits):缺乏职场认可度。

全段核心信息:

(1)缺少时间的学习者可以选择在线学习;

(2)在线学习的局限性。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 Why does social media trigger feelings of loneliness and inadequacy? 2 Because instead of being real life, it is, for the most part, impression management, a way of marketing yourself, carefully choosing and filtering the pictures and words to put your best face forward.?
1 Online "friends" made through social media do not follow the normal psychological progression of an interpersonal relationship. 2 You share neither physical time nor emotional conversations over the Internet. 3 You simply communicate photographs and catchy posts to a diverse group of people whom you have "friended" or "followed" based on an accidental interaction. 4 This is not to say that your social media friends can't be real friends. 5 They absolutely can, but the two are not synonymous. 6 Generally speaking, there are no unfiltered comments or casually taken photos on our social media pages. 7 And, rightfully so, because it wouldn't feel safe to be completely authentic and vulnerable with some of our "friends" whom we don't actually know or with whom trust has yet to be built.?
1 Social media can certainly be an escape from the daily grind, but we must be cautioned against the negative effects, such as addiction, on a person's overall psychological well-being.
1 As humans, we yearn for social connection. 2 Scrolling (滚动) through pages of pictures and comments, however, does not provide the same degree of fulfillment as face-to-face interactions do. 3 Also, we tend to idealize others' lives and compare our downfalls to their greatest accomplishments, ending in feelings of loneliness and inadequacy.
1 Social media can lead people on the unhealthy quest for perfection. 2 Some people begin to attend certain events or travel to different places so that they can snap that "perfect" photo.? 3 They begin to seek validation through the number of people who "like" their posts. 4 In order for it to play a psychologically healthy role in your social life, social media should supplement an already healthy social network. 5 Pictures and posts should be byproducts of life's treasured moments and fun times, not the planned and calculated image that one is putting out into cyberspace in an attempt to fill insecurities or unmet needs.?
1 Ultimately, social media has increased our ability to connect with various types of people all over the globe. 2 It has opened doors for businesses and allowed us to stay connected to people whom we may not otherwise get to follow. 3 However, social media should feel like a fun experience, not one that contributes to negative thoughts and feelings. 4 If the latter is the case, increasing face-to-face time with trusted friends, and minimizing time scrolling online, will prove to be a reminder that your social network is much more rewarding than any "like," "follow" or "share" can be.?

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What does the author imply social media may do to our life?

作者暗示杜交媒体可能会对我们的生活产生什么影响?

A. It may facilitate our interpersonal relationships.

    它可以促进我们的人际关系。

B. It may filter our negative impressions of others.

    它可以筛除我们对他人的负面印象。

C. It may make us feel isolated and incompetent.

    它可能使我们感到孤独和无能为力

D. It may render us vulnerable and inauthentic.

    它可能使我们变得脆弱和不真实。


【定位及答案】

本题考查社交媒体对人们生活的影响。根据social media和do to our life定位至首段①句(Why does social media trigger...)。首段①句设问“为什么社交媒体会引发孤独感和能力不足之感”,这暗示作者观点:社交媒体会让人们感到孤独和无能为力。C正确,选项同义改写trigger feelings of loneliness and inadequacy.


【错误选项分析】

A选项【常识干扰】：该选项借常识设置干扰,且符合末段①②句让步信息,但与作者整体观点相悖。

B选项【东拼西凑】：将首段②句impression management和filtering糅杂设置干扰,原文指“筛选展示自己的内容,以给他人留下好印象”,而非筛除他人留给自己的不好印象"。

D选项【偷换概念】：曲解第二段D句authentic and vulnerable,原文指“在社交媒体上完全展示自己真实、脆弱的一面会让我们不安 。(即，我们不会在社交媒体上完全展示自己真实、脆弱的一面)".


【解题思路】

本题表面考查对开篇部分作者观点的推理引申,深层考查全文主旨。解题时首先需要细读题干: do to our life提示本题考查社交媒体对我们生活的真实影响, imply提示要寻找文中隐含的作者观点。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

Why do people post comments selectively on social media? 

为什么人们在社交媒体上有选择性地发表评论?

A. They do not find all their online friends trustworthy.

   他们认为并非所有网友都值得信赖。

B. They want to avoid offending any of their audience.

    他们希望避免冒犯任何读者。

C. They do not want to lose their followers.

    他不想失去自己的追随者

D. They are eager to boost their popularity.

    他们渴望提升自己的受欢迎度。


【定位及答案】

本题考查人们在社交媒体上选择性地发表评论的原因。根据Why和post comments selectively定位至第二段⑥⑦句(no unfiltered comments... rightfully so, because... )。第二段⑥句指出社交媒体页面上不会出现未经筛选的评论(即题干所述的现象),⑦句解原因(so指代⑥句所述内容):人们未与某些网友建立信任关系,因此不敢完全展示真实的自己。A正确。


【错误选项分析】

B、C、D选项【过度推理】：这三个选项均基于现实中社交媒体的使用情形对第二段③句"friended" or "followed"主观臆断,得出“避免激怒读者或失去粉丝”或是“提升自己的受欢迎度",均不符合文意。


【解题思路】

本题考查文中的因果关系,需准确把握句间逻辑。另外,对于此类关注现实生活的文章,答题时一定要紧贴原文,避免受现实情形的干扰。具体来看,首段②句描述题干所述现象(carefully choosing and filtering the pictures and words),第二段对其进行解释,呈现完整的因果逻辑链条: 网络交友并不遵循人际关系的常规发展历程→网友之间并未建立信任关系一人们对于展示完全真实的自己感到不安→有选择性地发表内容。由此可选出与原文语义一致的A。其余三项方向一致,均指向人们希望维持、加强与网友的关系,在很大程度上符合社交媒体的使用情形,但均非文中的因果关联,需排除。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What are humans inclined to do according to the passage?

根据这篇文章可知人类倾向于做什么?

A. Exaggerate their life's accomplishments.

    夸大自己的人生成就。

B. Strive for perfection regardless of the cost.

    不计代价地追求完美。

C. Paint a rosy picture of other people's lives

    美化他人的生活

D. Learn lessons from other people's downfalls.

    从他人的失败中吸取教训。


【定位及答案】

本题考查人们的行为倾向。题干中humans, inclined to对应第四段的humans/we,tend to...第四段③句指出我们人类(we与上句humans同指)倾向于把别人的生活理想化,并把自己���失败与他们最大的成就相比较,C正确, Paint a rosy picture (把...描绘成美好图画)是对文中抽象表述idealize(把...理想化)的形象解读


【错误选项分析】

A、D选项【过度推理】：A，D选项将第四段 句信息“把自己的失败与别人的最大成就相比较”分别曲解为“夸大自己的人生成就”“吸取别人的失败教训". 

B选项【答非所问】：曲解第五段①句quest for perfection,该信息强调社交媒体对人们的不良影响(导致人们病态般地追求完美),而非题目所问的人类的本能倾向,


【解题思路】

本题解题时需注意两点:

1.理解题干中humans inclined to do的深层内涵,即“人类的自然/内在倾向”;

2.识别干扰项的迷惑性,警惕选项的“形似”陷阱:

A、D虽复现文中的accomplishments ,downfalls,但改变逻辑关系(把“放大别人的成就”改为“夸大自己的成就”,将“自己的失败”改为“他人的失败”);B虽体现第五段①②句情形“不顾一切追求完美”,却将“社交媒体诱导的行为”当作题干所问的“人类的内在倾向”和原文看似不一致,但结合rosy的词义(美好的,光明的)很容易确定Paint a rosy picture of other people's lives是对原文idealize others' lives的同义改写,体现了人类的内在倾向(we tend to对应humans inclined to)

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What is the author's view of pictures and posts on social media？

作者对社交媒体上的图片和帖子有何看法？

A. They should record the memorable moments in people's lives. 

    它们应该记录人们生活中的难忘时刻。

B. They should be carefully edited so as to present the best image.

    它们应该经过仔细的编辑,以便呈现出最佳形象。

C. They should be shown in a way that meets one's security needs.

    它们的展示方式应满足人们的安全感需求。

D. They should keep people from the unhealthy quest for perfection.

    它们应该阻止人们病态地追求完美。


【定位及答案】

本题考查作者对社交媒体内容的看法。结合题干关键词pictures and posts和“题文同序”原则可定位到第五段(photo,posts ,Pictures and posts)。第五段末句指出,(社交媒体上的)图片和帖子应该是人们生活中珍贵时刻和快乐时光的副产品,言外之意为,人们发布图片和帖子的目的应该是纪念生活中的难忘时刻,故A正确。


【错误选项分析】

B选项【反向干扰】：曲解第五段末句的取舍句式(should be. .. not.),将作者不赞同的做法(not之后的内容)当作作者认同的做法。

C选项【断章取义】：对第五段末句fill insecurities or unmet needs断章取义,将作者讽刺的现象“通过图片和帖子刻意营造美好形象来填补缺失的安全感”曲解为作者的建议“以满足自己安全感需求的方式展示图片和帖子"。 

D选项【答非所问】：利用第五段①句the unhealthy quest for perfection设置干扰,虽符合作者观点的大方向,但未涉及作者对“图片和帖子”的具体定位


【解题思路】

结合题干the author's view及各项should可知本题实际考查作者的劝诚或建议,根据关键词很容易确定第五段末句Pictures and posts should be. ..为正确项来源,由该句的取舍逻辑可基本确定A正确,同时排除B。

另外,C、D有很大的干扰性,两项似乎均由“问题/缺陷”反推出“对策/建议”(C由第五段末句的insecurities反推而来,D由该段首句的lead people on the unhealthy quest for perfection反推而来),看似合理,实则文不对题,考生解答这类题型时务必找到直接描述建议的句子,警惕由问题细节反向捏造建议的干扰项设置方式。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What does the author advise people to do when they find their online experience unconstructive?

当人们发现自己的网络体验缺乏建设性意义时，作者建议他们怎么做?

A. Use social media to increase their ability, to connect with various types of people.

   利用社交媒体提高他们与各类人沟通交往的能力。

B. Stay connected to those whom they may not otherwise get to know and befriend.

    与那些他们原本可能没有机会认识

C. Try to prevent negative thoughts and feelings from getting into the online pages.

    尽量避免把负面想法和情绪带到网页中

D. Strengthen ties with real-life friends instead of caring about their online image.

    加强与现实朋友的联系,别在意自己的网络形象。


【定位及答案】

本题考查作者建议(如何让网络体验更积极有益),可定位至末段:该段③句(social media) experience,negative thoughts and feelings对应题干中online experience, unconstructive (非建设性的;无助益的)。末段末句指出,若社交媒体让你产生消极想法和情绪(即用户体验缺乏建设性/积极意义),不妨多与好友面对面交流,尽量减少使用社交媒体的时间,最终你会明白现实中的社交网络比社交媒体更有意义(scrolling online和any "like," "follow" or "share"均指向社交媒体);且由上文可知社交媒体会诱发病态完美主义,让用户过度在意自己的网络形象。综合可知,D符合作者的建议。


【错误选项分析】

A,B选项【答非所问】：A，B选项分别来自第五段①句和②句,但这是社交媒体的正面作用(既定事实),并非题干所问当网络体验缺乏建设性时,作者建议怎么做)

C选项【过度推理】：错误理解末段3句的取舍结构,原文指出“社交媒体应带来快乐体验,而非让人产生负面想法和情绪”,并非建议“别把负面想法和情绪带到社交媒体中"。


【解题思路】

本题定位较难,题干中unconstructive是理解难点,可借更常见的constructive(建设性的;有助益的)把握其内涵,并搜寻到末段③句的contributes to negative thoughts and feelings(指向消极/负面作用),进而借If the latter is the case的回指作用进一步定位到末句,将选项与其比对,发现D项传达的取舍逻辑与句中increasing. .. minimizing..以及比较级句式...is much more rewarding than. ..暗含的取舍逻辑致,故正确;而C则直接截取文中短语设置“形似”陷阱,实际曲解了文意,可排除。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 Imagine that an alien species landed on Earth and, through their mere presence, those aliens caused our art to vanish, our music to homogenize, and our technological know-how to disappear. 2 That is effectively what humans have been doing to our closest relatives-chimps (大猩猩).?
1 Back in 1999, a team of scientists led by Andrew Whiten showed that chimps from different parts of Africa behave very differently from one another. 2 Some groups would get each other's attention by rapping branches with their knuckles (指关节), while others did it by loudly ripping leaves with their teeth. 3 The team identified 39 of these traditions that are practiced by some communities but not others — a pattern that, at the time, hadn't been seen in any animal except humans. 4 It was evidence, the team said, that chimps have their own cultures.?
1 It took a long time to convince skeptics that such cultures exist, but now we have plenty of examples of animals learning local traditions from one another.
1 But just when many scientists have come to accept the existence of animal cultures, many of those cultures might vanish. 2 Ammie Kalan and her colleagues have shown, through years of intensive fieldwork, that the very presence of humans has eroded the diversity of chimp behavior. 3 Where we flourish, their cultures wither. 4 It is a bitterly ironic thing to learn on the 20th anniversary of Whiten's classic study.?
1 It's amazing to think that just 60 years ago, we knew next to nothing of the behavior of our sister species in the wild, Whiten says. 2 But now, just as we are truly getting to know our primate (灵长类) cousins, the actions of humans are closing the window on all we have discovered.
1 Sometimes in the rush to conserve the species, I think we forget about the individuals," says Cat Hobaiter, a professor at the University of St. Andrews. 2 Each population, each community, even each generation of chimps is unique. 3 An event might only have a small impact on the total population of chimps, but it may wipe out an entire community-an entire culture. 4 No matter what we do to restore habitat or support population growth, we may never be able to restore that culture.?
1 No one knows whether the destruction of chimp culture is getting worse. 2 Few places have tracked chimp behavior over long periods, and those that have are also more likely to have protected their animals from human influence.
1 Obviously, conservationists need to think about saving species in a completely new way-by preserving animal traditions as well as bodies and genes. 2 Instead of focusing only on the conservation of genetically based entities like species, we now need to also consider culturally based entities, says Andrew Whiten.?

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What does the author say we humans have been doing to chimps?

作者说我们人类一直以来在对大猩猩做什么?

A. Ruining their culture.

    摧毁它们的文化。

B. Accelerating their extinction.

    加速它们的灭绝。

C. Treating them as alien species.

    将它们视作外星物种

D. Homogenizing their living habits.

    使它们的生活习惯趋于雷同。


【定位及答案】

本题考查人类一直以来对大猩狸所做之事,由humans have been doing to chimps可定位至首段。首段①句虚设情境“某外星物种登陆地球,凭一已之力将人类文明毁灭",②句回归现实,指出“这正是人类一直以来对大猩猩所做之事”,意即“人类一直都在摧毁大猩猩的文化", A正确。


【错误选项分析】

B选项【偷换概念】：该选项将“摧毁物种文化/摧毁艺术、音乐、技术知识等文化(our art to vanish. ..know-how to disappear)"偷换为“推动物种灭绝(their extinction)".

C选项【偷换概念】：该选项复现①句alien species, 但混淆虚拟情境和现实情况,文章实际旨在以类比手法说明“外星物种对人类的所作所为”即“人类对大猩狸的所作所为”,并非说明人类将大猩猩视为外星物种。

D选项【偷换概念】：复现①句homogenize,但将被同质化的事物由“音乐(代指文化活动)"偷换为“生活习惯”。


【解题思路】

本题易于定位,难点在于理解首段的类比手法,解题可采用以下思路:

首先由humans have been doing to chimps定位至②句,发现答案线索指向指示代词That; 随后上溯至①句设想的场景(Imagine);

最后联系①句虚拟情境和②句现实情况可知,...caused...及...have been doing to...均呈递施害者与受害者,作者以humans类比an alien species/ those aliens, our closest relatives/ chimps类比our (humans) , That指向caused. .. art to vanish. .. music to homogenize. .. technological know-how to disappear, 即"(现实中)人类正对大猩猩所做之事”正是“(设想中)外星人对人类所做之事:毁灭其文化”,锁定正确项A.

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What is the finding of Andrew Whiten's team?

安德鲁·怀滕团队的发现是什么?

A. Chimps demonstrate highly developed skills of communication.

    大猩猩展现出非常高超的交流技能。

B. Chimps rely heavily upon their body language to communicate. 

    大猩狸极度依赖肢体语言进行交流。

C. Chimps behave in ways quite similar to those of human beings. 

    大猩猩的行为方式与人类极为相似。

D. Different chimp groups differ in their way of communication.

    不同大猩猩群体的交流方式不一样。


【定位及答案】

本题考查Andrew Whiten团队的研究发现,可定位至第二段(a team of scientists led by Andrew Whiten showed. .. The team identified. ..)。第二段①句总述团队发现“非洲不同地区的大猩猩行为大不相同”,②句举例详释“群体间引起对方注意的方式完全不同",③句进一步指出“研究发现的这种"一些社群遵从奉行,其他社群则不然’ 的行为传统已达39种”。可见,不同大猩猩群体的交流方式截然不同, D正确。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【无中生有】：A选项中skills of communication体现于②句“大猩猩引起对方注意的方式(by rapping.. byloudly ripping. ..)",但文中并未体现“其交流技能高度发达”. 

B选项【无中生有】：B选项中their body language体现于②句with their knuckles, with their teeth,但文中并未强调大猩猩对肢体语言的高度依赖。

C选项【偷换概念】：C选项源自③④句体现的“大猩猩”与“人类”的相似性,但相似的是“二者都有文化/社群间传统迥异的生存模式”,并非“二者的行为方式”。


【解题思路】

本题问及研究发现,解题关键在于确定“研究对象”及“研究内容”:首先由①②③句所涉主体chimps from different parts of Africa. .. Some groups... others.. some communities. ..others可锁定研究对象“不同地区的大猩猩社群”,基本排除聚焦大猩猩物种(Chimps)的A、B、C三项;随后由动词behave... get each other's attention. .practiced. .明确研究内容为“大猩猩的行为/交流方式",且very differently from one another... some groups. .. while others... by some communities but not others. ..均体现“不同”,确定D正确。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What did Ammie Kalan and her colleagues find through their intensive fieldwork？

艾米·卡兰和她的同事通过多年深入实地考察发现了什么?

A. Whiten's classic study has little impact on the diversity of chimp behavior

    怀滕的经典研究对大猩猩行为多样性的影响微乎其微。

B. Chimp behavior becomes less varied with the increase of human activity.

    大猩猩的行为多样性随人类活动的增加而减少。

C. Chimps alter their culture to quickly adapt to the changed environment.

    大猩猩会改变自身文化以迅速适应业已改变的环境。

D. It might already be too late to prevent animal cultures from extinction.

    阻止动物文化消亡可能为时已晚。


【定位及答案】

本题考查Ammie Kalan团队的实地考察发现,可定位至第四段。第四段①句指出“多种动物文化可能消失不见”,②③句介绍Ammie Kalan团队的实地考察发现“正是人类的存在破坏了大猩猩行为的多样性,人类的发展繁荣之地恰是大猩猩文化的凋零之处”,综合可知“人类活动损害了大猩猩行为的多样性", B正确。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【无中生有】：该选项利用第四段段末Whiten's classic study捏造干扰,文章实则强调"Whiten的经典研究旨在提醒人们关注大猩猩的文化,但正值其发表20周年之际,我们却发现人类一直在破坏其文化”.

C选项【反向干扰】：该选项与第四段③句发现“人类发展繁荣之地恰是大猩猩文化凋零之所(wither)"相悖。

D选项【断章取义&反向干扰】：该选项对第四段末句It is a bitterly ironic thing断章取义,与末段作者建议“环境保护主义者需要保全动物的传统(阻止动物文化消亡)"相违背。


【解题思路】

本题易于定位,解题关键在于梳理定位处关系:第四段②③句以A has eroded B,where A... , B...提示“人类的存在/行为(the very presence of humans/ we flourish)"及“大猩猩的行为多样性/社群文化(the diversity of chimp behavior/their cultures)"之间的因果关联,B体现这一关联,

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What does Cat Hobaiter think we should do for chimp conservation?

卡特·赫伯特认为我们应如何保护大猩猩?

A. Try to understand our sister species' behavior in the wild.

    试着理解我们的姊妹物种在野外的行为。

B. Make efforts to preserve each individual chimp community

    努力保全每个独立的大猩猩社群

C. Study the unique characteristics of each generation of chimps.

    研究每一代大猩猩的独特特点。

D, Endeavor to restore chimp habitats to expand its total population. 

    努力恢复大猩猩栖息地以扩大整个种群。


【定位及答案】

本题考查Cat Hobaiter对大猩猩保护方式的建议,可定位至第六段(...says Cat Hobaiter)。第六段①句指出“人类急于保护整个大猩猩物种,却忽略了个体”, ②句强调“大猩猩的每个社群都独一无二",③④句补充指出“某事件可能对大猩猩整个种群影响极小,却可能彻底摧毁整个社群及整个文化,且社群文化一旦消失则极难复原”,可见,赫伯特认为应努力保全每个大猩猩社群,B正确。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念】：该选项由第五段①句we knew next to nothing. . in the wild反推而来,错误有二:1.张冠李戴,第五段为安德鲁·怀膝的观点;2,偷换时间,该句说的是60年前的情形,而不是当今状况。

C选项【过度推理】：该选项由第六段②句的客观描述“大猩猩的每一代都独一无二”过度推断出赫伯特的观点“我们要努力研究每一代大猩猩的独特特征"。

D选项【答非所问】：该选项将第六段④句前半部分所述的不当做法“只努力恢复栖息地,促进种群增长”当作赫伯特认为的努力方向。


【解题思路】

该题目为人物观点题。解答此类题时,需注意区分人物观点,准确定位正确项出处;并理顺其间逻辑,整体把握人物观点。首先根据题干中的Cat Hobaiter排除其他人物观点,定位至第六段。随后综合理解段内信息:三组表述(the species, the total population, population指向“整个大猩猩物种"; individuals, Each population, each community, even each generation, an entire community,an entire culture, that culture指向“个体社群/个体文化"; unique, wipe out an entire community, may never be able to restore指向个体的“独特、脆弱、难以恢复”)表明人物观点:努力保全每个独立的大猩猩社群。

questions.explanation:
【选项概览】

What does the author suggest conservationists do?

作者建议环境保护主义者作何行动?

A. Focus entirely on culturally-based entities rather than genetically-based ones

    完全致力于基于文化的实体而非基于基因的实体。

B. Place more stress on animal traditions than on their physical conservation

    相比于保护动物躯体,更重视动物传统。

C. Conserve animal species in a novel and all-round way

    用新颖而全面的方式保护动物物种。

D. Explore the cultures of species before they vanish.

    在物种消失前探究其文化。


【定位及答案】

本题考查作者对环保主义者的建议,可定位至第八段①句(conservationists need to. ..)。第八段首句作者提出建议“环境保护主义者需要考虑用一种全新的方式来拯救物种既保护动物的躯体和基因,也保全它们的传统”,C正确。


【错误选项分析】

A选项【反向干扰】：该选项将②句中的并重关系“既要保护基因实体,又要保护文化实体”改写为取舍关系“保护文化实体，而非基因实体”。

B选项【偷换概念】：该选项将①句的并重关系“既要保护躯体和基因,又要保护动物传统”改为主次关系“相比于保护动物躯体,更重视动物传统”。 

D选项【无中生有&答非所问】：该选项对文中信息“研究人员对动物文化的了解尚少”和“人类正在摧毁动物文化"强加关联,并将其当作对环境保护主义者的建议。


【解题思路】

本题考查作者建议,解题可采用以下思路:结合上文对问题的阐释来理解作者建议;理解作者建议的过程中要认真分析特殊句式(取舍结构、并列结构等)。具体来看:

1.本文整体关注现象为“人类正在摧毁大猩猩的文化”,而其发生的原因在于“人们对大狸狸的保护重基因、轻文化"。

2.第八段两句以a completelynew way、并列结构...as well as..和取舍结构Instead of focusing only on. .. we now need to also consider. ..共同说明作者建议为“采用全新的物种保护思路:文化和基因同等重要,应该双管齐下”。故C正确。

sections.passage:
Tonight, we have a special guest.
Mrs. Anna Sanchez is a three-time Olympic champion and author of the new book To the Edge. Mrs. Sanchez, thank you for joining us.
Thank you for having me.
Let’s start with your book. What does the title To the Edge mean?
What are you referring to?
The book is about how science and technology has helped to push humans to the edge of their physical abilities.
I argue that in the past 20 years we've had the best athletes the world has ever seen.
But is this a fair comparison?
How do you know how, say, a football player from 50 years ago would compare to one today?
Well, you are right.
That comparison would be perhaps impossible to make, but the point is more about our knowledge today of human biochemistry, nutrition and mechanics.
I believe that while our bodies have not changed in thousands of years, what has changed is the scientific knowledge.
This has allowed athletes to push the limits of what was previously thought possible.
That’s interesting.
Please tell us more about these perceived limits.
The world is seeing sports records being broken that could only be broken with the aid of technology, whether this be the speed of a tennis serve or the fastest time in a hundred-meter dash, or a two-hundred-meter swimming race.
Is there any concern that technology is giving some athletes an unfair advantage over others?
That is an interesting question and one that has to be considered very carefully.
Skis, for example, went from being made from wood to a metal alloy which allows for a better control and faster speed.
There is no stopping technological progress.
But as I said, each situation should be considered carefully on a case-by-case basis.
1. What do we learn about Anna Sanchez?
2. What is the woman’s book mainly about?
3. What has changed in the past thousands of years?
4. What is the man’s concern about the use of technology in sports competitions?
I've worked in international trade all my life.
My father did so too before me.
So, I guess you could say it runs in the family.
What products have you worked with?
All sorts, really. I've imported textiles, machinery, toys, solar panels … all kinds of things over the years.
Trends and demand come and go.
So, one need to be very flexible to succeed in this industry.
I see. What goods are you trading now?
I now import furniture from China into Italy and foods from Italy into China.
I even use the same container.
It’s very efficient way of conducting trade.
The same container?
You mean you own a 40-foot cargo container?
Yeah. That's right.
I have a warehouse in Genova, Italy and another in Shanghai.
I source mid-century modern furniture from different factories in China.
It's very good value for money.
I collect it all in my warehouse, and then dispatch it to my other warehouse in Italy.
Over there I do the same, but with Italian foods instead of furniture, things like pasta, cheese, wine, chocolates.
And I send all that to my warehouse in China, in the same freight container I use for the furniture.
So, I presume you sell both lines of products wholesale in each respective country.
Of course, I possess a network of clients and partners in both countries.
That's the main benefit of having done this for so long.
I've made great business contacts over time.
How many times do you ship?
I did 12 shipments last year, 18 this year, and I hope to grow to around 25 next year.
That’s both ways, there and back again.
Demand for authentic Italian food in China is growing rapidly, and similarly, sales of affordable yet stylish wooden furniture are also increasing in Italy.
Furniture is marginally more profitable, mostly because it enjoys lower customs duties.
5. What does the woman think is required to be successful in international trade?
6. What does the woman say is special about her way of doing trade?
7. What does the woman have in both Italy China?
8. What does the woman say makes furniture marginally more profitable?
“Too many people view their jobs as a five-day prison from which they are paroled every Friday,” says Joel Gookman, founder of the Humor Project, a humor-consulting group in Saratoga Springs, New York.
Humor unlocks the office prison because it lets adults bring some of their childlike spirit to the job.
According to Howard Pollio, professor of psychology at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, an office with humor breaks is an office with satisfied and productive employees.
Pollio conducted a study that proved humor can help workers excel at routine production tasks.
Employees perform better when they have fun.
In large corporations with a hierarchy of power, there is often no outlet for stress.
“Every company needs underground ways of poking fun at the organization,” says Lynn N. Mark, a speaker on workplace humor for St. Mary’s Health Centre in St. Louis.
Kodak’s Rochester, New York branch, discovered a way for its 20,000 employees to uncork their bottomed-up resentments.

Public interest was aroused by the latest discovery of a changed gene in obese mice.
The news was made known by Rockefeller University geneticist Jeffrey Friedman.
The researchers believe this gene influences development of a hormone that tells the organism how fat or full it is.
Those with the changed gene may not sense when they have eaten enough or if they have sufficient fatty tissue, and thus can’t tell when to stop eating.
The researchers also reported finding a gene nearly identical to the mouse obesity gene in humans.
The operation of this gene in humans has not yet been demonstrated, however.
Still, professionals like University of Vermont psychologist Esther Rothblum reacted enthusiastically.
This research indicates that people really are born with a tendency to have a certain weight, just as they are to have a particular skin color or height.
Actually, behavioral geneticists believe that less than half of the total weight variation is programmed in the genes, while height is almost entirely genetically determined.
Whatever role genes play, Americans are getting fatter.
A survey by the Center for Disease Control found that obesity has increased greatly over the last 10 years.
Such rapid change underlines the role of environmental factors, like the abundance of rich foods in Americans’ over eating.
The Center for Disease Control has also found that teens are far less physically active than they were even a decade ago.
Accepting that weight is predetermined can relieve guilt for overweight people.
But people’s belief that they cannot control their weight can itself contribute to obesity.

Qualities of a relationship such as openness, compassion and mental stimulation are of concern to most of us regardless of sex, but ‒ judging from the questionnaire response ‒ they are more important to women than to men.
Asked to consider the ingredients of close friendship, women rated these qualities above all others.
Men assigned a lower priority to them in favor of similarity in interests, selected by 77% of men, and responsiveness in a crisis, chosen by 61% of male respondents.
Mental stimulation, ranked third in popularity by men as well as women, was the only area of overlap.
Among men, only 28% named openness as an important quality; caring was picked by just 23%.
It is evident by their selections that when women speak of close friendships they’re referring to emotional factors, while men emphasize the pleasure they find in a friend’s company.
That is, when a man speaks of " a friend " he is likely to be talking about someone he does things with — a teammate, a fellow hobbyist, a drinking buddy.
These activities are the fabric of the friendship ; it is a “doing” relationship in which similarity in interests is the key bond.
This factor was a consideration of less than 11% of women.
Women opt for a warm, emotional atmosphere where communication flows freely; activity is mere background.
Lastly, men, as we have seen, have serious questions about each other’s loyalty.
Perhaps this is why they placed such strong emphasis on responsiveness in a crisis ‒ “someone I can call on for help.”
Women, as their testimonies indicate, are generally more secure with each other and consequently are more likely to treat this issue lightly.
In follow-up interviews this was confirmed numerous times as woman after woman indicated that being there when needed was taken for granted.
As for the hazards of friendship, more than a few relationships have been shattered because of cut-throat competition and feelings of betrayal.
This applies to both men and women, but unequally.
In comparison, nearly twice as many men complained about these issues as women.
Further, while competition and betrayal are the main thorns to female friendship, men are plagued in almost equal amounts by two additional issues, lack of frankness and a fear of appearing unmanly.
Obviously, for a man, a good friendship is hard to find.

The partial skeletons of more than 20 dinosaurs and scattered bones of about 300 more have been discovered in Utah and Colorado at what is now the Dinosaur National Monument.
Many of the best specimens may be seen today at museums of natural history in the larger cities of the United States and Canada.
This dinosaur pit is the largest and best preserved deposit of dinosaurs known today.
Many people get the idea from the massive bones in the pit wall that some disaster such as a volcanic explosion or a sudden flood killed a whole herd of dinosaurs in this area.
This could have happened, but it probably did not.
The main reasons for thinking otherwise are the scattered bones and the thickness of the deposit.
In other deposits where the animals were thought to have died together, the skeletons were usually complete and often all the bones were in their proper places.
Rounded pieces of fossil bone have been found here. These fragments got the smooth round shape by rolling along the stream bottom.
In a mass killing the bones would have been left on the stream or lake bottom together at the same level.
But in this deposit the bones occur throughout a zone of sandstone about 12 feet thick.
The mixture of swamp dwellers and dry-land types also seems to indicate that the deposit is a mixture from different places.
The pit area is a large dinosaur graveyard, not a place where they died.
Most of the remains probably floated down an eastward flowing river until they were left on a shallow sandbar.
Some of them may have come from far-away dry-land areas to the west.
Perhaps they drowned trying to cross a small stream or were washed away during floods.
Some of the swamp dwellers may have got stuck in the very sandbar that became their grave.
Others may have floated for miles before being stranded.
Even today, similar events take place .
When floods come in the spring, sheep, cattle and deer are often trapped by rising waters and often drown.
Their dead bodies float downstream until the flood recedes and leaves them stranded on the bar or shore where they lie, half buried in the sand, until they decay.
Early travelers on the Missouri River reported that shores and bars often were lined with the decaying bodies of buffalo that had died during spring floods.

I would like particularly to talk about the need to develop a new style of aging in our own society.
Young people in this country have been accused of not caring for their parents the way they would have in the old country.
And this is true, but it is also true that old people have been influenced by an American ideal of independence and autonomy.
So we live alone, perhaps on the verge of starvation, in time without friends, but we are independent.
This standard American style has been forced on every ethnic group, although there are many groups for whom the ideal is not practical.
It is a poor ideal and pursuing it does a great deal of harm.
This ideal of independence also contains a tremendous amount of unselfishness.
In talking to today’s young mothers, I have asked them what kind of grandmothers they think they’re going to be.
I hear devoted loving mothers say that when they are through raising their children, they have no intention of becoming grandmothers.
They were astonished to hear that in most of the world throughout most of its history, families have been, three- or four-generation families, living under the same roof.
We have over-emphasized the small family unit ‒ father, mother, small children.
We think it is wonderful if grandma and grandpa, if they’re still alive, can live alone.
We have reached the point where we think the only thing we can do for our children is to stay out of their way.
And the only thing we can do for our daughter-in-law is to see as little of her as possible.
Old people’s nursing homes, even the best run, are filled with older people who believe the only thing they can do for their children is to look cheerful when they come to visit.
So in the end, older people have to devote all their energies to “not being a burden.”
We are beginning to see what a tremendous price we've paid for our emphasis on independence and autonomy.
We've isolated old people and we've cut off the children from their grandparents.
One of the reasons we have as bad a generation gap today as we do is that grandparents have stepped out.
Young people are being deprived of the thing they need most ‒ perspective, to know why their parents behave so peculiarly and why their grandparents say the things they do.

sections.passage: 1 The Romance of the Three Kingdoms, which was written in the fourteenth century, is a famous historical novel in China. 2 Based on the history of the Three Kingdoms period, this novel describes the war between Wei, Shu and Wu from the second half of the second century to the second half of the third century. 3 It depicts nearly a thousand characters and countless historical events. 4 Although these characters and events are based on the real history, they are dramatized and exaggerated to varying degrees. 5 The Romance of the Three Kingdoms is widely acknowledged to be a literary masterpiece. 6 Since its publication, it has attracted and deeply influenced generations of readers in China, and also has exerted an extensive and far-reaching influence on Chinese history.

1 The report from the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES) is clear on what's at 3 and what needs to change.? 2 IPBES chair Robert Watson says the 4 evidence " presents an " ominous (凶兆的) picture ".? 3 " The health of ecosystems on which we and all other species depend is 5 more rapidly than ever, " Robert Watson said.? 4 " We are 6 the very foundations of our economies, livelihoods, food security, health and quality of life worldwide. "? 5 The report says it's not too late if we make " transformative change " — fundamental, system-wide reorganization — at every level from local to global, and we need to focus on how to make that happen.
1 First, don't indulge in despair, because despair leads to inertia and doing nothing means certain 7.? 2 Every action to save nature will improve our collective and personal futures and the only way to respond to a threat of this scale is with 8 action rooted in headstrong optimism.? 3 Second we need relentless focus, just like when paramedics (救护人员) arrive on a scene and use the concept of " triage (伤员鉴别分类) " to ensure the most 9 cases get treated first.? 4 Saving the natural world needs that kind of thinking. 5 We don't have the 10 to do everything at once.? 6 We need to make hard choices.

questions.explanation:
【确定词性】

空格所在主句"it (主语) + naturally (状语) +_____+ headiness (宾语)”缺少谓语动词,结合时间状语从句When the report came out可知空格词应为及物动词过去式。

【答案解析】

首句介绍联合国最新报告发现:人类对自然的快速破坏导致地球上的生命面临生存威胁,③句中headlines, news agenda提示此两句探讨该报告受媒体关注的程度,两句借But转折,由③句“但这项报告并没有如重大恐怖袭击事件那般抢占新闻议程(hijack the news agenda)"可反向推知,空格句是在让步肯定“报告在发布之时取得了不少媒体关注”,G符合文意。

注: grab (the) headlines意为“占据新闻头条;成为新闻焦点”,强调事件刚刚发布时大受媒体关注; hijack the news agenda意为“抢占/劫持新闻议程”,强调媒体对事件的持续关注。

【确定词性】

_____of war与a major terrorist attack并列,空格词应为名词。

【答案解析】

由并列连词or前后语义同向可知,“_____战争”应与"重大恐怖袭击”同为重大事件,再结合整句可知,二者往往会获得新闻媒体的持续关注。备选项中B最合文意,declaration of war为固定搭配,意为“宣战”。

E) disaster符合词性要求,也符合空格处对“危机、灾难”等消极语义的要求,因此干扰性极强,但可以通过如下方法排除:1,由上述分析可知, _____of war应指向重大事件,而disaster代入空格处意为“战争造成的灾祸”,指向事件的影响;2. disaster在表示“某事造成的灾难/祸患/负面后果”时通常使用其复数形式。

【解题技巧】

26,27题的解答关键在于借助逻辑连词But, or确定句际或短语间的逻辑关系。由But可知②③句间为“让步一转折”逻辑,由此可判断“_____headlines"和"didn't hijack the news agenda"应语义对立。由or可知_____of war 与a major terrorist attack为并列语义,应共同指向“重大危机事件”。

【确定词性】

空格位于宾语从句what's at_____ 中,空格词应为名词或-ng分词,且能与at搭配

【答案解析】

空格句介绍IPBES发布的报告内容“明确了什么正处于_____,以及我们需要作出哪些改变”。结合首段报告发现“人类对自然的破坏正危及全球生命”可知,报告应先分析具体存在哪些问题(即人类活动对生态系统的哪些方面构成威胁),才能对症下药去寻求变革措施,空格词应表示“(处于)危险/灾难/危急情形”等意,M正确, at stake为固定搭配,意为“处于危险境地/生死攸关之际". E) disaster有干扰性,但其搭配为in a/the disaster。

【确定词性】

空格词所在宾语从句中, the " _____evidence"为主语,所以空格词可能为形容词、名词、ec分词或-ing分词(修饰名词evidence)

【答案解析】

空格句介绍IPBES主席Robert Watson之言:“_____证据”展现出“不祥的景象”。其中“不羊的景象”照应上文报告发现“人类活动正威胁到地球上所有生命”,再据由“证据→发现/结论”的常识逻辑可,报告发现应当有大量的/确凿的证据作支撑,K符合要求。

【确定词性】

空30所在主句结构为"The health of ecosystems (主语) +is+_____+more rapidly than ever (状语)",根据副词rapidly(表示动作的快慢)可排除空格词为名词或形容词(作表语)的情况,确定空格词应为不及物动词的-ing分词(构成进行时态)或-ed分词(构成被动语态),且更可能是强调变化的-ing分词。

【答案解析】

第二段③④句继续引述Robert Watson的话语,指出“人类及其他物种所依赖的生态系统的健康状况正以前所未有的速度_____ ;我们正在_____我们的经济、生计等的根基”。其中,空30前的“生态系统的健康状况”指向“自然环境(nature)",再结合空格前句“大量证据呈现出不祥的景象”以及后句“如果我们能作出"变革性改革,还为时未晚”可知,此空应填入“恶化/破坏”等表示消极趋势的词汇,以实现“问题一表现一对策”的呼应衔接。C) deteriorating(“恶化;变坏”)为不及物动词,符合空30词义及词性要求

【解题技巧】

报告/研究负责人的话语往往是对报告内容及意义的总结提炼,应与文中对报告的相关介绍一致,解题时需寻找对应信息。空30,31所在句均为报告相关负责人Robert Watson的话语,故应与首段报告发现humans are destroying nature at such a rate that life on Earth is at risk、第二段首句报告内容what's at stake and what needs to change、下文报告所述解决对策it's not too late if we make "transformative change"形成照应,才能实现上下文语义的连贯一致。

【确定词性】

空31前为We are,后为名词短语the very foundations of..,空格词可能是及物动词的-ing分词(构成进行时态)或副词(构成主系表结构）。

【答案解析】

第二段③④句继续引述Robert Watson的话语,指出“人类及其他物种所依赖的生态系统的健康状况正以前所未有的速度_____ ;我们正在_____我们的经济、生计等的根基”。其中空31后的“经济、生计等的根基”指向“自然环境(nature)",再结合空格前句“大量证据呈现出不祥的景象”以及后句“如果我们能作出"变革性改革,还为时未晚”可知,此空均应填入“恶化/破坏”等表示消极趋势的词汇,以实现“问题一表现一对策”的呼应衔接。F) eroding(“损害;削弱")可作及物动词,符合空31词义及词性要求。

【解题技巧】

报告/研究负责人的话语往往是对报告内容及意义的总结提炼,应与文中对报告的相关介绍一致,解题时需寻找对应信息。空30,31所在句均为报告相关负责人Robert Watson的话语,故应与首段报告发现humans are destroying nature at such a rate that life on Earth is at risk、第二段首句报告内容what's at stake and what needs to change、下文报告所述解决对策it's not too late if we make "transformative change"形成照应,才能实现上下文语义的连贯一致。

【确定词性】

空格所在分句结构为"doing nothing(动名词短语作主语)+ means(及物动词作谓语)+certain_,空格词应为名词,作certain______的修饰对象、means的宾语。

【答案解析】

第二段末句提出问题“如何实现变革性改变(how to make that happen)",末段①句(空格句先指出第一项做法“不要沉沦于绝望”,并解释原因“绝望会导致懒惰,不作为意味着某种______”。可见本句是在暗示人们要采取行动,空格词应表示“(什么都不做会导致)灾难/困境/危害"等负面结果,E正确。

L) stagnation有较强干扰,但“停滞”仅为“懒惰(inertia)/不作为(doing nothing)"的同义表述,无法体现means所暗藏的因果逻辑“懒惰/不作为/停滞导致危害”,故排除。

【确定词性】

空格所在分句主干为"the only way(主语)+is(系动词)+ with______action(介宾结构作表语)",空格词应作名词action的修饰成分,可能为名词、形容词、ed分词、-ing分词。

【答案解析】

空格所在句指出,采取行动拯救自然会改善人类的未来,采取根植于顽强乐观主义的______行动是解决环境威胁的唯一方法。空格词应体现积极正向的色彩,且呼应the only way(唯一方法),a threat of this scale(如此大规模的威胁)以及headstrong optimism(顽强的乐观主义)所体现的“任务艰巨性/行动必要性/坚决性",D正确。

【解题技巧】

借助因果关联词明确逻辑链条。末段①②句借助多个显性/隐性因果关联词(because. leads to means, will, the only way to)构建两条逻辑链:1.陷入绝望一懒惰/不作为→______ ;2.采取______行动一应对当前巨大的环境威胁&改善人类的未来。两条逻辑链恰为正反论证,表达同一语义,由此可明确两空答案。

【确定词性】

空格词位于ensure的宾语从句(that) the most______ cases get treated first中,空格前为最高级标志the most,后为名词cases,空格词应为形容词。

 

【答案解析】

末段③句先概述指出拯救自然的第二项做法“我们需要relentless focus",随后以just like....类比解释：就像救护人员抵达现场后会采用“伤员鉴别分类”概念来确保最______病例最先得到治疗。结合常识、relentless focus的大概含义,以及句子逻辑可推知类比解释关系:救护人员要确保最紧急的/严重的病例最先得到治疗à拯救自然也需要类似的“残酷聚焦（虽然都亟待处理，但还是必须要做出艰难的选择，先处理最为紧急的事情）”。故O正确。

【确定词性】

空格前为We don't have the,空格后为不定式to do everything...,可推知空格词应为名词,与the共作have的宾语。

【答案解析】

空格句及前后句三句一体,指出拯救自然界需要这种思维(残酷聚焦:确保最紧急的事情最先得到处理）; 我们没有_____来同时做所有的事情;我们需要作出艰难的抉择。可见,作者是在呼吁人们在能力/精力/资源有限的情况下要作出取舍,率先解决最紧急的事情,A正确。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Until a few decades ago, scholars believed that young children know very little, if anything, about in what others are thinking. 2 Swiss psychologist Jean Piaget, who is credited with founding the scientific study of children's thinking, was convinced that preschool children cannot consider what goes on in the minds of others. 3 The interviews and experiments he conducted with kids in the middle of the 20th century suggested that they were trapped in their subjective viewpoints, incapable of imagining what others think, feel or believe.?
1 Much of the subsequent research on early childhood thinking was highly influenced by Piaget 's ideas. 2 Scholars sought to refine his theory and empirically confirm his views. 3 But it became increasingly clear that Piaget seemed to have gravely underestimated the intellectual powers of very young kids before they can make themselves understood by speech. 4 Researchers began to devise ever more ingenious ways of figuring out what goes on in the minds of babies, and the resulting picture of their abilities shows subtle variations. 5 Consequently, the old view of children's egocentric (自我中心的) nature and intellectual weaknesses has increasingly fallen out of favor and become replaced by a more generous position that sees a budding sense not only of the physical world but also of other minds, even in the "youngest young."?
1 Historically, children didn't receive much respect for their mental powers. 2 Piaget not only believed that children were "egocentric" in the sense that they were unable to differentiate between thein own viewpoint and that of others; he was also convinced that their thinking was characterized by systematic errors and confusions. 3 When playing with others, they don't cooperate because they do not realize there are different roles and perspectives. 4 He was convinced that children literally cannot "get their act together": instead of playing cooperatively and truly together, they play side by side, with little regard for others. 5 And when speaking with others, a young child supposedly cannot consider the listener's viewpoint but "talks to himself without listening to others.?
1 Piaget and his followers maintained that children go through something like a dark age of intellectual development before slowly and gradually becoming enlightened by reason and rationality as they reach school age. 2 Alongside this enlightenment develops an ever-growing understanding of other persons, including their attitudes and views of the world
1 Today, a very different picture of children's mental development emerges. 2 Psychologists continually reveal new insights into the depth of young children's knowledge of the world, including their understanding of other minds. 3 Recent studies suggest that even infants are sensitive to others' perspectives and beliefs.?
1 Part of the motivation to revise some of Piaget's conclusions stemmed from an ideological shift about the origin of human knowledge that occurred in the second half of the 20th century. 2 It became increasingly unpopular to assume that a basic understanding of the world can be built entirely from experience. 3 This was in part prompted by theorist Noam Chomsky, who argued that something as complex as the rules of grammar cannot be picked up from exposure to speech, but is supplied by an inborn "language faculty." 4 Others followed suit and defined further "core areas' in which knowledge allegedly cannot be pieced together from experience but must be possessed at birth. 5 One such area is our knowledge of others' minds. 6 Some even argue that a basic knowledge of others' minds is not only possessed by human infants, but must be evolutionarily old and hence shared by our nearest living relatives, the great apes.?
1 To prove that infants know more in this realm than had been acknowledged, researchers needed to come up with innovative ways of showing it. 2 A big part of why we now recognize so much more of kids' intellectual capacities is the development of much more sensitive research tools than Piaget had at his disposal.?
1 Instead of engaging babies in dialog or having them execute complex motor tasks, the newer methods capitalize on behaviors that have a firm place in infants' natural behavior repertoire: looking, listening, sucking, making facial expressions, gestures and simple manual actions. 2 The idea of focusing on these "small behaviors" is that they give kids the chance to demonstrate their knowledge implicitly and spontaneously without having to respond to questions or instructions. 3 For example, children might look longer at an event that they did not expect to happen, or they might show facial expressions indicating that they have sympathetic concern for others. 4 When researchers measure these less demanding, and often involuntary, behaviors, they can detect a sensitivity to others' mental states at a much younger age than with the more taxing methods tha Piaget and his followers deployed.?
1 In the 1980s, these kinds of implicit measures became customary in developmental psychology. 2 But it took a while longer before these tools were employed to measure children's grasp of the mental lives of others.
1 In a set of experiments, my colleagues at the University of Southern California and I found evidence that babies can even anticipate how others will feel when their expectations are disappointed. 2 We acted out several puppet (木偶) shows in front of two-year-old children. 3 In these puppet shows, a protagonist (Cookie Monster) left his precious belongings (cookies) on stage and later returned to fetch them. 4 What the protagonist did not know was that an antagonist had come and messed with his possessions. 5 The children had witnessed these acts and attentively watched the protagonist return. 6 We recorded children's facial and bodily expressions. 7 Children bit their lips, wrinkled their nose or wiggled (扭动) in their chair when the protagonist came back, as if they anticipated the bewilderment and disappointment he was about to experience. 8 Importantly, children showed no such reactions and remained calm when the protagonist had seen the events himself and thus knew what to expect. 9 Our study reveals that by the tender age of two, kids not only track what others believe or expect; they can even foresee how others will feel when they discover reality.?
1 Studies like this reveal that there is much more going on in small kids' and even infants' minds than was previously believed. 2 With the explicit measures used by Piaget and successors, these deeper layers of kids' understanding cannot be accessed. 3 The new investigative tools demonstrate that kids know more than they can say: when we scratch beneath the surface, we find an emerging understanding of relations and perspectives that Piaget probably did not dream of.
1 Despite these obvious advances in the study of young children's thinking, it would be a grave mistake to dismiss the careful and systematic analyses compiled by Piaget and others before the new tests dominated the scene because the original methods revealed essential facts about how children think that the new methods cannot uncover.?
1 There's no consensus in today's science community about how much we can infer from a look, a facial expression or a hand gesture. 2 These behaviors clearly indicate a curiosity about what goes on in the mind of others, and probably a set of early intuitions coupled with a willingness to learn more. 3 They pave the way to richer and more explicit forms of understanding of the minds of others. 4 But they can in no way replace the child's growing ability to articulate and refine her understanding of how people behave and why.?

questions.explanation:
【题干翻译】

皮亚杰认为幼儿在玩耍时不能相互协作。


【定位】

36题could not collaborate with others while playing应C段③句When playing with others... don't cooperate...及④句instead of playing cooperatively.

 

【答案解析】

C段③④句呈现皮亚杰对幼儿玩耍行为的观察“他们不会相互协作,而是各玩各的,因为他们意识不到玩耍时别人的视角和角色与自己不同”,试题是对两句内容的提取及改写。

【题干翻译】

作者与其同事的研究表明,两岁儿童可能具备预料他人感受的能力。

 

【定位】

37题The author and his colleagues' study对应J段首句my colleagues. .. and I found... two-year-olds复现②句two-year-old children. J段首句中作者与其同事的研究发现可匹配37题核心义。

 

【答案解析】

首句概述作者及其同事的研究发现“幼儿可预料他人感受”,下文介绍实验过程,并明确实验对象“两岁儿童”。试题是对首句研究发现的同义改写,may be able to predict对应can... anticipate.

【题干翻译】

上世纪下半叶,认为“人类对世界的认识完全基于经验”的人越来越少。

 

【定位】

38题In the latter half of the last century替换F段①句in the second half of the 20th century wholly empirical对应②句built entirely from experience.①②句人们观念的转变“知识完全基于经验,这一观念失去市场”可匹配38题核心义。

 

【答案解析】

F段①句指出对皮亚杰儿童自我中心论的修正源于20世纪下半叶的一次观念转变,②句介绍具体转变趋向“"仅靠经验就能建立起对世界的基本认知,的设想越来越不流行”。试题是对两句内容的归纳概括,其中fewer and fewer people believed对应It became increasingly unpopular to assume...

【题干翻译】

让·皮亚杰在上个世纪所做的研究表明,幼儿对他人的所思所想不敏感。

 

【定位】

Research conducted by Jean Piaget in the last century对应A段③句The interviews and experiments he conducted...in the middle of the 20th century, insensitive to others' thinking同义替换 incapable of imagining what others think.

 

【答案解析】

A段③句提及皮亚杰在20世纪中期的研究发现“儿童无法设想他人的想法、感受及观念",试题是对该句的提取及转述,其中babies为kids的下义词。

【题干翻译】

我们对幼儿智力的理解有所加深,这得益于研究工具的改进。

 

【定位】

40题is attributable to对应G段末句A big part of why... is... better research tools概括该句much more sensitive research tools。 G段末句大意“我们对儿童智力有了更多认识,主要原因在于研究工具更加灵敏”可匹配40题核心义。

 

【答案解析】

G段末句解释我们对儿童智力的理解有所加深的主要原因是研究工具更加灵敏。试题是对该句的同义改写,Our improved understanding of babies' intellectual power改写we now recognize so much more of kids' intellectual capacities。

【题干翻译】

近期研究发现即便是小婴儿也能敏锐地感知到他人的看法。

 

【定位】

41题recent research对应E段③句Recent studies , sensitive to other people's points of view复现该句sensitive to others' perspectives and beliefs.③句近期的研究发现“即便婴儿也对他人的视角敏感”贴合41题核心义。

 

【答案解析】

E段③句句介绍近期的研究发现“即便是婴儿也对他人的视角和观点敏感”,试题是对该句的同义改写,其中small babies同义替换infants。

【题干翻译】

我们能从儿童的某些身体表现中推断出什么信息,对此科学家仍争论不休。

 

【定位】

42题what inference can be drawn对应M段中的how much we can infer.M段首句大意“科学界尚未就'眼神、表情或手势能反映多少信息,达成共识”匹配42题核心义。

 

【答案解析】

M段首句指出科学界的现状“尚未就"我们可从某个眼神、表情或手势中推断出多少信息达成共识”。试题改写该句, Scientists are still debating对应There's no consensus in today's science community,明确“科学家尚未达成一致/仍在争论”的现状;certain physical expressions of a child概括a look, a facial expression or a hand gesture, of a child虽未在文中明示,但结合本段大意“儿童思维研究领域的新方法的局限性”可知,科学家争论的焦点是“我们能从儿童的眼神、表情、手势等自然行为中推断出多少有关其思维能力的信息”,因此of a child是对原文暗含信息的明示.

【题干翻译】

新研究方法不要求婴儿回答问题,而是关注他们的简单行为。

 

【定位】

43题newer research methods复现H段首句newer methods; simple behaviors概括首句behaviors... simple manual actions; answer questions同义替换①句respond to questions.①②句所述新方法的特点可匹配43题核心义.

 

【答案解析】

H段①②句通过对比凸显新研究方法的特点:观察婴儿已经牢牢掌握的自然行为,而非其对话、执行复杂肌肉运动的表现(对问题和指令的回应)。试题是对两句文意的概括, simple一词准确概括了②句中implicitly and spontaneously的内涵:新方法关注的是婴儿自然、自发的行为,即无需刻意引导就会做出的简单行为。

【题干翻译】

由于心理学的发展,“儿童天生以自我为中心、思维能力有限”这一传统观点的影响力越来越小。

 

【定位】

44题self-centered nature, limited thinking abilities分别同义替换B段⑤句egocentric nature、 intellectual weaknesses

 

【答案解析】

B段①句指出皮亚杰的“儿童自我中心论”最初对学界影响极大(subsequent指代皮亚杰学说建立后紧接着进行的研究),①至④句描述后世心理学者如何逐步另立门户“发现皮亚杰低估了儿童智力,采用新的方法评估,得出不同发现”,⑤句指出这种进步的最终结果“导致"儿童自我中心论,日渐失宠”。本题是对上述因果关系的归纳概括,其中progress in psychology对应①至④句后世学者循序渐进的研究进程, With(后接原因)呼应Consequently.

【题干翻译】

尽管儿童认知能力研究已取得显著进展,但否定皮亚杰的奠基性贡献不可取。

 

【定位】

45题marked advances同义替换L段obvious advances; it is wrong to dismiss对应it would be a grave mistake to dismiss. L段大意“尽管幼儿思维研究取得了显著的进步,但否定皮亚杰的重要贡献不可取”可匹配45题核心义。

 

【答案解析】

本段强调应正视皮亚杰的学术贡献,试题是对段落大意的概括。Even though...对应Despite...; Piaget's fundamental contributions...对应the careful and systematic analyses compiled by Piaget and others,概括了皮亚杰的重要贡献。

sections.title: Section C passage 1
sections.passage:
1 People often discuss the dangers of too much stress, but lately a very different view of stress is gaining popularity: this view of stress, held by members of the positive stress movement, argues that stress might actually be beneficial.? 2 The positive stress movement is made up of people such as Zachary Rapp who are looking for an edge in a competitive world, and Rapp's routine is a good example of followers of the movement. 3 He wakes up most mornings at dawn, goes for a run, sips black coffee while ripping through emails, and then steps into freezing cold shower. 4 This is a routine designed to reduce the stress of running simultaneously three different health and biotechnology companies for 18 hours a day.
1 Although Rapp's practices may sound extreme, he is part of a growing movement, consisting largely of tech industry workers who claim that such radical tactics will help them live better and longer.? 2 Inspired by influential figures in different fields, including entertainers, athletes, entrepreneurs and scientists, positive stress practitioners seek out some combination of extreme temperatures, restrictive diets, punishing exercise routines and general discomfort.
1 Rapp argues that positive stress keeps him balanced. 2 In addition to running and freezing showers, Rapp uses ice baths, hot yoga, and unconventional eating practices such as eliminating dairy, sugar, alcohol and various other foods high in carbohydrates.? 3 He believes that these practices, which put stress on his body, actually make him feel less stress from work. 4 However, Rapp does not credit anyone in particular for his choices; he said he started using these methods in college, where he got into the habit of taking ice baths to recover from sports. 5 He got back into it while trying to get his three companies off the ground.
1 Rapp works long hours and sleeps only five to seven hours a night but he said he only gets sick once a year. 2 For him, the difference between day-to-day stress, like the kind we feel when moving apartments, and positive stress is that the latter involves pushing the body to extremes and forcing it to build up a tolerance.?
1 One thought leader in the positive stress world is Dutch extreme athlete Wim Hof, who earned the name "ice man" for his ability to withstand severe cold using deep breathing exercises. 2 Hof 's ideas have become popular among tech industry elites and, thanks to Hof, cold showers are now a trend; indeed some even call it a form of therapy.
1 But it is important to note that not everyone agrees with these practitioners; indeed, some medical professionals argue that positive stress is not for everyone, and that it might even be dangerous for people who are unhealthy or older.?

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What do we learn about followers of the positive stress movement?

关于积极压力运动的追随者,我们了解到什么？

A) They are usually quite sensitive to different types of stress.

他们通常对不同类型的压力很敏感

B) They hold a different view on stress from the popular one.

他们对压力的看法与大众看法不同。

C) They derive much pleasure from living a very hectic life.

他们从极其忙碌的生活中获得许多乐趣,

D) They gain a competitive edge by enjoying good health.

他们因享有健康的体魄而获得竞争优势。

 

【定位及答案】

本题考查“积极压力运动追随者”的相关事实,可定位至1段(the positive stress movement, followers of the movement)。1段①句借由转折词but就常规看法(often)与新近非常规看法(lately a very different view)作出详细对比:普通大众通常认为,压力过大危害重重vs积极压力运动者们则认为,压力实际可能有益。由此可知B正确, They hold a different view on stress from. ..改写a very different view of stress. .. held by..., the popular one对应People often...

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【偷换概念&反向干扰】：该选项利用1段①句different, stress等词汇捏造干扰,将文中“不同类型的压力观”窜改为“不同类型的压力”，且quite sensitive to. ..stress“极易受压力影响”与第四段文意“积极压力运动的追随者具有更强的身体忍耐力,抗压性更强”相悖。

C选项【偷换概念】：该选项将1段④句reduce the stress of running. . . for 18 hours a day“减轻繁忙工作带来的压力”歪曲为“从繁忙工作中获得乐趣".

D选项【偷换概念】：该选项混淆逻辑关系:首段②句looking for an edge...提示“寻找竞争优势”是积极压力运动成员/追随者的目的,2段①句help them live better and longer提示“享有健康”是积极压力运动带来的结果,而选项则将其因果倒置为“通过享有健康(手段)获得竞争优势(结果)。

 

【解题思路】

开篇对比处常为出题点所在。首句虽较长,但对比标志明显(but体现转折,其前的People often...体现大众看法,其后的lately a very different view...体现新奇观点),再借助冒号(特殊标点符号)的解释说明作用,可知该新奇观点由积极压力运动成员/追随者所持有,故可以很快理清对比信息“不同的压力观(大众观点vs追随者观点)",锁定正确项B。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What do followers of the positive stress movement usually do to put their ideas into practice?

积极压力运动的追随者通常做什么来将他们的想法付诸实践?

A) They keep changing their living habits.

他们不断改变自己的生活习惯。

B) They network with influential figures.

他们与具有影响力的人物交往。

C) They seek jobs in tech industries.

他们在科技行业求职。

D) They apply extreme tactics.

他们使用极端的策略。

 

【定位及答案】

本题考查积极压力运动追随者将理念付诸实践的具体做法,根据题干关键词followers of the positive stress movement, put their ideas into practice及试题命制先后顺序原则定位至2段(practices positive stress practitioners seek out...)。注:practitioners“实践者,从事者”实际暗藏“将知识理论等付诸实践的人”之意,对应题干中put.., ideas into practice. 第二段①句首先指出，以拉普为代表的积极压力运动参与者采取的是极端做法、激进策略;②句随后阐释,实践者们寻求极端温度、限制性饮食、魔鬼式锻炼等的混合体验。可见,该运动的实践者/追随者将想法付诸实践的具体做法是使用极端的策略,D正确, extreme tactics是对段中practices…extreme, radical tactics, some combination of extreme temperatures, restrictive diets, punishing exercise routines and general discomfort所展示的语义场的高度凝练。

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【反向干扰】：该选项由②句seek out some combination of...推导出“运动成员在生活方式上做出了改变”,但首段末句routine提示这种新的生活方式已成为一种日常惯例,而非在不断改变(keep changing),

B选项【偷换概念】：该选项将②句“运动成员采取极端策略的原因:受到有影响力的人物的启发”曲解为“运动成员采取的策略:与有影响的力人物交往”。

C选项【偷换概念】：该选项将①句“运动成员的身份:大多为科技工作者”偷换为“运动成员的行为:在科技行业找工作”。

 

【解题思路】

本题实际考查对第二段长难句的理解及其与上下文的联系。解题需：

一、认识到第二段①句中such radical tactics实际回指Rapp's practices. .. extreme"拉普所采取的那些极端做法”,既概指上段具体人物事例Rapp's routine. .. He wakes up. . . and then steps into a freezing cold shower, 也概指下句积极压力运动践行者的集体行为positive stress practitioners seek out some combination of extreme temperatures... general discomfort.

二、借助语法知识准确切分句子并提取关键信息(追随者做法“采取激进策略”、追随者身份“科技行业工作者”、追随者灵感来源“受到有影响力的人物的启发”);

三、借助近、同、上、下义等语义关联建构核心语义场, (practices...) extreme, radical (tactics)、extreme (temperatures ), restrictive (diets)punishing (exercise routines) 、general discomfort共同指向“挑战身体极限的、令周身都很难受的方法”。在梳理上下文关联、提取关键信息、构建语义场的过程中不仅锁定了正确项,同时也排除了干扰项。

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What does Zachary Rapp say about his unconventional practices?

关于他的非常规做法,扎卡里·拉普说了什么？

A) They help him combat stress from work.

它们帮助他应对工作压力

B) They enable him to cut down living expenses.

它们使他能够削减生活开支。

C) They enable him to recover from injuries and illnesses.

它们使他能够从伤病中恢复。

D) They help him get three companies enlisted all at once.

它们帮助他同时成立三家公司。

 

【定位及答案】

本题考查“拉普如何看待自身的非常规做法”,题干关键词unconventional practices复现于3段②句，可定位至此。第三段②句提到拉普的非常规做法,③句进而给出拉普的观点“这些做法实际上可以让他感受到的工作压力更少”，即“有助于他应对工作压力”,故A正确。

 

【错误选项分析】

B选项【过度推理】：B干扰来自②句“不吃乳制品、糖、酒精以及其他各种高碳水化合物食物”,但这是在介绍非常规饮食法本身的特征,不能主观推出拉普对该饮食法的看法“有助于节省生活开支”。

C选项【偷换概念】：该选项将④句冰浴/非常规做法的促进对象“运动后的恢复”篡改为“伤病后的恢复”。

D选项【张冠李戴】：该选项将末句事实陈述“拉普因需同时让三家公司顺利开张而压力重重，故而重拾冰浴习惯”当作拉普的观点“冰浴/非常规习惯有助于同时成立三家公司”

 

【解题思路】

本题考查人物观点,可在定位段搜寻观点来源句(①句Rapp argues. ..)句He believes. ...④句 he said he...), 比对观点句内容与选项内容, 发现正确项A与原文图句完全对应。但需注意, 干扰项大多并非出自观点来源句，考生切忌利用客观事实主观臆断人物观点(如B和D).

questions.explanation:
【题干及选项概览】

What can be inferred from the passage about day-to-day stress?

从文中我们可以推断出关于日常压力的什么信息？

A) It is harmful to one's physical and mental health.

它会损害人们的身心健康。

B) It does not differ in essence from positive stress

它和积极压力没有本质区别。

C) It is something everybody has to live with.

它是每个人都必须忍受的事物,

D) It does not help build up one's tolerance.

它无助于增强人们的忍耐力。

 

【定位及答案】

本题考查“日常压力”的相关信息。由题干关键词day-to-day stress可定位至4段②句。4段②句指出日常压力与积极压力的区别;后者(即积极压力)能通过把身体推向极限的方式来提高身体忍耐力。换言之，日常压力无助于增强人体忍耐力,故D正确,同时排除B.

 

【错误选项分析】

A选项【常识干扰&偷换概念】：该选项由末句involves pushing the body to extremes“将身体推向极限”以及常识“压力有损身心健康”臆断而来,该信息实际指向的是“积极压力”而非“日常压力".

C选项【词汇干扰】：该选项利用day-to-day的“日常/寻常”之意，tolerance"忍耐力”等碎片信息以及末段信息“积极压力并不适用于所有人”捏造出原文未提及的信息“日常压力是所有人都必须忍受的寻常事”。

 

【解题思路】

本题考查对文中信息的逻辑推理。解题关键是从“X区别于Y的优点”反推出"Y的缺点",第四段2句主干结构可归纳为the difference between Y and X is that X involves. .. to build up tolerance, 即X相比于Y)的优点是“可增强耐力”,进而可反推出Y(相比于X)的缺点是“没有增强耐力的作用”。本题的另一个难点是A项非常贴合“压力影响身心健康”这一常识,有很强的干扰性,必须速览全文进行信息核实,确定中未论及此信息才能排除该项。
