questions.explanation:
【考点】名词辨析，考查根据上下文语境选择合适的名词，与 "cast a..."构成短语，来形象地表达负面能量对建立共识努力的影响。

【语法分析】"cast a..."为固定短语搭配，此处需要一个名词作宾语，根据语境要体现负面能量像投下某种东西一样影响后续努力，且 "a"提示名词为可数单数形式。

【解析】"shadow"作名词有 "阴影"的意思，"cast a shadow"表示 "投下阴影”，符合此处负面能量给建立共同理解的努力带来不良影响，像蒙上阴影的语境，所以答案是 L。

【考点】形容词辨析，要依据并列结构以及对积极氛围营造的描述，选择恰当的形容词修饰 "smiles”，使句子表达更符合逻辑。

【语法分析】"appreciation,... smiles, and warm comments"构成并列结构，此处需要一个形容词与另外两个并列的名词短语在词性和表意上相匹配，共同描述积极的元素，修饰 "smiles”。

【解析】"affectionate"意为 "充满深情的，亲切的”，"affectionate smiles”（亲切的微笑）与 "appreciation”（欣赏）、"warm comments”（热情的评论）一起从不同方面体现出积极的氛围，符合语境要求，答案是 A。

【考点】动词辨析，考查根据句子中对话氛围变化以及主从句的逻辑关系，选择合适的动词，同时要注意时态和主谓一致等语法点，且要与 "from...to..."搭配合理。

【语法分析】句子主语是 "the dialogue”，此处缺少谓语动词，根据语境描述的是对话状态的转变，且 "if"引导的条件状语从句用一般现在时表假设，主句常用一般将来时或一般现在时，结合选项应选择合适的动词第三人称单数形式，与 "from...to..."构成表示 "从…… 转变到……"的结构。

【解析】"flips"有 "（使）快速翻转，（使）突然转变"的意思，"flips from collaborative to adversarial"准确表达出如果对话气氛升温、愤怒爆发时，对话会从协作性转变为对抗性的意思，符合语境，答案是 F。

【考点】名词辨析，根据前文提到对话进展受阻以及 "come to an immediate..."这一常用表达结构，选择能体现进展停滞状态的名词。

【语法分析】"come to an immediate..."中需要一个名词，构成固定短语表示达到某种即时的结果或状态，结合前文说的对话转变为对抗性后对进展的影响，应选择表示停止、停滞相关含义的名词。

【解析】"halt"作名词意为 "停止，停顿”，"come to an immediate halt"表示 "立即停止，戛然而止”，符合此处表达对话进展因变为对抗性而马上停滞的语境，答案是 G。

【考点】副词辨析，考查根据句子中描述沉默一方的状态以及句子整体逻辑，选择合适的副词来修饰动词 "tires”，体现出通常情况下的状态特点。

【语法分析】"...tires of..."是谓语动词短语，此处需要一个副词修饰 "tires”，根据语境要体现出沉默的一方通常会出现厌烦这种情况的意思，所以要选择能体现一般性、通常性情况的副词。

【解析】"typically"表示 "通常，典型地”，"The silent partner typically tires of only listening"说明沉默的一方通常会对只是倾听感到厌烦，符合语境中对这种常见情况的描述，答案是 N。

【考点】形容词辨析，依据前文提到的对话不平衡情况以及说话者一方的感受，结合上下文逻辑选择合适的形容词来体现其感受特点。

【语法分析】"feel..."后需要一个形容词作表语，描述说话者的感受，根据前文提到的一方说得多，另一方沉默听得多这种不平衡状态，分析说话者相应的感受，选择合适的形容词。

【解析】"overburdened"意为 "负担过重的”，在这里说话者一直说得多，可能会感觉负担过重，符合语境中因对话不平衡导致的说话者的感受情况，答案是 H。

【考点】动词辨析，考查根据句子中关于不同语速和音量对对话对称性影响的描述，选择合适的动词原形，且要符合句子整体的逻辑和语法结构。

【语法分析】"can..."后需要接动词原形，构成谓语动词短语，结合语境表达不同语速和音量能够对对称性产生某种影响的意思，所以要选择能体现影响、破坏等相关含义的动词。

【解析】"erode"有 "侵蚀，削弱，破坏"的意思，"Different rates of speech and levels of voice volume can erode symmetry"表示不同的语速和音量水平会破坏对称性，符合语境中描述的对对话平衡产生不良影响的情况，答案是 D。

【考点】形容词辨析，根据前文提到一方意见更有分量以及句子中对表达风格影响的描述，选择合适的形容词来修饰 "style of expression”，以体现其能让意见更受重视的特点。

【语法分析】"more..."提示使用形容词比较级形式，修饰 "style of expression”，根据语境要体现出某种表达风格因为具有特定特点而使意见更有影响力，所以选择能体现积极、有力等相关含义的形容词比较级。

【解析】"vigorous"表示 "有力的，精力充沛的”，"more vigorous"修饰 "style of expression”，说明其表达风格更有力，进而使意见更有影响力，符合语境中一方意见因表达风格更有力而更受重视的情况，答案是 O。

【考点】副词辨析，结合前文提到一种观点容易被忽视以及句子整体逻辑，选择合适的副词来修饰动词 "is expressed”，体现出表达的方式特点导致其被忽视的情况。

【语法分析】"is expressed..."是被动语态结构，此处需要一个副词修饰动词 "expressed”，根据语境要体现出因为表达得比较怎样而使观点容易被忽视的意思，所以选择能体现不突出、不明显等相关含义的副词。

【解析】"tentatively"意为 "试探性地，不确切地”，"expressed more tentatively"表示表达得比较不明确、不坚定，这样的观点容易被忽视，符合语境中一种观点因表达特点而容易丢失的情况，答案是 M。

【考点】动词辨析，考查根据句子中关于对话双方若出现某种情况对对话模式的影响，选择合适的动词第三人称单数形式，且要符合句子整体逻辑和语法结构。

【语法分析】"either partner..."为主语，此处缺少谓语动词，根据语境表达如果任何一方持续做某事的意思，结合选项应选择动词第三人称单数形式，且要使句子整体表意符合改变对话模式会有帮助这一语境。

【解析】"predominates"有 "占主导地位，占优势"的意思，"either partner fairly consistently predominates"表示任何一方相当持续地占主导地位，会导致对话不平衡，所以改变这种模式会有帮助，符合语境要求，答案是 I。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Blue moons, rose moons, supermoons. 2 For some reason all the websites seem to think you really want to know all about these moons. 3 "Catch This Weekend's AMAZING SUPERMOON," one headline will announce. 4 "The Supermoon Isn't Actually A Big Deal And You're All Ruining Astronomy," another will complain.
1 The latest example is the super blood wolf moon eclipse which sounds like the name of an emotional song I would have performed a modern dance routine to in 9th grade, but is, in fact, an astronomical event set to occur on January 20. 2 As we'll explain below, there is nothing truly mysterious or otherwise special about this moon, and it will not look like a bloody wolf head in the sky or anything wild like that.? 3 We get these super lunar events by smashing together all the qualifiers we've historically used to keep track of full moons throughout the year, and in the age of the internet we can get a little too enthusiastic.
1 Consider this your go-to resource for all moon-gazing news. 2 Here's what you need to know about the latest lunar event.
1 Look, it's okay if you don't know. 2 There are probably loads of folks who walk around pretending they totally know why that thing in the sky seems to get bigger and smaller at regular intervals but who totally do not.?
1 The moon orbits Earth, and it's tidally locked — that means it always shows us the same face instead of spinning around like our planet does. 2 That's why you can always see the man on the moon (or the moon rabbit, depending on your cultural preferences) even as it spins around us. 3 But while the moon is big and bright in the sky when it's full, that's only because it's reflecting light from the sun. 4 But the moon is always moving, so it's getting hit with sunlight at different angles. 5 It's invisible to us during the new moon, because our satellite is parked right between us and the sun; the so-called dark side of the moon is lit up like Las Vegas, but the side we can see is in shadow.? 6 A full moon happens when the earth is right between the sun and the moon, so sunlight hits the part we can see. 7 And all the other phases are just the transition from one of those extremes to the other.
1 The moon isn't always exactly the same distance from Earth, because its orbit isn't perfectly circular.? 2 We call the closest point perigee (近地点), and the most distant point is apogee (远地点). 3 2018's closest perigee and most distant apogee both happened in January, and the difference was about 30,000 miles.
1 The reason you care about this ordinary change in distance is that it turns a moon super. 2 When a full moon happens close to perigee, it's going to look a bit bigger. 3 Honestly, the difference is not that profound, but if you're in a position to photograph the supermoon next to something that shows the slight increase in scale, it can look pretty cool.? 4 January's super blood wolf moon eclipse is super because the date lines up with the closest the moon will get to us during January, but the moon won't actually be at its closest for the year until February's supermoon, which you can expect plenty of undue excitement over.
1 Blood moons only occur during total lunar eclipses (which can happen a few times a year in any given location). 2 When the moon slips through our shadow, we give it a reddish coloring. 3 The moon can also look orange whenever it's rising or setting, or if it hangs low in the horizon all night — the light bouncing off of it has to travel through a thicker atmosphere there, which scatters more blue light away.? 4 But you'll probably only see that deep, sinister red during an eclipse.
1 A lot of headlines about moons are just ridiculous (you do not need to be particularly excited about a blue moon, it just looks like a regular full moon), but you should definitely roll out of bed to look at a blood moon if one is going to be visible in your region, even though they're just lunar eclipses and not evidence of bloody battles between the sky gods.
1 In March of 2018, we had our second "blue moon" of the year, to much acclaim. 2 And while that's not necessarily special in an oh-gosh-get-out-and-look-at-it way, it's certainly special: a blue moon is a nickname for when two full moon s fall in the same calendar month, and we hadn't previously had two in one year since 1999. 3 We won't have it happen again until 2037.? 4 Astronomer David Chapman explained that this is merely a peculiarity of our calendar; once we stopped doing things based on the moon and started trying to follow the sun and the seasons, we stopped having one reliable full moon per month. 5 The moon cycle is 29.53 days long on average, so in most months we still end up with a single new moon and a single full one. 6 But every once in a while, one month steals a full moon from another. 7 In 2018 (and in 1999, and again in 2037) both January and March stacked full moon s on the first and last nights of the month, leaving February in the dark.
1 Getting two blue moons a year is rare, but we have individual blue moons every few years. 2 Also, fun fact: not actually blue. 3 A moon can indeed take on a moody blue color, but this only happens when particles of just the right size disperse through the sky — and it has nothing to do with the moon's status as "blue."? 4 Big clouds of ash from volcanic eruptions or fires can do the trick, but it doesn't happen often, and the stars would certainly have to align for two such rare instances to occur at once.
1 You may have heard that the super special second blue moon of 2018 was also a Paschal moon. 2 This is true! 3 That just means it was the first full moon of spring, which is often used to determine the date of Easter Sunday. 4 All of this is just calendar nonsense and we refuse to go into it further.
1 Sometimes you'll see a headline that promises a moon with so many qualifiers it makes your head spin. 2 A super blue blood worm moon, perhaps? 3 Or a super blood wolf moon?? 4 Lots of websites will tell you that "wolf moon" is the traditional name of the first full moon of the year in "Native American" cultures, which is kind of a weird thing to claim given that there are 573 registered Tribal Nations in the U.S. alone today, not to mention historically. 5 The idea that hungry, howling wolves were such a universal constant in January that all of North America with its different cultures, geographies, and languages spontaneously came up with the same nickname is illogical.
1 Many cultures have traditional names for the full moon in a given month or season, so there's quite a list to draw from if you're trying to really juice up a story on a slightly-bigger-than-average view of the moon.? 2 But these are all based on human calendars and activities and folklore; you will not go outside and see a pink moon in April, though I wish it were so.

questions.explanation:
【定位】题目中的 “the moon is positioned right between the earth and the sun” 与 E 段第 5 句中的 “our satellite is parked right between us and the sun” 相对应，都表示月球位于地球和太阳之间；“We cannot see the moon” 与 “the so-called dark side of the moon is lit up like Las Vegas, but the side we can see is in shadow” 相对应，都表明这种情况下我们看不到月球。

【解析】根据对月球位置和我们能否看到月球的原理描述，E 段第 5 句准确解释了题目中月球在特定位置时我们看不到它的情况，所以答案是 E。

【定位】题目中的 “Volcanic eruptions” 与 K 段第 3 句中的 “Big clouds of ash from volcanic eruptions” 相对应；“cause the moon to assume a moody blue color” 与 “can do the trick（使月亮呈现蓝色）” 相对应，都表达了火山爆发会让月亮呈现蓝色的意思。

【解析】K 段第 3 句明确指出火山爆发产生的大量火山灰可以使月亮呈现蓝色，与题目内容匹配，所以答案是 K。

【定位】题目中的 “the supermoon occurs in February” 与 G 段第 3 句中的 “February's supermoon” 相对应，“The moon will be closest to the earth” 与 “the moon won't actually be at its closest for the year until February's supermoon” 相对应，都表明 2 月超级月亮出现时月球离地球最近。

【解析】G 段第 3 句提到了 2 月的超级月亮是当年月球离地球最近的时候，与题目意思相符，故答案为 G。

【定位】题目中的 “There is nothing unusual about the super blood wolf moon” 与 B 段第 2 句中的 “there is nothing truly mysterious or otherwise special about this moon” 相对应，“which will bear no resemblance to a bloody wolf head” 与 “it will not look like a bloody wolf head in the sky” 相对应，意思均为超级血狼月没什么特别且不会像血红色狼头。

【解析】B 段第 2 句对超级血狼月进行了说明，指出其没有特别之处且不像血红色狼头，与题目内容一致，所以答案是 B。

【定位】题目中的 “The moon will appear orange” 与 H 段第 3 句中的 “The moon can also look orange” 相对应，“the light reflecting from it travels through an atmosphere thicker than usual” 与 “the light bouncing off of it has to travel through a thicker atmosphere” 相对应，都说明了月球光线穿过厚大气层会呈现橙色。

【解析】H 段第 3 句解释了月球在什么情况下会呈现橙色，与题目表述一致，故答案为 H。

【定位】题目中的 “It is contrary to logic” 与 M 段第 3 句中的 “is illogical” 相对应，“claim the name of wolf moon originates from the cultures of American Indians” 与 “‘wolf moon’ is the traditional name of the first full moon of the year in ‘Native American’ cultures...is illogical” 相对应，都表达了认为狼月名字源于美洲印第安文化不合逻辑的意思。

【解析】M 段第 3 句明确指出认为狼月名称起源于美洲印第安文化是不合逻辑的，与题目内容相符，所以答案是 M。

【定位】题目中的 “the moon's orbit is not a hundred-percent circle” 与 F 段第 1 句中的 “its orbit isn't perfectly circular” 相对应，“its distance from the earth changes” 与 “The moon isn't always exactly the same distance from Earth” 相对应，都表明��球轨道非正圆导致其与地球距离变化。

【解析】F 段第 1 句说明了月球轨道不是完美圆形，所以与地球距离会变化，与题目内容一致，故答案为 F。

【定位】题目中的 “A full moon in a given month or season” 与 N 段第 1 句中的 “the full moon in a given month or season” 相对应，“gets a specific name in different cultures” 与 “Many cultures have traditional names” 相对应，都表示不同文化中特定月或季的满月有特定名称。

【解析】N 段第 1 句提到很多文化中特定月份或季节的满月有传统名称，与题目意思相符，答案是 N。

【定位】题目中的 “There are likely lots of people” 与 D 段第 2 句中的 “There are probably loads of folks” 相对应，“know absolutely nothing about why the moon appears to change its size regularly” 与 “pretending they totally know why that thing in the sky seems to get bigger and smaller at regular intervals but who totally do not” 相对应，都表明很多人不懂却装作懂月亮大小变化原因。

【解析】D 段第 2 句描述了有很多人不懂月亮大小变化原因却装作懂的情况，与题目内容一致，所以答案是 D。

【定位】题目中的 “When a full moon appears twice in the same month” 与 J 段第 3 句中的 “a blue moon is a nickname for when two full moons fall in the same calendar month” 相对应，都表达了一个月内出现两次满月被称为蓝月亮的意思。

【解析】J 段第 3 句对蓝月亮的定义进行了说明，即一个月内出现两次满月的情况，与题目内容相符，故答案为 J。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 With population increases and global urbanisation ever accelerating, much attention is focused on the sustainability of our cities and scarce attention is paid to the countryside.
1 Rural life is associated with closely-knit communities, sense of belonging, and a simple, tranquil life. 2 Yet whilst some or all of these elements exist in the countryside, so do conservatism and a lack of employment opportunities. 3 And it is mostly due to the latter that rural communities are suffering. 4 Attracted by the improved economics of urban areas, country-dwellers across the world are moving out, contributing to the excessive crowdedness of densely populated cities, and leaving the countryside in desolation.?
1 So how can the countryside ensure its survival among these changes, or should it at all? 2 Due to both the distance between residences and facilities and often intermittent public transport, those living in the countryside are heavier automobile users. 3 Rural dwellers also use more energy maintaining their mostly detached buildings. 4 We may be piled up like boxes in the city, but this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match. 5 Rural energy requirements result in higher carbon emissions per person than in the city, so it is actually irresponsible to endorse such a lifestyle choice.?
1 Protecting the countryside is a hot topic. 2 Those who have made their fortunes in the city often buy second homes in the countryside, visiting intermittently for a sample of a supposedly simple life. 3 The side-effect of this is that house prices are pushed up due to increased demand, leaving them unaffordable for local people. 4 A solution has yet to be found for this challenge, for market forces are further forcing residents out of the countryside. 5 For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable.?
1 Whilst an idealised view of the countryside is common, the reality is that rural life has continuously evolved. 2 Industrialisation brought an increase in divisions of labour, changing social links between rural people. 3 The internet has introduced once foreign cultures into the countryside. 4 Improved travel connections and affordability have made the world more accessible, creating a ‘global village’. 5 Considering these changes, surely an evolving countryside is inevitable.?
1 Perhaps the countryside should also prepare itself for massive population increases in the future. 2 With cities across the world growing rapidly, how will the current urban generation respond to the inevitable social changes of mass urbanisation? 3 Will the longing for a simpler life become stronger, fueling a rural renaissance?
1 As the world continues to urbanise, the voices calling for rural preservation may well grow louder. 2 But change is inevitable. 3 We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities, but the future of the countryside is less clear.?

综上可知，A选项"They are becoming somewhat deserted.（它们正变得有些荒芜）”与定位句中"leaving the countryside in desolation”表述相符，所以A选项正确。

根据题干中的定位关键词：the future of the countryside, compared with cities可以定位到文章7段3句：We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities（原词复现） growing into megacities, but the future of the countryside（原词复现） is less clear.

7段3句指出：我们知道（We know that）世界将会见证新的城市（the world is going to see new cities）从尘埃中崛起（emerging from the dust），现有的城市发展成为巨型城市（current cities growing into megacities），但乡村的未来（the future of the countryside）却不太明朗（is less clear）。

综上可知，作者对于乡村的未来持不确定的态度，认为和城市发展的明确趋势相比，乡村的未来的不太明朗。故D选项"It is less easy to envisage.（它的未来更难以想象。）”与定位句中"the future of the countryside is less clear”表述相符，所以D选项正确。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 Statements, like "beauty is in the eye of the beholder (观看者)," are rarely questioned.? 2 They’ve become so embedded in our consciousness that people think it’s absurd to think otherwise. 3 It might be useful, however, to at least push back on this assumption because people evaluate environment, situations, and people aesthetically. 4 We may find that we still believe it is correct, but we may also find that there is a lot more to the situation than you suppose.
1 A recent study exploring aesthetic taste was published in Cognition. 2 The results from this study show that people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects, but they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects.?
1 The study found that shared taste was most common for faces and natural landscapes, but least common among works of architecture and art. 2 The hypothesis is the commonly pleasing features, like proportion or symmetry, are at work.
1 Preferences for natural scenes might be learned through life experiences. 2 Factors like habitability, safety, and openness might be preferred as people develop. 3 Some of the details of landscapes change, but the basics are more common, e.g., water, open spaces, and signs of care.
1 Art and architecture, unlike natural spaces, do not have the same level of exposure. 2 So, people do not have the same level of shared taste.?
1 It’s possible that the lower amount of agreement in the shared taste of artifacts has to do more with elements of style, rather than ‘behavioral consequences.’
1 All of the consequences seem reasonable (or at least possible), but I think there might be an interesting philosophical conclusion that they did not draw. 2 It seems that there is an objective ground to our aesthetic preferences or evaluations. 3 I am not saying this would mean beauty is completely objective, just that there could possibly be general objective principles at work, i.e., beauty is not simply in the eye of the beholder.
1 Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world. 2 It’s not exactly the same everywhere, but it is common. 3 For example, a sunset is similar enough in different places to warrant almost universal appeal.?
1 Possible universal principles of beauty — such as proportion, fitness, radiance, and others — are general categories, which allow for a wide array of embodiments. 2 When people get involved in making artifacts in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways. 3 But the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal.?
1 This is why it’s important to experience diverse cultures and their artifacts because it opens us up to different ways of approaching or constructing beauty. 2 And it is always good to question our assumptions.

综上可知，A选项"It has hardly ever been disputed.（它几乎从未受到过争议。）”与定位句表述一致，故A选项正确。

根据题干中的定位关键词：a recent study exploring aesthetic taste可以定位到文章第2段1句：A recent study exploring aesthetic taste（原词复现） was published in Cognition.

2段1句：该句提出了题干中所描述的研究，但并未指出该研究的结果，故应继续阅读下句。

2段2句：该句为对研究结果的阐述，即：人们在对自然物体的审美评价上非常一致（people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects），但在对人工制品（artifacts），人造物品的（human-made objects）评价上则分歧较大（disagree more）。

综上可知，这项研究表明人们对自然物体审美评价上人们一致性高，而对人工制品的审美评价分歧更大。故C选项"There is less consensus on objects shaped by human craft.（人们对人工制作的物品的审美共识较少。）”与定位句中对人工制品审美分歧大相符，故C选项正确。

5段1句指出：与自然空间不同（unlike natural spaces）,艺术和建筑（art and architecture）没有相同的曝光程度（do not have the same level of exposure）,换而言之，也就是说艺术和建筑这种“人工制品”较少进入人们的视野，人们很少见到。

5段2句指出：所以（So），人们对艺术和建筑的共同品位（shared taste）水平也不尽相同（ do not have the same level ）。由句首的so可知上一句解释了原因，也就是题干所问的为什么人们对人工制品的审美评价存在差异。

综上可知，人们对人工制品的审美评价差异，是因为人工制品较少进入人们的视野,故D选项为对原文表意的同意替换，是正确��案。

根据题干中的定位关键词：artifacts，universal appeal”定位到文章9段2，3句：When people get involved in making artifacts（原词复现） in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways. But the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal（原词复现）.

9段2句指出：当人们参与建筑或艺术中的（in architecture or art）人工制品创作时（When people get involved in making artifacts），他们会以独特的方式（in unique ways）应用这些非常宽泛的概念（they apply these very general concepts）。

9段3句转折指出：但（But ）他们应用这些原则的方式（the way they applied the principle，其中they就指代2句中的artifacts）可能并不具有普遍的吸引力（may not have universal appeal.）

综上可知，人工制品创作者应用美的原则的独特方式可能不被所有人喜欢，所以不是总有普遍吸引力。故C选项"The way their creators apply the principle of beauty may not be pleasing to everybody.（创作者应用美的原则的方式可能并非让每个人都喜欢）”与定位句表述相符，故C选项正确。

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 The successful development of the Beidou Satellite Navigation System is a major scientific and technological achievement that China has made since its reform and opening-up. 2 Through unremitting efforts, researchers have overcome a series of technical difficulties. 3 Eventually, the Beidou system has achieved global coverage and successfully launched multiple navigation satellites. 4 This achievement not only makes China one of the few countries in the world that independently own global satellite navigation systems but also marks China's significant progress in the aerospace field. 5 The Beidou system is widely used in many fields such as transportation, disaster relief, weather forecasting, and public safety. 6 The successful application of the Beidou system has not only enhanced China's national defense capabilities but also provided more precise navigation services for the world. 7 As the Beidou system continues to be improved and developed, it will play important roles in more fields and bring more convenience to human life.

questions.stem: ①北斗（Beidou）卫星导航系统的成功研制是中国自改革开放以来取得的一项重大科技成就。②研发人员经过不懈努力，攻克了一系列技术难题。③北斗系统最终实现了全球覆盖，并成功发射了多颗导航卫星。④这一成就不仅使中国成为世界上少数几个独立拥有全球卫星导航系统的国家之一，也标志着中国在航天领域取得了显著的进步。⑤北斗系统广泛应用于交通运输、灾害救援、天气预报、公共安全等诸多领域。⑥北斗系统的成功应用，不仅提高了中国的国防实力，��为全球提供了更加精确的导航服务。⑦随着北斗系统的不断完善和发展，它将在更多的领域发挥重要作用，为人类的生活带来更多的便利。
questions.answer: 1 The successful development of the Beidou Satellite Navigation System is a major scientific and technological achievement that China has made since its reform and opening-up. 2 Through unremitting efforts, researchers have overcome a series of technical difficulties. 3 Eventually, the Beidou system has achieved global coverage and successfully launched multiple navigation satellites. 4 This achievement not only makes China one of the few countries in the world that independently own global satellite navigation systems but also marks China's significant progress in the aerospace field. 5 The Beidou system is widely used in many fields such as transportation, disaster relief, weather forecasting, and public safety. 6 The successful application of the Beidou system has not only enhanced China's national defense capabilities but also provided more precise navigation services for the world. 7 As the Beidou system continues to be improved and developed, it will play important roles in more fields and bring more convenience to human life.

questions.explanation:
【考点】形容词辨析，考查根据上下文语境选择合适的形容词来描述一种品质，且该词要与后文提到的不同生活方式观点形成关联。

【语法分析】“Being...” 此处需要一个形容词作表语，与系动词 “Being” 构成系表结构，用来表达某种状态或特性，在句子中作为被讨论的一种品质概念出现。

【题目解析】“thrifty” 意为 “节俭的”，前文提到人们思想随经济发展而变化，后文又列举了不同的生活方式偏好，这里说节俭不再被一些人视为美德，符合语境逻辑，所以答案是 O。

【考点】副词辨析，根据句子中对不同生活方式花费情况的描述，以及与其他并列成分的呼应，选择合适的副词来修饰动词 “spend”，体现花费的程度特点。

【语法分析】“spend...” 中 “spend” 为动词，需要一个副词来修饰它，表明花费的方式或程度，且与前文 “some prefer simplicity” 等形成并列对比，展现不同的消费风格。

【题目解析】“extravagantly” 表示 “奢侈地，挥霍无度地”，与前文提到的不同生活方式偏好相呼应，描述了一部分人在消费时大手大脚的情况，符合语境要求，答案是 B。

【考点】名词辨析，考查依据前文对乡村生活的描述以及句子整体表意，选择恰当的名词，使 “lose its...” 结构表达出乡村生活对 “我” 的某种影响变化情况。

【语法分析】“lose its...” 需要一个名词作宾语，构成动宾结构，表达失去某种东西的意思，根据语境应是体现乡村生活原本具有的、但可能会失去的某种吸引力、魅力等方面的含义。

【题目解析】“appeal” 作名词有 “吸引力，感染力” 的意思，“seldom loses its appeal” 表示很少失去其吸引力，符合 “我” 虽出身乡村、但即便处境变化后乡村生活仍对 “我” 有吸引力的语境，答案是 A。

【考点】动词辨析，根据句子中提到与新富阶层的互动以及整体语境，选择合适的动词原形，且要考虑该动词与 “with” 搭配后的表意合理性，来体现相应的社交行为。

【语法分析】“have an opportunity to...” 后接动词原形，构成不定式短语作后置定语修饰 “opportunity”，同时要与 “with” 搭配使用，表达有机会与某人进行某种行为的意思，结合语境应是表示社交互动方面的动作。

【题目解析】“mingle” 有 “（使）混合；交往，交际” 的意思，“mingle with” 表示 “与…… 交往，与…… 打成一片”，这里说有机会与新富阶层交往，符合语境中因自身处境变化而产生的社交体验描述，答案是 J。

【考点】名词辨析，考查根据后文关于世界借贷和消费趋势的描述，选择合适的名词来体现这种整体的状态或趋势情况，且要符合 “in a...” 这一常用结构搭配。

【语法分析】“in a...” 需要一个名词，构成介词短语，在句中作状语，描述世界所处的一种���态、情形，结合后文提到的借贷消费潮流，要选择能体现这种趋势性的名词。

【题目解析】“rage” 有 “风靡一时的事物；时尚；流行” 的意思，“in a rage” 在这里表示 “处于一种流行（的趋势）”，符合世界都流行借贷和消费这种语境，答案是 L。

【考点】名词辨析，根据句子中提到美国最富有强大却向别人借钱的反差情况，选择合适的名词来准确概括这种具有讽刺意味的现象。

【语法分析】“the...” 后需要一个名词作主语，结合语境要体现出句子所描述情况的一种性质、特点，即富有却借钱这种矛盾现象所对应的概念性名词。

【题目解析】“irony” 表示 “讽刺；具有讽刺意味的事”，用在此处能准确概括美国作为最富强国却向别人借钱这一充满讽刺意味的情况，答案是 D。

【考点】名词辨析，依据前文提到对相关现象的认知以及句子中表明自身在经济学方面身份的语境，选择合适的名词来体现自身的角色定位。

【语法分析】“a...” 提示此处需要一个可数名词单数形式，根据语境应是表达在经济学领域 “我” 的一种身份、角色，来引出后面关于经济学知识的阐述。

【题目解析】“layman” 意为 “外行，门外汉”，“a layman of economics” 表示经济学方面的门外汉，符合后文说自己至少知道一些经济学知识的语境，体现自己虽非专业但也有所了解的意思，答案是 E。

【考点】名词辨析，考查根据句子中关于借贷投资后角色转变以及与 “lender”（出借人）对比的描述，选择合适的名词来体现借入方变成的负面角色特点。

【语法分析】“turn...into the...” 结构中需要一个名词作宾语补足语，与 “the” 连用，表明借入方变成的对象，结合语境要体现与善良正派的出借人相对的负面角色概念。

【题目解析】“predator” 原指 “捕食者，食肉动物”，在这里可引申为 “掠夺者，剥削者” 的意思，体现借入方用借来的钱投资后可能变成不良的、类似剥削者的角色，与 “lender” 形成对比，答案是 K。

【考点】形容词辨析，根据句子中关于通过房产买卖获利的描述以及对这类人群特点的暗示，选择合适的形容词来修饰那些进行房产操作的人，体现其精明、善于把握机会的特点。

【语法分析】“Those who are...” 中 “are” 为系动词，后面需要一个形容词作表语，修饰先行词 “Those”（那些人），根据语境要体现那些在房产买卖中获利的人的一种特质。

【题目解析】“shrewd” 表示 “精明的，机灵的”，用来形容那些精明地从银行贷款买房然后高价卖出获利的人，符合语境对这类善于把握机会赚钱的人的描述，答案是 N。

【考点】动词辨析，结合前文提到贫困父母送孩子上大学以及句子整体表意，选择合适的动词原形，且要考虑 “scrape a living” 这一常用短语搭配，来体现他们艰难维持生计的情况。

【语法分析】“have to...” 后接动词原形，构成情态动词短语，结合语境要表达这些父母尽管处于艰难维持生活的状态但仍受益于送孩子上大学这一投资的意思，所以要选择能体现艰难维持生活的动词。

【题目解析】“scrape” 有 “艰难取得；勉强维持” 的意思，“scrape a living” 表示 “勉强维持生计”，符合语境中那些贫困但有远见的父母的生活状况描述，答案是 M。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 On a small fruit farm near the Straits of Malacca, Lim Kok Ann is down to just one tree growing kedondong, a crunchy, sour berry that Malaysians mostly use in pickles (腌菜) and salads. 2 “It’s not very well-known,” says the 45-year-old, who is instead focusing on longan (龙眼) berries and pineapples, which have bigger markets. 3 “We have to grow what is profitable,” he says.
1 But less than an hour away in the Malaysian countryside, inside three giant, silver domes, scientists are trying to change the future of food. 2 They’re pushing the boundaries of what humans eat by growing and processing so-called ‘alternative’ crops — such as kedondong. 3 At the headquarters of global research centre Crops For the Future (CFF) this particular under-used fruit has been turned into a sugar-free juice, high in vitamin C and getting top marks in sensory evaluations. 4 “Anything you see here is a forgotten crop,” says Sayed Azam-Ali of the abundant plants weaving through the gardens of CFF outside Malaysia’s capital Kuala Lumpur.
1 Prof Azam-Ali explains that just four crops — wheat, maize, rice and soybean — provide two-thirds of the world’s food supply. 2 “We’re dependent on these four,” he says. 3 “But actually there’s 7,000 crops we’ve been farming for thousands of years.? 4 We ignore all of those.” 5 Researchers are trying to unlock the potential of these ignored crops — plants they describe as forgotten, under-used or ‘alternative’ as they are displaced by increasingly uniform diets fuelled by processed ingredients from the major crops.
1 It’s a timely quest. 2 The food sector is already responsible for nearly a third of global greenhouse gas emissions. 3 By 2050 it estimates the world must produce 50% more food to feed the projected global population of 10 billion.? 4 Meeting this demand without contributing to climate change calls for urgent solutions.
1 Forgotten crops hold key answers. 2 By investing in neglected local plants, countries can reduce their reliance on imported crops and their carbon-heavy supply chains. 3 Bringing back the variety of crops humans once ate also boosts food security at a time warming climates threaten existing crops.? 4 On top of that forgotten crops are among the most climate-resilient (具有气候韧性的) and nutritious, argues Azam-Ali. 5 His summary is plain: “ Dietary diversification is critical to the future of humanity.”
1 Food security experts agree. 2 “There is no food insecurity in the world, there is food ignorance,” says Cecilia Tortajada, a senior research fellow at the Institute of Water Policy at the National University of Singapore. 3 “Whenever we have native crops we tend to disregard them as if they were not valuable but they are,” she adds.?
1 Azam-Ali knows that skepticism firsthand. 2 He came across alternative crops in the 1980s through the work of women farmers he met in Niger. 3 The then-PhD student remembers marvelling at the crops they grew in their backyards, without the benefits of technology, to feed their families when the big crops failed.? 4 He saw a tremendous opportunity to build alternative food systems. 5 But “the resistance was enormous,” he recalls.
1 Undeterred, he ploughed on. 2 Project after project helped prove these crops were viable in different environments as alternatives to the staple ones. 3 But the question of whether these crops would be marketable remained.? 4 “That’s the critical thing,” he says. 5 In one of the centre’s domes, food technologist Tan Xinlin uses powdered moringa (辣木) leaves in place of some wheat flour to bake a cake lower in gluten (谷胶) and higher in nutrients. 6 Tan’s job is to create recipes with these still-unfamiliar ingredients that will appeal to both local and international tastes. 7 In recent years she has used some of the forgotten crops grown at CFF, such as moringa and bambara groundnut, to make everything from instant soup to Indian snacks. 8 “I try to modernise forgotten crops instead of using old recipes,” says Tan, who is also a trained chef. 9 It’s a strategy to appeal to the world’s growing middle classes who are increasingly turning to the fast and processed food industries. 10 It’s also a way to help counter perceptions of local crops as “old or poor people 's food” or as inferior “women's crops”, adds Tan.
1 The roots of these connotations about local foods can run deep. 2 The bambara groundnut, a protein-rich native crop of sub-Saharan Africa that is also grown in parts of southeast Asia, can trace its marginalisation to colonial rule. 3 “African women who grew bambara groundnut were actually punished for growing it,” says Azam-Ali.? 4 “Colonial powers said you can't grow that because there's no oil. 5 We can't get a market for it.” 6 But today the bambara murukku is one of CFF's best-reviewed foods and they are aiming to get it into grocery stores, pointing to the success of crops like quinoa to potential investors. 7 Some 30 years ago, quinoa was virtually unheard of outside its native mountains in Bolivia and Peru. 8 Today the nutritious grain is found on the menus of lavish restaurants across the world.
1 Measuring crops by nutrition instead of yield is at the heart of the forgotten foods enterprise. 2 Ever since the “green revolution” of the 1960s, high-yielding crops have dominated modern agriculture.? 3 That was in part a crucial response to devastating famines at a time when the world needed to increase its food supply. 4 Today “nutrition is becoming a time bomb”, says Azam-Ali, as growing carbon dioxide levels strip crops of their minerals. 5 Instead of bio-fortifying major crops we should be investing in those forgotten crops that are already more nutritious, he asserts.
1 In the bowels of CFF's third dome, lab manager Gomathy Sethuraman opens a window into the centre’s “crown jewels”, revealing vines of winged beans growing under a bright yellow light. 2 It’s one of multiple chambers where scientists are studying the impact of higher temperatures and carbon dioxide levels on the nutritional make-up of alternative crops.? 3 This research is “the game changer", says Azam-Ali, ensuring that ‘future crops’ are also the healthiest ones in warmer climates.
1 There is a growing global momentum around forgotten foods, says Danielle Nierenberg, president of Food Tank, a US-based think tank. 2 Other than CFF, which bills itself as the world's first research centre dedicated solely to under-utilised crops, there are other key groups championing agricultural diversity including Crop Trust, Slow Food, Icrisat and Bioversity International. 3 Add to that more middle-income consumers searching for nutritious foods and others eager to try the unprocessed foods their grandparents once ate, she says.
1 But the rising interest in forgotten foods in some quarters is overtaken by the global spread of Western-style diets heavy in sugar, fat and processed foods in others.
1 A key obstacle to promoting fading local crops in Malaysia, for example, is “the obsession with imported products”, says Jenifer Kuah, co-founder of a restaurant that champions locally-sourced food in an affluent suburb of Kuala Lumpur. 2 Customers at Sitka, regarded as a pioneer in the country's small farm-to-table dining scene, still seek foreign ingredients as a “status symbol”, she says.
1 The argument for forgotten foods feels intuitive. 2 Some analysts say it is in fact inevitable. 3 “Climate change is going to mean almost certainly tastes are going to be forced to change,” says Tim Lang, professor of food policy at City University of London.? 4 We “have to get used to eating other crops” as yields of staple crops fall, he says.

questions.explanation:
【定位】题目中 “a senior researcher” 对应 F 段中的 “Cecilia Tortajada, a senior research fellow”；“rid ourselves of ignorance about native crops” 与 “Whenever we have native crops we tend to disregard them...but they are” 意思相近，都在说不能忽视本地作物；“have secure food supply” 与 “there is no food insecurity” 相对应，即重视本地作物就能保证粮食安全。

【解析】F 段中塞西莉亚・托尔塔哈达的话表明，人们对本地作物的忽视是粮食安全的问题所在，消除这种忽视，粮食就有保障，与题目表述相符，所以答案是 F。

【定位】“Most of the world's food supply” 对应 “two-thirds of the world’s food supply”；“a tiny number” 对应 “just four crops”；“thousands of crops that have been grown for centuries” 对应 “7,000 crops we’ve been farming for thousands of years”。

【解析】C 段指出世界粮食供应主要依赖小麦、玉米、大米和大豆这四种作物，而人类种植过的作物有 7000 种，与题目中大部分食物供应来自少数几种作物的意思一致，故答案为 C。

【定位】“provide their family with food when the staple crops failed” 与 “to feed their families when the big crops failed” 意思相同；“African women farmers” 对应 “women farmers he met in Niger”；“grew local crops in their backyards” 对应 “grew in their backyards”。

【解析】G 段中阿扎姆-阿里回忆在尼日尔遇到的女农民在主要作物欠收时，在后院种植本地作物养家，与题目内容相符，所以答案是 G。

【定位】“High-yielding crops” 与 “high-yielding crops” 对应；“occupied a dominant position” 与 “dominated” 对应；“since the green revolution in the last century” 与 “Ever since the ‘green revolution’ of the 1960s” 对应。

【解析】J 段明确提到自 20 世纪 60 年代绿色革命以来，高产作物主导了现代农业，与题目表述一致，故答案为 J。

【定位】“Growing alternative crops proved feasible” 与 “Project after project helped prove these crops were viable” 对应；“in a variety of environments” 与 “in different environments” 对应；“the critical question was whether they would be marketable” 与 “the question of whether these crops would be marketable remained” 对应。

【解析】H 段提到项目证明替代作物在不同环境可行，但市场性是关键问题，与题目内容匹配，答案是 H。

【定位】“a professor” 对应 “Tim Lang, professor of food policy”；“the yields of staple crops fall” 与 “yields of staple crops fall” 对应；“adapt to eating foods from alternative crops” 与 “have to get used to eating other crops” 对应。

【解析】O 段中蒂姆・朗教授说随着主粮作物产量下降，人们得习惯吃其他作物，与题目意思相符，答案为 O。

【定位】“Urgent measures” 与 “urgent solutions” 对应；“provide food for the projected world population” 与 “produce 50% more food to feed the projected global population of 10 billion” 对应；“without aggravating the climate” 与 “without contributing to climate change” 对应。

【解析】D 段提到到 2050 年要为 100 亿人口多生产 50% 的食物且不加剧气候变化需要紧急解决方案，与题目意思一致，答案是 D。

【定位】“Colonial rule marginalised local crops” 与 “bambara groundnut...can trace its marginalisation to colonial rule” 对应；“punishing Africans who grew them” 与 “African women who grew bambara groundnut were actually punished for growing it” 对应。

【解析】I 段以班巴拉花生为例，说明殖民统治惩罚种植本地作物的非洲妇女，使本地作物边缘化，与题目表述相符，答案是 I。

【定位】“existing crops are endangered by global warming” 与 “warming climates threaten existing crops” 对应；“increase food security” 与 “boosts food security” 对应；“bringing back the many forgotten food crops” 与 “Bringing back the variety of crops humans once ate” 对应。

【解析】E 段指出气候变暖威胁现有作物，恢复被遗忘的作物能提高粮食安全，与题目意思相符，答案为 E。

【定位】“Researchers” 与 “scientists” 对应；“higher temperatures and CO₂ levels” 与 “higher temperatures and carbon dioxide levels” 对应；“affect the nutritional composition of alternative crops” 与 “impact of...on the nutritional make - up of alternative crops” 对应。

【解析】K 段提到科学家在研究高温和二氧化碳水平对替代作物营养成分的影响，与题目内容一致，答案是 K。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 Imagine you're an alien sent to Earth to document the behaviour of the mammals inhabiting the planet. 2 You stumble into a movie theatre that's showing the latest Hollywood horror film.
1 Several dozen humans are gathered together in a dark, undecorated room. 2 They're all staring at a rectangular area on which patterns of light change rapidly.
1 They are clearly in a state of high arousal. 2 Their heart rate is elevated, they occasionally glance around nervously, and they sometimes jump collectively in their seats, and emit high-pitched warning calls.?
1 Eventually, the lights come up and the rectangular screen goes black. 2 The humans stand up and leave the room, chatting and laughing, and showing signs of pleasure.
1 Why do these humans voluntarily expose themselves to what appears to be a deeply unpleasant experience? 2 And why do they react so strongly to those patterns of light on a screen?
1 I am fascinated with the paradox of horror — the strange fact that many people seek out scary entertainment.
1 I think the answer to the puzzle lies in human nature.
1 My research suggests that we humans evolved to find pleasure in situations that allow us to experience negative emotions in a safe context.? 2 You can see these elements of horror in children's games. 3 Take hide-and-seek for example, which is a simulation of a predator-prey interaction. 4 The kid hides and the adult pretends to be a predator, searching for the child while howling like a dangerous beast.
1 This simulation gives the child crucial information about how to avoid becoming prey, and children tend to find that kind of activity deeply satisfying, presumably because it gives them a safe experience of a potentially catastrophic scenario.?
1 They find it pleasurable, and pleasure is evolution's way of motivating us toward adaptive behaviour.
1 Horror is pleasurable to many people because it lets us play with negative emotions and develop coping strategies. 2 We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid, and we learn how to handle negative emotion.?
1 How, then, does horror work? 2 My research suggests that horror works by exploiting an ancient set of biological defence mechanisms — an evolved fear system, which we share with other animals. 3 But humans are uniquely imaginative, and we use our evolved imagination to travel into virtual worlds that are full of danger.
1 There are good reasons for watching a horror film, even if you're not a loyal horror fan. 2 If you make it through the film in one piece, you'll probably experience a strong sense of mastery, a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience.? 3 Anyway, watching a horror film makes you better at handling your own fear, and who knows when that will become critically relevant?

questions.explanation:
根据题干中的定位关键词：alien, audience, in a state of定位到文章3段1句：They（=audience） are clearly in a state of（原词复现） high arousal.

3段1句描述了关注的状态，即：他们处于高度兴奋的状态（in a state of high arousal）。

此外，3段2句进一步补充了人们的具体反应，即：心率加快（heart rate is elevated），偶尔会紧张地四处张望（occasionally glance around nervously），有时会一起从座位上跳起来（jump collectively in their seat），还会发出尖锐的惊呼声（emit high-pitched warning calls）。

综上可知，外星人会发现电影院里的观众明显处于一种很兴奋的状态，故B选项“extreme excitement（极度兴奋）”与原文“high arousal”以及一系列兴奋的表现（心率加快、紧张张望、惊跳、尖叫）相符，所以B选项正确。

6段1句指出：作者对恐怖的矛盾性（the paradox of horror）非常着迷，也就是很多人寻求恐怖娱乐（many people seek out scary entertainment）的这种奇怪现象（the strange fact），但该句只提到了题干中所描述的现象，而并未解释这种现象产生的原因，故需要继续阅读下文。

7段1句：该句解释了作者对这种现象的看法，即：问题的答案在于人性，但此处依旧不是题干中所问的作者研究内容，故需要继续阅读下文。

8段1句：该句提出了作者的研究（author's research）对这种现象的解释，即：人类在进化过程中（we humans evolved），会在安全的情境下（in a safe context）体验负面情绪（in situations that allow us to experience negative emotions）并从中获得愉悦（to find pleasure）。

综上可知，作者的研究认为，人们寻求恐怖娱乐的原因在于，人们能在安全环境中（（in a safe context））体验负面情绪（experience negative emotions）并获得愉悦（to find pleasure）。故B选项“They find joy in going through simulated horrible experiences.（他们在经历模拟的恐怖体验中找到了乐趣。）”符合定位句的意思，所以B选项正确。

13段2句：该句提到，如果你能完整地看完一部恐怖片（If you make it through the film in one piece），你很可能会体验到一种强烈的掌控感（you'll probably experience a strong sense of mastery），一种你能够挺过一段可怕经历的感觉（ a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience）。

综上所述，文中内容表明，如果一个人完整看完恐怖片且没受伤，那么他会体验到强烈的掌控感。故D选项“A strong sense of being in control.（一种强烈的掌控感。）”与原文表述一致，所以D选项正确。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 An awakening has been taking place in the physical world against the beauty model that has been dictated to us for years. 2 But in the digital arena, social media determines what is considered beautiful.?
1 The two opposing struggles are taking place in parallel. 2 In the physical world, the struggle goes against the underlying pressure exerted on women to conform to an unrealistic beauty ideal.? 3 As part of the struggle, various media outlets have presented women whose bodies don't correspond to the so-called ideal. 4 All those women who had previously been excluded from the covers of magazines, television series and the public agenda, have become “legitimate.” 5 At the same time, a group of influencers have begun to upload to social media photos of themselves without makeup, and even photos in which they highlight supposed flaws.
1 Technology has reshaped our beauty ideal and is doing a great job communicating that message to the masses. 2 One of the bizarre legacies of the past decade is the popularity of the “cyborg look,” which illustrates what Americans will look like in 2050.
1 The cyborg look spread rapidly.? 2 Today, however, the Instagram face has become the new beauty ideal.
1 The internalization of accepted beauty norms is much more effective when there is active involvement in the learning process. 2 The active involvement of users is reflected in the gamified (游戏化的) interaction offered by the social media platforms — the ability to like, write a comment, compare, share.
1 Once the desired beauty ideal has been internalized, users are given tools or features to change their appearance to suit the accepted beauty ideal such as editing the image, choosing the ideal filter, the right background.
1 A survey conducted in the United States revealed that more than 50% filter the images before posting them. 2 And you will not be surprised to hear that the majority of them are women. 3 One of the significant consequences of obsessive filtering is the emerging tendency to treat oneself as an object to be observed and valued, in the same way another person observes and judges from the side.?
1 The effect of the filters is already far beyond amiable amusement. 2 The filters and the entire game played on the networks affect the mental health of the users. 3 According to a study, apps like Instagram, Snapchat and FaceTune allow users to achieve a level of perfection that was previously only observed in beauty magazines.
1 Even though humanity has always cherished beauty, in the last decade our obsession with looks has reached an unprecedented peak. 2 The time spent on social media creates an urge to achieve an impossible beauty ideal so powerful that the only thing that can fix it is not cosmetic intervention, but mental health care.?

题干问“过度使用滤镜导致了什么结果”，由此可知，其考察因果逻辑，为原因细节题，且根据题干中的定位关键词：“obsessive filtering resulted in”可定位到文章7段3句：“One of the significant consequences（等同于resulted in） of obsessive filtering（原词复现） is the emerging tendency to treat oneself as an object to be observed and valued, in the same way another person observes and judges from the side.

7段3句指出：过度使用滤镜（obsessive filtering）的一个重大后果是（One of the significant consequences），人们逐渐倾向于（the emerging tendency）将自己视为一个供人观察和评判的对象（to treat oneself as an object to be observed and valued），就如同他人从旁观察和评判一样（in the same way another person observes and judges from the side）。

综上可知，过度使用滤镜导致了人们会产生一种将自己视为一个供人观察和评判的对象的倾向。这意味着在过度滤镜使用的影响下，人们对自身的认知发生了改变，将自己物化，以一种外在观察者的视角来看待自己。故C选项“A tendency to regard one's body as an object of observation and judgment.（一种将自己的身体视为观察和评判对象的倾向。）”与定位句表述高度契合，准确概括了过度使用滤镜导致的结果，所以C选项正确。

9段1句指出：在过去十年里（in the last decade），我们（即美国人）对外表的痴迷（our obsession with looks）达到了前所未有的高度（has reached an unprecedented peak）。 但该句仅提出了题干中所述的现象，并未指出作者对此想要强调的观点，故需要继续阅读下文。

9段2句，作者提出了对于这个问题的观点，即：解决这一问题的唯一办法（the only thing that can fix it）并非美容干预（is not cosmetic intervention），而是心理健康治疗（but mental health care）。

综上可知，文末，作者对于美国人对于外表的痴迷这一现象，强调了解决美国人对外表的痴迷问题，需要的是心理健康治疗，即心理干预。故B选项“Psychological intervention should be introduced to alleviate it.（应该引入心理干预来缓解这种情况。）”与定位句意思相符，所以B选项正确。

Thank you for meeting with me, Stephen, at such a short notice.
Not a problem, Margaret.
Now please give me some good news.
Have you agreed to my last proposal?
I have indeed and I wish to sign the agreement, pending one small change to be made a contract.
Margaret, we've been through this for almost a year now, back and forth making alterations.
Are you sure you want to make a sponsorship deal for your clients or not?
I ask this because frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience.
I understand your concerns, but as I'm sure you understand, we hold our clients' best interests to be of the utmost concern.
We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts.
Rest assured we all appreciate your firm's patience.
Okay, fine.
So what changes do you wish to make?
Essentially, we would like the new deal to exclude the Middle East.
That's all.
The Middle East? Why?
My client has a couple of other prospective marketing deals from companies in the Middle East.
Those offers, should they materialize, would exclusively employ my client's image in the Middle East only.
Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically.
What business sector in the Middle East are we talking about here?
Real estate.
Well, that should be okay then.
So long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market, there should be no conflict of interest.
Nevertheless, I will have to run this through my people.
I don't foresee any problem, though.
The Middle East is a negligible market for us.
But I still need to check this with a couple of departments.

Next, we have a special science-related new story.
Paula Hancock is at the Denver Observatory.
Paula, what is the big story over there?
Hi, John.

In fact, space enthusiasts all across North America and the rest of the Northern Hemisphere will be congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night's sky.

Tonight, the Earth will come into close proximity with the Oppenheimer comet.
It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years.
For this reason, it is expected that thousands of people will gaze up at the sky tonight in order to see this formidable object.
How far away is this comet?
Will people be able to see it with the naked eye?
The Oppenheimer comet will still be millions of miles away on the edge of our galaxy.
But nevertheless, this is a relatively close distance, close enough for people to observe in good detail through a telescope.
People will only see a blur without one.
However, that does not mean one needs professional equipment.
Even the most ordinary of telescopes should be conducive for people to observe and wonder at this flying object.
Many of our viewers will be wondering how they too can take part in this once-in-a-lifetime event.
Where will this comet be in the sky?
How can people find it?
The comet will be almost exactly due north, at 60 degrees above the equator.
However, finding the comet is indeed very tricky.

How fantastic !

Dietary guidelines form the basis for nutrition advice and regulations around the world.
While there is strong scientific consensus around most existing guidelines, one question has recently stirred debate: should consumers be warned to avoid ultra-processed foods?
Two papers published today in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition outline the case for and against using the concept of "ultra-processed foods" to help inform dietary guidelines, beyond conventional food classification systems.
The authors, Carlos Monteiro of the University of São Paulo and Arna Ostrupn of Novo Nordisk Foundation, will discuss the issue in a live virtual debate, August 14th, during NUTRITION 2024 Live Online.
The debate centers around a system developed by Monteiro and colleagues that classifies foods by their degree of industrial processing, ranging from unprocessed to ultra-processed.
The system defines ultra-processed foods as those made using sequences of processes that extract substances from foods and alter them with chemicals in order to formulate the final product.
Ultra-processed foods are characteristically designed to be cheap, tasty, and convenient.
Examples include soft drinks and candy, packaged snacks and pastries, ready to heat products, and reconstituted meat products.
Studies have linked consumption of ultra-processed foods, which are often high in salt, sugar, and fat, with weight gain and an increased risk of chronic diseases, even after adjusting for the amount of salt, sugar, and fat in the diet.
While the mechanisms behind these associations are not fully understood, Monteiro argues that the existing evidence is sufficient to justify discouraging consumption of ultra-processed foods in dietary recommendations and government policies.

Believe it or not, human creativity benefits from constraints.
According to psychologists, when you have less to work with, you actually begin to see the world differently.
With constraints, you dedicate your mental energy to acting more resourcefully.
When challenged, you figure out new ways to be better.
The most successful creative people know that constraints give their minds the impetus to leap higher.
People who invent new products are not limited by what they don't have or can't do.
They leverage their limitations to push themselves even further.
Many products and services are created because the founders saw a limitation in what they use.
They created innovation based on what was not working for them at the moment.
Innovation is a creative person's response to limitation.
In a 2015 study which examined how thinking about scarcity or abundance influences how creatively people use their resources, Ravi Mehta at the University of Illinois and Meng Zhu at Johns Hopkins University found that people simply have no incentive to use what's available to them in novel ways.
When people face scarcity, they give themselves the freedom to use resources in less conventional ways because they have to.
Obstacles can broaden your perception and open up your thinking processes.
Consistent constraints help you improve the connecting unrelated ideas and concepts.
Marissa Meyer, former vice president for search products and user experience at Google, once wrote in a publication on Bloomberg, “Constraints shape and focus problems and provide clear challenges to overcome; creativity thrives best when constrained.”

Q13: What does the passage say about innovation?

Q15: What did Marissa Meyer once write concerning creativity?
Different people use different strategies for managing conflicts.
These strategies are learned in childhood.
Usually, we are not aware of how we act in conflict situations.
We just do whatever seems to come naturally.
But we do have a personal strategy, and because it is learned, we can always change it by learning new and more effective ways of managing conflicts.
When you get involved in a conflict, there are two major concerns you have to take into account: achieving your personal goals and keeping a good relationship with the other person.
How important your personal goals are and how important the relationship is to you affect how you act in a conflict.
Given these two concerns, five styles of managing conflicts can be identified.
The turtle.
Turtles withdraw into their shells to avoid conflicts.
They give up their personal goals and relationships.
They believe it is easier to withdraw from a conflict than to face it.
The shark.
Sharks try to overpower opponents by forcing them to accept their solution to the conflict.
They seek to achieve their goals at all costs.
Sharks assume that conflicts are settled by one person winning and one person losing.
Winning gives sharks a sense of pride and achievement.
Losing gives them a sense of weakness, inadequacy, and failure.
The teddy bear.
Teddy bears want to be accepted and liked by other people.
They think that conflict should be avoided in favor of harmony, and believe that conflicts cannot be discussed without damaging relationships.
They give up their goals to preserve the relationship.
The fox.
Foxes are moderately concerned with their own goals and about their relationships with other people.
They give up part of their goals and persuade the other person in a conflict to give up part of his goals.
They seek a solution to conflicts where both sides gain something.
The owl.
Owls view conflicts as problems to be solved.
They see conflicts as improving relationships by reducing tension between two people.
They try to begin a discussion that identifies the conflict as a problem.
By seeking solutions that satisfy both themselves and the other person, owls maintain the relationship.
Owls are not satisfied until a solution is found that achieves their own goals and the other person's goals, and they are not satisfied until the tensions and negative feelings have been fully resolved.

The genetic code of all 1.5 million known species of animals and plants living on Earth will be mapped to help save species from extinction and boost human health.
Scientists hope that cracking the genetic code of plants and animals could help uncover new treatments for infectious diseases, slow aging, improve crops and agriculture, and create new bio-materials.
In Britain, organisations including the Natural History Museum, the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew and the Wellcome Sanger Institute have joined forces to sequence Britain's 66,000 species of animals and plants.
Dubbed the Darwin Tree of Life Project, it is expected to take 10 years and cost 100 million pounds.
Once completed, all the information will be publicly available to researchers.
Many scientists believe that Earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction, with humans creating a toxic mix of habitation loss, pollution and climate change, which has already led to the loss of at least 77 species of mammals and 140 types of birds since 1500.
It is the biggest loss of species since the dinosaurs were wiped out 66 million years ago.
Scientists say that sequencing every species will revolutionize the understanding of biology and evolution, bolster efforts to conserve as well as protect and restore biodiversity.
Dr.Tim Littlewood, head of Life Sciences Department at the Natural History Museum said,“ Whether you are interested in food or disease, he history of how every organism on the planet has adapted to its environment is recorded in its genetic makeup.
How you then harness that is dependent on your ability to understand it.
We will be using modern methods to get a really good window on the present and the past.
And of course, a window on the past gives you a prospective model on the future.”
Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome said, “Try as I might, I can't think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely, or more internationally inspirational project.
Since 1970, humanity has wiped out 60 percent of animal populations.
About 23,000 of 80,000 species surveyed are approaching extinction.
We are in the midst of the sixth great extinction event of life on our planet, which not only threatens wildlife species, but also imperils the global food supply.
As scientists, we all realize we desperately need to catalogue life on our fragile planet now.I think we're making history.”

John Donne, the English poet, wrote in the 17th century, “No man is an island, entire of itself; every man is apiece of the continent, apart of the main.”
Now, a British academic has claimed that human individuality is indeed just an illusion, because societies are far more interconnected at a mental, physical, and cultural level than people realize.
In his new book, The Self Delusion, Professor Tom Oliver, a researcher in the Ecology and Evolution group at the University of Reading, argues there is no such thing as “self”, and not even our bodies are truly “us”.
Just as Copernicus realized the Earth is not the center of the universe, Professor Oliver said society urgently needs a Copernican-like revolution to understand people are not detached beings but rather part of one connected identity.
“A significant milestone in the cultural evolution of human minds was the acceptance that the Earth is not the center of the universe, the so-called Copernican Revolution, "he writes.
“However, we have one more big myth to dispose of: that we exist as independent selves at the center of a subjective universe.
You may feel as if you are an independent individual acting autonomously in the world; that you have unchanging inner self that persists throughout your lifetime, acting as a central anchor-point with the world changing around you.
This is the illusion I seek to tackle.
We are intimately connected to the world around us.”
Professor Oliver argues there are around 37 trillion cells in the body but most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks, so the material “us” is constantly changing.
In fact, there is no part of your body that has existed for more than ten years.
Since our bodies are essentially made anew every few weeks, the material in them alone is clearly insufficient to explain the persistent thread of an identity.
Professor Oliver claims that individualism is actually bad for society, and only by realizing we are part of a bigger entity can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems.
Through selfish over-consumption we are destroying the natural world and using non-renewable resources at an accelerating rate.
“We are at a critical crossroads as a species where we must rapidly reform our mindsets and behavior to act in less selfish ways,” he said.
“So let's open our eyes to the hidden connections all around us.”

questions.explanation: 【题目】What did a 2015 study by Ravi Mehta and Meng Zhu find?2015年拉维·梅塔和朱蒙的一项研究发现了什么?【解析】文章后半部分介绍了2015年的一项研究，拉维·梅塔和朱蒙在这项研究中发现，人们根本没有动力以新颖的方式使用现有资源。选项C中的have no incentive是文中的原词，use available resources和in new ways分别对应原文的use what's available to them和in novel ways,因此选项C正确。选项A、B是利用文中的个别词汇(scarcity or abundance、connecting unrelated ideas and concepts)设置的干扰项，因此排除这两项；选项D文中没有提到，故排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is key to a company's survival.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is essential to meeting challenges.

questions.explanation: 【题目】What did Marissa Meyer once write concerning creativity?关于创造力，玛丽莎·梅耶尔曾经写过什么?【解析】文章最后提到了谷歌前副总裁玛丽莎·梅耶尔对于创造力的看法：局限性可以塑造和聚焦问题，并提供需要克服的明确挑战；创造力在受到限制的情况下最能蓬勃发展。选项D的表述与原文完全一致，故正确，同时排除据此设置的干扰项B、C。选项A玛丽莎·梅耶尔并未提及，故排除。

questions.explanation: 【题目】Why does the speaker say strategies for managing conflicts can always be changed?为什么讲话者说冲突解决策略总是可以改变的?【解析】演讲开头，讲话者指出，我们处理冲突的策略源自童年学习，随后解释道，正因为这些策略是后天习得，我们就有可能通过学习更有效的新方法来处理冲突。因此，可以明确地得出结论，正确答案是A。

choices.label: B

choices.label: C
choices.text: The importance of one's goals and of the relationship.

choices.label: D

questions.explanation: 【题目】What is said to affect the way one acts in a conflict?什么被认为会影响一个人在冲突中的行为方式?【解析】讲话者在讨论冲突时指出，需要考虑两个核心问题：一是达成个人目标，二是维护与对方的和谐关系。讲话者进一步强调，个人目标的重要性和关系的紧密程度将直接影响一个人在冲突中的行为方式。因此，可以确定选项C是正确答案。

【题目】Of the five styles the speaker discusses, which views conflicts as problems to be solved?在讲话者提及的五种方法中，哪种方法把冲突看作是一个待处理的问题？【解析】在讲话者描述的五种处理冲突的方法中，提及猫头鹰方式时，讲话者明确指出，“采取猫头鹰方式的个体会将冲突视为一个需要解决的问题”。因此，可以确定选项B是正确答案。

questions.explanation: 【题目】What do scientists hope to do by cracking the genetic code of plants and animals?科学家们试图通过解码植物和动物的基因组来实现什么目标？【解析】在演讲的起始部分，演讲者指出，“将绘制出地球上已知的150万种动植物的遗传密码，这将有助于保护物种免遭灭绝并促进人类健康。”因此，可以明确选项A是正确答案。题目中提到的“科学家们希望通过破解植物和动物的遗传密码”实际上是对演讲开头所述内容的进一步阐释，而其他三个选项与演讲内容不符，因此被排除。

questions.explanation: 【题目】What do many scientists believe with regard to Earth?科学家们对地球的现状有何观点？【解析】在演讲的中间部分，演讲者提到，“许多科学家认为地球已经进入了第六次大规模灭绝事件。”因此，可以确定选项B是正确答案。尽管演讲中也提到了恐龙(dinosaurs)和气候变化(climate change)，但这些内容与题目所问的科学家对地球的整体看法不符，所以排除选项A和D。选项C在演讲中没有被提及。

questions.explanation: 【题目】How does Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome, describe the Darwin Tree of Life Project?威康桑格研究所的科学总监吉姆·史密斯爵士是如何评价“达尔文生命之树项目”的？ 【解析】在演讲的尾声，讲话者引用了吉姆·史密斯爵士对该项目的评价，他强调：“我竭尽全力也难以找到一个项目，能比这个更加令人振奋、更加密不可分、更加紧迫或更加具有全球启发性。”基于这一表述，可以确定选项D是正确答案。尽管讲话中提到了选项A中提到的保护、维护和恢复生物多样性（conserve, protect and restore biodiversity），但这并非史密斯爵士的原话，且与题目要求的内容不符。选项B虽然是演讲中的内容，但并非出自史密斯爵士之口，因此被排除。选项C的内容则是对演讲的过度解读，同样被排除。

【题目】What is indeed just an illusion according to Professor Tom Oliver? 根据汤姆·奥利弗教授所言，什么的确只是一种错误的观念?【解析】在演讲中，一位英国学者提出，个体的人类性实际上是一种幻觉，因为社会在心理、生理和文化层面的联系比人们所认识到的要紧密得多。虽然这句话没有明确指出这位学者的身份，但紧接着的下一句话揭示了学者的身份：雷丁大学的汤姆·奥利弗教授认为，“自我”这个概念根本不存在，甚至我们的身体也不是真正的“自我”。因此，可以推断出这位学者就是汤姆·奥利弗教授。所以，正确答案是选项D。选项C与演讲内容相悖，因为演讲中提到奥利弗教授认为社会需要一场哥白尼式的革命，这意味着在他看来，哥白尼式的革命并不是幻觉，因此排除C。其他两个选项在演讲中没有被提及，因此也可以排除。

choices.label: A

questions.explanation: 【题目】What does Professor Tom Oliver think of the idea that we exist as independent selves at the center of a subjective universe?汤姆·奥利弗教授是如何看待“我们作为主观宇宙核心的独立个体”这一理念的？【解析】在演讲的中间部分，汤姆·奥利弗教授明确指出：“我们必须放弃一个巨大的幻觉，即我们作为独立的自我，处于主观宇宙的中心。”因此，可以确定选项A是正确答案。其他三个选项在演讲中没有被提到，故予以排除

questions.explanation: 【题目】Why does Professor Tom Oliver claim that the material “us” is constantly changing?为何汤姆·奥利弗教授提出我们在物质层面上是不断变化的？【解析】在演讲的后半段，奥利弗教授指出，人体包含约37万亿个细胞，而这些细胞中的大多数只有短暂的寿命，仅能存活几天到几周。因此，他在物质层面上认为“我们”是不断变化的。基于这一点，可以确定选项D是正确答案。其他三个选项并未在演讲中被提到，因此被排除。

questions.explanation: 【题目】How can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems according to Professor Tom Oliver?汤姆·奥利弗教授认为我们应如何面对当前的环境和社会挑战？ 【解析】在演讲的后半部分，奥利弗教授提出，个人主义对社会是有害的，我们必须认识到自己是更大整体的一部分(part of a bigger entity)，才能有效应对迫在眉睫的环境和社会问题。根据之前的论述可以推断，“更大的实体(a bigger entity)”指的是我们所在的更广阔的世界。因此，选项C是正确答案。其他三个选项在演讲中没有被提到，故予以排除。

1 There is a growing awareness of the importance of digital literacy and skills in today's world. 【提出问题：数字素养和技能的重要性】 2 Some contend that digital literacy is the gateway to success, while others opine that it is not mandatory for everyone to acquire such skills. 【陈述正反两面观点】 3 For my part, I find the former perspective to be more convincing. 【提出作者观点：赞同前者】

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 Traditional Chinese wedding customs have a long history. 2 A complete set of wedding ceremonies were gradually formed in the Zhou Dynasty, and some of them are still in use today. 3 Nowadays, although Chinese wedding conventions have changed a lot, the ceremony is still a very grand occasion, when the wedding venue is carefully decorated, with red as the main color to symbolize happiness, and with many special objects placed to wish the couple well-being. 4 At the wedding ceremony, the couple should bow to heaven and earth, to their parents and to each other, and afterwards hold a banquet to entertain and toast to the guests. 5 Today, many young people still love the traditional Chinese wedding to experience the unique and beautiful Chinese romance.

questions.stem: ①中国的传统婚礼习俗历史悠久。②从周朝开始就逐渐形成了一套完整的婚礼仪式，有些一直沿用至今。③如今的中式婚礼习俗已有很大变化，但婚礼庆典仍然十分隆重。婚礼场地经过精心装饰，以象征喜庆(jubilance)的红色为主色调，摆放着许多祝愿新人幸福的物件。④在婚礼上，新人要拜天地(bow to Heaven and Earth)，拜父母和相互对拜，然后设宴招待宾客，并向宾客敬酒致谢。⑤今天，许多年轻人依然钟情于传统的中式婚礼，体验独特而美好的中国式浪漫。
questions.answer: 1 Traditional Chinese wedding customs have a long history. 2 A complete set of wedding ceremonies were gradually formed in the Zhou Dynasty, and some of them are still in use today. 3 Nowadays, although Chinese wedding conventions have changed a lot, the ceremony is still a very grand occasion, when the wedding venue is carefully decorated, with red as the main color to symbolize happiness, and with many special objects placed to wish the couple well-being. 4 At the wedding ceremony, the couple should bow to heaven and earth, to their parents and to each other, and afterwards hold a banquet to entertain and toast to the guests. 5 Today, many young people still love the traditional Chinese wedding to experience the unique and beautiful Chinese romance.
