choices.text: Adapt themselves to different social contexts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Work hard to interact with experimenters.

questions.explanation: 【解析】讲话者在讲话最后讲述了婴儿在实验中的表现及实验的结果有何发现。讲话者先说，看到成年人坚持努力并成功的孩子按下按钮的次数大约是看到成年人轻松成功的孩子的两倍，即婴儿在观看了两个成年人努力并成功的例子后，学会了努力是有价值的。而这可以证明，婴儿并不是仅仅模仿成年人的动作，而是将努力的价值推广到了一个新的任务中。其实，讲话者早在讲话中间就提到了 generalizable inferences 这个关键词，实验结果也确实表明，婴儿可以做到。由此可知，选项 B 为正确答案。

choices.label: A
choices.text: Offering advice on overcoming habitual lateness.

questions.explanation: 【解析】讲话者通篇都围绕着 lateness 这个关键词展开。由此很容易得出，选项 A 为正确答案。虽然 recreational opportunities、defining trait 讲话中也有原词复现的情况，但都是讲话中的细节，并非讲话者发表演讲的目的，而 setting priorities 则是基于 prioritize 的过度推断，均可直接排除。

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ready yourself in the early dawn.

questions.explanation: 【解析】讲话者在中间提到，“If mornings are a struggle for you”，和题干属于原词复现，很容易定位到答案位置，即 “do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before（那就尽量在前一天晚上做好准备）”。由此可知，选项 D 为正确答案。

choices.label: A
choices.text: Finish the prior task 30 minutes earlier.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Keep ourselves from hitting a bump.

questions.explanation: 【解析】讲话者在最后提到了 unexpected delays，但其所在的句子大意为：计算好活动之间的交通时间，然后再加上 10 到 30 分钟以应对可能出现的意外延误。大家可能会被 “30 分钟” 误导，进而错选选项 A。但其实，这句话的重点是预留时间以应对意外延误，也就是末段段首提到的 “学会在任务和会议之间留出时间”。由此可知，选项 C 为正确答案。
【解析】讲话者在讲话开头提到，不同的城市给游客的感觉不同。由此可知，选项 D 为正确答案。其余三项讲话者均未提及，均可排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are not as willing to help strangers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are not as patient with one another.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They violate traffic rules more frequently.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They become more easily irritated in public.

questions.explanation: 【解析】讲话者在讲话中提到，一项研究发现，与美国其他城市的居民相比，波士顿人不太愿意主动帮助陌生人。由此可知，选项 A 为正确答案。选项 B 和 C 虽是讲话中关于波士顿人的描述，但是这两点并不是和美国其他城市的居民进行对比的，故均排除。选项 D 在讲话中没有明确的对应句，故也排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: It was practiced by Boston’s founding fathers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is not deemed exotic by Proper Bostonians.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It was adopted by Boston’s upper class.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is not part of Boston’s local culture.

questions.explanation: 【解析】讲话者在讲话中间提到，托马斯・奥康纳说，在波士顿，陌生人之间相互打招呼这种想法根本不属于当地文化。因此，选项 D 为正确答案。其余三项讲话者均未提及，可排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: Stick to its own way of showing courtesy to strangers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Follow the examples set by Paris and New York City.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Learn from the world’s major cities in promoting tourism.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Take pride in its history and adhere to its cultural tradition.

questions.explanation: 【解析】讲话者在讲话末尾部分提到，巴黎和纽约这两个因更加过分的粗鲁无礼而声名狼藉的城市都在努力改变自己的形象，波士顿也许也应该效仿。故选项 B 为正确答案。其余三项讲话者均未提及，可排除。

sections.title: Part 1 Writing 写作
sections.passage:
1 As requirements for job applications are getting increasingly higher, college students ought to be better prepared for their future career. 2 Some think developing this ability is key to professional strength and adaptability, while others say it’s hard to keep in today’s fas -changing, competitive world. 3 Personally, I find the former view more convincing.
1 There are reasons why active career preparation matters. 2 To begin with, students who develop this ability tend to perform better academically, as they can align their coursework with industry demands and secure internships early. 3 Second, in the workplace, professionals with this trait are usually more efficient, capable of navigating technological disruptions, which accelerates their career advancement. 4 Also, in daily life, those with such foresight balance work and life better, improving skills without getting too tired. 5 Who wouldn’t respect a purposeful person?
1 In short, wise career preparation is key to work success. 2 To build it, we can learn from mentors who show this ability—their advice helps us pick up useful habits. 3 Also, we should actively do industry research, find skill gaps, and keep improving to stay competitive.

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 The Tiangong Space Station is China’s first space laboratory, boasting over 110 cubic meters of usable space and capable of hosting three astronauts in orbit 400-450 kilometers above Earth’s surface. 2 It has conducted more than 180 scientific research and application projects spanning fields such as space life science, space medicine, and space materials science. 3 The research achievements of the Tiangong Space Station have been widely applied in China, generating significant economic benefits. 4 For instance, space breeding alone has created direct economic value amounting to hundreds of billions of yuan. 5 This not only marks a huge advancement in China’s aerospace technology, but also demonstrates the country’s substantial contributions to global space research and applications.

questions.stem: ①天宫空间站是中国首个太空实验室，拥有超过 110 立方米的可用空间，能够在距地球表面 400 至 450 公里的轨道上容纳三名宇航员。②天宫空间站已实施180多个科学研究与应用项目，涉及空间生命科学、太空医学、空间材料科学等领域。③天宫空间站的研究成果在我国得到了广泛应用，产生了显著的经济效益。④例如，太空育种创造的直接经济效益高达数千亿元。⑤这不仅标志中国在航天技术上取得了巨大进步，也表明中国为全球的太空研究和应用做出了重大贡献。
questions.answer: 1 The Tiangong Space Station is China’s first space laboratory, boasting over 110 cubic meters of usable space and capable of hosting three astronauts in orbit 400-450 kilometers above Earth’s surface. 2 It has conducted more than 180 scientific research and application projects spanning fields such as space life science, space medicine, and space materials science. 3 The research achievements of the Tiangong Space Station have been widely applied in China, generating significant economic benefits. 4 For instance, space breeding alone has created direct economic value amounting to hundreds of billions of yuan. 5 This not only marks a huge advancement in China’s aerospace technology, but also demonstrates the country’s substantial contributions to global space research and applications.

sections.title: Section A 选词填空
sections.passage:
1 In her second year, Charlene Duong learned of the use of poisonous, synthetic pesticides on her college campus. 2 Shocked but not surprised, she knew she had to do something. 3 Along with a couple of classmates, Charlene did a quick web search and discovered a small but growing movement led by the organization, Herbicide-Free Campus (HFC), to rid college campuses of artificial herbicides (除草剂). 4 They were 1.?
1 Like many, Charlene experiences climate anxiety — a 2 fear of a climate catastrophe — and was, at the time, looking for an 3.? 2 When she discovered the HFC movement, she said she felt she " had found a specific area to focus on that still fit into the larger picture of fighting for a healthier, safer, cleaner 4 for all. "?
1 Toxic herbicide use in university land care is not unique. 2 Most institutions of higher education rely on synthetic pesticides and fertilizers to achieve 5 goals.? 3 Having a " beautiful " campus means green and perfectly maintained lawns along with flower beds and paved sidewalks. 4 But these 6 managed campuses can come at a cost: increased cancer risk, 7 waterways, poisoned wildlife and lifeless soil.?
1 Pesticide use on college campuses also contributes to our global climate crisis. 2 The use of chemicals to get rid of insects or unwanted plant life can increase indirect 8, as they can include petroleum-based ingredients.? 3 Pesticide use also decreases the life in soil, 9 the ability of soils to absorb carbon or retain water and thus reducing campuses' ability to recover quickly from climate-related extreme weather events like droughts and floods.?
1 Instead of using toxic chemicals, students working with HFC help out with 10 the campus grounds.?
1 " This work reminds me to be in the present moment as I play my role in reducing herbicide use and keeping my campus safe and healthy, " says Charlene.

questions.explanation:
【词性判断】

空格前是 be 动词 were，空格后是句点，由此可知，空格处应填入一个形容词或分词。

【解析】

首段前面几句提到杨夏琳得知校园在使用有毒杀虫剂时决定做些什么，她和同学通过网上搜索找到了 “无灭草剂校园” 组织发起的一项消除大学校园人造灭草剂的运动，由此可知，“无灭草剂校园” 组织发起的运动与他们的理念一致，他们对该运动应该是十分感兴趣的，故 intrigued 符合语境，本题应选 J。

【词性判断】

空格前是不定冠词 a，空格后是 fear of a climate catastrophe，由此可知，空格处应填入一个形容词或分词，充当名词 fear 的定语。

【解析】

由破折号之前的 Charlene experiences climate anxiety 可知，夏琳受到气候焦虑的困扰，说明她处于一种长期担忧、害怕的心理状态，故 chronic 符合语境，本题应选 B。

【词性判断】

空格前是不定冠词 an，空格后是句点。由此可知，空格处应填入一个发音以元音开头的单数名词。

【解析】

上文提到夏琳饱受气候焦虑的困扰，长期对气候灾难感到恐惧，本句承接上文，她当时正在寻找这种焦虑情绪的发泄方式，故 outlet 符合语境，本题应选 L。

【词性判断】

空格前是 fighting for a healthier, safer, cleaner，空格后是介词短语 for all，由此可知，空格处应填入一个名词，作动名词短语 fighting for 的宾语。

【解析】

上文提到夏琳和同学发现的 “无灭草剂校园” 消除大学校园中的人造灭草剂运动让他们很感兴趣，“无灭草剂校园” 运动属于环保运动，其最终目的应该是建设更健康、更安全、更清洁的环境，故 environment 符合语境，本题应选 F。

【词性判断】

空格前是不定式 to achieve，空格后是名词 goals，由此可知，空格处应填入一个形容词或分词，充当 goals 的定语。

【解析】

下文提及所谓 “美丽” 校园要达到的标准。结合本段首句 “大学绿化养护中使用有毒灭草剂的现象并非个例” 可知，此处是指多数高等教育机构依赖合成杀虫剂和化肥来实现景观美化目标，故 aesthetic 符合语境，本题应选 A。

【词性判断】

空格前是 But these，空格后是 managed campuses can come at a cost，由此可知，空格处应填入一个副词，修饰过去分词 managed。

【解析】

由 come at a cost 可知该管理模式是需要付出代价的，代价就是癌症风险上升等，这应该是使用有毒杀虫剂清理校园草坪的结果，是惯例做法或者说是传统做法。故 conventionally 符合语境，本题应选 D。

【词性判断】

空格前是 increased cancer risk，空格后是 waterways, poisoned wildlife and lifeless soil，由此可知，此处应是并列的名词短语，空格处应填入一个形容词或分词，充当 waterways 的定语。

【解析】

通读本段的内容可知，大学绿化养护中心使用有毒灭草剂清理校园草坪的传统管理方式是需要付出代价的，冒号后面便列举了具体的代价，包括癌症风险上升和野生动植物中毒以及土壤失去活性，由此可知，与之并列的应该是水道的污染，故 contaminated 符合语境，本题应选 C。

【词性判断】

空格前是 can increase indirect，空格后是逗号以及一个由 as 引导的原因状语从句，由此可知，空格处应填入一个名词，充当 increase 的宾语。

【解析】

由空格后的原因状语从句 “因为它们可能含有石油基成分”，再结合全文主要探讨的主题，即校园人造灭草剂对环境和健康造成危害可知，此处是说，化学药剂在灭杀害虫或杂草时会增加间接排放，故 emissions 符合语境，本题应选 E。

【词性判断】

空格前是主谓宾俱全的句子，空格后是名词短语 the ability of soils to...，由此可知，空格处应填入一个非谓语动词，与 ability 构成逻辑上的动宾关系。

【解析】

此处在讲述使用有毒药剂的危害，应是负面的，故与 ability 构成搭配的非谓语动词应该是 “阻碍，妨碍” 的意思，即妨碍土壤固碳蓄水的能力，故 hampering 符合语境，本题应选 G。

【词性判断】

空格前是 help out with，空格后是名词短语 the campus grounds，由此可知，空格处应填入一个动名词，充当 with 的宾语，且与 grounds 构成逻辑上的动宾关系。

【解析】

结合文章提到的 “无灭草剂校园” 运动致力于消除大学校园中的人造灭草剂，再根据本段句首的 Instead of using toxic chemicals（不使用有毒化学品）可知，此处是说，参与 “无灭草剂校园” 运动的学生们帮助校园进行人工除草，故 weeding 符合语境，本题应选 O。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 Librarians know the value of their community services, and their patrons appreciate their importance as well. 2 But in an increasingly digital world, we see the role of libraries as community and cultural centers at times undervalued.? 3 When shrinking municipal budgets combine with the nonstop technological revolution, public library services that focus on building communities face-to-face, inspiring and educating patrons about art, literature, and music, and helping the patrons engage in civil discourse can seem old-fashioned. 4 But it is precisely those shrinking budgets and the assault of technologically mediated life that make public libraries’ cultural and community offerings more important than ever.
1 Many people point out the value public libraries bring to their communities. 2 More than just books and banks of computers, libraries are still places where individuals gather to explore, interact, and imagine. 3 Some of the specific ways in which libraries add value to our communities and serve as cultural centers for our patrons are community builders, centers for the arts, and champions of youth. 4 Libraries serve in these capacities and are more than just about information.?
1 As community builders libraries are engaged in incredible work. 2 From tiny public libraries to huge city institutions with multiple branches, libraries across the United States are building community and supporting local culture in exciting ways. 3 These are inspiring and hopefully will encourage librarians interested in community services and cultural outreach to make connections with each other, share ideas, and build partnerships. 4 Supporters of libraries as community builders claim that unless you are out there changing neighborhoods, you are not completing the work you are to do.? 5 Strengthening neighborhoods and championing the cultural lives of communities are big responsibilities.
1 Place-based economic development stresses the importance of offering attractive, functional, and community-based places, such as libraries, in town squares and depressed neighborhoods. 2 Like a major department store in a mall, libraries attract large numbers of people, creating economic opportunities for numerous businesses and organizations in the surrounding area.? 3 Large cities, medium-sized ones, and even small towns have successfully transformed their libraries into the hubs (枢纽) of vibrant neighborhoods.
1 As key municipal agencies, and focal points for community education, libraries are major players in creating livable, environmentally friendly cities and towns. 2 The Urban Libraries Council released a report detailing the unique ways in which libraries can further sustainability at the local level. 3 Beyond ensuring that library construction projects consider environmental impact, libraries can take a lead in supporting local foods and craftsmen, like the Peabody Institute Library’s partnering with local businesses to pioneer a farmers’ market in their courtyard, or the Richmond Public Library’s seed lending library which “nurtures locally-adapted plant varieties, and fosters community resilience (韧性), self-reliance and a culture of sharing.”
1 Archives preserve historic artifacts, oral histories, digital history projects, and scholarly writings relevant to the community, including minority groups. 2 Communities lucky enough to have archivists have a great advantage when it comes to organizing historical records and artifacts. 3 An organized archive is a place where people can research their ancestry and immigration history, do environmental research, and more.? 4 An archivist is an advocate for preservation who, among other things, coordinates the restoration of maps and paintings, the digitization of vital records, and the creation of oral history projects. 5 With projects like the Massachusetts Memories Road Show and the Veterans History Project, evidence of the importance of archives is everywhere.
1 In the words of Robert Putnam, “People may go to the library looking mainly for information, but they find each other there.”? 2 New moms connect at baby story-times; elderly people, often facing difficult life transitions, attend events and find that they make new friends; teenagers meet up in libraries’ teen spaces after school; and readers discuss current events in the periodicals room. 3 In libraries, community-building connections are happening all the time.
1 As Keith Richards said, “The public library is the great equalizer.” 2 Despite the rising costs of concert and theater tickets, public library events (including concerts, author visits, and gallery displays) are often offered free of charge, enabling people of any income level to attend.? 3 In addition, library book groups allow people to explore and discuss the literary arts, and the Great Stories Club introduces at-risk youth to literature. 4 The best part: it’s all free and open to the public.
1 In a time when education is increasingly expensive, public libraries provide information and educational opportunities free for all people, regardless of their socio-economic status.? 2 Offered by libraries across the country, American Library Association’s Let’s Talk about It programs are wonderful examples of scholar-facilitated learning opportunities in libraries. 3 In addition, many libraries present classes and discussion programs, and some even provide online continuing education courses such as the Universal Class database.
1 Librarians know that patrons aren’t just information consumers, they’re information producers. 2 Patrons use the library to gain knowledge in order to create their own new and independent works. 3 Increasing numbers of libraries provide spaces and services that meet the needs of people who want to learn how to edit Wikipedia, set up blogs or podcasts, create their own magazines, and so much more. 4 Many libraries offer art or writing workshops and groups, and some provide music practice rooms for patrons. 5 Programs like ImaginOn in Charlotte, North Carolina, provide exciting models that take community partnership, creativity, and creation to a new level.
1 The decline of civil discourse stems in part from the fact that it is so easy for people to watch news about, buy products from, and engage — in both the virtual and real worlds — only with those of similar backgrounds and ideologies. 2 Public libraries, through such programs as The Human Library and SocratesCafé, can help build small communities of difference that encourage people to interact with and learn from each other through dialogue.? 3 By both actively promoting civil discourse through these programs, and modeling and upholding the principles of free inquiry and expression for all, libraries help individuals rediscover the importance of and increased need for civil discourse in American life.
1 Free tutoring, homework help programs, and summer reading programs for kids and teens help bridge the economic divide that impacts students’ academic performance.? 2 The cost of hiring a private tutor is well beyond what many library patrons can afford, so libraries offer homework help and tutoring online, by phone, in person, and even through social media and homework apps. 3 Annual summer reading programs also have a positive impact on student performance and, according to a 2010 study conducted by Dominican University’s Graduate School of Library and Information Science, students’ reading skills get a boost from these popular nationwide events.
1 Through library collections, programs, and physical spaces, children learn to share, to be engaged in their communities, to participate in the arts, and to explore their immediate world and the world at large. 2 There are surely endless examples of innovative library services for children, including the Middle Country Public Library’s Nature Explorium, which engages children in learning about the natural world.
1 These examples are just a few of the many amazing things that public libraries around the United States (and the world) are doing to build and maintain strong community connections. 2 We encourage you to try some of these ideas in your own libraries, and we hope that these ideas will help you be better able to convince your community leaders of the important role that public libraries play in communities large and small.

questions.explanation:
【定位】

由题干关键信息 “in search of information” 和 “build connections with each other” 定位到 G 段。

【解析】

该段首句提到，用罗伯特・普特南的话来说，“人们去图书馆可能主要是为了寻找信息，但他们在那里也找到了彼此。” 随后以新手妈妈、老年人、青少年、读者为例，说明人们在图书馆建立了彼此之间的联系。由此可知，题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的 “in search of” 对应原文中的 “looking…for”；题干中的 “build connections with each other” 对应原文中的 “find each other”。

【定位】

由题干关键信息 “advocates of libraries”、“not doing their job well” 和 “change their communities” 定位到 C 段。

【解析】

该段第四句提到，支持图书馆作为社区建设者的人士称，如果不出去改变社区，就没有完成应尽的职责。由此可知，题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的 “advocates” 对应原文中的 “Supporters”；题干中的 “not doing their job well” 对应原文中的 “not completing the work you are to do”；题干中的 “if they do not change their communities” 对应原文中的 “unless you are out there changing neighborhoods”。

【定位】

由题干关键信息 “costs of education continually rising” 定位到 I 段。

【解析】

该段首句提到，在教育日益昂贵的时代，公共图书馆为所有人提供免费的信息和教育机会，无论其社会经济地位如何。由此可知，题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的 “costs of education continually rising” 对应原文中的 “education is increasingly expensive”；题干中的 “all people can have access to education” 对应原文中的 “provide information and educational opportunities free for all people”。

【定位】

由题干关键信息 “draw large crowds” 和 “creating lots of business opportunities” 定位到 D 段。

【解析】

该段第二句提到，就像购物中心里的大型百货商店一样，图书馆吸引着大量人群，为周边地区的众多企业和组织创造经济机会。由此可知，题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的 “draw large crowds” 对应原文中的 “attract large numbers of people”；题干中的 “creating lots of business opportunities in neighboring areas” 对应原文中的 “creating economic opportunities for numerous businesses and organizations in the surrounding area”。

【定位】

由题干关键信息 “more and more digitalized” 和 “underestimate the role of libraries” 定位到 A 段。

【解析】

该段第二句提到，在日益数字化的世界中，我们有时会看到图书馆作为社区和文化中心的作用被低估。由此可知，题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的 “the world more and more digitalized” 对应原文中的 “an increasingly digital world”；题干中的 “sometimes underestimate the role of libraries as community and cultural centers” 对应原文中的 “see the role of libraries as community and cultural centers at times undervalued”。

【定位】

由题干关键信息 “programs…for children and adolescents”、“help narrow the gap” 和 “varying economic backgrounds” 定位到 L 段。

【解析】

该段首句提到，为儿童和青少年提供的免费辅导、家庭作业辅导项目和暑期阅读项目有助于缩小影响学生成绩的经济差距。由此可知，题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的 “for children and adolescents” 对应原文中的 “for kids and teens”；题干中的 “narrow the gap between students from varying economic backgrounds” 对应原文中的 “bridge the economic divide that impacts students’ academic performance”。

【定位】

由题干关键信息 “an organized archive”、“family history” 和 “ancestors” 定位到 F 段。

【解析】

该段第三句提到，一个井然有序的档案馆可供人们研究家族史和移民史、进行环境研究等。由此可知，题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的 “an organized archive” 属于原词重现；题干中的 “their family history…the new land” 对应原文中的 “their ancestry and immigration history”。

【定位】

由题干关键信息 “people of different income levels” 和 “free of charge” 定位到 H 段。

【解析】

该段第二句提到，尽管音乐会和剧院门票的价格不断上涨，但公共图书馆的活动（包括音乐会、作者访问和画廊展览）通常都还是免费提供的，使得任何收入水平的人都能参加。由此可知，题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的 “free of charge” 属于原词重现；题干中的 “cultural events” 对应原文中的 “public library events (including concerts, author visits, and gallery displays)”；题干中的 “allowing” 对应原文中的 “enabling”；题干中的 “people of different income levels” 对应原文中的 “people of any income level”。

【定位】

由题干关键信息 “being an information provider” 和 “many other important services” 定位到 B 段。

【解析】

该段第二至四句提到，图书馆不仅仅是书籍和电脑的集中存放地，还是人们聚在一起探索发现、交流互动和展开想象的场所。图书馆为社区增添价值并成为读者文化中心的具体方式包括：促进社区建设、成为艺术中心以及支持青少年成长。图书馆在这些方面都发挥着作用，其意义远不止于提供信息。由此可知，题干是对原文的同义概述。

【定位】

由题干关键信息 “help build small communities” 和 “backgrounds and ideologies” 定位到 K 段。

【解析】

该段第二句提到，公共图书馆通过 “人类图书馆” 和 “苏格拉底咖啡馆” 等项目，帮助建立小型的多元社区，鼓励人们通过对话相互交流和学习。由此可知，题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的 “small communities of people with different backgrounds and ideologies” 对应原文中的 “small communities of difference”。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 Nationally, one in six children miss 15 or more days of school in a year. 2 Education officials have deplored all this missed instruction.
1 These chronically absent students suffer academically because of all the classroom instruction they miss out on. 2 In 2015, the U.S. secretary of education responded to this crisis, urging communities to support every student to attend every day and be successful in school. 3 His open letter stated that missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason — excused or unexcused — is a primary cause of low academic achievement.?
1 Worrying about whether children attend school makes sense. 2 After all, if students don’t show up, teachers can’t teach them.
1 But what if America’s attendance crisis is about much more than students missing class? 2 What if, instead, it is a reflection of family and community crises these students face — such as being ejected from the family apartment, fearing for their safety in their neighborhood or suffering an illness?
1 As social scientists we investigated how excused and unexcused absences relate to children’s academic achievement.
1 We find that absences excused by a parent do little to harm children’s learning. 2 In fact, children with no unexcused absences — but 15 to 18 excused absences — have test scores equal to their peers who have no absences.
1 Meanwhile, the average child with even just one unexcused absence does much worse academically than peers with none.?
1 We believe unexcused absence is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face, including economic and medical hardships. 2 Unexcused absences can be a powerful signal of how those out-of-school challenges affect children’s academic progress.?
1 Our evidence suggests unexcused absences are problematic, but for a different reason than people often think. 2 Absence from school, and especially unexcused absence, matters mainly as a signal of many crises children and their families may be facing. 3 It matters less as a cause of lower student achievement due to missed instruction.
1 How we choose to think of school absences matters for educational policy. 2 School attendance policies typically hold schools and families accountable for the days children miss, regardless of whether they were excused or unexcused absences.
1 These policies assume that missing school for any reason harms children academically because they are missing classroom instruction. 2 They also assume that schools will be able to effectively intervene by reducing student absences. 3 We find neither to be the case.?
1 As a result, these attendance policies end up disproportionately punishing families dealing with out-of-school crises in their lives and pressuring schools who serve them to get students to school more often.
1 We instead suggest using unexcused absence from school as a signal to channel resources to the children and families who need them most.?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is of vital importance to respond promptly to the school absence crisis.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The academic performance of chronically absent students is deplorable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Low academic achievement is mainly attributed to school absences.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The effect of school absences on American education is worrisome.

questions.explanation:
由题干信息词 “U.S. secretary of education” 和 “open letter” 可将答案线索定位至第2段2，3句。

2段2句指出：美国教育部长对这场危机做出了回应（the U.S. secretary of education responded to this crisis），敦促各社区支持每一位学生每天到校上课（urging communities to support every student to attend every day），并在学校取得成功（and be successful in school.），但该句中并未提及公开信，故需要继续阅读下一句。  

2段3句以公开信开头，信中指出：无论出于何种原因（ for any reason），一年中缺课天数达到 10% （missing 10% of school days in a year）是学业成绩低下的主要原因（is a primary cause of low academic achievement）。

综上可知，美国教育部长在公开信中说到的是内容是学生成绩低下的主要原因（是因为缺课），故C 项（Low academic achievement is mainly attributed to school absences 学业成绩低下主要归因于缺课）与原文表述相符，该选项中的 ���Low academic achievement” 是原词复现，“is mainly attributed to” 是原文中 “is a primary cause” 的同义转述，故为正确答案。

choices.label: B

questions.explanation:
【定位】由题干信息词 “find” 和 “school absences” 可将答案线索定位至第 6 段和第 7 段。

【定位内容分析】

第 5 段阐述了调查内容，即：可谅解和不可谅解的缺课与儿童学业成绩的关系（how excused and unexcused absences relate to children’s academic achievement）。

第 6 段指出研究发现：家长批准的缺课（absences excused by a parent）对孩子的学习几乎没有损害（do little to harm children’s learning）。

第 7 段提出递进支持研究发现：即使只有一次无故缺课的普通孩子（the average child with even just one unexcused absence），在学业上也比没有无故缺课的同龄人差得多（does much worse academically than peers with none）。

【正确选项对比】综上，第 6 段明确提到家长批准的缺课（即因故缺课）对孩子学习影响小，A 选项（Excused school absences have little impact on children’s learning. 因故缺课对儿童学习影响甚微）与原文表述一致，故为正确答案。

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are likely to cause a decrease in students’ academic achievements due to missed instruction.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are matters the American government typically ignores when formulating educational policies.

choices.label: D

questions.explanation:
【定位】根据顺序出题原则，结合题干定位关键词 “unexcused school absences” 可将答案线索定位至第 8 段1句。

【定位内容分析】

8段1句指出：作者认为不可谅解缺课是儿童和家庭面临许多挑战的强烈信号（unexcused absence is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face），包括经济和医疗困难（including economic and medical hardships）。

8段2句递进指出：不可谅解缺课（Unexcused absences）可以有力地表明（can be a powerful signal of）那些校外挑战是如何影响儿童学业进步的（how those out-of-school challenges affect children’s academic progress）。

【正确选项对比】综上，B 选项（They point directly to many of the out-of-school challenges confronting children and their families. 它们直接指向儿童及其家庭面临的许多在学校以外的挑战）与原文中对无故缺课的看法一致，故为正确答案。

choices.label: B

choices.label: C

questions.explanation:
【定位】由题干信息词 “assumption” 和 “education policies” 可将答案线索定位至第 11 段。

【定位内容分析】第 11 段提到美国教育政策的两种潜在假设：一是无论出于何种原因缺课都会对孩子的学业造成伤害，因为他们错过了课堂教学（These policies assume that missing school for any reason harms children academically because they are missing classroom instruction）；二是学校能够通过减少学生缺课来有效干预（They also assume that schools will be able to effectively intervene by reducing student absences）。

【正确选项对比】综上，B 选项（Schools can boost children’s academic performance by effective intervention. 学校可以通过有效干预提高儿童的学习成绩）与第二种假设相符，故为正确答案。

choices.label: C
choices.text: Directing resources to helping needy children.

choices.label: D

questions.explanation:
【定位】由题干信息词 “suggest” 和 “school absences” 可将答案线索定位至文第 13 段。

【定位内容分析】13段提到：作者建议（We instead suggest）将不可谅解的缺课作为一种信号（using unexcused absence from school as a signal），将资源引导到最需要的儿童和家庭手中（to channel resources to the children and families who need them most）。

【正确选项对比】综上，C 选项（Directing resources to helping needy children. 将资源导向帮助贫困的儿童）与原文建议一致，其中选项中的Directing为对原文to channel的同义替换，选项中的to helping needy children为对原文to the children and families who need them most的同义替换，故该选项为正确答案。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 After earning a bachelor’s degree, I was determined to do what I love. 2 I headed straight to graduate school to investigate the social problems that fascinated me.
1 For almost a decade, I told everyone I encountered that they should do the same. 2 “Follow your passion,” I counseled. 3 “You can figure out the employment stuff later.”?
1 It wasn’t until I began to research this widely accepted career advice that I understood how problematic it really was.
1 As a sociologist, I interviewed college students and professional workers to learn what it really meant to pursue their dreams, which I will refer to here as the passion principle. 2 I was stunned by what I found out about this principle in the research for my new book.?
1 Surveys show the American public has long held the passion principle in high regard as a career decision-making priority. 2 And its popularity is even stronger among those facing job instability.
1 Advocates of the passion principle found it compelling because they believed that following one’s passion can provide workers with both the motivation necessary to work hard and a place to find fulfillment.
1 Yet, what I found is that following one’s passion does not necessarily lead to fulfillment, but is one of the most powerful cultural forces perpetuating overwork. 2 I also found that promoting the pursuit of one’s passion helps perpetuate social inequalities due to the fact that not everyone has the same economic resources to allow them to pursue their passion with ease.
1 While the passion principle is broadly popular, not everyone has the necessary resources to turn their passion into a stable, good-paying job. 2 Passion-seekers from wealthy families are better able to wait until a job they are passionate about comes along without worrying about student loans in the meantime. 3 They are also better situated to take unpaid internships to get their foot in the door while their parents pay their rent. 4 And they often have access to parents’ social networks to help them find jobs.? 5 Surveys revealed that working-class and first-generation college graduates, regardless of their career field, are more likely than their wealthier peers to end up in low-paying unskilled jobs when they pursue their passion.
1 Colleges, workplaces and career counselors who promote the “follow your passion” path for everyone, without leveling the playing field, help perpetuate socioeconomic inequalities among career aspirants.?
1 It’s not just well-off passion-seekers who benefit from the passion principle. 2 Employers of passionate workers do, too. 3 Potential employers showed greater interest in passionate applicants in part because they believed the applicants would work hard at their jobs without expecting an increase in pay. 4 They even sacrifice a good salary, job stability and leisure time to work in a job they love.?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Figure out what is the most fascinating job.

choices.label: D

【定位内容分析】

第2 段1句指出：在将近十年的时间里（For almost a decade），作者告诉每一个遇到的人也应该这样做（I told everyone I encountered that they should do the same），结合第 1 段可知作者所指是做自己热爱的事（After earning a bachelor’s degree, I was determined to do what I love）。

2段3句继续补充： “工作的事情可以以后再考虑”（You can figure out the employment stuff later）

【正确选项对比】综上可知，在近十年来，作者建议人们追随自己的热爱，故D 选项（Do whatever they are zealous for. 做任何他们热爱的事情）与原文中作者建议人们做自己热爱的事表述相符，是对原文的同义转述，故为正确答案。

questions.explanation:
【定位】由题干信息词 “author feel”、“passion principle” 和 “research” 可将答案线索初步定位于第 4 段-2句。

【定位内容分析】4段2句指出：在为新书做研究的过程中，作者对这一原则的发现让自己感到震惊（I was stunned by what I found out about this principle in the research for my new book）。后文详细阐述了 “热爱原则” 存在的问题，如导致过度工作、加剧社会不平等、被雇主利用等。

【正确选项对比】综上，可知，作者通过研究，对 “热情原则” 有何感受的感受为震惊，故A 选项（He was astonished by its consequences. 他对它的后果感到震惊）准确对应原文，其中 “consequences（后果）” 概括了后文分析的所有负面影响，原文中的 “stunned” 对应选项中的 “astonished”，故为正确答案。

【定位】由题干信息词 “turn one’s passion into a stable, good-paying job” 可将答案线索定位至8段1句。

【定位内容分析】

8 段1句指出：尽管 “热爱原则” 广受欢迎（While the passion principle is broadly popular），但并非所有人都拥有必要的资源将热爱转化为一份稳定且高薪的工作（not everyone has the necessary resources to turn their passion into a stable, good - paying job）。

8段2句进一步指出：来自富裕家庭、追求热爱的人（Passion-seekers from wealthy families）更有能力等待心仪工作机会（are better able to wait until a job they are passionate about comes along），无需担心学生贷款（without worrying about student loans in the meantime）。

8段4句还指出：他们还能借助父母社交网络找工作（And they often have access to parents’ social networks to help them find jobs.）。

【正确选项对比】综上可知若想要将热情转化为稳定高薪工作，重要的因素是需要有8段2-4句中提到的家庭经济支持和父母的社交网络支持，这些都体现了经济支持和社会关系的重要性，D 选项（Financial backing and social connections. 经济支持和社会关系）是对原文8段2-4句的合理概括和总结，故为正确答案。

【定位内容分析】9段1句指出：大学、职场以及职业顾问（Colleges, workplaces and career counselors）若向所有人宣扬 “追随热爱” 的道路（who promote the “follow your passion” path for everyone），却不创造公平的竞争环境（without leveling the playing field），这会加剧职业追求者之间的社会经济不平等（help perpetuate socioeconomic inequalities among career aspirants）。

【定位】由题干信息词 “potential employers” 和 “more interested in passionate job applicants” 可将答案线索定位至第 10 段2-3句。

【定位内容分析】

10段2句指出：潜在雇主（Potential employers）对有热爱的求职者更感兴趣（showed greater interest in passionate applicants），部分原因是（in part because）他们认为这些求职者会努力工作（they believed the applicants would work hard at their jobs），且不期待加薪（without expecting an increase in pay）。

sections.title: 听力
sections.passage:
W: We are down to two candidates for one position, and we need to decide by the end of the day in order to finalize this whole procedure.
M: [1] Yes, but it's not an easy choice to make. Both applicants are quite strong.
W: Let's get to it, then. Both of them went to good universities, and both of them studied business-related subjects. So academically, I'd say they're pretty much the same. What do you think?
M: I would agree, yes. [2] The only difference worth noting, perhaps, is that it looks like Rachel scored moderately stronger grades throughout high school and university. But as I said, only a tiny bit higher than Peter.
W: [2] That's true, and worth noting. Thank you. In addition, Rachel interviewed very well. I thought she came across as bright and alert.
M: Yes. She asked some very good questions about the position and the company, which made me think she is very keen about the job.
W: I thought so, too. Now, let's look at Peter's interview performance. I thought he also did very well. He came across as respectful and professional, wouldn't you say? Calm and poised. Very mature for his age.
M: Exactly. In my notes, I wrote that he seemed composed and in control of his emotions. I think he definitely looked more mature than Rachel.
W: Interesting. So, we agree that Rachel appeared inexperienced and less mature than Peter, even though both candidates are the same age and have practically no work experience.
M: [3] When comparing them side by side, yes, Peter seemed more self-assured somehow. Maybe it was something about their body language.
W: Sure. Maybe he was simply less nervous.
M: Maybe. Who knows? To be honest, I think I like Rachel better.
W: Hmm. Really? I think I like Peter.
M: Ah, well. [4] If there's a tie, and we can't come to an agreement, then we'll take it to John and let him cast the deciding vote.
Q1：Why does the man think it is difficult to make the decision?
Q2：What do the speakers say may be worth noting?
Q3：According to the man, what might account for Peter appearing somewhat more self-assured than Rachel?
Q4：What does the man say they will do if they can't reach an agreement?
M: [5] We're here with Clementine Ortega, head designer of the private fashion label L'Orange, to discuss her latest collection. Ms. Ortega, how would you describe this season's look?
W: To be honest, my preferred style has always been on the ambiguous side, and I think this collection is even more so. I try not to adhere to social norms and expectations. [6] Rather, I always try to incorporate something slightly absurd into my aesthetic.
M: The assortments of accessories in this collection have had quite the impact on critics. The dazzling cape deployed at the end of the show, for example, bewildered many in the audience. What was your inspiration for this piece?
W: Over the summer, I traveled through rural mountain villages throughout Asia in search of handicrafts to decorate my new studio with. The embroidery done by the women in a particular village was so exquisite. I couldn't stop thinking about it. Trying to recreate their designs would have been futile. So instead, I applied my own eccentric approach. Using glitter, I drew similar intricate patterns onto the velvet cape. This ended up in the glamorous, luminous look that concluded the show.
M: It was indeed majestic, and yet, dare I say, masculine at the same time.
W: Well, yes, that was intentional. [7] I like to merge styles that are often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum. Hence, the sparkling cape was paired with a traditional power suit you would typically see in a business setting. It was sensational, if I do say so myself.
M: Spectacular for sure! A stunning show all around. Going against stereotypes, the incorporation of indigenous aspects, along with your underlying signature touch, made this collection a statement of the season. [8] You have proven yourself a formidable young designer, and we can't wait to see what creations you come up with next.
Q5：What are the speakers mainly talking about?
Q6：What does the woman say she always tries to incorporate into her aesthetic?

Think your refrigerator is just one big box of evenly cold air?
Not so!
[12] The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies from front to back, bottom to top and everywhere in between.
Because of this, food product placement within the appliance is far more important than you probably realize.
[13] The whole purpose of the modern refrigerator is to slow the growth of bacteria, which thrive in temperatures from 4.4 to 60 degrees Celsius.
As a result, refrigerators are typically set at or below that low end to protect foods against bacteria.
Although it might seem like time spent organizing the fridge will spoil your day, doing so will actually make it more user-friendly, easier to clean and food safety-conscious.
Those little bins on the inside of refrigerator doors are convenient, but they don’t maintain a consistent temperature, so definitely refrain from putting perishable foods in there.
The top area is not as cold as the bottom of the fridge, so save it for the foods that don’t need extra-chilly temperatures.
[14] Store foods that are ready to eat or already cooked on the top shelf.
The middle shelf is the most temperature-controlled part of the fridge, so place eggs here.
Drinks and prepared foods can also live on the middle shelf if you ran out of room up top.
The back of the bottom shelf is the coldest spot in the fridge, so store perishable dairy products here to keep them edible longer.
[15] Never store foods with high water content here, because the water within them can and will freeze, effectively ruining them.

My current research is mainly looking at factors like stress and how it affects our immune system.

There’s a lot more people in the older generation who are living for longer but not necessarily staying healthy for a large part of their lives.

Americans are obsessed with celebrity chefs.
We talk about them and try to eat like them.
But could we learn something more from them than recipes and techniques?
According to market data enterprises, Americans spend nearly 10 billion dollars a year on self-help and personal-organization products.
[19] The market is huge, partly because most colleges and graduate schools don’t teach basic organization, but cooking schools and professional kitchens do.
Perhaps the principles of cooking organization can be extended to help even those of us who aren’t top chefs.
The system that makes kitchens function is called “mise-en-place”, or literally “put in place”.
It’s a French phrase that means to gather and arrange the ingredients and tools needed for cooking.
But for many professional cooks, the phrase means something deeper.
Some cooks call it their religion.
It helps them coordinate vast amounts of labor and material, and transforms the lives of its practitioners through focus and self-discipline.
[20] Students at the culinary institute of America view it as a way of life.
It’s a way of concentrating their mind to only focus on the aspects that they need to be working on at the moment, to kind of rid themselves of distractions.
And it’s a habit that some students carry with them even when they’re not in the kitchen.
They mise-en-place their life.
They set up their books for class.
They set up their chef whites.
They shine their shoes.
They know everything that they need every step of the day.
Then how does one attain this level of organization?
The key to high-level organization is the mindset.
Cooks can easily do six hours of preparation for a three-hour dinner shift.
“Mise-en-place forces cooks to account for every minute of their time and every movement.
Every component of one single dish is in one single corner, so their hand literally moves inches,” explains Dwayne Lipuma, an instructor at the culinary institute of America.
“Once students set up their station, I should be able to cover up their eyes.
And they should know that their knives are always here, their oil is always right here, their salt and pepper is always right here.”
[21] But practiced at its highest level, mise-en-place says that time is precious, resources are precious, space is precious, your self-respect and the respect of others are precious.
Use them wisely.
Isn’t that a philosophy for our time?

Why do we stop making goals for ourselves and stop progressing in life?
One reason is the belief that we should accept who we are and not constantly strive to improve ourselves.
[22] The mistake we make with this is that whilst self-acceptance is imperative, it should actually be used as the basis for growth.
When we're not growing, learning and seeking improvements in our lives, we tend to stagnate, accepting what is, and stop believing we can be better.
A key tool for creating goals and progressing, is using our imagination.
[23] Yet as is so often the case, by the time we've reached midlife, we've stopped dreaming about what we want to achieve and feel quite negatively about goal setting.
Instead of feeling confidence, happiness and satisfaction from achieving our goals, we feel we are always falling short.
That leads to disappointment, and we stop dreaming.
We stop imagining the life we'd like to have or the person we'd like to be, quickly finding ourselves shattered by the pain of our reality.
Up until now, unless we work in the creative industry, we've found the idea of using "play" a bit childish.
In the West, we're mostly operating from our heads, the rational mind.
But it's beginning to be better understood, because using our imagination is actually one of the most powerful things we could ever do.
[24] The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal is because the goal always changes and we're always adapting, whether we realize it or not.
What happens, therefore, is that we end up feeling like we're never going to reach our goals.
And herein lies one of the biggest misconceptions and reasons for failure, dissatisfaction and unhappiness.
We measure against the goal, rather than where we've come from.
Dan Sullivan calls this "the gap and the gain".
We measure always against the goal, which we never feel we're reaching, rather than the gain, that is where we've come from.
[25] In measuring where we've come from, rather than where we're trying to get to, we see results.
We see things we've taken for granted, or not noticed.
It's a simple, yet profound change in perception, and what I love about it is the power it has to instantly shift us up a gear.
It's so, so simple, yet has an immediate, positive impact on our thinking.

questions.explanation: 【解析】讲话者在讲话中提到，当��们步入中年时，我们便不再憧憬自己想要达成的目标，而且对设定目标这件事也产生了消极的看法。不再憧憬自己想要达成的目标，即不再憧憬更大的进步，选项 D 为正确答案。讲话者提到，步入中年后我们不再因实现目标而感到自信、快乐和满足，反而会觉得自己总是达不到目标，故排除选项 A 和选项 B。选项 C 讲话中并未提及，可排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: We feel we are always falling behind others.

choices.label: B
choices.text: We have to adapt to the ever-changing goal.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There are various misconceptions about goal setting.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There are always problems with the goal originally set.

questions.explanation: 【解析】讲话者在讲话中间提到，我们之所以会因未能达成目标而感到恼怒，是因为目标总是会变化，而我们也在不断调整适应。因此，选项 B 为正确答案。其余三项讲话者均未提及，可排除。

choices.label: A
choices.text: A noticeable change in the number of goals to achieve.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Measuring always against the gap rather than the gain.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Measuring where we’ve come from instead of measuring against the goal.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A proper conception of what we fail to notice in trying to achieve our goals.

questions.explanation: 【解析】讲话者在讲话末尾部分提到，当我们衡量曾经的境况（即 “收益”）而非要实现的目标时，才能真正看到成果。这是一个简单却意义深远的观念的转变，它有能力瞬间提升我们的思维层次。它如此简单，却能对我们的思维产生立竿见影的积极影响。故选项 C 为正确答案。而选项 B 与讲话内容完全相反，故排除。其余两项讲话者均未提及，可排除。

sections.title: Part 1 Writing 写作
sections.passage:
1 As social media is used more and more extensively, there is a growing awareness of the importance of using it properly and responsibly. 2 This growing concern may lead to polarized debates and eroded trust if not addressed properly. 3 From my perspective, multidimensional strategies can help society harness social media more constructively.
1 First, fostering digital mindfulness empowers us to scrutinize information sources, resisting algorithmic echo chambers and misinformation. 2 Setting intentional usage boundaries also matters—designating tech-free intervals and curating educational content in feeds reduces digital exhaustion while boosting knowledge. 3 Additionally, educational institutions and regulators should roll out systemic digital literacy programs. 4 With age-tailored curricula covering cyber ethics, privacy protection, and fact-checking skills, individuals can evolve into discerning digital citizens, less prone to manipulation or anxiety.
1 In essence, collaborative efforts can transform the digital realm into a driver of informed progress. 2 It’s time to engage with social media through critical thinking and ethical practice.

questions.answer: 1 The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area is endowed with exceptional geographic location, well-developed transportation infrastructure, and abundant industrial resources. 2 As one of China’s most open and economically vibrant regions, the Greater Bay Area holds significant strategic importance in the nation’s economic development. 3 It will be developed not only into a dynamic world-class city cluster and an international technology innovation hub with global influence, but also into a high-quality living circle ideal for working, shopping, and tourism. 4 With the deepening of reform and opening-up, the construction of the Greater Bay Area will further propel regional economic growth. 5 By 2035, the Greater Bay Area will achieve its goal of becoming a world-class bay area.

sections.title: Section A 选词填空
sections.passage:
1 No beast on Earth is tougher than the tiny tardigrade (缓步类动物). 2 It can 1 being frozen at -272° Celsius, being exposed to the vacuum of outer space and even being 2 with 500 times the dose of X-rays that would kill a human.? 3 In other words, the creature can endure conditions that don’t even exist on Earth. 4 And researchers are looking to the microscopic animals to learn how to prepare humans and crops to handle the 3 of space travel.?
1 The tardigrade’s indestructibility stems from its 4 to its environment — which may seem surprising, since it lives in 5 comfortable places, like the cool, wet patches of moss (青苔) that dot a garden wall.?
1 But it turns out that a tardigrade’s damp, mossy home can dry out many times each year. 2 Drying is pretty 6 for most living things.? 3 It does damage to cells in some of the same ways that freezing, vacuum and radiation do. 4 Tardigrades, however, have 7 special strategies for dealing with these kinds of damage.?
1 As a tardigrade dries out, its cells produce several strange proteins that are unlike anything found in other animals. 2 In water, the proteins are shapeless. 3 But as water disappears, the proteins self-assemble into long fibers that fill the cell’s 8.? 4 The fibers support the cell’s membranes (细胞膜) and proteins, preventing them from breaking or 9.?
1 Emulating tardigrades could one day help humans colonize outer space. 2 Food crops could be engineered to produce tardigrade proteins, allowing these organisms to grow more efficiently on spacecraft where levels of radiation are elevated compared with on Earth.
1 So if humans ever succeed in reaching the stars, they may accomplish this 10, in part, by standing on the shoulders of the tiny eight-legged endurance specialists in your backyard.?

questions.explanation:
【词义判断】

空格前是情态动词 can，空格后是 being frozen at，由此可知，空格处应填入一个动词原形，与动名词短语 being frozen at 构成动宾搭配。


【解析】

文章首句提及，地球上没有哪种生物比微小的缓步类动物更坚韧。本句承接上文，举例说明其坚韧性，由此可知，此处是说缓步类动物可以在零下 272 摄氏度的严寒中 “存活”，survive 符合语境，故选 K。

【词义判断】

空格前是 being，空格后是介词 with，由此可知，空格处应填入一个形容词或过去分词。


【解析】

由 and 可知前后为并列关系，故空格所在分句仍在举例说明缓步类动物的坚韧性。与 “在零下 272 摄氏度的严寒中存活” 构成并列关系的应该是 “甚至能承受比人类致死剂量高出 500 倍的 X 射线辐射”，blast 意为 “向…… 猛吹或喷射”，在此处可引申为 X 射线的辐射，符合语境，故选 B。

【词义判断】

空格前是定冠词 the，空格后是介词短语 of space travel，由此可知，空格处应填入一个名词。


【解析】

联系本段前面讲述的缓步类动物极度坚韧的特点可知，此处是说，研究人员正从这种微观动物身上探寻奥秘，以学习如何让人类和农作物做好准备，应对太空旅行的 “严酷” 挑战，rigors 符合语境，故选 I。

【词义判断】

空格前是形容词性物主代词 its，空格后是介词短语 to its environment，由此可知，空格处应填入一个名词，且能与介词 to 搭配使用。


【解析】

本句主语 tardestructibility 的意思是 “不可摧毁的特性”，而谓语 stems from 意为 “源于”，由此可知，本句揭示缓步类动物不可摧毁的特性的来源。这种动物能在各种极其恶劣的环境下生存，说明它们对环境的适应能力惊人，adaptations 符合语境，故选 A。

【词义判断】

空格前是动词短语 lives in，空格后是其宾语 comfortable places，由此可知，空格应填入一个副词，对形容词 comfortable 进行修饰和限制。


【解析】

由 which may seem surprising（这似乎令人惊讶）可知，此处用 since 引导原因状语从句解释它似乎令人惊讶的原因，由下一段的开头句 “但事实证明，缓步类动物潮湿的苔藓家园每年会多次干涸” 可知，缓步类动物生活的环境只是看似舒适，故空格处应填入 seemingly，表示 “看似（但可能并非如此）”，故选 J。

【词义判断】

空格前是 is pretty，空格后是介词短语 for most living things，由此可知，空格处应填入一个形容词，构成 “be+adj.+for” 的结构，pretty 为副词，意为 “十分，很”，修饰该形容词。


【解析】

由常识可知，生物生长需要水，干燥缺水对于大多数生物而言都是灾难性的，catastrophic 符合语境，故选 C。

【词义判断】

空格前为 Tardigrades, however, have，空格后为名词短语 special strategies，由此可知空格处应填入一个过去分词，构成 have done 现在完成时的结构。


【解析】

上文提到，干燥对大多数生物来说是灾难性的，它对细胞造成损害的方式与冷冻、真空和辐射造成损害的方式部分相同。本句话锋一转，讲述特殊情况，即缓步类动物例外，它们进化出了应对这类损害的特殊策略，故 evolved 符合语境，本题应选 D。

【词义判断】

空格前为 long fibers that fill the cell's，空格后为句点，由此可知 that 引导定语从句，修饰先行词 fibers，该定语从句的谓语动词 fill 缺少宾语中心词，空格处应填入一个名词。


【解析】

由下一句的内容 “这些纤维支撑着细胞的细胞膜和蛋白质，防止它们破裂……” 可知，在水分消失的情况下，缓步类动物的蛋白质自我生成的长纤维对细胞的细胞膜和蛋白质起支撑作用，因此它应位于细胞的内部，interior 符合语境，故选 F。

【词义判断】

空格前是连词 or，空格后是句点，由此可知，空格处应填入一个与 breaking 并列的动名词。


【解析】

结合上一题的分析，此处说的是长纤维的作用，即它支撑细胞的细胞膜和蛋白质，防止细胞膜和蛋白质破裂或 “展开”，unfolding 符合语境，故选 O。

【词义判断】

空格前是 they may accomplish this，空格后是逗号，由此可知，空格处应填入一个名词，充当 accomplish 的宾语。


【解析】

分析句意，空格处的名词与前面的 if 从句 if humans ever succeed in reaching the stars 表达的意思一致，“人类能成功抵达其他恒星” 显然是人类的壮举或功绩，故 feat 符合语境，本题应选 E。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 As the scale and impacts of climate change become increasingly alarming, meat is a popular target for action. 2 Advocates for the protection of the natural environment from destruction or pollution urge the public to eat less meat.? 3 Some activists have even called for taxing meat to reduce consumption of it.
1 A key claim underlying these arguments holds that globally, meat production generates more greenhouse gases than the entire transportation sector. 2 However, this claim is demonstrably wrong, as I will show. 3 And its persistence has led to false assumptions about the linkage between meat and climate change.
1 My recent research focuses on ways in which animal agriculture affects air quality and climate change. 2 In my view, there are many reasons for either choosing animal protein or opting for a vegetarian selection. 3 However, abandoning meat and meat products is not the environmental panacea many would have us believe.? 4 And if taken to an extreme, it also could have harmful nutritional consequences.
1 A healthy portion of meat’s negative reputation centers on the assertion that livestock is the largest source of greenhouse gases worldwide.? 2 For example, an analysis published in 2009 by the World Watch Institute based in Washington,D.C. asserted that 51 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions come from rearing and processing livestock. 3 According to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, the largest sources of U.S. greenhouse gas emissions in 2016 were electricity production (28 percent of total emissions), transportation (28 percent) and industry (22 percent). 4 All of agriculture accounted for a total of 9 percent, but all of animal agriculture contributes less than half of this amount, representing 3.9 percent of the total greenhouse emission in the U.S. 5 That is very different from claiming that livestock represents as much as or more than transportation.
1 Why is there such a misconception? 2 In 2006 the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) published a study titled “Livestock’s Long Shadow,” which received widespread international attention. 3 It stated that livestock produced a staggering 18 percent of the world’s greenhouse gas emissions. 4 The agency drew a startling conclusion that livestock was doing more to harm the climate than all modes of transportation combined.? 5 This latter claim was wrong, and has since been corrected by Henning Stenfeld, the report’s senior author.
1 The problem was that analysts from the FAO used a comprehensive life-cycle assessment to study the climate impact of livestock, but a different method when they analyzed transportation. 2 For livestock, they considered every factor associated with producing meat. 3 This included emissions from fertilizer production, converting land from forests to pastures, growing feed, and direct emissions from animals (manure as well as expelling of gas from the stomach) from birth to death.
1 However, when they looked at transportation’s carbon footprint, they ignored impacts on the climate from manufacturing vehicle materials and parts, assembling vehicles and maintaining roads, bridges and airports. 2 Instead, they only considered the exhaust smoke emitted by finished cars, trucks, trains and planes. 3 As a result, the FAO’s comparison of greenhouse gas emissions from livestock to those from transportation was greatly distorted.
1 I pointed out this flaw during a speech to fellow scientists in San Francisco on March 22, 2010, which led to a flood of media coverage. 2 To its credit, the FAO immediately owned up to its error.? 3 Unfortunately, the agency’s initial claim that livestock was responsible for the lion’s share of world greenhouse gas emissions had already received wide coverage. 4 To this day, we struggle to “unring” the bell. 5 In its most recent assessment report, the FAO estimated that livestock produces 14.5 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions from human activities. 6 There is no comparable full life-cycle assessment for transportation. 7 However, as Stenfeld has pointed out, direct emissions from transportation versus livestock can be compared and amount to 14 versus 5 percent, respectively.
1 Many people continue to think that avoiding meat as infrequently as once a week will make a significant difference to the climate. 2 But according to one recent study, even if Americans eliminated all animal protein from their diets, they would reduce U.S. greenhouse gas emissions by only 2.6 percent.? 3 According to our research at the University of California, Davis, if the practice of Meatless Monday were to be adopted by all Americans, we’d see a reduction of only 0.5 percent.
1 Moreover, technological, genetic and management changes that have taken place in U.S. agriculture over the past 70 years have made livestock production more efficient and less greenhouse gas-intensive.? 2 According to the FAO’s statistical database, total direct greenhouse gas emissions from U.S. livestock have declined by 11.3 percent since 1961, while production of livestock meat has more than doubled.
1 Demand for meat is rising in developing and emerging economies, especially in the Middle East, North Africa and Southeast Asia. 2 For example, raising livestock such as goats in Kenya is an important source of food and income for many small-scale farmers and herders. 3 But meat consumption per person in these regions still lags that of developed countries.? 4 In 2015, average annual meat consumption per person in developed countries was 92 kilograms, compared to 24 kilograms in the Middle East and North Africa and 18 kilograms in Southeast Asia. 5 Still, given projected population growth in the developing world, there will certainly be an opportunity for countries such as the United States to bring their sustainable livestock rearing practices to the table.
1 Removing animals from U.S. agriculture would lower national greenhouse gas emissions to a small degree, but it would also make it harder to meet people’s nutritional requirements.? 2 Many critics of animal agriculture are quick to point out that if farmers raised only plants, they could produce more pounds of food and more calories per person. 3 But humans also need many essential micro- and macro-nutrients for good health. 4 It’s hard to make a compelling argument that the United States has a calorie deficit, given its high national rates of adult and child obesity. 5 Moreover, not all plant parts are edible or desirable. 6 Raising livestock is a way to add nutritional and economic value to plant agriculture.
1 As one example, the energy in plants that livestock consume is most often contained in cellulose, which is indigestible for humans and many other mammals. 2 But cows, sheep and other ruminant animals can break cellulose down and release the solar energy contained in this vast resource. 3 According to the FAO, as much as 70 percent of all agricultural land globally is range land that can only be utilized as grazing land for ruminant livestock.?
1 The world population is currently projected to reach 9.8 billion by 2050. 2 Feeding this many people will raise immense challenges. 3 Meat is more calorie-dense per serving than vegetarian options, and ruminant animals largely thrive on feed that is not suitable for humans. 4 Raising livestock also offers much-needed income for small-scale farmers in developing nations. 5 Worldwide, livestock provides a livelihood for 1 billion people.
1 Climate change demands urgent attention, and the livestock industry has a large overall environmental footprint that affects air, water and land. 2 These, combined with a rapidly rising world population, give us plenty of compelling reasons to continue to work for greater efficiencies in animal agriculture. 3 I believe the place to start is with science-based facts.

questions.explanation:
【定位】

由题干关键词 farm animals were producing more greenhouse gases than 和 transportation 定位到 E 段第四句。

【解析】

The agency 即指代前文提到的联合国粮食及农业组织，句意为 “该机构得出了一个令人震惊的结论，即畜牧业对气候的危害超过了所有交通运输方式的总和”。题干是对文章此句的同义转述，其中 concluded 对应原文中的 drew a conclusion，farm animals 对应 livestock，were producing more greenhouse gases 对应 was doing more to harm the climate，all modes of transportation combined 为文章中的原词复现。故答案为 E。

【定位】

由题干中的 Consumption of meat per person in developing countries 定位到 K 段第三句。

【解析】

本句提到了发展中国家和发达国家人均肉类消费量的对比，明确指出，这些地区的人均肉类消费量仍低于发达国家。此处的 “这些地区” 指代上文提到的中东、北非和东南亚地区等发展中国家。接下来第四句给出具体数据，进一步证明第三句所述观点。题干是对 K 段第三句的同义转述，其中 Consumption of meat per person 对应原文中的 meat consumption per person，in developing countries 对应 in these regions（指代上文中的 developing and emerging economies），is much less than 对应原文中的 lags，countries like the U.S. 对应 developed countries。故答案为 K。

【定位】

由题干关键词 the FAO 和 admitted its mistake 定位到 H 段第二句。

【解析】

第二句提到了 FAO 承认其所犯错误，指出 “值得肯定的是，联合国粮食及农业组织立即承认了这一错误”。题干是对此句的同义转述，其中 was worthy of praise 对应原文中的 To its credit，it admitted its mistake once it was pointed out 对应 the FAO immediately owned up to its error。故答案为 H。

【定位】

由题干关键词 Environmentalists 和 make people consume less meat 定位到 A 段第二句。

【解析】

该句指出，倡导保护自然环境免受破坏或污染的人士敦促公众少吃肉。题干是对此句的同义转述，其中 Environmentalists 对应原文中的 Advocates for the protection of the natural environment from destruction or pollution，try hard to make 对应 urge。故答案为 A。

【定位】

由题干关键词 Americans quit eating meat altogether 和 reduction of greenhouse gases in the U.S. 定位到 I 段第二句。

【解析】

I 段集中分析了减少食用肉类与温室气体排放量降幅之间的关系。第二句指出，近期一项研究表明，即便美国人从饮食中剔除所有动物蛋白质，美国的温室气体排放量也仅能减少 2.6%。题干是对此句的总结概括，其中 Americans quit eating meat altogether 对应原文中的 Americans eliminated all animal protein from their diets，would be slight 对应 only 2.6 percent。故答案为 I。

【定位】

由题干关键词 farmland is suitable only for animals 和 to graze on 定位到 M 段最后一句。

【解析】

该句提到，根据联合国粮食及农业组织的数据，全球高达 70% 的农业用地是牧场，这些土地只能用作反刍牲畜的放牧场地。题干是对原文此句的同义转述，其中 More than half of the world’s farmland 对应原文中的 as much as 70 percent of all agricultural land globally，is suitable only...to graze on 对应 can only be utilized as grazing land，animals like cows 对应 ruminant livestock。故答案为 M。

【定位】

由题干关键词 meat’s bad reputation 定位到 D 段第一句。

【解析】

该句指出，肉类的负面声誉在很大程度上源于一种说法，即畜牧业是全球最大的温室气体排放源。题干是对此句的同义转述，其中 allegation 对应原文中的 assertion，farm animals produce the world’s largest portion of greenhouse gases 对应 livestock is the largest source of greenhouse gases worldwide，is responsible for 对应 centers on。故答案为 D。

【定位】

由题干关键词 Raising farm animals 和 meet people’s nutritional needs 定位到 L 段的第一句。

【解析】

该句提到，若将畜牧业从美国农业中移除，会使满足人们的营养需求变得更加困难。反过来说，也就是发展畜牧业更有助于满足人们的营养需求。题干是对文章此处的同义转述，其中 Raising farm animals 对应原文中的 Removing animals from U.S. agriculture，makes it easier 对应 make it harder，needs 对应 requirements。故答案为 L。

【定位】

由题干中的关键词 a cure-all for the environmental problem 定位到 C 段第三句。

【解析】

该句提到，彻底放弃肉类及肉制品并非许多人想让我们相信的那样，是环境的 “万能解药”。题干是对原文此句的同义转述，其中 giving up 对应原文中的 abandoning，a cure-all for the environmental problem 对应 the environmental panacea。故答案为 C。

【定位】

由题干关键词 Changes in America’s farming technology and management 定位到 J 段第一句。

【解析】

该句提出，过去 70 年间美国农业领域在技术、基因和管理方面的变革已使畜牧业的生产效率提升，温室气体排放强度降低。题干是对文章此句的同义转述，其中 Changes in America’s farming technology and management 对应原文中的 technological, genetic and management changes that have taken place in U.S. agriculture，in the past decades 对应 over the past 70 years，increased efficiency 对应 made...more efficient，reduced greenhouse gas emissions 对应 less greenhouse gas-intensive，meat production 对应 livestock production。故答案为 J。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 Why are we so worried about our careers? 2 Partly it’s to do with money, but there’s a psychological aspect to our fears as well.
1 We worry because we suspect — not wrongly — that the world is full of a frightening sort of person ready to judge us ruthlessly and swiftly: a person we can call a snob.?
1 A snob is anyone who takes a relatively small part of us and uses it to come to a rigid conclusion about how much of their attention we deserve. 2 In the past, that might be your ancestry and royal connections. 3 Nowadays, the snob cares about one thing only: what you do for a living.?
1 This explains why the first question we will be asked in any new social context is ‘What do you do?’ and according to how we answer, snobs will either welcome us with broad smiles, or leave us in the cold.
1 And that is why we are fired up by such a desperate urge to achieve and impress.
1 Sometimes our behaviour is mistaken for greed and vanity, but it is more than this. 2 A lot of our interest in fancy cars, jobs and houses has nothing to do with materialism. 3 It has to do with a hunger for the respect and esteem that is only available in our societies through the acquisition of material goods.? 4 It isn’t the goods themselves we seek, it is the love we stand to gain through our possession of them. 5 The next time we see someone driving a Ferrari, we shouldn’t condemn them for their greed, we should pity them for the intensity of their need for love from the world.
1 At the root of snobbery is a lack of imagination and confidence about how to decide who in the world is valuable. 2 The snobs are brutally misguided and slavish in their beliefs about how the superior individuals can be identified. 3 For snobs, it is the already acclaimed and already successful who are the only ones worthy of respect.? 4 There is no room in their timid regimented minds to imagine that someone might be clever, kind or good — and yet somehow have been overlooked entirely by society, their qualities lying hidden beneath an unfamiliar veil, and having as yet discovered no obvious outlet.
1 The true answer to snobbery is not to say that there is no such thing as a better or worse person, but to insist that better or worse exist in constantly unexpected places and carry none of the outward signs of distinction.? 2 And because we are such poor judges of the worth of others, our ultimate duty remains to be kind, good, curious and imaginative about pretty much everyone who ever crosses our path.

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 Women have historically been paid less. 2 But in the US in the 1980s, they began to catch up — fast. 3 During that decade, the gender pay gap closed by about one percentage point a year. 4 Had that trend continued, the gender wage gap would have been closed by 2017.?
1 But the trend didn’t continue, and the gap remains yawning.
1 According to a new study from academics at Harvard, the stagnation can be put down, perhaps counterintuitively, to the introduction of state and federal family leave policies.
1 The academics argue that during the 1990s, as governments began to introduce leave policies, it was mainly women who took advantage of them. 2 Though the leave policies might have helped those women to stay in the workplace — instead of dropping out to have families — those who returned saw their wages had increased at lower rates than the men.
1 After family leave was introduced in the US, in fact, the rate of gender wage convergence fell to just 0.03 percentage points per year, and has remained there ever since.?
1 Those monitoring the process towards salary equity at work have long watched as progress slowed in many countries around the world. 2 In fact, that progress began to reverse during the pandemic (大流行病).
1 The gender pay gap is one of the most outstanding examples of that lack of parity (平等), and still exists just about everywhere. 2 The motherhood penalty has become a shorthand for describing why: In many places, especially rich countries, women earn the same as men until they reach their childbearing years.
1 Part of this is because women take on more of the unpaid labor at home, which can eat into time available for work and energy for career advancement.? 2 But it’s also because mothers are passed over for raises and promotion, and because time out of the workplace sets women back, even if that time is taken voluntarily, and supported by company or government policy.
1 What would have happened if leave policies hadn’t been introduced? 2 The study doesn’t go into that question, other than to say that if the 1980s trend continued, we would have been at parity by now.?
1 It’s possible, however, that the journey towards wage parity would have stalled either way. 2 If women’s gains in the 1980s were made through the erasure of things like bias, once those less uncontrollable problems had been addressed, there would still have been an issue with women — who are the ones to bear children and take care of them in the early weeks because of biological factors like the ability to breastfeed, forcing them to take breaks, whether or not those breaks were mandated.?

【定位内容分析】

【正确选项对比】综上可知，20 世纪 80 年代美国的性别薪资差距正在快速缩小，故B 选项（It was shrinking rapidly. 它正快速缩小）准确概括了 20 世纪 80 年代美国性别薪资差距快速缩小的现象，故为正确答案。

文中在4段进一步指明这种薪资差距停滞的含义，即4段2句后半句指出：政策实施后，返回工作岗位的女性工资增长速度比男性慢（those who returned saw their wages had increased at lower rates than the men）。

【正确选项对比】综上可知，在实施各州和联邦家庭休假政策后，这种薪资差距停滞意味着：从每年缩小约一个百分点降至 0.03 个百分点，说明性别薪资差距缩小速度显著下降，B 选项（The rate of gender wage convergence started to fall noticeably. 性别薪资差距缩小速度开始显著下降）与原文相符，故为正确答案。

1 With the increasing application of AI technology, there is a growing concern that it may negatively impact human creativity. 2 This escalating issue may lead to creative stagnation and intellectual dependency if unaddressed. 3 Yet, practical actions can help us tackle this issue.
1 First, maintain calm and open-mindedness. 2 This avoids overreaction to AI-generated content or automation, letting us see AI as a prompt to rethink human creativity’s value. 3 Also, strengthen creative skills like critical thinking and interdisciplinary knowledge to reduce algorithm reliance. 4 Educational bodies and governments should offer support, such as ethical AI workshops and innovation-focused curricula, to foster human-AI synergy.
1 In short, proactive adaptation turns AI challenges into chances to reaffirm human uniqueness. 2 It’s time to engage with AI confidently and wisely, ensuring human ingenuity thrives.

sections.title: Part 4 Translation
sections.passage: 1 Since ancient times, China has faced an uneven distribution of water resources, with the north being water-scarce and the south water-abundant. 2 To effectively address the critical water shortage in the northern regions, the Chinese government implemented the South-to-North Water Diversion Project. 3 This is a grand water conservancy project for allocating water resources across regions. 4 After decades of planning and preparation, construction on the project began in 2002 and is divided into three routes: East, Central, and West, with a total length of 4,350 kilometers, benefiting a population of over 400 million. 5 Since its operational launch in 2014, the project has transferred more than 50 billion cubic meters of water to the north, providing a reliable water supply for the people in northern regions while significantly improving the local ecological environment and promoting sustainable and healthy economic development.

questions.stem: ①自古以来，中国的水资源北缺南丰，分布极不均衡。②为了有效解决北方严重缺水问题，中国政府实施了南水北调工程(the South-to-North Water Diversion Project)。③这是一项跨区域配置水资源的宏大水利工程。④历经数十年的规划与筹备，工程于2002年开工建设，分为东、中、西三条线路，总长4350公里，惠及人口将超过4亿。⑤自2014年通水以来，工程向北方调水累计已超500亿立方米，为北方地区的人民提供了可靠的水资源，同时也极大地改善了这一地区的生态环境，促进了经济的可持续健康发展。
questions.answer: 1 Since ancient times, China has faced an uneven distribution of water resources, with the north being water-scarce and the south water-abundant. 2 To effectively address the critical water shortage in the northern regions, the Chinese government implemented the South-to-North Water Diversion Project. 3 This is a grand water conservancy project for allocating water resources across regions. 4 After decades of planning and preparation, construction on the project began in 2002 and is divided into three routes: East, Central, and West, with a total length of 4,350 kilometers, benefiting a population of over 400 million. 5 Since its operational launch in 2014, the project has transferred more than 50 billion cubic meters of water to the north, providing a reliable water supply for the people in northern regions while significantly improving the local ecological environment and promoting sustainable and healthy economic development.
