questions.explanation:
【词性判断】

此处为because引导的原因状语从句，其主语为the number of women，而空格前为has significant，空格后为for all the policies，policies后面被that引导的定语从句修饰。由此可知，该原因状语从句缺少宾语，空格处应填入一个名词，充当has的宾语。

【解析】

下一句提到，相较于男性，女性立法者更倾向于提出、讨论并推动通过那些对妇女和女孩影响尤为显著的政策，前后句具有承接关系，可知空格所在句陈述的应该是女性立法者对国家政策的影响，consequences符合语境，故选B。

【词性判断】

结合上一题的分析可知此处为that引导的定语从句，修饰policies，而该定语从句中governments为主语，句子缺少谓语，故空格处应填入一个谓语动词。

【解析】

上文提及女性立法者会对国家政策产生影响，此处应该是指由政府“制定”的政策，enact符合语境，故选E。

【词性判断】

空格前为such as paid family leave, pay，空格后为and gender-based violence，由此可知，此处是由such as引出的表列举的事项，“pay 28”应该与paid family leave以及gender-based violence一起构成并列关系，均为名词短语，故空格处应填入一个名词。

【解析】

本句提及相较于男性，女性立法者更倾向于提出、讨论并推动通过那些对妇女和女孩影响尤为显著的政策，此处就是列举对妇女和女孩有影响的政策，由此可知，与“带薪家庭假”“性别暴力”构成并列关系的应该是“（男女）薪酬平等”，故equity符合语境，本题应选F。

【词性判断】

空格前为主语it，空格后为名词短语women's sense，由此可知，空格处应填入一个动词，充当谓语。

【解析】

本段首句提及增加国会女性席位还能增强女性选民与政府之间的联结感，这是女性从政人数增加的好处，由that引导的同位语从句that government cares about their concerns（政府关注其诉求）可知，此处要表达的意思是增加国会女性席位会强化女性对“政府关注其诉求”的���知，bolsters符合语境，故选A。

【词性判断】

空格前为is a particularly，空格后为problem in the United States，由此可知，空格处应填入一个被副词particularly修饰的形容词，充当problem的定语。

【解析】

由句首的While表达的让步转折关系和地点状语in governments around the globe可知，此处是说，尽管全球各国政府普遍存在女性代表不足的现象，但美国的这一问题尤为“严峻”，formidable符合语境，a particularly formidable problem意为“一个特别让人害怕的问题”，也就是问题比较严重的意思，故选I。

【词性判断】

空格前是副词so，空格后是形容词underrepresented，由此可知，空格处应填入一个副词，修饰underrepresented。

【解析】

上一段提及美国政府女性代表不足现象尤其严重，本段承接上一段的语义，探讨其中的原因，可知此处应填入dramatically，表示程度严重，dramatically underrepresented与上一段中的a particularly formidable problem相呼应，故选D。

【词性判断】

空格前是with similar，空格后是句号，由此可知，空格处应填入一个被similar修饰的名词，充当介词with的宾语。

【解析】

上一句提及，美国政界女性代表严重不足并非选民抵制或筹款困难，本句使用了表示情况相反的短语On the contrary（相反），可知，本句陈述的是女性政客的筹款能力或选民支持情况。由本句中提到的女性候选人筹款能力与胜选率与男性政客持平的内容可知，此处是说“在资质相当的情况下”，这样两者才具有可比性，credentials符合语境，故选C。

【词性判断】

分析本句结构可知，more women need to run是主句，句首是目的状语，空格后on Republican tickets是介词短语，也充当状语，故空格处应填入一个副词，充当状语修饰介词短语on Republican tickets。

【解析】

下一句提及这要求共和党整体优先招募女性，众所周知，美国是两党制，这里特别提到美国共和党要招募女性，可知空格所在句是说，为了让女性获得国会半数席位，就需要更多女性参选——尤其是作为共和党候选人，故especially符合语境，本题应选G。

【词性判断】

空格前是This will require the Republican Party as a whole to，空格后是recruiting women，可知空格处应填入一个动词原形，与to一起构成不定式短语，表示目的。

【解析】

recruiting women是该不定式的宾语，意为“招募女性”，再结合全文反复提及的要增加女性在国会中的席位可知，此处说的是要把招募女性作为优先事项来考虑，prioritize符合语境，故选L。

【词性判断】

空格前为in a，空格后为way，由此可知，空格处应填入一个形容词或分词，充当定语修饰名词way。

【解析】

本句为破折号后的内容，表示进一步说明，且采用了not just... but...的并列结构，表示“不仅……而且……”，那么由not just for one election cycle（不仅仅是在一个选举周期内）可知，but后面的部分应表示“长期”的含义，sustained表示“持续的”，暗含长期的意味，符合语境，故选N。

sections.title: Section B 快速阅读
sections.passage:
1 I can be a reluctant socialiser. 2 I’m sometimes secretly pleased when social plans are called off. 3 I get restless a few hours into a hangout. 4 I even once went on a free 10-day silent meditation retreat — not for the meditation, but for the silence.
1 So I can relate to author Anneli Rufus, who wrote in Party of One: The Loners’ Manifesto: “When parents on TV shows punished their kids by ordering them to go to their rooms, I was confused. 2 I loved my room. 3 Being there behind a locked door was a treat. 4 To me a punishment was being ordered to play games with my cousin Louis.”
1 Unsociable tendencies like these are often far from an ideal. 2 Abundant research shows the harms of social isolation, considered a serious public health problem in countries that have rapidly ageing populations (though talk of a “loneliness epidemic” may be exaggerated).? 3 In the UK, the Royal College of General Practitioners says that loneliness has the same risk level for premature death as diabetes. 4 Strong social connections are important for cognitive functioning, motor function and a smoothly running immune system.
1 This is especially clear from cases of extreme social isolation. 2 Examples of people kept in captivity, children kept isolated in abusive orphanages, and prisoners kept in solitary confinement all show how prolonged solitude can lead to hallucinations and other forms of mental instability.
1 But these are severe and involuntary cases of aloneness. 2 For those of us who just prefer plenty of alone time, emerging research suggests some good news: there are upsides to being alone — for both our work lives and our emotional well-being.?
1 Solitude is a time for reflection, for thinking about things more deeply. 2 In a world increasingly focused on speed and competitiveness, solitude is precious and something to be treasured. 3 And there are benefits in learning to love your solitude.
1 One key benefit of solitude is improved creativity. 2 Gregory Feist, who focuses on the psychology of creativity at California’s San Jose State University, has defined creativity as thinking or activity with two key elements: originality and usefulness. 3 He has found that personality traits commonly associated with creativity are openness (receptiveness to new thoughts and experiences), self-confidence, and autonomy — which may include “a lack of concern for social norms” and “a preference for being alone”. 4 In fact, Feist’s research on both artists and scientists shows that one of the most prominent features of creative folks is their lesser interest in socialising.
1 One reason for this is that such people are likely to spend sustained time alone working on their craft. 2 Plus, Feist says, many artists “are trying to make sense of their internal world and a lot of internal personal experiences that they’re trying to give expression and meaning to through their art.” 3 Solitude allows for the reflection and observation necessary for that creative process.?
1 A recent justification of these ideas came from University at Buffalo psychologist Julie Bowker, who researches social withdrawal. 2 Social withdrawal is usually categorised into three types: shyness caused by fear or anxiety; avoidance, from a dislike of socialising; and unsociability, from a preference for solitude. 3 A paper by Bowker and her colleagues was the first to show that a type of social withdrawal could have a positive effect — they found that creativity was linked specifically to unsociability. 4 They also found that unsociability had no correlation with aggression (shyness and avoidance did).? 5 This was significant because while previous research had suggested that unsociability might be harmless, Bowker and colleagues’ paper showed that it could actually be beneficial. 6 Unsociable people are likely to be “having just enough interaction,” Bowker says. 7 “They have a preference for being alone, but they also don’t mind being with others.”
1 Still, it turns out that solitude is important for more than creativity. 2 It’s commonly believed that leaders need to be sociable. 3 But this depends, among other things, on the personalities of their employees. 4 One 2011 study showed that in branches of a pizza chain where employees were more passive, outgoing bosses were associated with higher profits. 5 But in branches where employees were more active, introverted leaders were more effective. 6 One reason for this is that introverted people are less likely to feel threatened by strong personalities and suggestions. 7 They’re also more likely to listen.
1 Since ancient times, meanwhile, people have been aware of a link between isolation and mental focus. 2 After all, cultures with traditions of religious hermits believe that solitude is important for enlightenment. 3 Recent research has given us a better understanding of why. 4 One benefit of unsociability is the brain’s state of active mental rest, which goes hand-in-hand with the stillness of being alone. 5 When another person is present, your brain can’t help but pay some attention. 6 This can be a positive distraction. 7 But it’s still a distraction.
1 Daydreaming in the absence of such distractions activates the brain’s default-mode network. 2 Among other functions, this network helps to consolidate memory and understand others’ emotions. 3 Giving free rein to a wandering mind not only helps with focus in the long term but strengthens your sense of both yourself and others.? 4 Paradoxically, therefore, periods of solitude actually help when it comes time to socialise once more. 5 And the occasional absence of focus ultimately helps concentration in the long run.
1 A more recent advocate of thoughtful and productive solitude is Susan Cain, author of Quiet: The Power of Introverts in a World That Can’t Stop Talking and founder of Quiet Revolution, a company that promotes quiet and introvert-friendly workplaces. 2 “These days, we tend to believe that creativity emerges from a decidedly unreserved socialising process, but in fact it requires sustained attention and deep focus,” she says. 3 “Also, humans are such absorbent social beings that when we surround ourselves with others, we automatically take in their opinions and aesthetics. 4 To truly chart our own path or vision, we have to be willing to isolate ourselves, at least for some period of time.”
1 Still, the line between useful solitude and dangerous isolation can be blurry. 2 “Almost anything can be adaptive and maladaptive, depending on how extreme they get,” Feist says. 3 A disorder has to do with dysfunction. 4 If someone stops caring about people and cuts off all contact, this could point to an irrational neglect of social relations. 5 But creative unsociability is a far cry from this. 6 In fact, Feist says, “there’s a real danger with people who are never alone.” 7 It’s hard to examine one’s own thoughts, feelings and motives, to be self-aware, and fully relaxed unless you have occasional solitude.? 8 In addition, introverts tend to have fewer but stronger friendships — which has been linked to greater happiness.
1 As with many things, quality reigns over quantity. 2 Nurturing a few solid relationships without feeling the need to constantly populate your life with endless chatting ultimately may be better for you.?
1 Thus, if your personality tends toward unsociability, you shouldn’t feel the need to change. 2 Of course, that comes with qualifications. 3 But as long as you have regular social contact, you are choosing solitude rather than being forced into it, you have at least a few good friends and your solitude is good for your well-being or productivity, there’s no point agonising over how to fit a square personality into a round hole.

questions.explanation:
【定位】

由题干关键信息 Lots of research 和 harmful to the elderly 定位到 C 段。

【解析】

该段第二句指出，大量研究表明了社交孤立的危害，这在人口迅速老龄化的国家被视为一个严重的公共健康问题。由此可知，题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的 Lots of research 对应原文中的 Abundant research；题干中的 the elderly 对应原文中的 ageing populations。

【定位】

由题干关键信息 artists、think and observe 和 a must for their creation 定位到 H 段。

【解析】

该段提到费斯特的观点：许多艺术家 “都在努力理解自己的内心世界，以及理解他们试图通过艺术来表达和赋予意义的大量内心的个人经历”。独处为这种创作过程所需的反思和观察提供了条件。由此可知，题干是对原文的总结概括。题干中的 artists 是原词重现；题干中的 think and observe 对应原文中的 reflection and observation；题干中的 a must for their creation 对应原文中的 necessary for that creative process。

【定位】

由题干关键信息 one writer、being forced to play with others 和 being kept alone in a room 定位到 B 段。

【解析】

该段最后两句作者说：“在锁着门的房间里待着是一种享受。对我来说，被命令和我的表弟路易斯一起玩游戏才是一种惩罚。” 由此可知，题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中 one writer 指的就是作者自己；题干中的 being forced to play with others 对应原文中的 being ordered to play games with my cousin Louis；题干中的 being kept alone in a room 对应原文中的 Being there behind a locked door。

【定位】

由题干关键信息 Recent research、for the first time 和 a specific link between being creative and being unsociable 定位到 I 段。

【解析】

该段第三句指出，鲍克尔及其同事的论文首次表明，一种形式的社交退缩可能有积极影响 —— 他们发现，创造力与不爱交际有特定联系。由此可知，题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的 Recent research 对应原文中的 A paper by Bowker and her colleagues；题干中的 the first 是原词重现；题干中的 a specific link between being creative and being unsociable 对应原文中的 creativity was linked specifically to unsociability。

【定位】

由题干关键信息 willing to stay alone at least for some time 和 plot our own course 定位到 M 段。

【解析】

该段引用了苏珊・凯恩的话，其中最后一句指出：“要真正规划自己的道路或愿景，我们必须愿意至少在一段时间内独处。” 由此可知，题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的 We must be willing to stay alone at least for some time 对应原文中的 we have to be willing to isolate ourselves, at least for some period of time；题干中的 plot our own course 对应原文中的 chart our own path or vision。

【定位】

由题干关键信息 new research、people who prefer being alone 和 work lives and emotional health 定位到 E 段。

【解析】

该段第二句指出，对于我们这些只是更喜欢许多独处时间的人来说，新近的研究带来了好消息：独处是有好处的 —— 无论是对我们的工作生活，还是对我们的情绪健康。由此可知，题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的 new research 对应原文中的 emerging research；题干中的 people who prefer being alone 对应原文中的 those of us who just prefer plenty of alone time；题干中的 work lives 是原词重现，emotional health 对应原文中的 emotional well-being。

【定位】

由题干关键信息 cultivate a few steady relationships 和 busy themselves socialising 定位到 O 段。

【解析】

该段第二句指出，培养几段稳固的关系，而无需不断地用无休止的聊天来填充生活，最终可能对你更有益。由此可知，题干是对原文的同义���述。题干中的 cultivate a few steady relationships 对应原文中的 Nurturing a few solid relationships；题干中的 busy themselves socialising 对应原文中的 constantly populate your life with endless chatting。

【定位】

由题干信息 Allowing your mind to wander freely 和 sharpening your focus in the long run 定位到 L 段。

【解析】

该段第三句指出，让思绪自由驰骋不仅有助于长期的专注，还能增强你对自己和他人的感知。由此可知，题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的 Allowing your mind to wander freely 对应原文中的 Giving free rein to a wandering mind；题干中的 sharpening your focus in the long run 对应原文中的 helps with focus in the long term。

【定位】

由题干信息 Research conducted on artists and scientists 和 creative people are less interested in hanging out with others 定位到 G 段。

【解析】

该段最后一句指出，事实上，费斯特对艺术家和科学家的研究表明，富有创造力的人最显著的特点之一是对社交的兴趣相对较小。由此可知，题干是对原文的同义转述。题干中的 Research conducted on artists and scientists 对应原文中的 Feist’s research on both artists and scientists；题干中的 creative people 对应原文中的 creative folks；题干中的 are less interested in hanging out with others 对应原文中的 their lesser interest in socialising。

【定位】

由题干关键信息 Feist、have difficulty knowing yourself 和 do not stay alone occasionally 定位到 N 段。

【解析】

该段主要介绍了费斯特的观点，其中倒数第二句指出，除非你偶尔独处，否则很难审视自己的思想、感受和动机，很难做到有自我意识和完全放松。由此可知，题干��对原文的同义转述。题干中的 have difficulty knowing yourself 对应原文中的 It’s hard to examine one’s own thoughts, feelings and motives, to be self-aware；题干中的 do not stay alone occasionally 对应原文中的 unless you have occasional solitude。

sections.title: Section C Passage 1
sections.passage:
1 Simulators are most often utilized within industries such as nuclear power, aviation and surgery where failure results in disastrous consequences. 2 To maximize the value from a simulation learning experience, participants should immediately and directly apply their learning to a specific intervention within their organization.
1 Most organizations aspire to deploy significant change programs, only to find them nearly impossible to implement. 2 That is largely because successful change requires more than a vision, it requires a workforce that not only doesn’t resist change, but embraces it.?
1 To achieve success, an organization must build a transformation program that will allow change to be rapidly pulled across its departments and throughout its layers. 2 Regardless of the level of senior management commitment, unless key thought leaders at all levels embrace the change, the initiative will wither and die. 3 To create this kind of widespread passion, learning leaders must expose the workforce to what could be, which will enable them to rethink their mental models, enable them to break free from their deep-rooted paradigms and embrace the opportunity to learn.?
1 Allowing participants to enter a simulated environment provides them with the opportunity to experience alternative realities which can prompt them to rethink their current beliefs.
1 Behavioral change is not easy for most adults. 2 Lectures, training programs and workshops can explain the intellectual elements of transformation, but they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative.? 3 Further, under normal working conditions, managers rarely see the full effect of their employee development efforts. 4 As such, an intervention like a simulation can provide the stimulus for change.
1 An effective simulation can be better than experience as a learning tool because it accelerates time, compresses space, and unlike reality, is specifically designed to maximize participant learning. 2 Simulations provide an immersive learning experience where skills and knowledge can be highlighted in a way reality cannot. 3 The ability to explore, experiment, repeatedly apply knowledge and practice in risk-free models is what makes simulation one of the most productive forms of learning.?
1 Well-designed simulations can enable individuals and groups to develop a deep level of understanding about how their decisions and intuitive responses to business stimuli affect their fellow participants and the organization as a whole. 2 To reap the benefits, however, simulations must feel like reality. 3 At the end of the successful simulation, participants must declare “this is us.” 4 If they don’t, they will view the experience as a game, which can be difficult to apply on the job, or worse, irrelevant to everyday work tasks. 5 To maximize benefits from simulation, participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience to forge a smooth link between learning and doing.?

【定位内容分析】文中2段2句提到：成功的变革不仅需要愿景（successful change requires more than a vision），还需要一支不仅不抵制变革、反而积极接纳变革的员工队伍（it requires a workforce that not only doesn’t resist change, but embraces it）。

【正确选项对比】综上可知，对于成功的变革，更重要的是积极接纳变革的员工，故C选项（They call for enthusiastic support from the workforce. 它们需要员工的热情支持）与原文中成功变革对员工队伍的要求相符，故为正确答案。

【定位内容分析】第 3 段第 3 句提到，为了激发这种广泛的热情（To create this kind of widespread passion），学习领域的负责人（learning leaders）必须让员工看到未来的可能性（must expose the workforce to what could be），这能帮助他们重新审视思维模式（which will enable them to rethink their mental models），摆脱固有观念（enable them to break free from their deep-rooted paradigms），并接纳学习机会（and embrace the opportunity to learn）。

【正确选项对比】综上可知，学习型领导者应该通过让员工看到未来的���能性从而才能激发学习者的变革热情，故A 选项（Allow them to see what could possibly be achieved. 让他们看到可能实现的成果）与原文表述相符，其中 “what could possibly be” 与原文中的 “what could be” 相对应，故为正确答案。

【定位内容分析】

5段2句指出：讲座、培训课程和研讨会（Lectures, training programs and workshops）能够解释变革的理性层面内容（can explain the intellectual elements of transformation），但在触及重大变革举措核心的行为层面时，它们往往效果不佳（but they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative）。此句明确了讲座、培训项目和研讨会在改变员工行为方面的效果是不够有效的。

【正确选项对比】综上可知，原文提到讲座、培训项目和研讨会在触及行为层面时效果不佳，即通常无法改变员工在工作中的行为。选项 A （They are generally incapable of changing workers’ behaviors on the job. 它们通常无法改变员工在工作中的行为）与原文表述相符，故为正确答案。

【定位内容分析】

第 6 段最后一句指出：能够在无风险的模式中探索、试验、反复应用知识并进行实践（The ability to explore, experiment, repeatedly apply knowledge and practice in risk-free models），这使得模拟成为最高效的学习形式之一（is what makes simulation one of the most productive forms of learning）。此句明确了模拟成为高效学习形式的原因。

【正确选项对比】原文提到在无风险模式中探索、试验等能力使模拟成为高效学习形式，选项 D（Its potential for learners to explore, experiment and practice without any risk.它能让学习者在没有任何风险的情况下进行探索、实验和实践。） 与原文表述相符，故为正确答案。

questions.explanation:
【定位】由题干信息词 “simulation”，“participants”，“reap the greatest benefits possible” 可将答案线索定位至7段5句：To maximize benefits（≈reap the greatest benefits possible） from simulation, participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience to forge a smooth link between learning and doing.

【定位内容分析】

7段3句指出：为了最大限度地从模拟中获益（To maximize benefits from simulation），参与者应立即将从体验中学到的知识应用起来（participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience），从而在 “学” 与 “做” 之间建立顺畅的联系（to forge a smooth link between learning and doing）。此句明确了参与者获得最大收益的做法是应用体验所学。

【正确选项对比】原文提到参与者应立即应用所学知识建立 “学” 与 “做” 的联系，也就是立即将所学知识应用到工作中。选项 B （Apply promptly what they learn to their jobs. 立即��他们所学到的知识应用到工作中）与原文表述相符，故为正确答案。

sections.title: Section C Passage 2
sections.passage:
1 GDP growth is not a good indicator of how well a country is performing, and should not be the primary goal of governments. 2 Unlimited growth is not sustainable, and economic thinking is moving toward the idea that we should aim for sustainability in our economic models.? 3 But while a sustainable economy is vital to our future, it is a means to an end, not an end in itself.
1 The idea that governments should focus on happiness has its critics. 2 There are concerns about how happiness can be measured. 3 Is happiness not a fleeting and subjective psychological state? 4 Don’t different people experience different levels of happiness? 5 Even on the broadest interpretation of ‘happiness’ as prosperity or ‘life satisfaction’, people want different things.?
1 Of course, governments cannot impose life satisfaction on citizens. 2 But our happiness relies on collaborative efforts as a society. 3 A government’s obligation lies in creating conditions that promote prosperity. 4 And there is good reason to suppose that such conditions exist, are globally applicable, and are discoverable through research.
1 In a recently published article, philosopher Julian Baggini suggests we should focus on ‘real wealth’ for citizens, which does not depend on GDP growth. 2 Access is key: people do not need to own, but rather access things that enable them to live well.? 3 Technological advances and changes in social behavior enable us to make more efficient use of the assets that we already have. 4 And focusing on access to the resources people need to live better lives could help reduce inequality.
1 As far as it goes, this has much in common with proposals tabled by ‘happiness’ advocates. 2 But it sets the bar far too low for what governments can and should be doing for their citizens.
1 For example, it’s not clear how a ‘real wealth’ economy would remedy the epidemic of mental ill-health that plagues our society. 2 In Western countries, at least — poor mental health is more detrimental to wellbeing than poverty. 3 Over and above a vastly improved provision of therapeutic mental health care, there are preventative measures for improving mental health that governments could and should adopt. 4 The WHO recommends establishing institutions that facilitate community participation—educational programs and interventions that provide skills for promoting mental wellbeing. 5 It says a lot, however, that the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to persuade governments that the cost of taking proposed measures is justified. 6 As long as the economy is their priority, governments need go no further than ensuring citizens’ continued productivity.?
1 To demand that governments set the ‘happiness’ of citizens as their highest priority is to demand that they view citizens as ends in themselves.?

questions.explanation:
【定位】由题干信息词 “more recent thinking of economic growth” 可将答案线索定位于1段1句：GDP growth is not a good indicator of how well a country is performing, and should not be the primary goal of governments.  

【定位内容分析】

1段1句指出：国内生产总值（GDP）增长并非衡量一个国家表现好坏的良好指标（GDP growth is not a good indicator of how well a country is performing），也不应成为各国政府的首要目标（and should not be the primary goal of governments）。此句否定了传统以 GDP 增长为主要目标的观点。

1段2句进一步指出 ：无限增长是不可持续的（Unlimited growth is not sustainable），当前经济理念正逐步向 “经济模式应以可持续性为目标” 转变（and economic thinking is moving toward the idea that we should aim for sustainability in our economic models）。此句明确了经济增长的最新观点是追求可持续性。

【正确选项对比】原文强调经济理念正转向追求经济模式的可持续性，选项 A（It should be made sustainable.它应具有可持续性。） 与之相符，准确体现了关于经济增长的最新观点，故为正确答案。

questions.explanation:
【定位】由题干信息词 “opposed” 和 “governments should focus on happiness” 可将答案线索定位于文章2段1句：The idea that governments should focus on happiness has its critics（≈opposed）.【定位内容分析】

2段1句指出：“政府应将民众幸福作为关注重点” 这一观点（The idea that governments should focus on happiness）不乏批评者（has its critics）。引出反对观点。

接下来，2段2-5句分别阐述了反对理由：人们对 “如何衡量幸福” 存在疑虑（concerns about how happiness can be measured.）；幸福是一种短暂且主观的心理状态（a fleeting and subjective psychological state）；不同的人感受到的幸福程度不同（different people experience different levels of happiness）；即便将 “幸福” 从最宽泛的角度解读为 “富足” 或 “生活满意度”，人们对其的需求也各不相同（people want different things.）。这些都体现了幸福的主观性和个体差异性。

【正确选项对比】综上可知，选项 C （Happiness means different things to different people.幸福对不同人群意义不同。）准确概括了反对者质疑的原因，即幸福对不同人群意义不同，与原文中关于幸福的主观性和个体差异性的描述相符，故为正确答案。

questions.explanation:
【定位】由题干信息词 “Julian Baggini suggest governments”，“ a recently published article” 可将答案线索定位于4段1句：In a recently published article, philosopher Julian Baggini suggests we should focus on ‘real wealth’ for citizens, which does not depend on GDP growth.

【定位内容分析】

4段1句指出：在最近发表的一篇文章中（In a recently published article），哲学家朱利安・巴吉尼提出（philosopher Julian Baggini suggests），我们应关注公民的 “真正财富”（we should focus on ‘real wealth’ for citizens），而这并不依赖于 GDP 增长（which does not depend on GDP growth）。该句引出巴吉尼的观点，并表明我们应该关注的并不是GDP增长。

4段2句进一步指出：“获取权” 是关键（Access is key）：人们无需拥有某物（people do not need to own），只需能获取那些能让他们生活美满的事物即可（but rather access things that enable them to live well）。该句进一步明确了巴吉尼建议的核心是：关注民众获取改善生活资源的途径。

【正确选项对比】综上可知，选项 B（Provide people with access to resources for a better life.为民众提供改善生活的资源获取途径。） 与巴吉尼建议的内容相符，准确概括了其核心观点，故为正确答案。

questions.explanation:
【定位】由题干信息词 “WHO” 和 “economic benefits” ，“improving mental health”可将答案线索定位于文章第 6 段5句：It says a lot, however, that the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to persuade governments that the cost of taking proposed measures is justified.

【定位内容分析】

6段5句指出：世界卫生组织认为有必要借助 “改善心理健康所带来的经济收益”（the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health） 来说服各国政府（to persuade governments）：采取拟议措施的成本是合理的（the cost of taking proposed measures is justified），本句提出了 WHO 借助经济效益说服政府的现象。

进而6段6句指出：只要经济仍是政府的优先事项（s long as the economy is their priority），他们就只需确保民众保持持续的生产力而无需更进一步（governments need go no further than ensuring citizens’ continued productivity）。 说明只要经济是政府优先事项，政府就只需关注公民生产力，暗示了政府以经济发展为优先，所以 WHO 才需要用经济收益说服。

【正确选项对比】综上可知，选项 D （Governments still take economic development as their priority.政府仍以经济发展为优先关注点）与原文中对 WHO 行为原因的分析相符，准确说明了政府仍以经济发展为优先，所以 WHO 要强调经济利益来证明建议合理，故为正确答案。

choices.label: C
choices.text: Governments should consider citizens’ views in decision-making.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Governments should set sustained productivity as their top priority.

questions.explanation:
【定位】由题干信息词 “the end of the passage” 结合段落顺序出题原则可将答案线索定位于文章7段：To demand that governments set the ‘happiness’ of citizens as their highest priority is to demand that they view citizens as ends in themselves.  

【定位内容分析】

7段指出： 要求政府将公民的 “幸福” 定为最高优先事项（To demand that governments set the ‘happiness’ of citizens as their highest priority），等同于要求政府将公民本身视为最终目标（is to demand that they view citizens as ends in themselves），而非实现其他目标的手段，此句强调政府应将公民幸福作为最高优先级，将公民视为终极目标。

【正确选项对比】综上可知，选项 B “政府目标应以人为本” （Governments’ goal should be people-oriented.）准确概括了作者在文末表达的核心信息，与原文中强调以公民幸福为最高目标、将公民视为终极目标的观点相符，故为正确答案。
